signals.title: [Core][Distributed] Size custom all-reduce buffers at init so batch-invariant mode can use them
signals.text: ### Purpose Fixes #50136. `CustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar()` decides per call whether to use the custom all-reduce or fall through to NCCL, based on `inp_size < self.max_size`. The all-reduce tensor is `[num_tokens, hidden_size]`, so that decision tracks the token count of the forward pass — i.e. batch composition — and the same request can take different reduction orders in different batches. Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` that is a correctness bug, which is why `ParallelConfig` currently forces `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` and every batch-invariant TP run pays the pinned-NCCL path. This removes the size dependency instead of the whole code path. **Which review this is, settled.** The open question was whether the intended guarantee is *per request* (a request is bitwise reproducible under any batching) or *per engine* (a given engine configuration is internally consistent) — a bug under the first reading, a documented limitation under the second. @tolleybot answered it on this thread: per-request is what the production case needs, since regression tests and trusted production output require a prompt to give bitwise-identical logprobs however it is batched, across runs and restarts. This PR is therefore a fix, not a feature. ### What changed **1. Decide once, at init** (`custom_all_reduce.py`). Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, derive the largest all-reduce the engine can ever issue from `max_num_batched_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size` and size `max_size` — and therefore the IPC buffers — to cover it. The gate can then never flip mid-run. If the requirement exceeds the cap, or the config cannot be read, custom all-reduce declines at init and logs why, rather than disabling itself silently. **2. Fail loud, never fall back silently** (`should_custom_ar`). If an all-reduce still exceeds the buffer, raise instead of falling through to NCCL. This is the load-bearing design decision. A silent fallback is precisely the mechanism in #50136; a fix whose failure mode reproduces the bug it fixes would be worse than no fix. If the bound is ever wrong — an unmodelled path, a padded width I did not account for — the run stops with a message naming the tensor size and the buffer, instead of quietly producing non-reproducible logprobs. **3. Pin the kernel** (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh`). Force `cross_device_reduce_1stage` for all sizes under batch invariance, and hard error on an explicit `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage`. The 1-stage kernel sums over absolute rank indices with no address reordering (its own comment notes the result is bitwise identical across ranks); the 2-stage kernel partitions by size and rotates accumulation order per rank, so it cannot be invariance-safe. **4. Drop unaudited backends** (`cuda_communicator.py`). Under batch invariance, exclude AITER's custom all-reduce from the dispatch chain. FlashInfer is already excluded upstream by #52998, which landed the same guard while flipping the FlashInfer default on; this change builds on that guard rather than repeating it. QuickReduce is not excluded — it is constructed only on ROCm (`current_platform.is_rocm()`), so it is unreachable on the CUDA configurations validated here, but on ROCm it would be tried first. Under batch invariance on CUDA the chain is `['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']`. The env pin in `override_envs_for_invariance()` is retained as belt-and-braces: since #52998, the communicator itself excludes FlashInfer under batch invariance, so the pin is redundant for dispatch but guards against future refactors of that logic. **5. Stop forcing the disable** (`config/parallel.py`), now that (1) makes the decision fixed for the process lifetime. The platform-support disable (`if not current_platform.use_custom_allreduce()`) is untouched. **6. Test + docs.** A TP≥4 batch-invariance test in `tests/v1/determinism/` (the suite currently runs everything at TP=1, so the all-reduce path was untested — that gap is why #50136 was possible to write), and `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` updated to describe the new behaviour. ### Validation Bitwise comparison of output token IDs **and** per-step logprobs as raw float32 bit patterns (not `allclose`) across batch compositions: bs=1 reference, full mixed batch, shuffled batch, and tile-boundary batches of 17 and 65. | Arm | Config | Invariance | Custom AR engaged | Largest tensor | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | dense, TP=4, patched | clean | 4/4 ranks, 9918 calls each | 25,165,824 B | | 2 | dense, TP=4, `disable_custom_all_reduce` (control) | clean | none, as expected | — | | 3 | dense, long context (2048/4096) | clean | 4/4 ranks | 25,165,824 B | | 4 | MoE (Qwen3-30B-A3B), TP=4 | clean | 4/4 ranks | 33,554,432 B | | 5 | fault injection (buffer forced to 4 KiB) | raises | — | — | | 6 | throughput, patched vs control | clean both | 4/4 vs none | 25,165,824 B | Three things make those greens checkable rather than merely green. **The bound predicts the observed maximum exactly.** Dense: largest tensor through the custom kernel = 25,165,824 B = `8192 × 1536 × 2`. MoE: 33,554,432 B = `8192 × 2048 × 2`. Both are exactly `max_num_batched_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size`, which is the formula the buffer is sized from. Resulting buffers were 30 MiB and 40 MiB per rank. Engagement counts are read from each worker with `collective_rpc`, so they are exact per-rank values (`calls=9918`, identical on ranks 0–3), not log-derived estimates. **Every patched arm crossed the old threshold.** 25,165,824 B is 3.0× the 8 MiB constructor default that applied before this change, and the MoE arm's 33,554,432 B is 4.0×. (The `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` clamp is unreachable under batch invariance, since `override_envs_for_invariance()` sets `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0`.) So these runs exercised tensors that previously fell through to NCCL — they sat in the regime where the gate used to flip, not one where it never would have. **Both guards fire with their intended messages.** Injecting a 4 KiB buffer so a real all-reduce exceeds it: ``` RuntimeError: custom all-reduce received a 25165824 byte tensor, above the 4096 byte batch-invariant buffer. Falling back to NCCL would break batch invariance. Re-run with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT unset, or file a bug with the model and max_num_batched_tokens so the bound can be corrected. ``` And `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage` under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: ``` VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage is incompatible with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1: cross_device_reduce_2stage partitions the message by size and accumulates in a rank-rotated order, so an element's summation order changes with message size (i.e. with batch composition) and differs across owning ranks. ``` Throughput, batch-invariant mode, same workload, identical output (14,784 tokens in both arms): ``` patched (custom AR) 8006.4 tok/s TTFT p50 53.40 ms TPOT p50 8.48 ms control (NCCL only) 3906.0 tok/s TTFT p50 67.61 ms TPOT p50 17.34 ms → 2.05x ``` See the note on this number in "Tested / not tested" below — an earlier run on a different workload measured +84%, so the direction reproduces but the magnitude does not. #### Re-validation on current main (post-#52998) Rebased onto `main` @ `6259572b2` (which includes #52998's FlashInfer default flip and its batch-invariance guard) and re-validated on the same hardware class: 4× A100-SXM4-40GB, NVSwitch NV12 all-to-all (P2P 262.0 GB/s, 24 µs/hop — matching the original run). - Dispatch under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, TP=4, with FlashInfer **installed**: resolves to `['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']`; FlashInfer, AITER, QuickReduce, and both symm-mem paths not constructed. - Dense arm: CLEAN across all 5 batch compositions, 4/4 ranks engaged (exact per-rank counts via `collective_rpc`), largest tensor 25,165,824 B = 8192 × 1536 × 2 — byte-identical to the original bound prediction — within the 30 MiB buffer, `largest <= max_size` on every rank, zero tracebacks. - Routing tests 5/5 green; `pre-commit --all-files` clean for this PR's files (mypy ran and passed; the one repo-wide failure, `test-nonroot-entrypoint`, also fails on unpatched main). Two recorded deviations from the original run: host driver 595.71.05 (vs 580.65.06; same nvcc 13.0.88 toolchain), and `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="8.0;9.0a"` — required because current main does not compile for SM 8.0 alone (a GDN/KDA `#ifdef` guard mismatch in `csrc/libtorch_stable`, upstream and unrelated to this PR; will be reported separately). The A100 still executes SM 8.0 code. GPU evidence above was gathered at `d3cb5924b6`; the pushed commit `edfb2f5b2d` differs from it by a one-line ruff-format wrap in a test file (no runtime code). The full determinism harness used for the matrix above now lives on a follow-up branch -- https://github.com/mosafariuk/vllm/tree/test/batch-invariant-validation-harness -- so this PR carries the fix plus its regression test: 131 LOC functional (`vllm/` + `csrc/`) and 158 LOC of test. ### Tested / not tested **Tested.** 4× A100-SXM4-40GB with NVSwitch (`NV12` all-to-all), driver 580.65.06, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, built from source. TP=4, bf16, chunked prefill and CUDA graphs enabled, for a dense model (Qwen2.5-1.5B, `hidden_size=1536`) and an MoE model (Qwen3-30B-A3B, `hidden_size=2048`). **Not tested, and guarded rather than assumed:** - **The MXFP4-padded MoE path.** `fused_moe` pads the routed hidden dimension before the all-reduce and truncates after, so the reduced tensor is wider than `hidden_size`. That padding is gated to the TRT-LLM MXFP4 path (`hidden_dim_unpadded > 0`), which needs Blackwell-class hardware I do not have. The MoE arm exercised MoE collectives and expert-parallel shapes but not the padded width. - **Multi-node symmetric memory / MNNVL multicast.** It disables itself when the group is not single-node, so TP=4 on one node cannot reach it. - **TP sizes other than 4**, non-NVSwitch topologies, and speculative decoding. - **QuickReduce on ROCm.** It is constructed only on ROCm and would be tried first in the dispatch chain there; the CUDA validation cannot reach it. Not excluded and not validated. Every unreached path above except QuickReduce on ROCm either declines custom all-reduce at init with a logged reason or hits the fail-loud `RuntimeError` in `should_custom_ar()`; QuickReduce is unguarded and would be selected ahead of the custom path there. **The throughput result is directional, not a specification.** Two runs on this configuration measured **+84%** and **+105%** on different workloads — same direction, materially different magnitude. The control is not ordinary NCCL: `override_envs_for_invariance()` pins `NCCL_MIN/MAX_NCHANNELS=1` and `NCCL_NTHREADS=1`, so the baseline is deliberately serialised NCCL, which is the cost this change removes. Treat the direction as reproducible and the magnitude as workload-specific. ### The memory trade-off — the call I made The buffer now scales with model width. Measured and projected, per rank: | `hidden_size` | raw bound | with 1.25× margin | outcome | |---|---|---|---| | 1536 (Qwen2.5-1.5B, measured) | 24 MiB | 30 MiB | fits | | 2048 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, measured) | 32 MiB | 40 MiB | fits | | 8192 (70B class) | 128 MiB | 160 MiB | fits | | 16384 | 256 MiB | 320 MiB | exceeds cap → declines at init, uses NCCL | Only the 1536 and 2048 rows are measured; the 8192 and 16384 rows are the formula evaluated, not runs. I capped it at 256 MiB/rank — a number chosen against that arithmetic rather than against a wide-model run — so everything up to roughly `hidden_size ≈ 13k` gets the custom path and wider models fall back cleanly at startup with a logged reason. That is where I chose to stop paying, given the alternative is the serialised-NCCL path. Both the cap and the 1.25× margin (which exists because I could not bound the MoE padding exactly) are policy numbers and one-line changes if you would put them elsewhere. If you would rather not spend the memory at all, the alternative is to keep the blanket disable and document why it is load-bearing — I am happy to send that instead; it is a small docs-and-comment change. ### How the validation was checked Five defects were found during this work by cross-checks rather than by the tests passing. Each is listed with the check that now catches its class, because the checks are the part that generalises. 1. **`git apply --3way` reported per-file success, then rolled the whole patch back** when a later file failed — leaving the kernel gate, the config change and the backend filtering absent with no error printed. Caught by a semantic grep for the changed symbols, not by the tool's output. That grep now runs before every build. 2. **The hand-port to current `main` dropped `self._custom_ar_calls = 0` and `self._custom_ar_max_bytes = 0`** while keeping all six uses. `__init__` has ten early returns, so grepping the attribute name still passed; the defect surfaced as an `AttributeError` at engine init. Now covered by an AST check asserting that any attribute other methods read is assigned at the **top level** of `__init__`, so completing the constructor guarantees it exists. The check was verified to fail on the pre-fix file. 3. **The semantic grep itself produced two false alarms** — it matched lowercase `batch_invariant` where the code says `envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, and matched `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` against upstream's unrelated platform-support guard. It now asserts the batch-invariance disable is absent **and** the platform guard is present, as separate conditions. 4. **The test's engagement assertion read `capfd` before engine shutdown.** Under `capfd`, fd 1 is a regular file rather than a tty, so worker processes block-buffer their output and flush only on exit. The assertion read zero markers while 21 were present in the log — a false red that, if "fixed" by weakening the assertion, would have removed the guard. The test now reads the counters directly from each worker via `collective_rpc`, which is immune to buffering, yields exact per-rank counts, and additionally asserts `largest <= max_size`. 5. **An earlier harness summed per-rank milestone floors** and reported a call count the data did not support. It now reports rank count and per-rank floor separately, and the test reports exact counts. The test ships with a counterpart, `test_engagement_assertion_can_fail`, that runs the same engine with the custom path disabled: output stays invariant, so a test checking only reproducibility would pass, and the engagement assertion must fail. It runs by default rather than being skipped. ### The contract question — resolved Is the intended guarantee **per request** (this request is bitwise reproducible under any batching) or **per engine** (a given engine configuration is internally consistent)? The size gate is a bug under the first reading and a documented limitation under the second. I had assumed the first because it is what makes batch invariance useful for RL rollouts where trainer and sampler must agree, but flagged it as an assumption about intent. @tolleybot resolved it in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50505#issuecomment-5246281546: per-request is what the production case needs — regression tests plus trusted production output mean a prompt has to give bitwise-identical logprobs no matter what it is batched with, across runs and restarts, and per-engine consistency does not help there. He also noted that the `ParallelConfig` guard in #51292 was a placeholder rather than a vote for per-engine. This PR is scoped as a fix on that basis. --- *Disclosure: this work was done with AI assistance (Claude). I ran the experiments, reviewed the changes, and take responsibility for the content.*

signals.title: [Core][MRV2] Support eagle3 spec decode with pipeline parallel
signals.text: ## Purpose EAGLE3-style speculative decoding (`eagle3` / `dflash` / `dspark`) is rejected outright when pipeline parallelism is enabled: ``` ValueError: <method> with pipeline parallel is not supported. ``` The drafter runs on the last PP rank, but it consumes auxiliary hidden states tapped from target layers that may live on earlier stages, and those tensors were dropped at the stage boundary. This PR forwards them and lifts the guard. Lifting the guard alone is not sufficient. The code behind it had never executed, so it hid a stack of latent defects in the shared PP path — all of them reachable only once spec decode and PP run together, which means they were unobservable rather than latent-but-live: 1. **Draft tokens never reached the non-last ranks.** Only the last rank runs the drafter, so `req_states.draft_tokens` is written nowhere else — yet the *first* rank owns `embed_tokens` and builds the embeddings for the whole pipeline. It was embedding the scheduler's `PLACEHOLDER_TOKEN_ID` (`-1`) into the draft slots, so the last rank verified real proposals against logits computed from placeholders. Silent corruption. Fixed by broadcasting the proposals from the last rank on the existing deferred slot, which has identical production and consumption timing. 2. **`compute_need_sampled_mask` ended the broadcast early.** The scheduler advances `num_computed_tokens` by the full scheduled width up front and rolls the rejected part back in `update_from_output`, which under PP lands *after* the next batch is scheduled. Reading the inflated count marked requests as finishing up to `num_speculative_tokens` early, after which the last rank stopped broadcasting and the other ranks' `last_sampled_tokens` froze, repeating a stale token. 3. **The sampled-token broadcast width could mismatch.** `receive()` always allocates `max_sample_len` columns while `broadcast()` sent whatever width the sampler produced, and the non-spec path returns width 1. NCCL does not diagnose the count mismatch: the root completes and the peer hangs until the watchdog fires, so any PP + spec-decode run deadlocked on its first prefill. Fixed by padding the send side; `post_update` stops at `num_sampled`, so the pad columns are never read. ### Design Aux-state forwarding is added generically on `EagleModelMixin`. A stage packs its own taps plus those inherited from upstream into the `IntermediateTensors` payload, and sizes its recv buffers from the same rule — a tap `a` is upstream iff `a <= start_layer` — so send and recv counts agree with no negotiation. Models opt in with `supports_aux_hidden_states_over_pp`. The previous blanket error is retained for those that do not, now raised with the offending model named. Kimi-K3 opts in; no other model does, so **EAGLE3 and dflash under PP remain gated and untested.** Two smaller changes ride along, both no-ops for configurations that worked before (spec decode under PP > 1 was rejected outright): the DSpark drafter gets a real vocab embedding on the last stage, where the target's is a `PPMissingLayer`; and the draft parallel config stops inheriting the target's PP size, since the drafter is instantiated only on the last stage and is never itself pipelined. ### Scope: capped at `pipeline_parallel_size <= 2` `GPUModelRunner.load_model` raises `NotImplementedError` above 2. This reflects validation coverage, not a known defect. The forwarding rule is size-agnostic by construction and the accounting is unit-tested up to pp=8. But pp>2 is the first topology with a **middle** stage, which must both adopt upstream taps and contribute its own to the same payload, and no such run has happened on hardware. The conservative default is deliberate because this feature does not fail loudly: a drafter fed mis-ordered or missing taps still emits syntactically valid proposals that simply get rejected more often, so the only symptom is a depressed acceptance rate. Lifting the cap should require an acceptance-rate comparison at pp>2, not just a successful boot. Happy to drop the cap if maintainers would rather have the untested-but-general path available. ### Note on commit 1 The first commit is an independent bugfix — `MambaHybridModelState.postprocess_state` feeds an int32 `idx_mapping` to `index_fill_`, which accepts only int64: ``` IndexError: index_fill_(): Expected dtype int64 for index. ``` **This is reachable on main today with no speculative decoding involved.** Its only caller is the non-last-PP-rank path in `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`, so any Mamba-hybrid model (Jamba, Falcon-H1, Nemotron-H, Qwen3-Next, MiniMax, Kimi Linear) crashes under `pipeline_parallel_size >= 2` with a chunked-prefill batch. It is included here because Kimi-K3 is a hybrid model and hits it under PP. Glad to split it into its own PR if preferred. ## Test Plan **Unit.** A CPU test for the aux accounting invariant, no distributed init required: ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py ``` 12 cases over pp ∈ {1,2,3,4,6,8}, exercising the real `EagleModelMixin` and real `get_pp_indices`. Covers tap ordering and the boundary-tap double-count hazard (a tap landing exactly on `start_layer` must be counted as upstream by exactly one stage). The parametrization intentionally runs past the pp<=2 cap, since the accounting is general and this is what a future enablement would build on. **End-to-end.** Kimi-K3 (93 layers, DSpark drafter, `num_speculative_tokens=7`) at TP8 × PP2 on 2× 8×B200 with EFA. Two checks: 1. *Correctness*: greedy decode compared token-for-token against the identical topology with speculative decoding disabled. Speculative decoding is supposed to be output-neutral, so any divergence is a bug. 2. *Acceptance rate*: the sensitive detector. Corruption of aux taps crossing the PP boundary degrades acceptance before it produces visibly wrong text. Throughput measured on 128 fixed GSM8K prompts, same seed, concurrency 1 → 32. ## Test Result Unit: 12 passed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean. **Correctness**: greedy output is token-for-token identical to the same topology without speculative decoding. **Acceptance**: 2.32 of 7 draft tokens per step. **Throughput** (output tok/s, GSM8K, 128 prompts): | Concurrency | No spec | Spec (PP2) | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 77.30 | 174.52 | 2.26× | | 4 | 255.77 | 461.53 | 1.80× | | 8 | 423.86 | 714.01 | 1.68× | | 32 | 1138.69 | 1584.07 | 1.39× |

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fix MiniMax M3 prompt reasoning initialization
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #46042. Fixes #50549. MiniMax-M3 adaptive reasoning can leak `<mm:think>` or `</mm:think>` into streaming `content` because parser initialization scans the entire rendered prompt. Instructional or example marker pairs can therefore make the parser conclude that reasoning already ended before generation starts. This PR adds a prompt-boundary state hook and initializes MiniMax-M3 from `thinking_mode`: `enabled` starts in reasoning, `disabled` starts after reasoning, and `adaptive` lets generated output markers determine the state. ## Implementation summary - preserves the existing reasoner behavior by default, with MiniMax-M3 overriding only prompt-boundary initialization - carries the request-local reasoning state through Chat Completions, Responses, streaming parsing, structured output, offline chat, and batched serving - keeps unresolved adaptive state deferred until generated tokens establish a boundary - handles structured-output masks, alternative marker tokenizations, direct-content replay, continuation state, and parser reset after built-in tool turns Although the visible symptom is parser-level, the state has to cross each place that creates or reuses a reasoning parser. Otherwise one serving path can fall back to the old full-prompt scan or leak continuation state between requests. <details> <summary>Detailed implementation scope</summary> - uses `is_reasoning_end_from_prompt()` in online, offline, Responses, streaming, and structured-output initialization - scopes deferred adaptive marker checks to generated tokens so prompt examples cannot activate the grammar - allows grammar-valid tokens plus every decoded reasoning-marker tokenization while adaptive state is unresolved - replays direct adaptive content through the grammar, including ambiguous prefixes and speculative draft state - derives continuation state from the final assistant message only and preserves open or closed `thinking` content parts - propagates incomplete Responses reasoning items to frontend and engine parsers - clears continuation-only state and refreshes the frontend parser after Responses built-in tool turns rerender the prompt - keeps batch parsers request-local and initializes each engine-side structured-output parser from its prompt once </details> ## Review focus 1. Default compatibility of `is_reasoning_end_from_prompt()` and the MiniMax-M3 `thinking_mode` override 2. Deferred adaptive transitions in structured output, including generated-token-only checks and marker tokenization boundaries 3. Request isolation and continuation reset across Responses, batch, offline chat, and built-in tool turns ## Validation Local focused validation: - MiniMax-M3 reasoning parser: 44 passed - reasoning-aware structured output: 21 passed - offline chat prompt-state forwarding: 1 passed - batch prompt-state forwarding: 3 passed - Responses serving: 23 passed, 1 expected xfail - `ruff check`, `ruff format`, Python `compileall`, and `git diff --check` passed The 92 focused tests ran in a CPU-only temporary environment with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty`. External MiniMax-M3 validation: - [Parser validation on aarch64](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50594#issuecomment-5281778580): 44/44 parser tests passed and the deployed prompt-state failure was reproduced and confirmed - [Production end-to-end validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50594#issuecomment-5290659689): the streaming marker leak was fixed on both OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible APIs, Anthropic streaming `thinking` blocks were restored, and tool calls remained working The production deployment backported the parser, chat utility, and serving call-site changes rather than running the complete 17-file branch. The remaining Responses, batch, offline, and structured-output paths are covered by the focused CPU tests above and still need repository CI. ## Current CI status The current `pre-run-check` is stopped by the first-contributor authorization gate, and the pre-commit job was skipped. CI requires a `verified`, `ready`, or `ready-run-all-tests` label, or a trusted reviewer action such as `/ci run`. Repository-wide GPU CI has not run yet. ## Related work - #45718 fixed split-token MiniMax-M3 marker parsing, but not prompt-boundary state initialization. - #50152 identified the same full-prompt scan failure and demonstrated the production symptom, but closed without merging. - #48550 also addresses prompt-mode initialization while adding broader speculative-decoding and tool-parser changes. - This PR is limited to prompt-boundary reasoning initialization and the state propagation needed to preserve it across supported serving paths. <details> <summary>Focused test commands</summary> ```bash uv run pytest -q tests/reasoning/test_minimax_m3_reasoning_parser.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_reasoning_structured_output.py uv run pytest -q tests/entrypoints/llm/test_offline_reasoning_state.py uv run pytest -q tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py -k batch_forwards_prompt_reasoning_state uv run pytest -q tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py ``` </details> ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and regression-test drafting. The commits include `Assisted-by` trailers. The submitter requested the changes after reviewing the proposed scope.

signals.title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Spec Decode] Fix defects on the Kimi-K3 DSpark decode path
signals.text: ## Purpose Two defects on the Kimi-K3 DSpark decode path: 1. The draft model turns cudagraphs off for the whole target model. 2. The multi-token verify is split into one decode per token, which costs two waits on the GPU every forward. ### (1) A draft's attention decides the target's cudagraph mode Before it captures anything, vLLM asks every attention group whether it can be graphed and takes the lowest answer. Groups that belong to a spec-decode draft are asked too: ```python for group in groups: cg_support = builder.get_cudagraph_support(vllm_config, group.kv_cache_spec) if cg_support.value < min_cg_support.value: min_cg_support = cg_support # draft-owned groups included ``` That lowest answer then decides the mode for the *target*: ```python if (cudagraph_mode.decode_mode() == CUDAGraphMode.FULL and uniform_decode_query_len > 1 and min_cg_support.value < AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH.value): cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.NONE # PIECEWISE only if splitting_ops ``` Kimi-K3 meets all three conditions. The target runs AiterMLA, which reports `UNIFORM_BATCH`, and the recipe puts the draft on TritonMLA, which reports `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE`. The draft's answer is the lower one, so **5 draft layers turn cudagraphs off for all 93 target layers**. The draft never needed that help: `init_cudagraph_manager` already looks at its own support level and runs the draft eagerly when it cannot be graphed. **Fix: leave a draft that already checks itself out of the target's decision, and keep a second minimum for the check that still needs every group.** Some drafts do not check themselves. Eagle, mtp and gemma4 (`AutoRegressiveSpeculator`), and `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`, simply use whatever mode the target ended up with. For those the downgrade is doing real work: take it away and they would capture in a mode their own backend cannot run. So the test is a flag on the speculator, not its class: ```python if isinstance(speculator, DraftModelSpeculator) and speculator.sizes_own_cudagraph_mode: return speculator.draft_attn_layer_names ``` `init_attn_backend` now takes two minimums instead of one. The old `min_cg_support` still covers every group, and adaptive verification reads it, so that check is unchanged. The new `graph_min_cg_support` leaves out groups made up entirely of draft layers, and only the cudagraph decision reads it. A group that mixes target and draft layers stays in both. Today only `DFlashSpeculator` and `DSparkSpeculator` set the flag. ### (2) The verify block is split into one decode per token The draft proposes several tokens at once and the target checks them in one block — 8 of them with the `num_speculative_tokens=7` this recipe uses. Each token in the block may only look at the text before it, not after it. In bf16 there is no asm kernel for fewer than 16 heads with more than one query token, so a 12-head rank sends this block to Gluon instead. (With an fp8 cache the q-row fold — folding query rows into the head dimension — does give it an asm kernel, so only bf16 comes here.) The old code faked the "look backward only" rule by issuing one single-token decode per verify token, each with its own slice of the KV list. Building those slices meant rewriting the paged-KV table on every forward, and twice asking the GPU for a value and waiting for it: ```python new_indptr = torch.cat([old_indptr.new_zeros(1), row_len.cumsum(0)]).to(torch.int32) total = int(new_indptr[-1].item()) # host sync ... new_indices = decode.paged_kv_indices[src] # gather over the whole batch mla_gluon(..., page_table=new_indices, seq_info=new_indptr, min_kv_seq_len=int(row_len.min())) # host sync ``` **Fix: give Gluon the whole block at once, which it already accepts, and delete the splitting.** Gluon takes a `[batch, qlen, nhead, dim]` query and applies the backward-only rule itself, so reshaping the query is all that is needed. The page table goes through untouched: ```python q_nope = q_nope.view(batch_size, qlen, num_q_heads, self.kv_lora_rank) q_pe = q_pe.view(batch_size, qlen, num_q_heads, self.qk_rope_head_dim) mla_gluon(..., page_table=decode.paged_kv_indices, seq_info=decode.paged_kv_indptr, min_kv_seq_len=decode.min_kv_seq_len) ``` Net −71 lines in `rocm_aiter_mla.py`. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py # 8, CPU only pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py # 2, ROCm + AITER ``` The first needs no GPU: it drives `init_attn_backend` with stubs. The second builds the real AITER backend and metadata on device and replaces the Gluon kernel with a spy, so it skips off ROCm. End to end on 8x MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-aa9903490c616dc6871e5acc62cec7bb1e5e9434`, with `/model` = `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` and `/draft` its DSpark draft. Serve flags follow #51253: ```bash vllm serve /model --served-model-name k3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 --block-size 128 --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --load-format auto --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \ --compilation-config '{"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/draft", "num_speculative_tokens":7, "attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA"}' \ --port 8000 ``` Run it twice: as written for the fp8 numbers, then with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` dropped for the bf16 numbers. That one flag is what sends the verify to the padded asm decode or to Gluon. ```bash for C in 1 8; do vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --model k3 --tokenizer /model --trust-remote-code --port 8000 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \ --ignore-eos --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((C == 1 ? 16 : 48)) done lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \ --model_args model=k3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 \ --apply_chat_template --gen_kwargs temperature=0 ``` `--apply_chat_template` and `tokenized_requests=False` are both needed against a chat endpoint. `--gen_kwargs temperature=0` matters because this model's `generation_config.json` sets no temperature, so the default is 1.0 and the run would otherwise be sampled. ## Test Result Unit tests: **10 passed** (8 without a GPU, plus the 2 ROCm ones). For the end-to-end runs the control is this branch's base and the patched side is its head, in the same container, against the same aiter build. Both dtypes are here because the KV cache dtype picks the decode kernel, and only one of them reaches the kernel (2) changes. **fp8 sends the verify to the aiter asm decode**, and that is the production setup — the Kimi-K3 recipe runs `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Both of Gluon's checks turn a quantized cache away, so the verify falls through to the padded asm path: `get_mla_padded_q` pads 12 heads to 16, then `mla_decode_fwd`. That run covers (1), and the asm decode is the kernel that restored capture now has to hold. **bf16 sends the verify to Gluon**, and it is the only setup that does, so it is the one that covers (2). | KV cache | decode kernel | conc. | base | patched | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | fp8 | aiter asm (padded) | 1 | 14.82 tok/s, TPOT 66.09 ms | **67.41 tok/s, TPOT 13.44 ms** | **4.5x** | | fp8 | aiter asm (padded) | 8 | 108.49 tok/s, TPOT 66.72 ms | **291.06 tok/s, TPOT 23.96 ms** | **2.7x** | | bf16 | Gluon | 1 | 15.01 tok/s, TPOT 65.00 ms | **72.22 tok/s, TPOT 12.24 ms** | **4.8x** | | bf16 | Gluon | 8 | 102.57 tok/s, TPOT 68.88 ms | **309.07 tok/s, TPOT 22.37 ms** | **3.0x** | Both control runs report `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, 8 downgrade warnings and 0 captures. Both patched runs report 0 warnings and 8 captures, with the draft eager on all 8 ranks. Accuracy, on the full GSM8K test set (1319 questions), 5-shot, greedy, fp8 KV: | | flexible-extract | strict-match | |---|---|---| | base | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 | 0.9598 ± 0.0054 | | patched | 0.9651 ± 0.0051 | 0.9644 ± 0.0051 | Operator benchmark for (2), against Gluon directly: 12 heads, kv_lora 512, rope 64, bf16 KV. The splitting work is inside the timed region, because the old code did it on every forward. Over batch 8-32, qlen 2-8 and ctx 8k-32k, sending all the tokens at once is **1.52-4.07x faster** — 383.8 us down to 148.0 us at batch 8, qlen 8, ctx 8192. Outputs agree to 1.5e-05. --- Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the commits carry `Co-authored-by: Claude`. I reviewed every changed line, ran the unit tests and the end-to-end runs above myself, and am responsible for the result.

signals.title: [KV offload] Order CPU->GPU loads against the compute stream
signals.text: On models that zero freshly allocated KV blocks (any model with mamba layers, i.e. `needs_kv_cache_zeroing`), a CPU->GPU load in the offloading connector can be silently wiped. `SingleDirectionOffloadingHandler.transfer_async` waited on the compute stream only for GPU->CPU. Loads ran on their own stream with no ordering against the compute stream, which zeroes freshly allocated blocks. When the copy lands first, a pending zeroing of its destination blocks wipes it and the request attends over zeros for its whole cache-hit prefix. No crash, no error, just degraded output. Why the scheduler-side guard doesn't cover this: `_skip_zero_block_ids` only edits the zero list of the step being scheduled — it cannot retract a zeroing already shipped in an earlier step's `SchedulerOutput` for a since-reallocated block. Sync scheduling makes that safe implicitly: the engine blocks on each step's output, so shipped zeroing has provably executed before any later load submits. Async scheduling removes that wait, leaving the pair unordered across the two streams — safe by timing only, which nothing enforces. The skip set remains the only possible guard for writers that bypass CUDA streams (NIXL/RDMA); the stream wait is the only ordering against zeroing already dispatched. Verified on H100 that it is a real guard — same test, same image, with and without the one-line change: | | result | |---|---| | without the fix | fails, 4/5 trials, all 32 loaded blocks zeroed | | with the fix | passes, 5/5 trials |
signals.author: Etelis

signals.title: [Core][RL] Support sparse checkpoint updates through native weight loaders
signals.text:
## Purpose ### Motivation Online RL trainers commonly produce updates in checkpoint/Hugging Face coordinates: a checkpoint name, the full checkpoint shape, and either a dense tensor or flat changed indices and values. These coordinates are not the same as vLLM's runtime parameter coordinates. For example, a checkpoint tensor may be split across tensor-parallel ranks, packed with another checkpoint tensor, or mapped into expert-parallel runtime weights. The existing `sparse_nccl` backend expects an already-resolved runtime parameter name and rank-local indices, so it cannot serve as a general bridge for checkpoint-coordinate updates. This PR adds a small model-loader API that keeps the model's native `model.load_weights()` path as that bridge. The native loader continues to own checkpoint-name mapping, TP/EP placement, and packed/model-specific layouts. ### Design ```mermaid flowchart LR A["One patch-loading call
checkpoint name, full shape/dtype,
values and optional flat indices"] A --> B{"All patches in this call"} B -- "Dense" --> C["Build full checkpoint tensors"] B -- "Sparse" --> D["Build full checkpoint-shaped NaN tensors
index_copy_ fills changed checkpoint positions"] C --> L["One or more model.load_weights(...) calls
native checkpoint-to-runtime mapping
for TP/EP and packed/model-specific layouts"] D --> P["Temporarily replace process-wide
torch.Tensor.copy_
during each serialized sparse loader call"] P --> L L -- "Dense: native loader semantics" --> U["Runtime tensors updated"] L -- "Sparse: each Python Tensor.copy_" --> E{"Floating source and destination
with the same shape?"} E -- "Yes" --> M["Cast source, merge with
where(isnan(source), destination, source),
then call the original copy_"] E -- "No" --> N["Call the original copy_ unchanged
unsupported for sparse patches"] L -. "Sparse custom or non-copy_ write" .-> X["Not intercepted
unsupported for sparse patches"] M --> U N --> Y["Outside the supported sparse behavior"] X --> Y P -. "finally, after model.load_weights
returns or raises" .-> R["Restore the original Tensor.copy_"] ``` `CheckpointWeightPatch` represents either: - a dense checkpoint replacement (`indices=None`), or - a sparse checkpoint patch (`indices` and `values` over the full checkpoint shape). Sparse patches are expanded into checkpoint-shaped NaN staging tensors. The model's native loader maps those tensors into runtime-local destinations. For the supported single-copy loader path, the final same-shaped floating-point `Tensor.copy_` keeps the existing destination at NaN positions and copies the changed values elsewhere. Patches are validated before the first load. Loader calls are bounded by a checkpoint-byte batching target, and a repeated checkpoint name begins a new loader call so repeated patches preserve input order. ### Scope and failure semantics The current implementation is intentionally narrow: - sparse patches require a floating checkpoint dtype and cannot carry NaN as a real update value; - the loader must preserve NaNs through checkpoint-to-runtime mapping and end in a same-shaped floating-point `Tensor.copy_`; - the validated integration uses exclusive, serialized weight updates and a single-copy loader; - composed/multi-stage loaders and custom write paths are not supported; - sparse application is not O(nnz): it allocates a full checkpoint-shaped NaN tensor and runs a dense `torch.where`/copy at the runtime destination; - updates are not transactional. A loader error can leave a partial update, so the caller must restore a known baseline or restart and reseed before serving. ### Companion VERL integration [VERL #7227](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7227) uses this API to add a vLLM consumer for VERL's `delta_sharded` checkpoint-engine wire format. The first update is a dense seed; steady updates contain checkpoint-coordinate indices and changed values. ### Duplication check I searched open vLLM PRs for checkpoint-coordinate weight patch loading and found no matching implementation. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/model_executor/model_loader \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py -q .venv/bin/ruff check --no-cache \ vllm/model_executor/model_loader/checkpoint_weight_patch.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check --no-cache \ vllm/model_executor/model_loader/checkpoint_weight_patch.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py ``` The focused CPU test covers the dense seed, checkpoint-global sparse indices, TP-local slicing, packed Q/K destinations, repeated patch ordering, and restoration of `Tensor.copy_` after the supported path. The companion VERL integration tests additionally cover: - Qwen3-30B-A3B TP8+EP8 sparse-vs-dense and restore comparisons; - real CUDA IPC/ZMQ transfer through the companion VERL adapter; - a two-node full-NCCL versus `delta_sharded` weight-sync comparison. ## Test Result ### Focused repository test - Pytest: **1 passed**. - Ruff check: **passed**. - Ruff format check: **passed**. ### TP8+EP8 integration correctness Qwen3-30B-A3B, BF16, vLLM TP8+EP8: - 8/8 workers passed. - 32/32 selected runtime tensors matched the dense-load target with `torch.equal` after sparse apply. - 32/32 tensors returned to the checkpoint baseline after restore. - The probe covered packed QKV, norm, routed-expert `w13`, and routed-expert `w2` mappings. This is a representative runtime-tensor mapping probe, not a full-model digest or a phase-for-phase training-trajectory comparison. ### Companion VERL integration performance These are end-to-end results from the companion VERL integration, not a microbenchmark of this helper alone. | mode | steady samples | mean | median | range | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Full NCCL | 11 | 51.814 s | 51.812 s | 51.457-52.051 s | | `delta_sharded` + vLLM | 11 | 7.200 s | 7.740 s | 5.943-8.686 s | The ratio of means is **7.196x**; the conservative observed steady ratio is **5.924x**. The mean changed ratio was **0.646%**, and the mean sparse payload was **1129.4 MiB**. The one-time dense seed took **51.9 s** and is excluded from steady-state statistics. Environment: two nodes with 8 H20 GPUs per node; Qwen3-30B-A3B; FSDP1 trainer on one node; vLLM TP8+EP8 Triton-MoE rollout on the other; BF16; VERL V1 `separate_async`; NCCL `NET/Socket` over `eth0`; 12 delta and 12 full steps, with steps 2-12 used for the primary statistics. The two async jobs did not produce phase-aligned reward trajectories. The performance claim is limited to sustained weight-sync time; correctness comes from the independent bit-exact probe. ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex was used for code exploration, implementation assistance, testing, and review.

signals.title: [Frontend] Add Holo2 reasoning parser
signals.text: ## Purpose Add Holo2 reasoning-parser support to the Rust frontend parity roadmap. Python registers `holo2` through `DeepSeekV3ReasoningWithThinkingParser`, which defaults to DeepSeek R1 behavior. The Rust `DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser` alias has a different no-boundary default, so this adds a semantic `Holo2ReasoningParser` alias directly to the prompt-first `DeepSeekR1ReasoningParser`. The change: - exposes `holo2` as an explicit reasoning-parser name; - automatically routes `HCompany/Holo2-*` models to it; - reuses the shared `<think>...</think>` parser without adding another state machine; - adds factory registration and model-routing coverage; - adds a real `HCompany/Holo2-4B` tokenizer/template roundtrip covering enabled, disabled, and default thinking behavior. No tool-parser or inference-engine behavior is changed. Refs #44280 ### Duplicate-work check I reviewed the roadmap comments and searched open PRs by the roadmap issue number and Holo2/Rust reasoning-parser keywords. No existing claim or open PR overlaps this implementation. ## Test Plan - Verify explicit parser registration and factory listing. - Verify automatic routing of `HCompany/Holo2-4B` to `holo2`. - Exercise the real Holo2 tokenizer and chat template through the existing reasoning-and-content roundtrip. - Cover `thinking=true`, `thinking=false`, and omitted/default thinking. - Run the complete `vllm-parser` and `vllm-chat` test suites. - Run repository pre-commit hooks on the changed files. ## Test Result Passed: ```text cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all --check ``` Passed all 698 tests: ```text nix develop path:. cargo nextest run \ --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \ --locked \ -p vllm-parser \ -p vllm-chat ``` Passed: ```text nix develop path:. -c pre-commit run ``` The real HCompany/Holo2-4B tokenizer/template roundtrip passed for enabled, disabled, and default thinking. Model-generation or accuracy evaluation is not applicable because this change does not modify inference, logits, or model output generation. The real-tokenizer/template roundtrip provides parser integration evaluation. Documentation was not changed because the existing reasoning-output documentation already lists holo2; this PR adds Rust frontend parity. ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance was used for repository exploration, implementation planning, code review, and identifying a model-ID casing correction. I reviewed every changed line and ran all tests listed above.

signals.title: [Core] Extensible (growable) KV cache
signals.text: > **Stacked on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51718. Only the commits above that PR's head belong to this one. > This is a **draft** — it cannot merge until https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51718 lands, after which the base will be retargeted to `main`. ## Summary Opt-in growable KV cache (`--enable-extensible-kv-cache`) built on the standardized KV cache layout from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51718. This is the productization of the demonstration https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47363 from @zhuohan123. vLLM sizes the KV cache from a profiling run, then allocates it up front. Any memory the engine consumes *after* profiling — CUDA graph pools, the spec-decode logits all-gather, workspace growth — has to be guessed at via headroom margins, and a wrong guess is either an OOM or wasted HBM. This change reserves virtual address space for the KV cache capacity but commits physical pages incrementally (CUDA `cuMem*` / ROCm `hipMem*`): 1. Allocate the VA reservation, commit one block per layout segment. 2. Run warmup and CUDA graph capture. 3. Measure *actual* post-warmup free memory and re-size. 4. `extend_kv_cache()` maps the remaining pages under the same base pointer. Because each block keeps a fixed offset within its layout segment and the base pointer never moves, captured graphs and layer views stay valid across the growth — no re-view, no re-capture. --- ### What https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51718 buys this The layout standardization removes most of what made the earlier version of this work invasive. Buffer segmentation is now a pure function of `KVCacheLayout.stride_order` (new `num_outer_segments()` helper) instead of per-backend shape/stride/block-dim probing; connector registration views are a plain `narrow(0)` of the logical `[B, H, N, C]` view; and the packed / `block_stride` special cases disappear entirely. The integration is ~30% smaller than the equivalent against `main`. ### Views are authoritative, not `storage.nbytes()` The one contract change worth reviewer attention. Under an extensible cache the untyped storage spans the **reserved** capacity, of which only each view's per-segment block prefix is physically backed. Any code deriving block geometry or registration extents from `untyped_storage().nbytes()` will compute a size that includes unbacked pages. Updated accordingly, with the contract documented on `KVConnectorBase_V1.register_kv_caches`: - `NixlBaseConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches` — collects per-region committed spans and registers those; falls back to the single per-allocation registration when the storage is fully backed. Block-major packing is detected from view strides rather than `nbytes()`. - `get_kv_cache_block_regions` (`v1/worker/utils.py`) — same, which also covers the CPU-offload connector. KV-transfer init is deferred until after `extend_kv_cache`, so connectors only ever register committed memory. On the NIXL path, extend also defragments (release + single-chunk recommit per segment): UCX cannot transfer a VMM region spanning multiple `cuMemCreate` handles. ## Relationship to existing work - **#47363** (@zhuohan123, "Demo implementation of extensible kv cache memory) — this is the productionization of that demo, not a competing implementation. It adds the V1 + V2 runner integration, the measured post-warmup sizing pass, VMM probe/fallback, sleep-mode support, KV connector support, and a ROCm backend. Happy to fold this into #47363 instead if that's preferred. - **#44458** — strictly a dependency; no overlap in changed behavior. - Searched open PRs for extensible/growable/VMM KV cache work; nothing else overlaps. Contributors: @zhuohan123 (original demo), @zjy0516 (packed-storage bounding, sleep gate). ## Testing Unless noted, run against this branch at its current head. **Unit** — `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py -v` → 29/29 pass (GB200, aarch64). **e2e, 1×GB200, CUDA graphs on** — outputs byte-identical to a non-extensible baseline for: standard generation, sleep(level=1)/wake, and `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`. **e2e, sizing under pressure** — Qwen3.5-4B TP4, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=100`, chunk 256, `gpu-memory-utilization=0.92` (a config that OOMs without this change): passes in both eager and cudagraph modes. Sizing 35,277→34,721 tokens (eager), 35,243→34,592 (cudagraph). Functional check 64/43 answers correct. **e2e, NIXL P/D disaggregation** — Qwen3-0.6B, HND, block 128, gsm8k via P/D proxy: | config | gsm8k | expected | |---|---|---| | 1P1D eager | 0.422 | ~0.41 | | 1P1D cudagraph | 0.418 | ~0.41 | | P(TP1)→D(TP2) | 0.415 | ~0.41 | | P(TP2)→D(TP2) | 0.415 | ~0.41 | **Model evaluation** — the feature is opt-in and does not change model outputs; the byte-identical-output comparison above and the gsm8k table are the evidence for that. ### Known gaps - The V2 encoder-cache profiling reservation (last commit) is validated on the equivalent branch against `main` (Qwen2-VL-2B: 16,384-token budget reserved, 238,148 blocks committed) but **has not been re-run on this branch** — the cluster battery above has no multimodal configuration. Will re-run before marking ready. - No unit coverage for `commit(defragment=True)` or the connector sleep gate; both are exercised only by the e2e NIXL runs. Adding these before ready. - Multi-node NIXL (NIC RDMA path with the GDR + POSIX-FD allocation flags) is unvalidated; the repro harness is localhost-only. - The ROCm `hipMem*` backend is written but untested on AMD hardware. - Encoder-decoder mixed layouts raise rather than falling back. ## AI assistance AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change: for the port onto the #44458 layout model, the connector geometry audit, and drafting. I have reviewed every changed line, and ran the tests and cluster validation above myself.

signals.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Scale UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs groups by DCP
signals.text: ## Purpose #49964 gated the DCP scaling of a group's token span on `isinstance(group.kv_cache_spec, AttentionSpec)` so that Mamba groups stay unscaled. `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` is a container rather than an `AttentionSpec` subclass, so DSA models — whose indexer and MLA layers merge into a single uniform group — lost the DCP factor too: - `build_offloading_config` reports `tokens_per_block = block_size` (64), - `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` still returns `block_size * dcp` (128) for a single group, so enabling CPU offload under DCP dies at startup: ``` AssertionError: tokens_per_block=64 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=128. Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes. ``` Reported by @Leoyzen on GLM-5.2, TP8/DCP2, `fp8_ds_mla`, MTP, `OffloadingConnector`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46514#issuecomment-5166406963 The scaling is now keyed off a helper that unwraps the container, so Mamba groups stay unscaled and every attention group keeps its DCP span. Same call site is fixed in `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` for multi-group configs. Related: #50823 fixes the other half of the same container-not-unwrapped family (block table width). ## Test Three tests, one per call site plus the hybrid case, next to the Mamba tests from #49964: - `offloading_connector/test_config.py::test_dcp_scales_uniform_type_attention_group_blocks` - `offloading_connector/test_config.py::test_dcp_scales_uniform_type_group_alongside_mamba` - `core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_resolve_block_sizes_scales_uniform_type_group_by_dcp` Verified fail→pass in a container built from the current nightly (`0.26.1rc1.dev255+g5e35a6f4f`); each test fails on unpatched `main` with the reported assert (`tokens_per_block=16 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=32`) or a wrong span, and the two suites pass with the fix: ``` python3 -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py -q # 115 passed ``` Config-level change, no effect on model output; no eval run. AI assistance (Claude) was used for this work; all changes reviewed.

signals.title: [ROCm][K3] Extend FP8 asm MLA prefill to non-divisor small head counts
signals.text: ## Context The AITER FP8 MLA **prefill** path (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`) is gated on `num_heads % 16 == 0`. Kimi-K3 has 96 heads over `kv_lora_rank=512` → **12 heads/rank at TP8**, a non-divisor of 16, so its FP8 prefill falls back to the BF16 FMHA decompress path. That fallback builds a bf16 working set not covered by the FP8 KV-pool accounting and exhausts the activation arena at long context (K3 OOM'd at ~197k tokens, KV pool <4% used). This is the **prefill counterpart to #50578** (asm decode pad 12→16). MLA attention is independent per query head over the shared latent KV, so padding the query heads up to 16 and slicing the result back is exact. Rebased onto current `main` (includes merged #50578). Prefill-only diff: **+48 / −11**, one file (`rocm_aiter_mla.py`). ## Changes **FP8 prefill enablement (this PR):** - Relax the `_fp8_prefill_enabled` gate to also allow `0 < num_heads < 16`, and **gate it on FP8 KV** (`kv_cache_dtype_str == "fp8"` in the metadata builder; `is_quantized_kv_cache(kv_cache_dtype)` in the impl). Without this, a bf16-KV serve would reserve PS workspace unnecessarily. - In `_mla_fp8_prefill_attn`: replicate-pad Q/K/V to 16 via `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` (from #50578), run PS asm prefill + `mla_reduce_v1` at 16 heads, slice output back to `num_heads`. - Set `num_head_k = max(16, num_heads)` in `_init_fp8_prefill_ps_buffers` and `_build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata` so work/reduce maps match padded tensors — also cuts partial tiles (`gcd(16,256)=16` vs `gcd(12,256)=4`), reclaiming **~6 GiB** PS workspace. Decode padding / Gluon routing is **not** in this PR — that is #50578 (merged). ## Dependencies / related - **#50578** (merged) — `AiterMLAHelper.get_mla_padded_q` / asm decode for non-divisor heads. - **ROCm/aiter#4452** (merged `a63ede724`) — 64-bit paged-KV byte offsets for >4 GB addressing. - Composes with **#48712** (gate PS workspace on fp8 KV) — this PR includes the same gate locally. ## vllm serve command **Hardware:** 8× MI355X (gfx950), TP8 **Model:** `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (mxfp4) ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 export GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 export HF_HUB_CACHE=/dev/shm/hf-cache HF_HOME=/dev/shm/hf-cache export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600 export VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 export HIPBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=32768 export CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=32768 MODEL=/path/to/Kimi-K3 # e.g. /shared_nfs/models/Kimi-K3 vllm serve "$MODEL" --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --max-num-seqs 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --trust-remote-code --load-format auto --moe-backend aiter \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --enable-prefix-caching --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prompt-tokens-details --disable-uvicorn-access-log ## Test results ### Long-context prefill (functional) | | Before PR-A | After PR-A | |---|-------------|------------| | Fresh prefill @ util 0.95 | OOM ~197k tokens (BF16 FMHA fallback, KV <4%) | **470k (68 s)**, **590k (28.6 s)** OK | | PS workspace | ~4032 partial tiles (~12 heads) | ~960 partial tiles (~6 GiB saved) | ### Accuracy — GSM8K (lm-eval, full 1319-test split, 5-shot greedy, conc=32, ctx=16384) Patches applied for this run: **#50578 + PR-A + #50618 only** (no cgmem/MoE/kv_b_proj). Server at `gpu-memory-utilization 0.88`. ```bash export HF_HUB_CACHE=/dev/shm/hf-cache HF_HOME=/dev/shm/hf-cache export OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python3 -m lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \ --include_path /path/to/InferenceX/utils/evals \ --tasks /path/to/InferenceX/utils/evals/gsm8k.yaml \ --output_path /tmp/eval_out --log_samples \ --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8888/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=32,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=16384" \ --gen_kwargs "max_tokens=12288,temperature=0,top_p=1" ``` | Run | n | strict-match EM | flexible-extract EM | |-----|---|-----------------|---------------------| | **With PR-A** (MI355X node 193, 2026-08-09) | 1319 | **97.04%** ± 0.47% | **96.97%** ± 0.47% | | Prior stack (cgmem+MoE+PR-A, node 1319, util 0.95) | 1319 | 96.89% ± 0.48% | 96.89% ± 0.48% | | Baseline replicate (stock + ASM deps, node 1319) | 1319 | 96.66% ± 0.49% | 96.66% ± 0.49% | No accuracy regression vs baseline; delta within run noise.

signals.title: [Bugfix][MLA] TritonMLA: fix illegal memory access on causal multi-token decode
signals.text: ## Purpose `TritonMLA` declared single-token decode support, so a speculative-decode verify block reached `forward_mqa` unflattened: `query_len * num_reqs` query rows against `num_reqs` rows of `block_table` / `seq_lens`. `decode_attention_fwd` launches one program per query row and indexes `tl.load(B_Seqlen + cur_batch)`, so every row past `num_decodes` is an out-of-bounds read. Reaching it takes a group whose reorder threshold is raised past 1. Ordinary MLA spec decode does not qualify: `TritonMLAMetadataBuilder` inherits `query_len_support = SINGLE_ONLY`, so multi-token queries route to prefill. The threshold is raised by the non-causal route (DSpark draft) which sets its flags after the base `__init__` has asserted `SINGLE_ONLY ⇒ threshold == 1`. `build()` then splits a *causal* batch with the raised threshold, and `forward_mqa` expands tables only under `if not causal`. Where that happens there is no fallback on either affected platform: - **NVIDIA sm_86** — `triton_mla` is the only MLA backend whose `supports_compute_capability` admits `major == 8` (CUTLASS/FlashInfer require 10, FlashAttn 9, FlashMLA 9 or 10). Reported as `Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access` (#51848). - **ROCm without AITER MLA** — `rocm.py` falls back to `[TRITON_MLA]` alone. Fixes #51848. On Kimi-K3 + DSpark, TP8, MI325: (18.01 → 45.00 tok/s), no quality regression (verified on gsm8k: **95%**) ## The fix `decode_attention_fwd` has no causal flag, but it reads each row's KV extent from `seq_lens`. A uniform verify block is a contiguous suffix, so intra-block causality is expressible as per-row extents: flatten to one decode row per query token and give row `t` extent `seq_len - (query_len - 1 - t)`. 1. `forward_mqa`: derive `query_len` from `q.shape[0] // seq_lens.shape[0]` and expand `block_table` / `seq_lens` to match, causal or non-causal. 2. `_cudagraph_support` → `UNIFORM_BATCH`, `query_len_support` → `UNIFORM`, so the reorder threshold admits `query_len > 1`. `attn_logits` workspace grows to match (workspace locks after capture). 3. `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()` asserts layers agree on `non_causal_multi_token_decode` instead of `any()`, so a non-causal draft group cannot be merged with a causal target group. ## Testing Validated on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (`ba07e4a48f`), gfx942. Rebased onto `origin/main` `9fd750f00d` ### Unit tests `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py` (new, 15) plus `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` (87): **102 passed**. The new file replaces the kernel with a spy and asserts on the `block_table` and `seq_lens` the backend actually submits, so it needs no GPU or Triton runtime. ### The decode path actually taken `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` already covers this: `spec_decode_small` (4x4) and `spec_decode_medium` (6x8) install an ngram `SpeculativeConfig`, with `torch` SDPA as reference. `decode_attention_fwd` was instrumented to confirm which path runs. ```bash HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 \ pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -q -k "1.0-1.0-auto-1-" ``` | | result | TritonMLA decode launches | |---|---|---| | before, spec_decode only | 4 passed, 16 skipped | 0 (routed to prefill) | | after, spec_decode only | 4 passed, 16 skipped | 4, causal staircase | | before, all batch specs | 24 passed, 96 skipped | 12 (single-token) | | after, all batch specs | 24 passed, 96 skipped | 16 (12 + 4 causal) | The "after, all batch specs" row re-verified on 2026-08-21 against the final tree, with 16 launches and the same shapes: ``` x2 q_rows=1 bt_rows=1 seq_lens[:8]=[1024] x4 q_rows=2 bt_rows=2 seq_lens[:8]=[32, 40] x2 q_rows=3 bt_rows=3 seq_lens[:8]=[512, 1024, 2048] x2 q_rows=8 bt_rows=8 seq_lens[:8]=[128, 256, 512, 1024] x2 q_rows=16 bt_rows=16 seq_lens[:8]=[125, 126, 127, 128, 253, 254, 255, 256] x2 q_rows=32 bt_rows=32 seq_lens[:8]=[2048] x2 q_rows=48 bt_rows=48 seq_lens[:8]=[505, 506, 507, 508, 509, 510, 511, 512] ``` Extents match `seq_len - (query_len-1-t)`. The 12 single-token launches are unchanged in count and shape, so the ordinary decode path does not regress. `bt_rows == q_rows` throughout, confirming the `block_table` expansion tracks the flatten. Skips are prefill-backend unavailability on this platform, not decode skips. ## Model evaluation GSM8K, all 1,319 questions, greedy (`temperature=0`, `seed=42`), `max_tokens=1024`, 8 concurrent clients, raw completions: | | | |---|---| | accuracy | **0.9507** (1254 / 1319) | | mean acceptance length | **3.279** of max 4.0, 40,823 drafts | | throughput | 0.449 q/s, 46.0 tok/s, 135,175 output tokens | | wall | 2,936 s | | worker faults / NaNs | none | Configuration: gfx942, 8x MI325X, TP8 + EP, target `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, drafter `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` on `TRITON_MLA` via `--attention-backend`, `dspark` method with 3 speculative tokens, 32,384 ctx. ```bash vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --enable-prompt-tokens-details --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --max-model-len 32384 --max-num-seqs 8 --speculative-config '{ "model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark", "num_speculative_tokens":3, "method": "dspark", "attention_backend": "TRITON_MLA", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}' ``` Spec-Bench: ```bash ---------------Speculative Decoding--------------- Acceptance rate (%): 63.11 Acceptance length: 2.89 Drafts: 16798 Draft tokens: 50394 Accepted tokens: 31804 Per-position acceptance (%): Position 0: 81.74 Position 1: 61.65 Position 2: 45.94 ================================================== ``` **The drafter is on TRITON_MLA precisely because this is the path the PR fixes.** **There is no same-flags unpatched baseline.** Without this patch the above configuration is the crash the PR fixes, so "unpatched, same flags" does not produce a number. This run is evidence that the causal flatten is correct under sustained load, not a before/after comparison. Independently corroborated by @maeehart on gfx942, 8x MI325X, TP8+EP, 7 spec tokens, same target/draft backend pairing, 262144 ctx: **GSM8K 95.6% strict and flexible over all 1,319 questions**, needle retrieval passed at 65K/131K/250K, 98.26% prefix-cache hit, no faults or NaNs. Their run bundles #50578 and AITER fixes, so it is integration evidence rather than an isolated measurement. @reger-men's gfx950 throughput numbers were obtained with a different implementation and are explicitly **not** a measurement of this PR. | | before | after | |---|---|---| | cudagraph mode | PIECEWISE (downgraded) | **FULL + PIECEWISE** | | throughput | 13.01 tok/s | **61.3 tok/s (4.0×)** | | per-step latency | 233.9 ms | **50.4 ms** | Removing per-launch overhead also removed cross-rank arrival skew that had been making TP collectives spin-wait: `vllm::all_reduce` 2.157 s (60.8% of Self CUDA) → 0.061 s (2.85%), arrival spread 313.8 µs → 7.1 µs. ## Correctness Same config (61.3 tok/s, including two unrelated tuning changes not in this PR): | benchmark | result | |---|---| | GSM8K, full test set (1319) | **97.2%** (1282/1319), 95% CI [96.3, 98.1] | | GPQA Diamond, 0-shot CoT (198) | **90.9%** flexible / **90.4%** strict | Hardware: - [x] Boots with FULL cudagraph capture, no downgrade message - [x] GSM8K 97.2%, GPQA Diamond 90.9% - [x] Concurrency sweep 1→128, zero errors across 100 800 generated tokens - [x] Causal-tail A/B showing acceptance is unaffected - [x] NVIDIA sm_86 — [nickus](https://github.com/nickus) on 4x RTX 3090: illegal memory access without the patch, serves with it ## AI assistance AI assistance was used. The submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. ## Related work - [#47310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47310) predates this PR and proposes the `query_len_support` half of this change and diagnoses the same flag coupling — credit there for that analysis. It has gone stale: Unmodified since 2026-07-09. - [#51171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51171) (open, 2026-08-05) also corrects cudagraph support reporting for non-causal draft groups, but keys a conditional `get_cudagraph_support` override on `non_causal_multi_token_decode`. That leaves the *causal* path still declaring single-token support — which is this bug. Causal is the base case, so the flag pair is set unconditionally here. The two changes are compatible; #51171 additionally moves an AITER host sync out of `forward_mqa`, which this PR does not touch. - [#51685](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51685) (open, 2026-08-10) reworks the same decode path for a native fp8 KV cache (`triton_mla.py` +97/-33). Different purpose, no overlap in intent. - [#51705](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51705) (open, 2026-08-10) is a Kimi-K3 DSpark decode-context-parallelism feature (+760/-107) that happens to carry this PR's `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()` fix verbatim — the same `any()` → set-and-pop rewrite under a byte-identical assertion message, differing only in a local variable name. This PR is six days earlier and is scoped to the bug; #51705 needs the same correction as a prerequisite for its own grouping work. - [#51848](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51848) is an issue, not a PR, and was closed on 2026-08-11. It is the independent sm_86 report of this bug. Its reporter confirmed there that this PR supersedes it and declined to open a competing one. - [#50911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50911) is complementary: the non-causal draft path on TokenSpeed/NVIDIA. No file overlap. - [#52218](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52218) (draft, opened 2026-08-13) — *"[Attention] Support speculative decode in Triton MLA"*. Same fix, same mechanism: uniform multi-token query support, the verify block flattened to decode rows, causal prefix lengths per row, padding rows clamped, split-KV workspace grown. This PR predates it by nine days and is a superset: #52218 is a draft touching only `triton_mla.py`, and does not correct `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()`, so a non-causal draft group can still be merged into a causal target group.

signals.title: [Rust Frontend] Skip full OpenAI-server CLI schema for the managed headless engine
signals.text: ## What `vllm-rs serve`'s managed-engine mode spawns Python via `vllm serve --headless`, which builds the full OpenAI-server CLI schema (tool/reasoning parsers, MCP, chat templates, ...) and imports every CLI subcommand module (`benchmark`, `launch`, `run_batch`, ...), even though the headless engine process only ever reads `EngineArgs`/`AsyncEngineArgs` fields. Adds `vllm/entrypoints/cli/headless_engine.py`: a lean entrypoint that parses only `AsyncEngineArgs` and calls the existing `run_headless()`. Moves the OpenAI-server-only imports in `serve.py` into the functions that use them, so `run_headless` can be imported without pulling them in -- `vllm serve` itself is unaffected (same imports, just deferred to first use). `ManagedEngineConfig::to_command()` now spawns the new entrypoint instead of `vllm serve --headless`. ## Why this is safe - Purely additive; only the one Rust spawn site changed. - `vllm serve` / `vllm serve --headless` (direct use, or via `tests/utils.py::RemoteOpenAIServer`) are unaffected. - Uses `FlexibleArgumentParser.parse_args` (strict, with full preprocessing), so behavior matches `vllm serve` exactly and unknown args still error -- see review discussion below. ## Not a duplicate Checked for related open work; closest is #40064 (prototype to overlap unavoidable imports with parent init), a different mechanism from eliminating imports that are never needed. ## Testing - `cargo test -p vllm-managed-engine` -- 2 tests, incl. updated snapshot - `pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_headless_engine_cli.py` -- 5 tests (parsed args reach `run_headless` correctly typed, `api_server_count` forced to 0, unknown/misspelled args raise `SystemExit`, underscore-form flags normalize correctly, defaults match `AsyncEngineArgs()`) - `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_cli_args.py tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_launch_cli.py` -- 40 existing, unaffected - `pre-commit run` on touched files -- clean - **Real end-to-end GPU measurement**: built before/after `vllm-rs` binaries, ran `vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --data-parallel-size-local 1` through both, measured wall-clock to the Rust frontend's `/health` with a local benchmarking tool (interleaved runs; not included in this PR): - `--enforce-eager`: 8 runs each, **24.47s -> 18.99s median (-22.4%)** - full compile + cudagraph (warm cache): 2 runs each, **26.74s -> 22.18s (-17.1%)** Root-caused via `python -X importtime`: importing `vllm.entrypoints.cli.main`'s full `CMD_MODULES` list costs ~2s by itself (`benchmark.main`/`launch`/`run_batch` are ~1.6-1.9s each), plus the OpenAI-server CLI schema's own tool/reasoning-parser/MCP imports. No model output/accuracy is affected (startup-path only). ## AI assistance disclosure Developed with AI assistance (OpenCode/Claude Sonnet), including the real GPU measurements above. I reviewed every changed line and ran all test/measurement commands myself.

signals.title: [ROCm][MLA] Reach FULL cudagraphs for AITER MLA speculative decoding
signals.text: ## Purpose Speculative decoding on ROCm cannot reach FULL cudagraphs, for two independent reasons. This fixes both. Measured on Kimi-K3 with a DSpark draft, TP8 on MI355X. **The reported support level.** A DSpark draft group serves its whole `1 + num_speculative_tokens` block through the decode path, but `TritonMLAMetadataBuilder` reports `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE` from a class constant, and the engine takes the minimum over attention groups -- so that one group downgrades the *whole engine* off FULL. `forward_mqa` flattens the block with `repeat_interleave` on a Python int and performs no device->host sync, so the group does satisfy `UNIFORM_BATCH`. `triton_mla.py` now reports that where the KV cache group is marked `non_causal_multi_token_decode`. Note the predicate is group scoped, not draft scoped, so a causal target sharing a draft's group is lifted too; `__init__` two lines below already uses it to raise `reorder_batch_threshold`, and the docstring records the scope. **Syncs inside the captured region.** `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mqa`'s small-head (< 16 query heads per rank) verify path expands each request's paged-KV range into one row per verify token on every MLA layer, with four device->host syncs and an allocation sized from what it just read back, each of which aborts HIP graph capture. That expansion moves into `_build_decode`, once per step, writing into persistent buffers so `mla_gluon` sees fixed addresses across replays. One sync remains there, because Gluon derives its split count from `min_kv_seq_len` and the merged causal-mask test pins that to the shortest row submitted; the builder runs outside the captured region, as `flex_attention.py`'s `.item()` in `build_for_cudagraph_capture` does. **`gpu_worker.py`.** `cache_config.kv_cache_size_tokens` is set in the engine core and the front end but never in the worker, which forward-propagates only `num_gpu_blocks`. The builder above therefore sees `None` in any multi-process deployment and falls back to a bound derived from `max_model_len`, roughly six times the real capacity. Filling it in `Worker.initialize_from_config` takes the verify buffer reservation from 295.3 MiB per rank to 46.6 MiB. The gap pre-dates this PR but is load-bearing for that reservation, so it is fixed here. **Related.** #50578 touches the same file and is best reviewed alongside. They merge cleanly in either order and do not collide on the verify path. ## Test Plan The merged causal-mask test covers exactly the code that moves here. Then serve and bench at concurrency `C` in `1 16`: ```bash pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 vllm serve /model \ --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8384 --max-num-seqs 32 --disable-custom-all-reduce \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/draft","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA"}' \ -cc '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[8,16,32,128,256]}' vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name random --ignore-eos \ --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \ --num-prompts $((C * 8)) --max-concurrency $C --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el ``` `Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL)` should appear in the server log, and `compilation.py`'s "not supported with spec-decode" warning should not. ## Test Result | | PIECEWISE (`main`) | FULL (this PR) | | --- | --- | --- | | c1 output tok/s | 12.10 | 46.30 | | c1 mean ITL | 186.98 ms | 34.26 ms | | c16 output tok/s | 174.01 | 326.46 | | c16 mean ITL | 188.28 ms | 92.91 ms | | capture memory per rank | 0.51 GiB | 2.11 GiB | | downgrade warning | present | absent | | acceptance length | 2.55 / 2.48 | 2.51 / 2.45 | Acceptance length is unchanged, so the gain is execution speed rather than better drafting. The causal-mask test passes, and the reservation logs 46.6 MiB against `GPU KV cache size: 814,051 tokens` -- from a later run than the table, which predates the `gpu_worker.py` fix; both patched runs agree on capture memory and graph mode. Absolute throughput came from `--dataset-name random`, whose synthetic prompts the draft predicts poorly (acceptance around 21%), so the FULL:PIECEWISE ratio is the controlled quantity and the absolutes are not representative of real prompts.
