signals.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Preserve engine content without tool calls
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52214. When an engine-backed tool parser is used without a reasoning parser, the non-streaming no-tool-call path currently discards the parser engine's normalized content and returns the original model output. This can leak format markers such as Inkling content-block delimiters into the API response. Return `tool_call_info.content` only for engine-based parser compositions when automatic parsing finds no tool call. Plain tool parsers keep the existing behavior of returning the untouched input. The regression coverage verifies both sides of that boundary: - an engine-backed, tool-only Inkling parser returns clean plain-text content when no tool is called; - a non-engine tool parser still returns the original input even if its no-call result contains transformed content. ### Duplicate-work check I searched open pull requests for #52214 and for DelegatingParser engine/no-tool-call content handling. No open PR addresses this issue. Nearby PRs concern token-ID preservation, streaming finalization, or `tool_choice="none"`, not this non-streaming no-call handoff. The issue reporter also confirmed that they are not preparing a patch and asked me to proceed. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py -q HF_HOME=/path/to/writable/cache .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/test_parse.py -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine -q PRE_COMMIT_HOME=/path/to/writable/cache .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \\ vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py \\ tests/parser/engine/test_inkling.py \\ tests/parser/test_parse.py ``` ## Test Result Before the production fix, the new Inkling regression fails with: ```text Expected: The answer is 42. Actual: <|content_text|>The answer is 42.<|end_message|> ``` With the fix: - focused parser tests: 106 passed; - full parser-engine suite: 3,784 passed; - all relevant pre-commit hooks passed; - `git diff --check` passed. ### Model evaluation Not run. This is a unit-level parser-composition fix that requires no model weights or GPU; the failure and corrected output are deterministically covered with the existing mock tokenizer and parser-engine tests. ### AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex was used to investigate, implement, test, and draft this pull request. I reviewed the changed lines and test results. --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist</summary> - [x] The purpose and linked issue are described. - [x] The test plan is provided. - [x] The before/after test results are provided. - [x] No documentation update is required because this corrects internal parser behavior without changing the public interface. </details>

signals.title: [Model][Generative Recommendation] Add HSTU model support to vLLM
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR adds HSTU-based generative recommendation model support to vLLM. HSTU is a ranking model architecture designed for generative recommendation. Unlike traditional language models, HSTU does not autoregressively generate text tokens. Instead, it synchronously computes ranking scores for all candidate items in a request. The goal of this change is to enable generative recommendation models to reuse the existing vLLM and large-model serving ecosystem, including: - Hugging Face model and configuration loading. - vLLM model registration. - GPU model execution. - Attention backend selection. - Optimized CUDA operators. - Request batching and scheduling. - Asynchronous output handling. - CUDA Graph execution. - Future distributed inference and online serving infrastructure. Generative recommendation and large language models have several common characteristics. Both can be represented as sequence models, use embedding layers and transformer-style computation, and benefit from optimized attention kernels, GPU batching, asynchronous execution, and production-level model serving infrastructure. By integrating HSTU into vLLM, generative recommendation models can reuse the existing large-model ecosystem instead of maintaining an independent inference stack. ## Inference Paradigm Although HSTU and large language models share several model and runtime components, their inference semantics are different. | Aspect | Large language model | Generative recommendation model | | --- | --- | --- | | Decode behavior | Autoregressively generates one token at a time | Synchronously computes scores for all candidates in a request | | Model output | Vocabulary logits for the next token | One ranking score for each candidate item | | Sampling | Requires token sampling and token ID generation | Does not generate a sampled token | | Request progress | Continues until the requested number of tokens is generated | Completes after all candidate scores are returned | | Output format | Usually `[num_tokens, vocab_size]` | Packed candidate-score output | | Scheduler signal | Uses sampled token IDs to update request state | Uses candidate scores to complete the request | The default vLLM generation path is designed around language-model execution: 1. Run the model forward pass. 2. Produce vocabulary logits. 3. Invoke the token sampler. 4. Generate token IDs. 5. Update the request state. 6. Continue decoding until the request is finished. This flow cannot be directly reused for HSTU because HSTU produces candidate ranking scores rather than vocabulary logits. Passing HSTU outputs through the normal sampler would incorrectly interpret candidate scores as vocabulary logits and could produce invalid token IDs. Therefore, this PR adds a score-only execution path: 1. Run the HSTU forward pass. 2. Extract the score corresponding to each candidate item. 3. Convert candidate IDs and scores into `LogprobsTensors`. 4. Return the scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. 5. Skip the standard token sampler. 6. Skip generated-token state updates. 7. Complete the request after all candidate scores are returned. The scheduler is also updated to support score-only recommendation requests. A request can be completed after candidate scores are produced even when no `new_token_ids` are returned. ## Implementation Overview This PR contains five main categories of changes. ### 1. Model Structure and Model Registration Files: - `vllm/model_executor/models/hstu.py` - `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` - `tests/models/registry.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU model implementation. - Add HSTU embedding layers, transformer blocks, normalization layers, and prediction heads. - Register the HSTU model with vLLM. - Support Hugging Face HSTU model loading. - Add HSTU to the model registry test data. - Add model registration and model import coverage. ### 2. Model Configuration and Configuration Registration Files: - `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/__init__.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/hstu.py` Changes: - Add HSTU-specific configuration classes. - Support HSTU model and task configuration fields. - Support `model_type = "hstu"`. - Convert HSTU configuration data from Hugging Face configuration files into the vLLM configuration representation. - Preserve compatibility with the existing vLLM configuration loading flow. ### 3. Model Operators and Operator Registration Files: - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/hstu_attn.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/selector.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU attention backend. - Integrate the external HSTU variable-length attention operator. - Register the HSTU attention backend with vLLM. - Automatically select `HSTU_ATTN` for HSTU or generative recommendation models when no explicit backend is configured. - Preserve explicit attention backend configuration as the highest-priority option. - Validate unsupported attention combinations and return clear errors. - Pass per-request context and candidate metadata to the HSTU attention implementation. Automatic backend selection is only applied when the user has not explicitly selected an attention backend. This preserves the existing backend override behavior. ### 4. Model Runner V1 Adaptation File: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` Changes: - Add generative recommendation metadata collection. - Add HSTU candidate score extraction. - Pass HSTU metadata through the forward context. - Bypass the standard token sampler for HSTU requests. - Return candidate scores through the prompt-logprobs output path. - Add recommendation-specific request completion handling. - Preserve the existing execution path for non-HSTU models. ### 5. Model Runner V2 Adaptation Files: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/gr_state.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py` - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` Changes: - Add `GRState` for request-scoped generative recommendation state. - Store user IDs, candidate count, prompt token IDs, and request stage. - Move candidate score extraction from the Model Runner into `GRState`. - Convert packed HSTU outputs into `LogprobsTensors`. - Add asynchronous score output handling. - Return candidate scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. - Skip token sampling and token-state updates for HSTU requests. - Complete score-only requests in the scheduler when candidate scores are available. - Preserve the one-token early-return behavior required by generative recommendation inputs. ## Test Plan ### 1. Environment Setup The operator is installed inside the following NVIDIA PyTorch container:`nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.06-py3` Install the required system dependency:`apt update && apt install -y libxcb1` ### 2.HSTU Operator Installation and Validation The HSTU attention operator is provided by the NVIDIA `recsys-examples` repository. Clone the recsys-examples repository:`git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/recsys-examples.git && cd recsys-examples/corelib/hstu` For H20 and other Hopper-based devices, enter the corresponding device directory before compiling: `cd hopper` Install the HSTU operator:`Install the HSTU operator:` After the compilation completes successfully, validate the operator installation with: `python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu_op.py` ### 3.vLLM Installation Clone the vLLM repository:`git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git && cd vllm` Install the current vLLM source with CUDA support:`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cuda pip install -v -e .` ### 4. HSTU Model Inference: After the HSTU changes are included in vLLM, run:`python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu.py` This test validates: * HSTU model loading. * HSTU configuration loading. * HSTU model registration. * HSTU attention backend initialization. * HSTU forward execution. * Candidate score extraction. * Candidate ID and score formatting. * Score-only execution without token sampling. * Recommendation request completion. * Model Runner integration. * CUDA Graph execution. ### 5. Model Registry and Hugging Face Loading Run the model registry tests:`pytest -q tests/models/test_registry.py -k HSTUForCausalLM` This validates that: * HSTUForCausalLM is registered. * The HSTU model class can be imported. * Hugging Face model metadata is available. * The HSTU configuration can be loaded. * The vLLM model registry can resolve the HSTU model. ## Test Result ### HSTU Operator The test returned like: ```text Input q shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Output shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Run success ``` ### HSTU Model Inference The test returned candidate IDs and their corresponding ranking scores. A truncated example of the output is: ```text Request 0: 12676:0.6602 47052:0.5078 45082:0.4336 79131:0.3984 34671:0.4844 5695:0.4570 95647:0.1777 60217:0.5273 70284:0.4258 16361:0.4238 Request 1: 8023:0.4863 24460:0.6094 ... ``` Each line follows the format:`Each line follows the format:` The output confirms that HSTU synchronously computes the scores of all candidates for a request and returns the scores through the generative recommendation output path. The test also confirms that: * HSTU outputs are not passed through the standard vocabulary sampler. * No artificial generated token IDs are produced. * Requests complete after candidate scores are returned. * Candidate scores are returned through prompt_logprobs_dict. * Both Model Runner V1 and Model Runner V2 execution paths are supported. * The HSTU attention backend is initialized and executed successfully. * CUDA Graph execution works in the validated CUDA environment. ### Model Registration and Hugging Face Loading The model registration and Hugging Face loading tests passed. HSTUForCausalLM can be resolved and imported through the vLLM model registry, and the HSTU configuration can be loaded from the Hugging Face model configuration. ### Scheduler and Score-Only Execution The scheduler validation passed for score-only recommendation requests. A recommendation request is correctly completed after candidate scores are produced, even when no new_token_ids are returned. The standard token sampling path is skipped for HSTU requests, and no regular language-model token state update is performed. ### Attention Backend Selection When no explicit attention backend is configured, the HSTU model automatically selects HSTU_ATTN. When an explicit attention backend is configured, the user-provided backend remains authoritative and is not overridden by the HSTU automatic selection logic. ### Current Scope and Limitations This initial integration focuses on bringing HSTU into the vLLM model and serving ecosystem. The current implementation assumes: * Prompt lengths are consistent across users. * Candidate lengths are consistent across users. * HSTU and non-HSTU requests are not mixed in the same batch. * Candidate scores are produced during an unchunked prefill. * Pipeline parallelism is not used. * PD-separated HSTU execution is not supported yet. * KV-cache-based or paged HSTU attention is not supported yet. * request_stage = 1 is not supported. * Each recommendation prompt contains at least one context/candidate pair. These limitations can be addressed in follow-up work after the basic HSTU execution path and serving interface are established.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Correct TRTLLM NVFP4 SiTU output scale
signals.text: ## Summary - centralize the TRT-LLM NVFP4 MoE `g1_scale_c` calculation - avoid folding `g1_alphas` into the SiTU output scale when the kernel already receives it through `output1_scale_gate_scalar` - use the same calculation during initialization and post-load processing - add focused coverage for gated SiTU and non-SiTU scaling ## Root cause The backend selected the gate/up scale solely from `is_act_and_mul`. For SiTU, that folded `g1_alphas` into `g1_scale_c` while also passing the same value separately to the kernel as `output1_scale_gate_scalar`, applying the gate scale twice. SiTU should pass only the cloned `a2_gscale` as the output scale; conventional gated activations keep the existing product. ## Duplicate-work check No open vLLM PR or issue was found for the TRT-LLM NVFP4 SiTU double-scaling bug. This backend correction is also independent of the generic ModelOpt mixed-quantization work in #50617. ## Validation - `../vllm-k3-fp8pb/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe_scale.py -q` — 2 passed - pre-commit hooks on all changed files — passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and forbidden-import checks The equivalent runtime correction has served the target Kimi-K3 NVFP4 checkpoint on 8 B300 GPUs during evaluation. This native branch itself was validated with the unit and static checks listed above. ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, tests, and PR preparation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and reviewed the validation results before publication.

signals.title: [Model] Register model capabilities directly
signals.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 MD018 MD041 --> ## Purpose #7168 moved model inspection into a subprocess so model imports and CUDA initialization stay out of the parent. #9208 changed its result transport, #9233 consolidated capability checks into one child per implementation, #23558 cached the result, and #46567 fixed package-submodule invalidation. #51746 added an explicit cache-preparation command. In a follow-up conversation, Simon and I agreed to close that approach because users were unlikely to pre-bake and re-check entries, and to study the subprocess inspection path from first principles. On a fresh cache, vLLM still launches that child once for each lazy implementation before the cache can help. The existing extractor derives 22 capability fields from the model class, including its bases, flags, and method signatures. It does not need weights or an initialized engine. This PR makes that same typed result an optional part of lazy model registration. For 320 of the 325 unique built-in implementations, `inspect_model_cls()` now returns the declaration before source lookup, cache access, model import, or child launch. The five dependency-bound implementations keep runtime inspection. Existing two-argument plugins also keep the current cache-backed subprocess path. ## Measured A Linux CUDA acceptance run on one NVIDIA RTX 4090 Laptop GPU (driver 595.71.05, Torch 2.13.0+cu132, CUDA runtime 13.2) compared every direct declaration with a fresh legacy subprocess inspection, n=1 per implementation. All 320 declarations matched across all 22 field values and runtime types. Parent CUDA remained uninitialized. The focused Qwen mechanism screen used five fresh processes per arm and an empty ModelInfo cache for every process: | Fresh Qwen lookup | Legacy path | Direct declaration | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Inspection child processes | 1 | 0 | | ModelInfo cache files written | 1 | 0 | | Median `inspect_model_cls()` time | 4.6166 s | 5.154 microseconds | | Median outer process time | 8.3860 s | 3.7417 s | The two arms ran sequentially, so these are descriptive mechanism measurements, not an end-to-end serving benchmark or a causal performance comparison. ## The fix `ModelInfo` is a public, frozen, keyword-only declaration with the same 22 typed fields produced by the existing extractor. A plugin can opt into the direct path at its existing registration site: ```python from vllm import ModelInfo, ModelRegistry ModelRegistry.register_model( "MyModelForCausalLM", "my_plugin.models:MyModelForCausalLM", model_info=ModelInfo( architecture="MyModelForCausalLM", is_text_generation_model=True, supports_pp=True, ), ) ``` Rather than store 320 copies of 22 fields, the built-in catalog maps each exact `(module, class)` implementation pair to one of 55 shared sparse profiles, then materializes the architecture name. Aliases therefore share the implementation declaration. Import-time validation rejects duplicate entries, overlap with the dynamic set, and any catalog drift from the live registry. The integration point is the existing built-in registry comprehension, which now passes `model_info=_get_builtin_model_info(mod_relname, cls_name)`. No model class or model runner changes. The five dependency-bound implementations remain explicit dynamic entries. When a registration omits `model_info`, the old fallback still runs. Cache entries now validate schema version, vLLM version, model-module hash, extractor hash, field names, and field types. Source discovery walks module specs with `PathFinder` without executing package parents. A declaration still does not bypass platform, dependency, or implementation-loading checks. ## Verification - The supported local registry suite passed with 365 passed, 18 skipped, and 2 deselected. The unfiltered file has two environment-only failures because this environment lacks optional `timm` for `HCXVisionForCausalLM` and `KananaVForConditionalGeneration`. - The branch collects 385 registry cases versus 392 at its tested upstream base. It adds one test function and no new test file. - Ruff, scoped mypy, the import-light probe, and `git diff --check` passed. All nine commits carry DCO signoffs. H200 and MI300 registry CI remain the cross-platform acceptance gate. This PR changes metadata discovery, not model implementations, sampling, or output semantics. ## Test plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_registry.py \ --deselect='tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[HCXVisionForCausalLM]' \ --deselect='tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[KananaVForConditionalGeneration]' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/models/test_registry.py::test_model_info_declaration_contract \ tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_inspects_builtin_without_import_or_cuda \ tests/models/test_registry.py::test_lazy_model_info_fallback_is_typed \ tests/models/test_registry.py::test_lazy_model_info_source_lookup_does_not_import_parent ``` AI assistance was used. I take responsibility for the implementation, compatibility boundary, and measurements.

signals.title: [Core][DP] Prefix-affinity tie-break in the internal DP load balancer
signals.text: ## Purpose Partial mitigation for #52463: the tie-break rotation added in #47420 degrades prefix-cache locality for multi-turn / shared-prefix traffic under the internal DP load balancer. Consecutive turns of one conversation are tied decisions at low load, so they rotate across DP ranks and every turn misses the prefix its previous turn cached. This PR remembers which engine served a prompt's first-block prefix (LRU of 16k entries, keyed on `cache_salt` + LoRA id + first `block_size` prompt token ids) and prefers that engine **only when scores tie**: - Load-aware decisions unchanged — a lower-scored engine always wins. - Unrelated tied requests still rotate — #47420's fairness fix is preserved (regression-tested). - Explicit `data_parallel_rank` and late-interaction routing bypass affinity, unchanged. - Stale entries from elastic-EP scale-in are discarded; sub-block prompts (which cannot hit the cache) are exempt. ## Test Plan - `tests/v1/engine/test_dp_lb_prefix_affinity.py` — 8 CPU-only unit tests driving `get_core_engine_for_request` directly: session stickiness across turns, tied-unrelated rotation preserved, load-beats-affinity, sub-block exemption, cache_salt separation, explicit-rank bypass, scale-in staleness, LRU bound. - Hardware A/B on 8×H100 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DP=4+EP, `--api-server-count 4`, fp8 KV, aiperf mooncake trace designed for 81.7% prefix reuse — full methodology in #52463): identical runs, only this patch differs. ## Test Result Unit: 8/8 pass (run inside `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image). Hardware A/B (prefix-cache hit rate, per-user output tok/s): | conc | hit rate before → after | tok/s/user before → after | |---:|---|---| | 1 | 37.6% → **61.5%** | 69.5 → 73.6 (+6%) | | 4 | 52.9% → 53.5% | 47.2 → 45.1 (−4%) | | 16 | 20.0% → 21.9% | 16.3 → 12.6 (−23%)* | | 32 | 16.0% → **23.2%** | 9.7 → 9.6 (−1%) | | 64 | 10.9% → 11.1% | 5.0 → 4.8 (−5%) | | 128 | 7.8% → 8.8% | 2.6 → 2.7 (+4%) | \* hit rate unchanged while throughput moved — consistent with run-to-run variance at 160 requests/level, not a cache effect; happy to re-run if reviewers want more samples. **Known limitation (why this is a mitigation, not the full fix):** with `--api-server-count N` each frontend process has its own client and affinity map, and SO_REUSEPORT spreads one session's connections across processes — client-side affinity only sees its own process's requests (this bounds the c=1 recovery at 61.5% vs 81.6% measured on v0.23.0, a pre-#47420 release — a version-level baseline, not a single-commit revert of #47420). The complete fix needs prefix-awareness at a shared layer (DP coordinator or a shared affinity table); #52463 is the home for that design discussion. FIX #52463 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [ROCm][CI] Fix intermittent GPU memory fault during sleep-mode wake-up
signals.text: ROCm sleep-mode wake-up can intermittently abort the EngineCore on MI300 while remapping roughly 172 GiB, as seen in [build 12090](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12090/list?sid=01a004a6-9a94-48ba-8be1-20f23544b8e0&tab=output) and the earlier signature-matched [build 11862](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11862/list?sid=019fe4e5-8d10-4dca-8454-8c50409fefda&tab=output). Both failures occurred about 0.53 seconds into the first wake on different MI300 hosts, with the same GPU address-`nil` fault and `create_and_map -> wake_up` stack, while their MI355 jobs passed. PR #44972 added an allocator-wide ROCm `hipMemset` after VMM remapping to scrub stale VRAM on older amdgpu drivers and prevent discarded Mamba/GDN state from corrupting generation. That memset is the only device-wide access at the observed fault point and unnecessarily touches the full attention KV allocation, making it the high-confidence vLLM trigger even though the underlying defect may be a ROCm VMM race. A controlled restoration of the old leaf passed 40/40 local cycles, so this remains an intermittent mitigation rather than a deterministic native A/B reproduction. This change forward-ports the unmerged `0ab7e793` design by clearing only bound Mamba/GDN state after KV remapping and preserving packed cache offsets and strides. It preserves the functional motivation of #44972 but intentionally does not retain its broader allocator-wide scrubbing guarantee for discarded bytes on affected old drivers. Proposed changes: - Remove the ROCm whole-allocation `hipMemset` from `create_and_map`. - Preserve packed Mamba cache offsets and per-block strides through the standardized `create_kv_cache_views` layout path. - Zero only bound Mamba/GDN conv and recurrent state views after a full or KV-tagged wake, without touching attention KV or weights-only wakes. - Deduplicate aliased state views so shared storage is cleared once. - Add assertion-level regression coverage that fails 4/4 on the pre-fix implementation and passes 4/4 with this change.
signals.author: AndreasKaratzas

signals.title: [Bugfix] Reload speculative draft weights after Level 2 sleep wake
signals.text: Addresses #52479 ## Problem After the documented Level 2 sleep/wake sequence, MTP speculative decoding silently stops helping: every drafted token is rejected (`Mean acceptance length: 1.00`, `Accepted throughput: 0.00`) and decode throughput falls to approximately the no-speculation rate. Target-model outputs remain correct, so the failure appears only as a large performance regression. Level 2 sleep discards draft parameters together with the target parameters. `wake_up()` restores the saved draft buffers, but the documented subsequent `reload_weights()` call reloaded only the target model. The drafter is a separate module and therefore continued with discarded parameter storage. ## Fix Put the disk-backed draft reload in `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`), on the existing `weights_iterator is None` path, before the target load: - Resolve the draft through the existing `get_draft_model()` accessor. - Read the configured draft checkpoint with its model loader. MTP configurations without a separate `draft_load_config` use the target load configuration. - Load in place through `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload`, preserving the parameter addresses captured by the compiled runtime. - Invoke the helper unbound (`GPUModelRunner._reload_draft_weights_from_disk(self)`) because Model Runner V2 already delegates this method with a V2 `self` and does not inherit the helper. - During that draft load, temporarily unbind any draft submodule that is the same object as a target module. A discard dummy swallows checkpoint tensors for those aliases so layerwise reload and `load_weights` cannot shape-mismatch or rewrite live target storage (Gemma4 MTP after `_maybe_share_embeddings`). - If a detached `embed_tokens` weight shape differs from the draft `lm_head` (Gemma4 MTP: tied draft-dim head, then embed replaced with the backbone-dim target module), load those embed tensors into the still-live `lm_head`. Same-width shared embeds are discarded; a distinct head loads from its own entry. - Reload the target last so same-width shared storage (typical Qwen MTP / EAGLE) is restored from the target checkpoint. - Leave iterator-based reloads unchanged; those weights are supplied by their caller and are not assumed to contain a second draft checkpoint. Model Runner V2 keeps its existing one-line delegate into that method. There is no V2 wrapper and no production-file diff under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`. This mirrors Level 1 sleep semantics: both paths restore the existing target and draft modules in place. Level 1 restores their tagged allocations from host RAM, while Level 2 restores saved buffers during `wake_up()` and reloads model parameters from their disk checkpoints during `reload_weights()`. ### Why not `start_draft_weight_update()`? The draft weight-update API added by #46725 selects the draft as the destination of an already-configured `WeightTransferEngine`. Its built-in NCCL and IPC backends receive weights supplied by an external trainer; they do not accept a checkpoint path or read weights from disk. The API also requires the server to start with `weight_transfer_config`. It remains the correct path for runtime trainer/RL weight transfer; this PR does not replace it. The failing workflow is the separate, documented disk-restore path and does not require a trainer or weight-transfer engine: ```python llm.sleep(level=2) llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"]) llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights") llm.wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"]) ``` This change reuses #46725's `get_draft_model()` accessor and the same layerwise reload lifecycle used by checkpoint-format transfer engines, while keeping the checkpoint source appropriate to this workflow. This is not a duplicate of #46725: that change added externally supplied runtime draft updates, while this PR completes the separate documented disk-backed `reload_weights()` recovery path. ## Live evidence ### Qwen3.8 MTP (same-checkpoint, same-width share) Measured on an earlier MRV2-wrapper revision of this PR (same disk draft loader, layerwise lifecycle, and draft-first / target-last order) on 2x RTX 5090, TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=2`, with sleep mode enabled. Each throughput entry is the median of three 256-token HTTP generations. | State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Cold baseline | 109.4 tok/s | not recorded | — | | L2 wake cycle 1 | 108.9 tok/s (100% of baseline) | 2.17 | 4.18 s | | L2 wake cycle 2 | 104.9 tok/s (96% of baseline) | 2.43 | 4.11 s | Unpatched reproduction on that stack: 51.8 tok/s, acceptance length 1.00, zero accepted draft tokens. ### Gemma4 E2B MTP (dim-mismatched shared embeddings) Measured on this follow-up (identity detach + tied-embed sink) on the same 2x RTX 5090, TP=2, `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` + `google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant`, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=1`, sleep mode enabled. Each throughput entry is the median of three 64-token HTTP generations. Assistant `hidden_size=256`, `backbone_hidden_size=1536`. | State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Cold baseline | 297.5 tok/s | 1.50 | — | | L2 wake cycle 1 | 293.0 tok/s (98% of baseline) | 1.50 | 1.15 s | | L2 wake cycle 2 | 304.6 tok/s (102% of baseline) | 1.50 | 1.08 s | Both models used the documented staged sequence plus a prefix-cache reset. Outputs were coherent. No shape-mismatch traceback. A discard-only detach avoided the crash but left acceptance at 1.00 (tied `lm_head` never refilled); the sink is what restored 1.50. ## Tests Seven focused unit tests cover: 1. A disk-backed reload restores the draft through its configured loader and the layerwise lifecycle before reloading the target. 2. The same disk path through Model Runner V2's existing `GPUModelRunnerV1.reload_weights(self, ...)` delegate. 3. A disk-backed reload without a draft still reloads the target normally. 4. A caller-supplied weight iterator does not trigger an implicit draft reload. 5. A dim-mismatched aliased `embed_tokens` is not written; the tied draft-dim `lm_head` still receives the embed checkpoint tensor. 6. A same-width shared embed is discarded; a distinct `lm_head` is not filled from `embed_tokens`. 7. The same target `lm_head` aliased at `draft.lm_head` and every `shared_head.head` is detached (`named_modules(remove_duplicate=False)`). ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::TestReloadDraftWeights -q # 7 passed ``` ## Scope and limitations - The serving path of interest is Model Runner V2. The implementation lives in the shared `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` that V2 already calls, so a legacy V1 engine using that method also gets the disk draft reload. - Live validation covers Qwen3.8 same-checkpoint MTP and Gemma4 E2B MTP with a separate assistant checkpoint, both TP=2. EAGLE3 and DSpark were not run live. Independent drafts are unbound only when a module is the same object as the target; embed tensors are redirected to `lm_head` only when that head's weight shape differs from the shared embed. - The configured draft checkpoint remains the source of draft weights. This change does not redefine draft selection during `weights_path` model swaps. - Draft formats whose loaders do not implement `get_all_weights` raise `NotImplementedError`, matching the existing target-model disk reload. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, review-response analysis, and test orchestration. The submitter reviewed the changes and the live validation described above.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Core] Count SWA in-flight KV once per pool, not per request (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 #51041)
signals.text: Fixes #51041 ## Summary `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config()` divided the KV cache pool by each group's **full per-request admission cap**, which includes the `max_in_flight_tokens` allowance inside `SlidingWindowSpec.max_admission_blocks_per_request()`. But in-flight tokens are bounded **system-wide** by the scheduler's token budget across *all* requests — at most `max_in_flight_tokens` tokens are unsettled at any moment, regardless of concurrency. Multiplying a global bound by max concurrency over-reserves the pool by `(max_concurrency − 1) × transient` blocks per SWA-class group. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (H20 TP=2, `fp8_ds_mla`, block size 256, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, doubled under async scheduling) the four SWA-class groups of the 5-group hybrid layout each charge in-flight tokens at tiny compressor block granularity (`cdiv(16384, 4) = 4099` pages, `cdiv(16384, 8) = 2065` pages …), inflating the per-request footprint from ~3.6 KiB/token to ~53.5 KiB/token and capping `max_model_len` at ~121K instead of ~1M. This matches every datapoint in the issue (Burlesque1's 53.5 KiB H20 TP=2, kezboard233's V100 α/β regression, @CHNtentes' healthy 10.07 KiB DSpark run). ### The change - `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`: add `steady_memory_usage_bytes()` / `transient_memory_usage_bytes()` to `KVCacheSpec` with the exact identity `admission == steady + transient`. Defaults preserve byte-identical behavior for every other spec type; overridden only in `SlidingWindowSpec`, `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec`, and `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` (the DSv4 aggregated worker-config shape). - `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`: reserve the transient part once per pool instead of per request: ``` N_max = (num_blocks − Σ_g transient_g) / Σ_g steady_g ``` The runtime per-request admission gate is unchanged, so startup sizing and runtime admission stay consistent: `N × steady + transient ≤ num_blocks`. Pool sizing (`_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups`, the `max`-based conservative bound) is untouched. ### Note on 0731 vs preview The checkpoint config delta (2 trailing zeros in `compress_ratios`, `dspark_*` fields) is a red herring — layer indices ≥ `num_hidden_layers` are clamped and every `dspark_*` consumer is gated behind `use_dspark()`. The regression tracks the **vLLM version**, not the checkpoint: the admission formula was introduced by #40946 and widened to `max_in_flight_tokens` by #47728 (2026-07-08, shortly before 0.26.0). The preview checkpoint's older config format simply doesn't form the 5-group hybrid layout on 0.26.0, so it never hits the SWA-group overcharge. ### Not duplicating existing PRs Checked open PRs referencing #51041 / KV-cache accounting — none. This PR is distinct from: - #37584 (auto-revert of #36030) — concerns the pool-sizing **sum** in `_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups`, untouched here; the #48317/#36030 per-group sums are preserved for the steady part. - #40694 — fixes the capacity **log** for Qwen3.5 hybrid, log-only. - #41834 — SM12x enablement, no accounting changes. ## Behavior change Capacity/concurrency **reporting and admission headroom only** — no attention kernels, no KV layout, no numerics. Model outputs are unchanged, so no model evals were run. ## Test Plan / Results All on CPU (no GPU on the dev machine — GPU test suites were **not** run): ``` pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py # 78 passed pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \ tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py # 100 passed pytest tests/v1/test_kv_cache_spec_registry.py \ tests/v1/engine/test_init_error_messaging.py # 45 passed pytest tests/v1/core/ # 496 passed; 3 e2e tests fail # engine init identically on # the base commit (GPU-less host, # pre-existing, not a regression) pre-commit run --files <changed files> # all passed (ruff, format, mypy-3.10) pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual # passed ``` New regression test `test_dsv4_flash_0731_kv_capacity` builds the real 0731 architecture (43 layers, `compress_ratios = [0, 0, (4, 128)×20, 0]`, real per-layer spec shapes from `deepseek_v4/attention.py` / `compressor.py`) through the actual grouping → packed-layout → concurrency pipeline, and asserts: 1. the 5-group hybrid layout forms with 20/20 compressor layers, 2. `steady + transient == max` holds per group, 3. per-token cost < 10 KiB at 1M context (pre-fix ~53 KiB), 4. the new formula strictly beats the pre-fix per-request-peak formula. Four existing assertions in `test_get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` / `test_get_max_concurrency_packed_kv_cache_config` were updated to the new (documented-in-comment) expected values. ## AI-assistance statement **The code, tests, and this PR description were entirely generated by an AI agent (Claude); the change was reviewed line-by-line by the human submitter (@volkermauel), who also ran the full CPU test suites and lint/mypy checks listed above and verified the root-cause analysis against the numeric evidence in the issue thread.** Co-authored-by: Claude Agent Here <claude@anthropic.com>

signals.title: [Spec Decode] Warn that speculative max_model_len has no effect
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52258. `speculative_config.max_model_len` is accepted and validated, then never read. V0 used it to skip speculation for sequences past a threshold. V1 has no consumer: ``` $ grep -rn "draft_model_config" vllm/ --include=*.py | grep max_model_len \ | grep -v ^vllm/config/ (no matches) $ grep -rn "speculative_config\.max_model_len" vllm/ --include=*.py \ | grep -v ^vllm/config/ (no matches) ``` For `ngram` and `custom_class`, `draft_model_config` aliases `target_model_config` (`config/speculative.py:834`, `:848`), so the override at `:1127` never runs. For draft-model methods the override does run, but nothing reads the result. ## Modifications Warn at the end of `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` when the field is set, and replace this PR's original test with one asserting the warning. Warn rather than reject so existing configs keep starting, and rather than implementing the V0 skip, which is a feature rather than a bug fix and needs a scope decision. I asked about scope on #52258 and have not heard back, so this PR covers only the silent-ignore part; I'm happy to follow up with the skip if maintainers want it. Note on the change of approach: this PR previously added a failing test asserting the value reached the draft config. That test was wrong. For `ngram` the draft and target configs are the same object, so it asserted `draft == 80` and `target == 200` simultaneously, which cannot hold. Even un-aliased it would have passed while the option stayed unread, which is worse than no test. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_max_len.py -k warns_that_it_has_no_effect ``` ## Test Result `1 passed`. Reverting only the `speculative.py` change makes it fail, so it is not passing vacuously. Whole file on an RTX 4090, `6 failed, 6 passed`, against `6 failed, 5 passed` for the same file on `017e9f4448` without this change: the same six `test_eagle_max_len` cases fail either way (pre-existing on this hardware) and the extra pass is the new test. Note the file imports `get_attn_backend_list_based_on_platform()` at module scope, so it does not collect without a supported accelerator. ## Notes Not a duplicate: no other open PR references #52258. No model output changes, so no evals: the only runtime change is an added warning. AI assistance was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line.

signals.title: [Deprecation] Remove dead use_prefill_decode_attention flag
signals.text: ## Purpose `--attention-config.use_prefill_decode_attention` is accepted, documented, and has no effect. It used to select `ROCM_ATTN` on ROCm. #36702 made `ROCM_ATTN` the unconditional first entry in the ROCm priority list and removed the branch that read the flag, so the field has had no reader in `vllm/` since. Its original purpose is now the default behaviour, making this leftover surface rather than a regression. Two tests suggest otherwise: `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` asserts the flag parses, and the `RocmAttn` entry in `tests/v1/attention/utils.py` passes it beside an explicit `"backend": "ROCM_ATTN"`. ## Modifications This opened as stage 1 of the [deprecation pipeline](docs/contributing/deprecation_policy.md) — a warning naming v0.29.0 for removal. Per review, the flag is now removed outright: - delete `use_prefill_decode_attention` from `AttentionConfig` - drop it from the `RocmAttn` test config; the explicit backend selection is unchanged, so behaviour is identical - drop the parse assertions from `test_attention_config` The pipeline exists to give users notice before behaviour changes under them. Here there is no behaviour to preserve: the flag's effect is already the unconditional default, so no working configuration changes meaning. The only user-visible difference is that passing the flag now raises instead of being silently ignored, which surfaces a setting that was already doing nothing. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py ``` ## Test Result `97 passed`. `pre-commit` passes on the three changed files, mypy included. `grep -rn use_prefill_decode_attention` over the tree returns nothing after this change. ## Notes Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue references `use_prefill_decode_attention`. No evals included; the flag has no consumer and there is no runtime change. AI assistance was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. cc @gshtras (authored #36702), @yewentao256 (reviewed)

signals.title: [Model] Add Qwen3-Omni DSpark support
signals.text: ## Purpose Add framework support for using a `Qwen3OmniDSparkModel` draft architecture with a Qwen3-Omni thinker target. This change: - registers the dedicated Qwen3-Omni DSpark architecture while reusing the shared `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM` runtime implementation; - exposes the target thinker's post-DeepStack auxiliary hidden states required by DSpark; - preserves the dedicated architecture and DSpark sampling fields when converting msModelSpec configuration; - validates the target/draft hidden size, attention geometry, target-layer selection, vocabulary contract, and DSpark algorithm settings at startup; - makes embedding and lm-head sharing safe when the draft input/output vocabulary differs from the target vocabulary; - relies on the draft-logits cache stride fix from #53017 instead of maintaining a model-specific resizing workaround; - adds focused registry, configuration, model-contract, and configuration-bridge tests. A repository search for `Qwen3 Omni DSpark` and `Qwen3OmniDSpark` found no existing PR implementing this support, so this does not duplicate known work. This is a framework integration PR. Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoints are not yet available, so it does not claim model quality or acceptance-rate results. AI assistance disclosure: this PR was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The submitter is responsible for reviewing every changed line and completing the required NPU/model evaluation. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/ruff check \ tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py \ tests/models/registry.py tests/test_config.py \ tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py \ vllm/config/speculative.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dspark.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py \ vllm/transformers_utils/configs/speculators/algos.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check <the same 11 files> .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py \ tests/test_config.py \ -k 'qwen3_omni_dspark or dspark_updater' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py \ -k 'incomplete_vocab_weights' ``` Outstanding NPU/model validation: - run the Qwen3-Omni hidden-state module tests in an environment with all multimodal dependencies; - load a compatible Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoint; - run NPU end-to-end eager and ACLGraph speculative-decoding tests in the dependent vLLM-Ascend PR; - report acceptance length, output correctness, memory, and throughput. ## Test Result - Ruff check: passed. - Ruff format check: passed; 11 files already formatted. - Direct registry smoke test: passed; `Qwen3OmniDSparkModel` resolves to `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM`. - Configuration and msModelSpec bridge tests: 21 passed, 201 deselected. - Vocabulary/weight-contract tests: 3 passed, 3 deselected. - `git diff --check`: passed. - `tests/models/test_registry.py` collection is blocked locally by the newly required `model_hosting_container_standards` package; the equivalent direct registry import check passed. - Model evaluation: not run because no Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoint is available.

signals.title: [Build] Propagate vLLM version to Rust binaries
signals.text: ## Summary - derive a device-independent vLLM source version with setuptools-scm for Python-driven and standalone Rust builds - embed the same version in `vllm-rs`, `vllm-bench`, and the Rust frontend version endpoint - expose Git metadata to selective Docker Rust build stages while suppressing the artificial dirty state caused by omitted tracked files ## Affected outputs | Surface | Effect | | --- | --- | | `vllm-rs --version` | Reports the embedded vLLM source version. | | `vllm-bench --version` | Reports the embedded vLLM source version instead of the workspace crate version (`0.1.0`). | | Rust frontend `GET /version` | `rust_frontend_version` reports the embedded vLLM source version. The engine-reported `version` field keeps its existing behavior. | ## Affected build paths | Build path | Embedded Rust version | | --- | --- | | Nightly/release wheel builds from a Git checkout | The setuptools-scm source version. `VLLM_VERSION_OVERRIDE` is honored through `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`. | | Docker builds using `docker/Dockerfile`, `.cpu`, `.rocm`, `.rocm_gfx1250`, or `.xpu` | The source version resolved from the mounted Git metadata. Selective-copy stages set `dirty=false` because omitted tracked files would otherwise make the partial worktree appear dirty. | | Local `bash build_rust.sh` | The setuptools-scm source version when Git metadata is available. | | Direct `cargo build` | `VLLM_RS_BUILD_VERSION` when explicitly supplied; otherwise the workspace crate version (`0.1.0`). | The embedded Rust version stays device-independent. Python distribution version handling remains unchanged, including platform suffixes such as CPU, CUDA, ROCm, TPU, and XPU variants. Repackaging an existing prebuilt Rust binary preserves the version embedded when that binary was built. ## Motivation Rust artifacts currently identify themselves using workspace crate metadata, which stays at `0.1.0` and does not identify the corresponding nightly or release vLLM source revision. This change resolves the source version before compiling Rust and passes it through `VLLM_RS_BUILD_VERSION`. `get_vllm_version()` runs first during Python packaging so `VLLM_VERSION_OVERRIDE`, propagated through `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`, also applies to the Rust artifacts. ## Validation - `cargo nextest run -p vllm-build-info -p vllm-bench -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-server --no-fail-fast` (552 passed, 10 skipped) - injected version output: `vllm-bench 9.8.7` and `vllm-rs 9.8.7` - Cargo fallback output: `vllm-bench 0.1.0` - existing Docker build metadata tests (7 passed) - Ruff, Dockerfile parsing, shell syntax, and `git diff --check`

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 Fused kernels for KDA prefill
signals.text: ## Purpose On ROCm, Kimi-K3's KDA prefill chunk path currently runs a pipeline of nine Triton kernels. This PR adds a fusion path for ROCm that fuses these operations based on the characteristics of their workloads: **Prologue**: The kernel that prepares the chunks leading up to the recurrent state update. It normalizes `q` and `k`, cumsum gate into `g` and `beta`, builds `Aqk` in each chunk, inverts the transition `Akk`, and produces w and u. Each 64-token chunk can be processed in parallel, so it is dispatched in `(chunk, head)` grids for parallelism. **Chunk recurrence**: This does the remaining recurrence state update. For each sequence, the state update is sequential, and dispatching workgroups on the number of sequences can lead to low CU occupancy. This path breaks a sequence down into groups of chunks where the number of groups is determined by device capability, and takes a two-pass approach to increase parallelism within sequences: - Pass 1: Each group walks a recurrence from a zero state and records how it transforms an incoming state - Perform a scan across groups from a sequence to recover each group's true initial state - Pass 2: Re-walks each group from the correct start to produce outputs The fusion chain is ~2x faster than the Triton chain, especially in the chunk recurrance stage. E2E tests shows this reduces TTFT by ~4%. | tokens / seqs | Triton chunk stage | fused chunk stage | speedup | Triton chain | fused chain | speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1024 / 1 | 117.4 µs | 60.7 µs | 1.93× | 139.2 µs | 79.1 µs | 1.76× | | 4096 / 1 | 301.1 µs | 113.7 µs | 2.65× | 330.5 µs | 143.0 µs | 2.31× | | 4096 / 2 | 232.7 µs | 110.0 µs | 2.12× | 278.0 µs | 154.7 µs | 1.80× | | 4096 / 8 | 192.5 µs | 84.5 µs | 2.28× | 256.6 µs | 145.2 µs | 1.77× | | 16384 / 1 | 1174.2 µs | 335.9 µs | 3.50× | 1232.4 µs | 393.5 µs | 3.13× | The fusion path is packed into two pytorch interfaces that serve as a replacement for the original Triton chain. An additional engine argument option `--kda-prefill-backend=fused` is added to enable this fused path, and it's set as the default when it is supported. The kernels have only been tested on gfx950 at the moment, so its build and dispatch is guarded on gfx950 for now. ## Test Plan Unit tests for the fused kernels lm_eval with gsm8k on MI355X Server command ``` VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \ VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \ VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 \ vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --load-format auto \ --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kda-prefill-backend ["fused" | "triton"] ``` Benchmark ``` vllm bench serve --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --backend vllm --trust-remote-code --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency "$CONC" --num-prompts $((CONC * 4)) --temperature 0 --ignore-eos ``` lm_eval ``` lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --model_args "model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=8192,timeout=3600" --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --apply_chat_template --fewshot_as_multiturn --seed 1234 ``` ## signals.title: [ROCm] Enable fused AR draft metadata updates for DeepSeek V4
signals.text: Builds on vLLM PR #46849, which restores fused multi-step draft decode graphs for autoregressive speculative decoding when every attention backend can update step-dependent draft metadata in place. That PR left DeepSeek V4 ROCm sparse SWA disabled because the AMD path also materializes ROCm-specific ragged SWA indices and indptrs. Enable the ROCm DeepSeek V4 AITER SparseSWA metadata builder for fused draft decode by refreshing its ragged SWA representation after the generic dense SWA update. The refresh writes directly into the persistent metadata buffers returned by build(), avoiding temporary ragged flat/indptr allocations so captured HIPGraph replay keeps stable tensor storage addresses. Add focused tests for the direct-to-buffer helper and in-place metadata update. Validation used TP4 on MI355X against patched and control images built from vllm/main@c4e9692. Runtime logs confirmed the patched image used the fused speculator graph path, while control logged fallback because DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA did not support fused multi-step draft decode metadata updates. Smoke, GSM8K, c16, and c128 runs completed with no HIPGraph/cudagraph replay errors, illegal memory access, stale metadata symptoms, or failed benchmark requests. Serve command shape: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \ vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --attention_backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN"}' \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --max_model_len 4096 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max_num_seqs 256 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --trust-remote-code Accuracy command shape: lm_eval --model local-completions \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 8 \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:<PORT>/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenized_requests=False Accuracy results, full GSM8K 8-shot, no limit: patched flexible/strict: 0.9492 / 0.9500 control flexible/strict: 0.9416 / 0.9424 Benchmark command shapes: vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 512 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --temperature 0 \ --ignore-eos \ --max-concurrency 16 \ --num-prompts 160 \ --num-warmups 16 vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 512 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --temperature 0 \ --ignore-eos \ --max-concurrency 128 \ --num-prompts 1024 \ --num-warmups 128 Performance results, output throughput: c16 patched/control: 2000.58 / 1958.82 tok/s (+2.13%) c128 patched/control: 7852.55 / 7751.43 tok/s (+1.30%)

signals.title: [CPU] [1/n] Start migrating the CPU extension to the libtorch stable ABI
signals.text:
## Purpose This PR continues the libtorch stable ABI migration (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26946) for vLLM, and is the first PR dedicated completely to the stable CPU build. First CPU libtorch stable-ABI PR. Migrates `silu_and_mul`, `gelu_\*`, `rms_norm`, `fused_add_rms_norm`, and `rotary_embedding` into new corresponding `_C*_stable_libtorch` libraries. Leftover CPU kernels stay on `_C` / `_C_AVX*` until later PRs. cc @janeyx99, @Harry-Chen ### New file: `csrc/libtorch_stable/cpu/cpu_types_arm_vec.hpp` `cpu_types_arm.hpp` used to get its `Vectorized` primitives from `at::vec` (unstable ABI), so this header is a small header-only replacement using only `` and stable `torch/headeronly` types. It specializes `Vectorized` for `float/c10::Half/c10::BFloat16` and implements only the ops/conversions the migrated kernels actually call (no full `at::vec` API surface). `BF16` load/store/convert use hardware NEON instructions when `ARM_BF16_SUPPORT` is set, falling back to bit-manipulation on [uint16x8_t](url) otherwise (see truncation note below). **NOTE:** `csrc/libtorch_stable/cpu/cpu_types_arm_vec.hpp`'s `f32_to_bf16x4()` only uses the hardware `vcvt_bf16_f32` conversion when `ARM_BF16_SUPPORT` is defined (i.e. the build detected `FEAT_BF16`). On ARM hosts without that extension, it falls back to a plain bit-shift truncation. This is in contrast to ATen which does round-to-nearest-even with an explicit NaN check. Practical impact: at most a 1-ULP difference in bf16 outputs on non-FEAT_BF16 ARM hardware only. ## Test Plan - [x] CPU build produces leftover `_C` / `_C_AVX*` **and** the matching `*_stable_libtorch` modules. - [x] `torch-abi-audit` reports the three `*_stable_libtorch` libraries as **STABLE** (`unstable=0`) and leftover `_C` / `_C_AVX*` as **UNSTABLE**. **unit test** VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/core/test_cpu_activation.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/test_onednn.py Local testing was only done on the x86_64 architecture. The ARM CPU should be tested in the CI through `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-cpu-test-arm.sh`. ## Test Results ---
Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
Migration progress using the Audit Python extension [torch-abi-audit](https://pypi.org/project/torch-abi-audit/): ``` -- extensions -- [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok ] _C.abi3.so (stable_shim=0, unstable=119) [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok ] _C_AVX2.abi3.so (stable_shim=0, unstable=94) [STABLE ] [abi3-ok ] _C_AVX2_stable_libtorch.abi3.so (stable_shim=36, unstable=0) [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok ] _C_AVX512.abi3.so (stable_shim=0, unstable=97) [STABLE ] [abi3-ok ] _C_AVX512_stable_libtorch.abi3.so (stable_shim=36, unstable=0) [STABLE ] [abi3-ok ] _C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so (stable_shim=36, unstable=0) [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok ] fs_io_C.abi3.so [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok ] spinloop.abi3.so ``` Performance: Microbench of the migrated `torch.ops._C` kernels on the same machine (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=8`, bfloat16). signals.title: [Bugfix] Encode special tokens found in text for MistralCommonBackend in multimodal processors
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #50706 vLLM crashes at engine startup for Mistral3/Pixtral models whose tokenizer resolves to transformers' `MistralCommonBackend`. Per transformers' `AutoTokenizer` resolution, this happens whenever `mistral-common` is installed (`is_mistral_common_available()`) and the model's `model_type` (`mistral`/`ministral`/`mistral3`/etc) is mapped to `MistralCommonBackend` in `TOKENIZER_MAPPING_NAMES` — whether or not the checkpoint ships more than one tokenizer format plays no part (h/t @hmellor for the correction). Affected checkpoints include e.g. `nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4`, `mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B`. `MistralCommonBackend` never encodes special tokens (e.g. `"[IMG]"`) found in plain text. During dummy multimodal input profiling (run at engine startup to size the encoder budget), `PixtralProcessor` counts a mismatch between the placeholder in the templated text and the encoded ids and raises: ``` ValueError: Mismatch in `image` token count between text and `input_ids`. Got ids=[0] and text=[1]. ValueError: Failed to apply PixtralProcessor on data={'text': '[IMG]'} with kwargs={'truncation': False, 'return_tensors': 'pt'} ``` `InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor` now swaps in a `MistralCommonBackend` subclass (`with_placeholder_token_support`) that resolves known special-token strings found in text back to their ids, scoped only to the tokenizer instance handed to HF processors — never used for general/user-prompt tokenization. Conceptually related to but independently derived from: - #50752 — fixes the same root cause on the default tokenizer-mode path (currently blocked on the contributor-gate CI check, not real test failures) - #45525 — fixes the sibling issue (#45289) for `--tokenizer-mode mistral` ## Test Plan - Unit tests: `pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py -q` — 8 new tests against a real `mistralai/Pixtral-12B-2409` tokenizer, covering: bug repro (stock backend doesn't encode `[IMG]`), fix correctness, memoization/idempotency, plain-text passthrough (unaffected by the change), placeholder-prefix disambiguation (`[IMG]` vs `[IMG_BREAK]`/`[IMG_END]`), and `add_special_tokens` behavior. - Manual end-to-end repro against a real affected checkpoint, exercising the same code path as engine-startup profiling: ```python from vllm.config import ModelConfig from vllm.multimodal import MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY model_config = ModelConfig( "unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506", tokenizer="unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506", revision="3ed8d341b53ea3d0e4194689905477688a6cf733", tokenizer_revision="3ed8d341b53ea3d0e4194689905477688a6cf733", max_model_len=8192, ) processor = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(model_config) mm_inputs = MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.get_dummy_mm_inputs( model_config, mm_counts={"image": 1}, processor=processor, ) ``` - `pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/mistral.py vllm/utils/mistral.py vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py` ## Test Result - `tests/tokenizers_/test_mistral.py`: **69 passed, 2 skipped** (pre-existing, unrelated skips) - Manual end-to-end repro against `unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506`: dummy multimodal input generation **crashes** with the exact `ValueError: Mismatch in image token count...` shown above **before** this fix (verified via `git stash`), and **succeeds** after. - `pre-commit run` on all changed files: **clean** (ruff check/format, mypy, forbidden-imports check, SPDX headers, typos, etc.)

signals.title: [Bugfix] Skip Dynamic NTK scaling when served length is below trained length
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52665. Dynamic NTK scaling in `dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py` unconditionally applies its context-extension formula even when the served `max_position_embeddings` is *below* the checkpoint's `max_trained_positions`. Reducing the served length below the trained length is ordinary truncation, not context extension, but the formula ``` inner = scaling_factor * served / trained - (scaling_factor - 1) base = original_base * inner ** (rotary_dim / (rotary_dim - 2)) ``` goes negative in that regime. Raising a negative `base` to a fractional power produces a complex result, which is then silently cast to a real dtype (discarding the imaginary part) and leaves a cache with values on the order of `1e38`. This eventually surfaces as NaN outputs. Concretely, for `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1` served with `--max-model-len 512` and `scaling_factor=2`: ``` inner = 2 * 512 / 2048 - 1 = -0.5 base = 1000 * (-0.5) ** (64 / 62) # complex ``` ## Fix Guard the NTK formula behind `max_position_embeddings > max_trained_positions`. At or below the trained length, the original base is used unchanged, matching plain RoPE and the reference Nomic implementation. Extension behavior above the trained length is untouched — the existing formula already evaluates to the original base at equality, so the branch boundary is continuous. ## Test Plan Added regression tests in `tests/model_executor/layers/test_dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py` covering served length below/at/above the trained length, each asserting the cache matches the exact expected formula (unscaled base below/at, legacy NTK formula above). ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py -v # 3 passed ruff check vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py # All checks passed / already formatted ``` ## Model evaluation An end-to-end serving eval of `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1` wasn't completed: vLLM's engine bootstrap fails on this local CPU/macOS sandbox before the model loads, for reasons unrelated to this change. Verification instead relies on the regression tests above (which reproduce the exact reported symptom pre-fix and pass post-fix) and the issue's own module-level CPU repro. ## Not a duplicate Confirmed open PR #41301 (whose actual diff is a whitespace-only change) does not fix this issue. ## AI assistance disclosure This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude Code). The changes were reviewed and tested as described above before submission.

signals.title: [KV Offload] Pack disk backend slots into a single flat buffer for O_DIRECT alignment
signals.text: ## Context The disk KV offload backend uses O_DIRECT, which requires direct-I/O buffers, offsets, and transfer sizes to satisfy the underlying filesystem/device alignment requirements. The existing implementation aligned the base staging allocations, but individual per-tensor block views could still be misaligned when their bytes-per-block were not alignment-sized. This could cause O_DIRECT reads/writes to fail on some systems. This PR fixes that by packing each KV block into a single aligned, padded staging slot, so every disk transfer has an aligned buffer, offset, and length regardless of the individual tensor sizes. ## Purpose Improve disk-backed KV cache offloading by packing each KV block into one disk slot. This reduces each disk transfer to a single iovec while preserving the existing asynchronous GPU-to-disk transfer flow. This PR: - packs KV tensors back-to-back in a shared per-slot staging buffer; - computes slot padding and disk capacity from the complete packed KV block; - supports a configurable direct-I/O alignment through `kv_connector_extra_config.direct_io_alignment`, defaulting to 4096 bytes; - keeps page-cache mode unpadded, because it does not require direct-I/O alignment; and - copies only KV payload bytes between GPU memory and the staging buffer, while retaining zero-initialized trailing padding for disk I/O. For the disk backend, configure the alignment alongside the existing disk settings: ```json { "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "kv_offload_backend": "disk", "disk_path": "/mnt/nvme/kv-cache", "disk_capacity_bytes": 107374182400, "direct_io_alignment": 4096 } } ``` ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_disk_backend_config.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_disk_backend.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py -v ``` ## Validation The focused coverage exercises configurable slot alignment, padded-capacity accounting, page-cache sizing, single-iovec transfers, and store/load round trips. Model evaluation is not applicable because this change affects KV offload storage and transfer mechanics rather than model output.

signals.title: [Performance][MLA] Use FP16 logits for sparse indexer
signals.text: ## Summary - make the sparse-attention indexer request FP16 logits by default on CUDA, with an explicit `float16`/`float32` engine override - keep DeepGEMM output, local DCP top-k, and every vLLM selector on native FP16 without widening the materialized logits tensor - convert two packed FP16 score encodings to ordered keys at once, use exact native FP16 refinement, and retune persistent/decode crossover tiers - remove the experimental BF16 indexer/top-k surface and add rejection, correctness, engine-policy, DeepGEMM, DCP, and odd-length coverage - resolve the configured logits dtype during module construction so worker warm-up and inference do not depend on a thread-local config context - cover DeepSeek-V4 Flash's 64-head MXFP4 indexer in FP16 for both prefill and paged MTP decode with exact packed-cache-layout correctness tests ## Why GLM-5.2's sparse indexer materializes a large logits tensor before selecting top-k indices. Keeping the tensor and selection native FP16 reduces memory traffic. `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype` accepts `auto`, `float16`, or `float32`; `auto` chooses FP16 on CUDA and FP32 elsewhere. The final kernel transforms both packed halves with one 32-bit operation and reuses the exact keys in histogram and scatter. This reduced the unified FP16 kernel from 57 to 32 registers/thread at 1,024 rows and raised measured occupancy from 49.7% to 94.9%. The dtype is passed as a constant custom-op argument. Resolving it in the operator body originally failed during real-model warm-up because the worker callback does not run inside `set_current_vllm_config`; resolving it when the `SparseAttnIndexer` module is constructed fixes eager warm-up and graph replay. DeepSeek-V4 Flash's optional MXFP4 indexer cache uses the same FP16 logits path. The model-specific tests exercise 64 indexer heads, the packed 68-byte cache layout, and `next_n=3` (MTP=2), comparing both prefill and paged decode against dequantized MXFP4 references. ## Performance All selector measurements use captured real-model GLM logits, top-k 2,048, warmed CUDA graphs, and the repository `.venv`. CUDA events bracket graph replays and are not captured in the graph. Both the custom top-k and reference `torch.topk` run on CUDA; CPU transfers occur only in separate pytest failure diagnostics. Every result was checked against `torch.topk` before timing. ### Production-style fixed 256K decode graph The logits row stride and captured `max_seq_len` remain 256K while only the live KV length changes, matching reuse of a maximum-length graph. Entries are `FP16 us / FP32 us (FP32 / FP16 speedup)`: | Rows | 10K KV | 50K KV | 100K KV | 200K KV | 256K KV | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 4.242 / 4.609 (1.087x) | 7.527 / 9.742 (1.294x) | 8.144 / 10.485 (1.287x) | 9.383 / 12.028 (1.282x) | 9.820 / 12.383 (1.261x) | | 8 | 4.732 / 5.069 (1.071x) | 7.628 / 10.008 (1.312x) | 8.941 / 11.507 (1.287x) | 11.562 / 14.032 (1.214x) | 12.573 / 15.349 (1.221x) | | 32 | 4.838 / 5.242 (1.084x) | 9.639 / 12.419 (1.288x) | 13.138 / 16.068 (1.223x) | 18.901 / 22.429 (1.187x) | 21.295 / 25.228 (1.185x) | | 128 | 5.323 / 5.549 (1.042x) | 17.500 / 19.292 (1.102x) | 27.604 / 29.836 (1.081x) | 47.513 / 66.983 (1.410x) | 56.910 / 85.397 (1.501x) | | 1,024 | 23.967 / 33.269 (1.388x) | 94.387 / 139.846 (1.482x) | 153.163 / 221.120 (1.444x) | 271.360 / 470.133 (1.733x) | 334.933 / 574.720 (1.716x) | FP16 is faster in all 25 production-style shapes: 1.042x-1.733x. ### Exact-stride matrix FP16 speedup over FP32 after retuning the selector: | Rows | 10K KV | 50K KV | 100K KV | 200K KV | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 1.087x | 1.276x | 1.271x | 1.270x | | 8 | 1.062x | 1.300x | 1.290x | 1.214x | | 32 | 1.088x | 1.294x | 1.240x | 1.191x | | 128 | 1.051x | 1.084x | 1.048x | 1.387x | | 1,024 | 1.389x | 1.472x | 1.492x | 1.763x | | 8,192 | 1.528x | 1.627x | 1.628x | 1.839x | | 16,384 | 1.542x | 1.638x | 1.635x | 1.832x | FP16 is faster in all 28 exact-stride shapes: 1.048x-1.839x. The packed-key change invalidated the old decode crossover: persistent now wins through 32K, and measured row thresholds are 768 for 32K-64K, 512 for 64K-100K, and 1,024 for 100K-131K. ## Accuracy ### End-to-end long-context recall The final PR code was evaluated with the real `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` checkpoint and the standard Paul Graham NIAH corpus. The paired runs used TP4, greedy decoding, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, 2,048-token chunked prefill, one sequence at a time, eager execution, disabled prefix caching, disabled FlashInfer autotuning, and no GVR. The only changed engine setting was `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype=float32` versus `float16`. Each context used needle depths 10%, 50%, and 90%, with two independently generated seven-digit keys per cell: | Context | FP32 exact | FP16 exact | Paired identical responses | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 50K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | | 100K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | | 200K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | | 250K | 6/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 | | **Total** | **24/24** | **24/24** | **24/24** | Server-reported prompt lengths were 50,000-50,002, 100,001-100,002, 200,002, and 250,001-250,002 tokens. This is deterministic single-needle retrieval coverage, not a claim that every downstream task is unchanged. ### DeepSeek-V4 Flash FP4 indexer-cache NIAH The real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` checkpoint was evaluated with TP4, MTP=2, FP8 main KV cache, FP16 indexer logits, eager execution, disabled prefix caching, and disabled FlashInfer autotuning. Both arms used the same ordinary fused-MoE backend because the local mega-MoE extension has a stale ABI. The only paired change was an FP8 indexer cache versus `use_fp4_indexer_cache=true`, which startup resolved to `mxfp4` and confirmed with `Using MXFP4 indexer cache for Lightning Indexer`. The standard Paul Graham NIAH corpus used one deterministic seven-digit key per cell and greedy decoding: | Context | FP8 indexer exact | FP4 indexer exact | Paired identical responses | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 50K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | | 100K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | | 200K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | | 250K | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 | | **Total** | **12/12** | **12/12** | **12/12** | Needle depths were 10%, 50%, and 90%. Server prompt-token counts matched between paired arms for all 12 cells and ranged from 49,983 to 249,984, so no prompt was truncated. This is deterministic single-needle retrieval coverage, not a claim that every downstream task is unchanged. Request latency is not reported because the control arm absorbed first-use JIT compilation. ### Real-input top-k set recall To isolate selector-set changes, FP32 logits captured from real GLM decode for BEAM documents were rounded to FP16 and exact top-2,048 was recomputed. Recall is `|topk(FP16) intersect topk(FP32)| / 2048`. Two layer-74 snapshots with 1,024 real rows each and 199,401-199,481 live KV tokens produced: | Rows | Mean recall | Median | 1st percentile | Worst row | Mean / max changed indices | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 2,048 | **99.9313%** | 99.9512% | 99.8047% | 99.7070% | 1.41 / 6 | A separate context sweep used two selector positions and 64 real rows per length: | Live KV | Mean recall | Worst row | Mean changed indices | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 10K | 100.0000% | 100.0000% | 0.00 | | 50K | 99.9496% | 99.9023% | 1.03 | | 100K | 99.9733% | 99.9023% | 0.55 | | 200K | 99.9428% | 99.8535% | 1.17 | | **Overall** | **99.9664%** | **99.8535%** | **0.69** | This recall measurement isolates FP16 score rounding on real distributions; the end-to-end NIAH table above measures the actual native FP16 DeepGEMM and top-k execution path. ## Validation - `cmake --build build/gvr_native_fp16 --target _C_stable_libtorch -j16` - 65 workspace/backend correctness cases passed, including FP16 odd lengths - 20 indexer dtype and retuned-selector policy cases passed - real TP4 GLM launch and warm-up passed for explicit FP32 and FP16 engine settings after moving dtype resolution to module construction - full 1,024-row FP16 equality with CUDA `torch.topk` at 10K, 50K, 100K, 200K, and 256K with a fixed 256K stride - all 56 exact-stride and all 50 fixed-stride dtype/shape cells passed correctness before CUDA-graph timing - packed transform exhaustively matched the scalar ordered-key transform for all 65,536 FP16 encodings - real DSV4 TP4 NIAH passed 12/12 with the FP8 indexer cache and 12/12 with `use_fp4_indexer_cache=true`; all 12 paired responses were identical - all 12 DeepGEMM attention cases passed on GB200, including 64-head DSV4 MXFP4-to-FP16 prefill and paged `next_n=3` decode against dequantized references; 2 full DCP FP16/FP32 decode-parity cases passed earlier - `SWEEP_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1,8,32,256 SWEEP_NUM_PROMPTS_FACTOR=3 bash ../glm_bench.sh` and a matched concurrency-1,024 factor-1 run completed 1,915 requests per dtype with no failures - all applicable pre-commit hooks on the PR changes passed `uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto` was attempted. The full editable build is currently blocked on unmodified current-main QUTLASS code including ATen extension headers while `TORCH_TARGET_VERSION` is defined; both changed CUDA targets build successfully. ## Duplicate-work check This does not duplicate #52149, which fixes persistent top-k candidate overflow, or #48726, which adds an opt-in fused DSA indexer/top-k path. This PR changes dtype production and native selection for the existing materialized- logits path, including DeepGEMM and DCP. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to implement and benchmark this change. Before this draft is marked ready, the submitting human must review every changed line, reproduce the relevant validation, and be prepared to explain and defend the change end-to-end.
