signal.title: [ROCm] TurboQuant KV cache support for Gemma 4
signal.text: ## Purpose Enable TurboQuant KV cache quantization for Gemma 4 models on ROCm. Gemma 4 has two architectural properties that blocked TurboQuant from working: - Heterogeneous head dimensions — sliding-window layers use head_dim=256 while full-attention layers use global_head_dim=512. The existing Gemma4Config.verify_and_update_config forced a TRITON_ATTN backend override that conflicted with the TURBOQUANT backend. - ROCm flash_attn head-dim limit — ROCm's CK-based flash_attn only supports head_dim ≤ 256. Full-attention layers with head_dim=512 caused a RuntimeError: CK only supports head dimension at most 256 at warmup. Changes: - vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py: Add TQFullAttentionSpec, a FullAttentionSpec subclass with TurboQuant-aware page_size_bytes (using tq_slot_size instead of the standard head_size × dtype formula) and a largest_block_size_within helper for page-size unification. - vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py: Extend unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size to handle TQFullAttentionSpec layers whose page does not evenly divide the maximum page size by updating tq_slot_size to the padded value. - vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py: Fall back to fp8 for sliding-window layers when the global dtype is turboquant_*; return TQFullAttentionSpec from get_kv_cache_spec for full-attention TurboQuant layers. - vllm/v1/attention/backends/turboquant_attn.py: Add indexes_kv_by_block_stride (True) and supports_mm_prefix (True) classmethods; add _use_flash_attn per-instance flag that disables ROCm CK flash_attn for head_dim > 256; add _chunked_causal_attn fallback that processes queries in chunks to avoid OOM. - vllm/model_executor/models/config.py: Skip the FA3/Triton backend override in Gemma4Config when a turboquant_* KV cache dtype is requested. - vllm/platforms/rocm.py: Short-circuit to TURBOQUANT backend in get_attn_backend_cls for turboquant_* dtypes; exclude kv-first backends (ROCM_ATTN, ROCM_AITER_FA, ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN) from get_valid_backends when TurboQuant is active. - vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/turboquant/config.py: Skip boundary-layer protection for models with heterogeneous head dimensions (Gemma 4) to avoid inflating the shared page size. - vllm/platforms/interface.py: Include the fp8 sliding-window page in the LCM when computing attn_page_size_1_token for TurboQuant models with mixed attention types. ## Test Plan Testing with MI325X. Run vllm with ``` vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-model-len 32768 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \ --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_k3v4_nc ``` and test accuracy with ``` lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=google/gemma-4-31B-it,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True,num_concurrent=256 \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --output_path /tmp/lm_eval_gsm8k ``` Compare the result against --kv-cache-dtype fp8. ## Test Result | Configuration | KV cache capacity (tokens) | Accuracy GSM8K | |---|---|---| | Baseline fp8 | 738k | 71% | | TurboQuant k3v4_nc | 794k | 69% | Co-authored-by: Claude ---

signal.title: [KV Connector] Support heterogeneous TP sharing in Mooncake Store Connector
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR allows HND vLLM instances whose TP sizes divide a common Store TP size to share the same KV cache through Mooncake Store. Sharing vLLM instances must use the same PP size and satisfy the KV-head and topology requirements described below. Previously, Mooncake Store keys and physical data layouts were tied to the local TP rank. Even when Prefill and Decode instances used the same model, different TP sizes produced different Store shard counts, KV-head ranges, and key namespaces, so the instances could not hit the same KV cache entries. This PR introduces a fixed Store TP layout that decouples Store objects from the local TP size of a vLLM instance: - `store_tp_size` defines a stable number of logical Store shards; - for regular MHA/GQA sharing, each Store shard contains a fixed range of global KV heads; - one local TP rank maps to one or more consecutive Store shards; - HND vLLM instances with different local TP sizes can read and write the same key namespace when they select the same Store TP size; - a Decode consumer with `save_decode_cache` enabled writes newly completed decode KV blocks back in the same Store TP layout. For example, with Store TP size 4: - each TP4 rank maps to one Store shard; - each TP2 rank maps to two Store shards; - KV written by a TP4 Prefill instance can be read by a TP2 Decode instance; - KV written back by the TP2 Decode instance can be reused by compatible TP4 or TP2 instances. The Store uses head-major HND as its stable format. Each Store shard contains its assigned KV heads layer by layer. Since the local HND cache has the same head-major organization, Mooncake multi-buffer I/O reads and writes the corresponding head ranges directly without a layout-conversion staging buffer. Deployments with multiple Prefill TP sizes can explicitly select a common Store TP size: ```json { "kv_connector_extra_config": { "enable_store_tp_lcm": true, "prefill_tp_sizes": [4, 2] } } ``` When `enable_store_tp_lcm` is enabled, the connector uses the least common multiple of `prefill_tp_sizes` as the common Store TP size. For example, the least common multiple of 4 and 2 is 4, so the configuration above selects Store TP size 4. This selection does not change the runtime TP size of any vLLM instance. All Prefill and Decode instances sharing the namespace calculate the same Store TP size from the same configuration. Decode does not inspect which Prefill TP size produced an individual request and does not change its write layout per request. With HND Prefill TP sizes 4 and 2 and HND Decode TP size 2: - each TP4 Prefill rank writes one Store shard; - each TP2 Prefill rank writes two Store shards; - each TP2 Decode rank reads and writes two Store shards. Decode therefore writes according to the common Store TP size, rather than its own local TP size or the TP size of a particular Prefill instance. Its local KV heads are mapped back to the same global Store shards, so decode KV written by one compatible topology remains reusable by the others. When automatic common Store TP size selection is not enabled, all vLLM instances use the explicitly configured `store_tp_size` and follow the same mapping rules. The vLLM instances must already satisfy the existing Mooncake Store compatibility requirements (same model/KV format, block and hash configuration, and cache namespace). Heterogeneous-TP sharing additionally requires: - all sharing endpoints use HND KV cache layout; - Store TP size is greater than or equal to local TP size; - Store TP size is divisible by local TP size; - for MHA/GQA, the model's total number of KV heads is divisible by Store TP size; MQA (`Hkv == 1`) uses a replicated shared layout instead; - all sharing vLLM instances use the same PP size; - the KV cache contains one Full Attention group; - PCP, DCP, and cross-layer KV blocks are not used. Different local TP sizes give each rank a different number of KV heads. This implementation first divides the model's global KV heads into fixed Store shards and then maps each local rank's KV heads to one or more consecutive Store shards. MQA is handled separately: because every TP rank holds the same single KV head, it uses a replicated shared layout instead of regular Store-head partitioning. vLLM instances with different PP sizes do not share a Store namespace. The PP size is encoded in the namespace, preventing incompatible PP topologies from hitting each other's KV cache entries. If any sharing condition is not satisfied, the connector falls back to an isolated rank-local namespace that includes the local TP, PP, and KV layout. In particular, an explicitly configured NHD endpoint remains valid but does not participate in heterogeneous-TP sharing or access HND shared entries. This PR also updates the Mooncake Store Connector documentation and adds regression coverage for: - HND Store-shard mapping and round trips across different TP sizes; - vLLM instances whose ranks hold different numbers of KV heads; - the shared Store key namespace; - common Store TP size selection for multiple HND Prefill TP sizes; - PP namespace isolation; - rank-local fallback for NHD, malformed configurations, and incompatible topologies; - the shared MQA namespace. ## Related Issues and PRs - Issue #45036 tracks the Mooncake Store Connector roadmap and lists "Decode-Phase KV Cache Put with GQA TP Asymmetry" as an open item. This PR covers the Full Attention case where TP sizes are divisible, PP sizes match, and KV heads can be partitioned by a common Store TP size. - PR #36869 added heterogeneous-TP support to `MooncakeConnector` for direct P/D KV transfer. In contrast, this PR targets `MooncakeStoreConnector`, where KV is persisted using a stable Store-shard layout and can be reused and updated by multiple Prefill and Decode instances. - PR #52466 added Decode KV offloading to Mooncake Store consumers. This PR extends that path so Prefill and Decode instances with different TP sizes can read and write the same KV cache using a common Store TP size. - PR #52516 fixes heterogeneous-TP mapping in `MooncakeConnector` when TP size exceeds the number of KV heads and the heads are replicated. This PR uses a separate Store-shard mapping and limits regular sharing to topologies where the total number of KV heads is divisible by Store TP size. Unsupported topologies fall back to an isolated rank-local namespace. ## Test Plan ### Unit and static checks ```bash pre-commit run --files \ docs/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage.md \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \ vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/connector.py \ vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/data.py \ vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/worker.py python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py ``` ### RDMA cluster tests Reusable E2E test code: - [Heterogeneous-TP cluster test directory](https://github.com/ScaleX-IO/vllm/tree/40169553d0/examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store_connector/heterogeneous_tp_cluster) - [Single-node RDMA HND topology matrix](https://github.com/ScaleX-IO/vllm/blob/40169553d0/examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store_connector/heterogeneous_tp_cluster/run_single_node_rdma_layout_matrix.sh) - [Multiple-Prefill-TP HND correctness runner](https://github.com/ScaleX-IO/vllm/blob/40169553d0/examples/disaggregated/mooncake_store_connector/heterogeneous_tp_cluster/run_single_node_lcm_tp4_tp2_d2.sh) The topology matrix used the following configuration: | Item | Configuration | | --- | --- | | Model | Qwen3-32B-FP8 | | Hardware | One node with 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs and NVLink | | Store transport | Mooncake standalone Store over RDMA using `mlx5_bond_0` | | TP topologies | Prefill TP4 -> Decode TP2 and Prefill TP2 -> Decode TP1 | | KV layout | HND -> HND | | Functional workload | One 976-token prompt, 960 expected cached tokens, and 64 deterministic output tokens | | Functional criteria | Store hit covers the block-aligned prefix, generated token IDs match a same-TP no-connector reference, and no Store key fails | | Performance workload | 64 requests, concurrency 16, 64 output tokens per request, 2 warmup requests, and cold-before-cached ordering | | Performance criteria | Every cached request hits 1,041 tokens on average, cold requests have zero cached tokens, and Mooncake reports zero failed keys | The multiple-Prefill-TP correctness run used HND Prefill TP sizes 4 and 2, one HND Decode TP2 instance, and common Store TP size `lcm(4, 2) = 4`. Two distinct prefixes were written to the same Store pool, one by the TP4 Prefill and one by the TP2 Prefill. The same Decode instance reused both prefixes without knowing the source Prefill TP of each request. Decode writeback was also checked after each hit. This run was correctness-only; no performance claim is made from it. ## Test Result ### Unit and static checks ```text All pre-commit hooks passed. 176 passed ``` ### RDMA cluster tests Both HND topology combinations passed functional validation: | Prefill -> Decode | Layout | Cached / prompt tokens | Output tokens | Reference token IDs | Failed keys | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | | TP4 -> TP2 | HND -> HND | 960 / 976 | 64 | Match | 0 | | TP2 -> TP1 | HND -> HND | 960 / 976 | 64 | Match | 0 | Performance results are end-to-end server measurements. `Cached req/s` and `Cold req/s` include scheduling, Store reads, KV placement, and generation. `RDMA RPC GiB/s` measures successful Mooncake `load_get` RPC time, while `phase GiB/s` divides the same bytes by the complete cached-phase wall time. | Prefill -> Decode | Layout | Cached req/s | Cold req/s | Throughput speedup | Cached / cold mean latency (s) | RDMA RPC GiB/s | Phase GiB/s | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | TP4 -> TP2 | HND -> HND | 5.584 | 3.188 | 1.752x | 2.841 / 5.005 | 12.611 | 1.419 | | TP2 -> TP1 | HND -> HND | 4.733 | 1.955 | 2.421x | 3.368 / 8.174 | 24.531 | 1.203 | Each cached phase transferred 17,465,081,856 bytes from Mooncake Store, with no cache misses, unexpected cold hits, failed Store keys, or connector errors. Multiple-Prefill-TP HND correctness results: One TP2/HND Decode instance was connected to a single shared Store pool. The pool contained distinct prefixes produced with both supported Prefill TP sizes: | Prefix | KV producer in the shared pool | Decode consumer | Decode cached / prompt tokens | Decode output tokens | Decode-writeback verification | Result | | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | | A | TP4/HND Prefill | Same TP2/HND Decode | 1,056 / 1,057 | 64 | TP2/HND Prefill subsequently hit 1,104 tokens | Passed | | B | TP2/HND Prefill | Same TP2/HND Decode | 1,056 / 1,057 | 64 | TP4/HND Prefill subsequently hit 1,104 tokens | Passed | This demonstrates that one Decode service is not tied to a single Prefill TP size: across requests, it can reuse KV produced by both TP4 and TP2 through the same common Store TP size 4 namespace, without per-request source-TP metadata. It does not mean that one request splices together KV fragments from different Prefill executions. Mooncake reported zero failed keys and zero operation errors. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Mooncake: heterogeneous-TP support for hybrid GDN/Mamba models
signal.text: ### What Fix `MooncakeConnector` for **heterogeneous-TP** disaggregated prefill/decode (e.g. PP2TP2 prefill → TP4 decode) on **hybrid GDN/Mamba + full-attention** models (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next family). Without these changes, het-TP transfer on hybrid models either fails region validation or silently corrupts the mamba/GDN state on the consumer side. ### Changes 1. **Register every mamba state with its real, unpadded byte length** (`register_kv_caches`). The block page packs conv + ssm states contiguously before padding; registering the padded page length lets the TP-ratio slice cut across padding and misalign states. Each state now registers as its own region with its true payload size. 2. **Split the GDN conv state into per-sub-projection regions** (Q/K/V), reusing `derive_mamba_conv_split` from the NIXL path. Under the DS (dim, state_len) layout each sub-projection is contiguous and shards across TP independently; treating the conv page as one region lets the het-TP byte-split cut across the Q/K/V boundary and scrambles the state (consumer ranks receive Q-segment bytes in K position, etc.). Because the conv state only influences the first `kernel-1` decoded tokens, the corruption shows up as a moderate accuracy drop with occasional empty generations rather than a hard failure. Falls back to a single conv region under the SD layout (homogeneous-TP whole-region copies are unaffected by layout). 3. **Whole-region copy when the consumer TP exceeds the KV-head count** (`consumer_kv_replicated`). With 2 KV heads and consumer TP4, each consumer rank replicates its head group's region rather than slicing the producer's region; the generic ratio slicing would otherwise deliver only half the heads to each consumer rank. 4. **Tolerate peer-PP-stage layers** in `_get_transfer_regions`: remote layers from another PP stage are absent from the local spec table, so use `.get()` (their split flag is unused — region alignment only matches locally registered layers). 5. **Group-aware per-region length validation** in `_validate_asymmetric_region_lengths`: attention regions follow the replicated-consumer rule while mamba/GDN regions keep the TP-ratio rule. ### Tests - `test_register_kv_caches_splits_gdn_conv_sub_projections`: DS layout registers Q/K/V/ssm as separate regions with correct offsets and real byte lengths. - `test_gdn_conv_sub_projection_regions_align_across_het_tp`: P TP2 → D TP4 per-region transfer plan keeps every slice inside its sub-projection. - Existing hybrid-mamba cases updated (per-state registration, replicated consumer KV, PP peer layers) — the module's 12 tests pass. ### Notes - Homogeneous-TP paths (e.g. TP4→TP4) are unaffected: per-region copies degenerate to whole-region copies. - Heterogeneous-TP GDN requires `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`, the same requirement as the NIXL connector.

signal.title: Fix MNNVL Lamport mailbox publication and cleanup
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose Fix silent output corruption in vLLM's MNNVL Lamport all-gather and reduce-scatter. CUDA multicast addresses may only be written with `multimem.*`, so mailbox payloads use a relaxed, system-scope multicast store ([PTX ISA](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#data-movement-and-conversion-instructions-multimem-ld-reduce-multimem-st-multimem-red)). The payload words are also the readiness signal: volatile readers reject stale or partially visible values containing the Lamport sentinel and retry, so release/acquire ordering and `fence.proxy.alias` are unnecessary. Also fix triple-buffer cleanup. The current `(epoch + 1) % 3` rule can erase epoch N+1 after a faster peer publishes it while another rank is still finishing epoch N; cleaning `(epoch + 2) % 3` targets the previously consumed stage instead. DeepSeek-V4 with MegaMoE, expert parallelism, and TP8 across two four-GPU GB300 hosts reaches these kernels through sequence-parallel all-gather and reduce-scatter. Current K3 and DeepSeek-V4 with expert parallelism disabled do not enter this path. Open-PR searches for MNNVL Lamport, multicast publication, and mailbox-stage cleanup found no duplicate fix. ## Test Plan Run the new test in the two-GPU B200 Distributed job, which provides the required CUDA multicast mapping: ```bash pytest -v -s \ tests/distributed/test_custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.py ``` The test asserts a real CUDA multicast mapping and constructs a reachable one-epoch skew using the existing per-rank epoch metadata and mailbox stages. It invokes the shipping all-gather and reduce-scatter kernels, verifies the fast rank's N+1 publication arrived, then asserts that the slow rank's epoch-N cleanup preserves it. ## Test Result - Two-GPU GB300 production-kernel test: old `+1` cleanup erased both all-gather and reduce-scatter N+1 publications in 20/20 cycles; fixed `+2` retained both in 20/20. The final pytest covers all three stage rotations, fails on old code, and passes on fixed code. - Two-node GB300 TP8 DeepSeek-V4 with expert parallelism, MegaMoE, CUDA graphs, CUMEM/MNNVL, and custom collectives: sky-color 10/10 and bat-and-ball 10/10 before load, 128/128 correct concurrent requests, then both probes 10/10 again. - CUDA 13.2 codegen is identical on SM100 and SM103: plain CUDA C++ emits weak `STG.E.128`, while `multimem.st.relaxed.sys` emits `STG.E.128.STRONG.SYS`. Release plus proxy-fence added three memory barriers and was therefore removed. - A final two-host, eight-rank stress completed 2,000 epochs with zero mismatches for both weak and multicast stores on current GB300 hardware. The multicast spelling is retained because ordinary access to a multicast mapping remains undefined by PTX; the deterministic red/green regression is the independently reproducible stage-lifecycle bug. AI assistance was used during investigation and implementation; the human submitter reviewed the change and owns the design and validation. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose and root cause are described. - [x] The test plan provides the exact real-GPU test command. - [x] The test results include deterministic regression and end-to-end validation. - [x] Documentation impact was considered; the code and test describe this kernel-only change. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

signal.title: [Perf] Tune FlashInfer all-reduce selection on SM103
signal.text: Tune standalone FlashInfer all-reduce using conservative, topology-specific cutoffs on SM103. ## Scope - Keep the existing `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` gate and its default unchanged. - When enabled, try FlashInfer before NCCL symmetric memory for inputs that satisfy FlashInfer's eligibility checks. - Store standalone MNNVL tuning as `(compute capability, world size, node count)` in the shared all-reduce policy table. - Use strict per-rank payload limits of 80 MiB for single-node TP4, 64 MiB for two-node TP8, and 8 MiB for four-node TP16. - Keep TP2 on its existing 64 MiB default; the sweep validates it but does not require an override. - Keep TP12 on the existing fallback. FlashInfer MNNVL rejects world size 12 at runtime; its supported sizes are `{2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}`. - Promote the shared workspace to a tuned capacity only when standalone FlashInfer is enabled on a matching topology, keeping fusion-first CUDA graph pointers stable. - Preserve existing thresholds and workspace sizing on every other topology and backend. The separate fused all-reduce + RMSNorm threshold is intentionally excluded from this PR. ## Performance Hardware/software: GB300 GPUs in one NVL72 domain, PyTorch 2.13 / CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.15, and NCCL 2.30.7. Values are median slowest-rank CUDA times and include the steady-state glue required by each backend. The fallback is consumer-visible NCCL symmetric memory for TP4/TP8/TP16 and ordinary out-of-place PyNCCL for TP2, where the symmetric-memory selector is disabled. | Topology | Strict cutoff | Edge payload | FlashInfer AUTO | Fallback | Fallback / FI - 1 | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | TP2, 1 node | 64 MiB (existing) | 63.998 MiB | 146.95 us | 149.75 us | 1.9% | | TP4, 1 node | 80 MiB | 79.994 MiB | 209.26 us | 237.86 us | 13.7% | | TP8, 2 nodes | 64 MiB | 63.998 MiB | 180.87 us | 183.79 us | 1.6% | | TP12, 3 nodes | unsupported | 4.006 MiB | rejected | 111.04 us | n/a | | TP16, 4 nodes | 8 MiB | 7.998 MiB | 36.92 us | 37.34 us | 1.2% | The dense boundary sweeps used production-sized persistent workspaces. TP2 reaches parity and then loses with an 80 MiB workspace, so it retains 64 MiB. TP4 wins through 80 MiB, while a 96 MiB workspace loses at the 80 MiB point, so the cutoff stops at 80 MiB. TP16 wins through 8 MiB but loses clearly by 10 MiB, so it uses the strict 8 MiB cutoff. ### K3 TP8 + DSpark decode Three seed-matched measured cohorts per arm and concurrency, after two warmup waves. The setup used TP8, DCP1, DSpark7, FP8 KV cache, exact 1,024-token prompt KV state from `DecodeBenchConnector`, and 4,096 generated tokens per request. | Concurrency | Target AR activation | 2 MiB TPOT | 64 MiB TPOT | TPOT gain | Throughput gain | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16 | 1.750 MiB | 14.840 ms | 14.833 ms | 0.05% | 0.01% | | 32 | 3.500 MiB | 17.833 ms | 17.167 ms | 3.74% | 3.66% | C16 is a control because its target activation is already below the old 2 MiB limit. C32 crosses that limit; after subtracting the C16 control shift, its threshold-associated TPOT benefit is **3.69 percentage points** with a paired 95% interval of **[3.49, 3.89] points**. All 288 measured requests completed with no failures. Acceptance lengths were identical between policies for every paired seed. FlashInfer was enabled and NCCL symmetric-memory all-reduce was disabled in both serving arms to isolate the threshold change; the full-glue sweep above measures the FlashInfer/fallback crossover directly. ## Tests - `pytest -q tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k flashinfer`: 13 passed, 12 deselected. - File-scoped `pre-commit run` on all four changed files: all applicable hooks passed. - TP2/TP4/TP16 CUDA-graph sweeps checked numerical correctness and input preservation before and after replay. - TP12 eager smoke test confirmed one-shot and two-shot both reject world size 12 while the fallback completes correctly. ## Duplicate work and assistance An open-PR search found #44080, which adjusts the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm cap on SM90/Hopper. This PR changes standalone MNNVL all-reduce selection and workspace sizing on SM103/GB300; it does not modify the fusion threshold. No duplicate open PR was found. AI assistance was used to port, benchmark, test, and review this change. The submitter should review every changed line and the performance evidence before merge.
signal.author: GirasoleY

signal.title: turboquant decode attetnion optimization
signal.text: ## Purpose This work optimizes the TurboQuant decode path in vLLM while preserving compressed KV-cache semantics. It introduces three related changes: 1. A page-local KV-cache ABI shared by cache store, decode, dequantization, and continuation-prefill paths. 2. Fused store kernels that quantize, pack, and write directly to the new ABI without an intermediate layout conversion. 3. An optimized fused decode-attention operator. ## Support matrix The new page-local ABI is fully integrated across the TurboQuant cache lifecycle. All cache producers and consumers—including the MSE and FP8 store paths, decode attention, full dequantization, and continuation-prefill—use the same layout. The runtime contains neither a legacy-layout branch nor an ABI conversion operator. The table below describes only the coverage of the optimized decode-attention operator: | Capability | Supported range | |---|---| | Attention | Full causal self-attention, `q_len = 1` | | Query/output dtype | BF16 | | Head dimension | 64, 128, 256 | | Head geometry | MHA and GQA | | Page size | 16, 32, 64, 128 | | Cache preset | K4V4-NC | | Attention scale | `1 / sqrt(head_dim)` | | Execution mode | Eager and CUDA Graph | | GPU | NVIDIA Ampere / Hopper / Blackwell | Unsupported fast-path configurations continue to use the existing compressed TurboQuant implementation.

signal.title: [Kimi K3][Pref] Export prefill checkpoints in a single FlashKDA pass
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR adds an optional Kimi-K3 prefill checkpoint mode for fine-grained prefix caching. When enabled, FlashKDA exports an intermediate recurrent-state checkpoint during the prefill. The checkpoint is stored in an internal request-owned Mamba block, allowing prefix cache entries smaller than the Mamba block size to be reused without an additional FlashKDA forward. Main changes: - Export recurrent-state checkpoints from the existing packed FlashKDA prefill. - Export the matching causal-conv state. - Support partial prefix caching and spec decoding. - Add internal checkpoint block allocation, lifecycle management, and scheduler metadata. - Allow the scheduler to skip the additional checkpoint-boundary forward. - Add unit tests for checkpoint metadata, block lifecycle, and prefix caching. [#52789](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52789) introduced the prefill-checkpoint infrastructure. This PR adds efficient support for fine-grained partial prefix caching and exports the checkpoint directly from the existing FlashKDA kernel, avoiding an additional or split FlashKDA forward. ## Usage ```bash VLLM_KIMI_K3_KDA_CHECKPOINT_MODE=1 \ vllm serve <model> \ --kda-prefill-backend flashkda \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --prefix-match-unit 128 ``` This PR depends on [vllm-project/FlashKDA#7](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/7). The FlashKDA commit is temporarily pinned and should be updated after that PR is merged. ## Test Plan Setup: - TP8 on 2 × 4 GB300 - Growing prefix from 120K to 164K tokens - +2K tokens per round - 8 concurrent streams - Three runs per variant ## Test Result | Variant | P50 TTFT | **Improvement** | | --- | ---: | ---: | | #52789, non-partial | 2,151.53 ms | Baseline | | #52789, partial128 | 2,375.23 ms | **-10.40%** | | This PR, non-partial | 2,141.67 ms | Baseline | | **This PR, partial128** | **1,398.49 ms** | **34.70%** | ## Correctness Three consecutive full OCRBench runs with checkpoint mode and partial128 produced: 89.4% 89.6% 89.3% mean: 89.43% --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Spec Decode] Enable adaptive DSpark on SM100 sparse MLA
signal.text: ## Purpose Resolves #52785. This is part of the adaptive DSpark backend expansion tracked by #51303. Related GLM-5.2 DSpark bring-up context is in #50851. This enables adaptive DSpark verification with `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMBackend`. It was validated end to end with `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` and `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark` on 4× NVIDIA B300. Before this change, startup failed for two independent reasons: 1. The sparse-MLA metadata builder derived token-to-request mappings from CPU query boundaries. Adaptive verification changes those boundaries on device without synchronizing them back to the CPU. 2. The target graph capability check included the draft model's FlashAttention backend. Draft attention is captured and capability-checked by its own graph manager, and it never consumes the target's adaptive query lengths. ## Changes - Add an SM100 FlashInfer sparse-MLA metadata builder that derives request IDs from device query boundaries and declares variable-length CUDA graph support. - Scope target CUDA graph and query-length compatibility checks to target attention layers while retaining draft groups needed by draft prefill. - Add a real B300 kernel regression using GLM-5.2 dimensions. It compares FlashInfer sparse MLA against SDPA with device query lengths `[1, 7, 3, 5]` and deliberately stale CPU lengths `[4, 4, 4, 4]`. - Add a unit regression proving draft-only groups are excluded without hiding mixed target/draft groups that still participate in target execution. ## Performance Scaled SPEED Bench qualitative sweep, 16K context, 512 output tokens, temperature 1.0, seed 0. The c1 run used 32 prompts, c16 used 128, and the remaining points used 256. Both configurations completed with zero failed requests. | Concurrency | Fixed k=7 tok/s | Adaptive tok/s | Gain | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 306.7 | 310.6 | +1.3% | | 16 | 2,084.4 | 2,093.5 | +0.4% | | 32 | 3,525.0 | 3,595.8 | +2.0% | | 64 | 5,236.8 | 5,538.8 | +5.8% | | 128 | 7,172.9 | 8,190.7 | +14.2% | | 256 | 7,720.4 | 10,316.8 | +33.6% | At c256, mean TPOT improved from 23.24 ms to 17.37 ms. A direct B300 kernel comparison also favored the selected FlashInfer SM100 backend over FlashMLA by 2.1–2.6× for uniform decode batches and 31.9× for a mixed 1/3/5/7-token adaptive shape. ## Model evaluation GSM8K, five-shot, 200 examples, greedy decoding, 2,048-token output limit: | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid/truncated | |---|---:|---:| | Fixed k=7 | 89.0% | 1.0% | | Adaptive k≤7 | 91.0% | 0.5% | This shows no detected accuracy regression at this sample size; the two-point difference is not presented as statistically significant. HLE was also exercised, but 38/40 sampled outputs still truncated at an 8,192-token limit, so no HLE accuracy result is reported. ## Reproduction ```bash chg run -g=4 -- vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --load-format instanttensor \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 64 \ --max-model-len 16384 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --max-num-seqs 256 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \ --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":2048}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark","attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' ``` The full server completed target and draft CUDA graph capture and served the benchmark/evaluation requests successfully. ## Test plan ```bash chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py -q # 21 passed, 8 skipped .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -q # 7 passed .venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files .venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-format --files .venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files # all passed ``` The focused CPU and B300 tests plus lint and mypy were rerun after rebasing onto current `main`. ## Not a duplicate Duplicate checks covered #51303 and adaptive DSpark/sparse-MLA keywords. #52362 enables adaptive verification on ROCm and changes AMD model/indexer paths; it does not overlap this CUDA SM100 metadata and target/draft graph-scoping change. #50694 addresses earlier FA3 and DSpark/DFlash proposer wiring for GLM-5.2. ## AI assistance AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to investigate, implement, test, benchmark, and draft this change. signal.title: [KV Offload] Pack disk backend slots into a single flat buffer for O_DIRECT alignment
signal.text: ## Context The disk KV offload backend uses O_DIRECT, which requires direct-I/O buffers, offsets, and transfer sizes to satisfy the underlying filesystem/device alignment requirements. The existing implementation aligned the base staging allocations, but individual per-tensor block views could still be misaligned when their bytes-per-block were not alignment-sized. This could cause O_DIRECT reads/writes to fail on some systems. This PR fixes that by packing each KV block into a single aligned, padded staging slot, so every disk transfer has an aligned buffer, offset, and length regardless of the individual tensor sizes. ## Purpose Improve disk-backed KV cache offloading by packing each KV block into one disk slot. This reduces each disk transfer to a single iovec while preserving the existing asynchronous GPU-to-disk transfer flow. This PR: - packs KV tensors back-to-back in a shared per-slot staging buffer; - computes slot padding and disk capacity from the complete packed KV block; - supports a configurable direct-I/O alignment through `kv_connector_extra_config.direct_io_alignment`, defaulting to 4096 bytes; - keeps page-cache mode unpadded, because it does not require direct-I/O alignment; and - copies only KV payload bytes between GPU memory and the staging buffer, while retaining zero-initialized trailing padding for disk I/O. For the disk backend, configure the alignment alongside the existing disk settings: ```json { "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "kv_offload_backend": "disk", "disk_path": "/mnt/nvme/kv-cache", "disk_capacity_bytes": 107374182400, "direct_io_alignment": 4096 } } ``` ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_disk_backend_config.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_disk_backend.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py -v ``` ## Validation The focused coverage exercises configurable slot alignment, padded-capacity accounting, page-cache sizing, single-iovec transfers, and store/load round trips. Model evaluation is not applicable because this change affects KV offload storage and transfer mechanics rather than model output.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Core] Count SWA in-flight KV once per pool, not per request (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 #51041)
signal.text: Fixes #51041 ## Summary `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config()` divided the KV cache pool by each group's **full per-request admission cap**, which includes the `max_in_flight_tokens` allowance inside `SlidingWindowSpec.max_admission_blocks_per_request()`. But in-flight tokens are bounded **system-wide** by the scheduler's token budget across *all* requests — at most `max_in_flight_tokens` tokens are unsettled at any moment, regardless of concurrency. Multiplying a global bound by max concurrency over-reserves the pool by `(max_concurrency − 1) × transient` blocks per SWA-class group. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (H20 TP=2, `fp8_ds_mla`, block size 256, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192, doubled under async scheduling) the four SWA-class groups of the 5-group hybrid layout each charge in-flight tokens at tiny compressor block granularity (`cdiv(16384, 4) = 4099` pages, `cdiv(16384, 8) = 2065` pages …), inflating the per-request footprint from ~3.6 KiB/token to ~53.5 KiB/token and capping `max_model_len` at ~121K instead of ~1M. This matches every datapoint in the issue (Burlesque1's 53.5 KiB H20 TP=2, kezboard233's V100 α/β regression, @CHNtentes' healthy 10.07 KiB DSpark run). ### The change - `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`: add `steady_memory_usage_bytes()` / `transient_memory_usage_bytes()` to `KVCacheSpec` with the exact identity `admission == steady + transient`. Defaults preserve byte-identical behavior for every other spec type; overridden only in `SlidingWindowSpec`, `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec`, and `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` (the DSv4 aggregated worker-config shape). - `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`: reserve the transient part once per pool instead of per request: ``` N_max = (num_blocks − Σ_g transient_g) / Σ_g steady_g ``` The runtime per-request admission gate is unchanged, so startup sizing and runtime admission stay consistent: `N × steady + transient ≤ num_blocks`. Pool sizing (`_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups`, the `max`-based conservative bound) is untouched. ### Note on 0731 vs preview The checkpoint config delta (2 trailing zeros in `compress_ratios`, `dspark_*` fields) is a red herring — layer indices ≥ `num_hidden_layers` are clamped and every `dspark_*` consumer is gated behind `use_dspark()`. The regression tracks the **vLLM version**, not the checkpoint: the admission formula was introduced by #40946 and widened to `max_in_flight_tokens` by #47728 (2026-07-08, shortly before 0.26.0). The preview checkpoint's older config format simply doesn't form the 5-group hybrid layout on 0.26.0, so it never hits the SWA-group overcharge. ### Not duplicating existing PRs Checked open PRs referencing #51041 / KV-cache accounting — none. This PR is distinct from: - #37584 (auto-revert of #36030) — concerns the pool-sizing **sum** in `_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups`, untouched here; the #48317/#36030 per-group sums are preserved for the steady part. - #40694 — fixes the capacity **log** for Qwen3.5 hybrid, log-only. - #41834 — SM12x enablement, no accounting changes. ## Behavior change Capacity/concurrency **reporting and admission headroom only** — no attention kernels, no KV layout, no numerics. Model outputs are unchanged, so no model evals were run. ## Test Plan / Results All on CPU (no GPU on the dev machine — GPU test suites were **not** run): ``` pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py # 78 passed pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \ tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py # 100 passed pytest tests/v1/test_kv_cache_spec_registry.py \ tests/v1/engine/test_init_error_messaging.py # 45 passed pytest tests/v1/core/ # 496 passed; 3 e2e tests fail # engine init identically on # the base commit (GPU-less host, # pre-existing, not a regression) pre-commit run --files <changed files> # all passed (ruff, format, mypy-3.10) pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual # passed ``` New regression test `test_dsv4_flash_0731_kv_capacity` builds the real 0731 architecture (43 layers, `compress_ratios = [0, 0, (4, 128)×20, 0]`, real per-layer spec shapes from `deepseek_v4/attention.py` / `compressor.py`) through the actual grouping → packed-layout → concurrency pipeline, and asserts: 1. the 5-group hybrid layout forms with 20/20 compressor layers, 2. `steady + transient == max` holds per group, 3. per-token cost < 10 KiB at 1M context (pre-fix ~53 KiB), 4. the new formula strictly beats the pre-fix per-request-peak formula. Four existing assertions in `test_get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` / `test_get_max_concurrency_packed_kv_cache_config` were updated to the new (documented-in-comment) expected values. ## AI-assistance statement **The code, tests, and this PR description were entirely generated by an AI agent (Claude); the change was reviewed line-by-line by the human submitter (@volkermauel), who also ran the full CPU test suites and lint/mypy checks listed above and verified the root-cause analysis against the numeric evidence in the issue thread.** Co-authored-by: Claude Agent Here <claude@anthropic.com>

signal.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Do not let a recurrent group's unhashed block truncate the load boundary
signal.text: `update_state_after_alloc` scans the allocated block list for the first block that is `not is_null and block_hash is None` and treats that index as the start of the freshly allocated region. That index is load-bearing: it drives [`start_chunk_idx` / `keys_to_load`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py), `dst_block_ids`, `group_sizes` and `block_indices`. Getting it wrong loads the wrong keys into the wrong destination blocks. The scan started at **index 0** — inside the region already reported as locally computed, where every block is computed by definition. For a **recurrent (Mamba / GDN) group** that is not merely redundant but wrong. Such a group has no per-token KV at all: it carries a fixed-size state, which is why `get_sliding_window_size_in_chunks()` returns 1 for `MambaSpec` ("Mamba depends on a single state"). Most positions in its block table point at the shared null sentinel, and the one real block holding the state is legitimately **not full-and-cached** — non-null, unhashed, sitting below the computed mark. ``` legend [H] hashed [·] null placeholder [U] non-null, UNHASHED [F] fresh recurrent group (GDN/Mamba, window = 1 chunk), 21 chunks computed + 1 loaded: idx 0 1 2 3 4 ... 20 21 [H] [H] [·] [U] [·] ... [·] [F] ^ BEFORE scan starts at 0, stops here boundary = 3 |<-------- claimed computed: 21 ------------>| assert 21 <= 3 ✗ AssertionError load region would be blocks 3..21 -> 19 wrong destinations, wrong keys AFTER scan starts at first_fresh = 21 ------------>^ boundary = 21, assert 21 <= 21 ✓ load region = block 21 only -> matches the 1-chunk hit ``` For a full-attention group this is a **no-op**: every token has KV, every block below the boundary is full-and-cached, so the old scan skipped them anyway. The existing assert now holds by construction (`nlcgb >= cdiv(nlct, tpb)` ⟹ `nlct <= nlcgb * tpb`); it is kept as a guard against other causes rather than deleted. ## Reproduction 4-node GB200, Qwen3.5-family hybrid GDN+GQA (4 KV cache groups, 3 recurrent), MTP, 384 GiB host tier. Under sustained load the leader crashed after **47,142 requests**: ``` File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 963, in schedule self.connector.update_state_after_alloc( File ".../kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py", line 832, in update_state_after_alloc num_locally_computed_tokens AssertionError leader exit=1 | other three exit=137 (gang teardown) ``` The captured 3h22m window on the crashing rank makes the trigger unambiguous. It saw **22 lookups that hit offloaded tokens, but only 4 that were true partial hits** (`num_locally_computed_tokens > 0`) — and all four arrived in the last 36 seconds: | time | external tokens | locally computed | outcome | |---|---|---|---| | 00:57 – 04:18 | 18 lookups | **0** | fine — assert reads `0 <= X` | | 04:18:45 | 4256 | 8512 | ok | | 04:18:52 | 2128 | 4256 | ok | | 04:19:07 | 2128 | 10640 | ok | | 04:19:21 | 4256 | 10640 | **AssertionError, same second** | **Why this is easy to miss.** It needs `num_external_tokens > 0` **and** `num_locally_computed_tokens > 0`. Tests that flood to full eviction before re-sending produce `num_computed_tokens == 0` — 18 of the 22 lookups above — where the assert reads `0 <= X` and cannot fire. The rank sat clean for 3h21m under exactly that pattern before the first partial hits appeared. ### Reproduced on a build that carries the #49146 clamp The assert is **not** masked by [#49146](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49146)'s `num_allocated_chunks` clamp (`94ed0bf4e0`, in `main`). A build composed as `#49146 clamp + #52771, without this fix` was put under sustained production traffic and asserted **three times across two independent clusters**, at roughly **20 minutes / ~850 requests** each: ``` vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:963 schedule vllm/.../kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py:840 update_state_after_alloc AssertionError ``` Line 840 is this assert: in the same tree without the clamp it sits at 832, and the clamp inserts exactly 8 lines above it — the two tracebacks are the same assertion. Across four builds under the same workload and config, the correlation is with **this fix**, not the clamp and not #52771: | build | #49146 clamp | #52771 | this fix | fault-free lifetime | |---|---|---|---|---| | A | — | — | — | 22–70 min, 3 asserts | | B | — | ✓ | — | 10 / 30 / 40 / 88 min, ≥4 asserts | | C | ✓ | ✓ | — | ~20 min, 3 asserts | | D | ✓ | — | ✓ | **336 min, zero asserts** | Every build lacking this fix asserts, including one carrying the clamp; the only build carrying it is the only one that holds. Memory was never implicated (no `OOMKilled`; peak well under limit). A separate note on reproducing it: a synthetic driver that holds the hit *shape* constant does not surface this. On a smaller same-family deployment I drove **12,000 consecutive requests at a 100% true-partial-hit rate** with no assert — but every request had an identical `num_locally_computed_tokens`, so it probed one boundary alignment repeatedly. The production crashes arise under organically varied prefix lengths, which is what walks the boundary across block offsets. ## Relationship to #52735 / #52771 **This is independent of the drafter-annotation defect, and of the abort fix.** Three arms, all at current `main` (which already carries the [#49146](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49146) `num_allocated_chunks` clamp, commit `94ed0bf4e0`), running the regression test below: | arm | #49146 clamp | #52771 | this fix | `offloading_connector/` suite | |---|---|---|---|---| | A | ✓ (in `main`) | — | — | regression test **fails** | | B | ✓ | ✓ | — | **1 failed**, 254 passed | | C | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **255 passed, 0 failed** | Arms B and C were run back-to-back in a single GPU allocation, toggling only this hunk, so the environment is identical; the one failure in B is this PR's regression test and nothing else. Every test that passes without the fix still passes with it. Arm B is the decisive one: with #52771 (`44a3045ec1`) cherry-picked on top of `main`, the all-groups drafter fallback removed and no group marked as a drafter — so the volatile-tail pop never runs — the boundary assert still fires. The assert is not gated on `is_eagle_group` anywhere. #52771 is also **complementary**: by restoring real loads it raises how often `num_external_tokens > 0`, and therefore how often this path is reached. It is the right fix for the annotation defect and should land; this is the crash underneath it. *(This PR previously also carried a competing fix for #52735 — removing the eagle query-widen, `required_window += 1` and the volatile-tail pop. I have dropped all of it in favour of #52771, which was filed first, targets the root cause rather than the symptom, and additionally fixes a store-side hole mine did not. What remains here is only the boundary fix.)* ## Tests `test_recurrent_group_unhashed_block_does_not_truncate_load_boundary` plants exactly that block — non-null, unhashed, below the boundary — and asserts the **destination blocks** are correct (`41 not in loaded`, `42 in loaded`), not merely that nothing raised. Verified to **fail against unpatched `main`** and pass with this change. Full `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/` suite green on an aarch64 GB200 node.

signal.title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4] Handle trailing system messages in prompt rendering
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose Co-authored-by: laolaoPlayer <2584941823@qq.com> Address the DeepSeek V4 trailing-system prompt-rendering edge case reported in [#40854](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40854#issuecomment-4864596205) and [#46256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46256) and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/11951. When the final message has the `system` role, `render_message` leaves the prompt at a bare system-message boundary instead of appending the assistant transition. Generation can then stop immediately and return empty content. This change appends the existing assistant/thinking transition only when the `system` message is truly the final message. Existing `user` and `developer` behavior is unchanged, and no transition is inserted before a later `user`, `assistant`, or `latest_reminder` message. Open PR #43937 addresses the same symptom with an unconditional `system` allow-list entry. That broader condition changes existing `system -> latest_reminder` golden fixtures. This PR uses a trailing-only guard to preserve those prompts. The difference was documented in [#46256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46256#issuecomment-5204237778). No documentation update is needed because this fixes existing tokenizer behavior without adding an option or API. ## Test Plan - Add a regression test for `system -> user -> system`. - Add a non-regression test for `user -> assistant -> system -> user`. - Run the complete DeepSeek V4 tokenizer test file: ```bash VLLM_PLUGINS="" \ PYTHONPATH=/workspace/vllm-cpu-test-bootstrap-pr:/workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2 \ /workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ -p no:cacheprovider \ --confcutdir=/workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2/tests/tokenizers_ \ /workspace/vllm-pr-c14a568e2/tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py ``` - Run Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check`. - Reuse the completed real-environment validation through the production router. ## Test Result - Before the fix: `1 failed, 1 passed`; the trailing-system prompt was missing `<｜Assistant｜></think>`. - Focused regression tests after the fix: `2 passed`. - Complete `tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py`: `28 passed in 14.57s`. - Ruff check: `All checks passed!`. - Ruff format check: `2 files already formatted`. - `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`: passed. - Real environment: four scenarios were each run three times after deploying the source patch to all four nodes and restarting the cluster. All 12/12 requests passed. The target case returned `"4"` instead of an empty response, with no regression in the other scenarios. See the [full report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51262#issuecomment-5204365444). - No additional NPU run was performed after rebasing because the source patch was unchanged. ## AI Assistance AI assistance was used to inspect the renderer control flow, implement the regression coverage and fix, compare related open work, and prepare validation. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose and related issues are documented. - [x] The unit-test and static-check commands are provided. - [x] Unit-test, static-check, and real-environment results are recorded. - [x] Documentation impact was considered; no documentation change is needed. </details>

signal.title: [ROCm][MLA] Reach FULL cudagraphs for AITER MLA speculative decoding
signal.text: ## Purpose Speculative decoding on ROCm cannot reach FULL cudagraphs, for two independent reasons. This fixes both. Measured on Kimi-K3 with a DSpark draft, TP8 on MI355X. **The reported support level.** A DSpark draft group serves its whole `1 + num_speculative_tokens` block through the decode path, but `TritonMLAMetadataBuilder` reports `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE` from a class constant, and the engine takes the minimum over attention groups -- so that one group downgrades the *whole engine* off FULL. `forward_mqa` flattens the block with `repeat_interleave` on a Python int and performs no device->host sync, so the group does satisfy `UNIFORM_BATCH`. `triton_mla.py` now reports that where the KV cache group is marked `non_causal_multi_token_decode`. Note the predicate is group scoped, not draft scoped, so a causal target sharing a draft's group is lifted too; `__init__` two lines below already uses it to raise `reorder_batch_threshold`, and the docstring records the scope. **Syncs inside the captured region.** `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mqa`'s small-head (< 16 query heads per rank) verify path expands each request's paged-KV range into one row per verify token on every MLA layer, with four device->host syncs and an allocation sized from what it just read back, each of which aborts HIP graph capture. That expansion moves into `_build_decode`, once per step, writing into persistent buffers so `mla_gluon` sees fixed addresses across replays. One sync remains there, because Gluon derives its split count from `min_kv_seq_len` and the merged causal-mask test pins that to the shortest row submitted; the builder runs outside the captured region, as `flex_attention.py`'s `.item()` in `build_for_cudagraph_capture` does. **`gpu_worker.py`.** `cache_config.kv_cache_size_tokens` is set in the engine core and the front end but never in the worker, which forward-propagates only `num_gpu_blocks`. The builder above therefore sees `None` in any multi-process deployment and falls back to a bound derived from `max_model_len`, roughly six times the real capacity. Filling it in `Worker.initialize_from_config` takes the verify buffer reservation from 295.3 MiB per rank to 46.6 MiB. The gap pre-dates this PR but is load-bearing for that reservation, so it is fixed here. **Related.** #50578 touches the same file and is best reviewed alongside. They merge cleanly in either order and do not collide on the verify path. ## Test Plan The merged causal-mask test covers exactly the code that moves here. Then serve and bench at concurrency `C` in `1 16`: ```bash pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 vllm serve /model \ --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8384 --max-num-seqs 32 --disable-custom-all-reduce \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/draft","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA"}' \ -cc '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[8,16,32,128,256]}' vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --dataset-name random --ignore-eos \ --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \ --num-prompts $((C * 8)) --max-concurrency $C --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el ``` `Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL)` should appear in the server log, and `compilation.py`'s "not supported with spec-decode" warning should not. ## Test Result | | PIECEWISE (`main`) | FULL (this PR) | | --- | --- | --- | | c1 output tok/s | 12.10 | 46.30 | | c1 mean ITL | 186.98 ms | 34.26 ms | | c16 output tok/s | 174.01 | 326.46 | | c16 mean ITL | 188.28 ms | 92.91 ms | | capture memory per rank | 0.51 GiB | 2.11 GiB | | downgrade warning | present | absent | | acceptance length | 2.55 / 2.48 | 2.51 / 2.45 | Acceptance length is unchanged, so the gain is execution speed rather than better drafting. The causal-mask test passes, and the reservation logs 46.6 MiB against `GPU KV cache size: 814,051 tokens` -- from a later run than the table, which predates the `gpu_worker.py` fix; both patched runs agree on capture memory and graph mode. Absolute throughput came from `--dataset-name random`, whose synthetic prompts the draft predicts poorly (acceptance around 21%), so the FULL:PIECEWISE ratio is the controlled quantity and the absolutes are not representative of real prompts.

signal.title: [Model][Generative Recommendation] Add HSTU model support to vLLM
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR adds HSTU-based generative recommendation model support to vLLM. HSTU is a ranking model architecture designed for generative recommendation. Unlike traditional language models, HSTU does not autoregressively generate text tokens. Instead, it synchronously computes ranking scores for all candidate items in a request. The goal of this change is to enable generative recommendation models to reuse the existing vLLM and large-model serving ecosystem, including: - Hugging Face model and configuration loading. - vLLM model registration. - GPU model execution. - Attention backend selection. - Optimized CUDA operators. - Request batching and scheduling. - Asynchronous output handling. - CUDA Graph execution. - Future distributed inference and online serving infrastructure. Generative recommendation and large language models have several common characteristics. Both can be represented as sequence models, use embedding layers and transformer-style computation, and benefit from optimized attention kernels, GPU batching, asynchronous execution, and production-level model serving infrastructure. By integrating HSTU into vLLM, generative recommendation models can reuse the existing large-model ecosystem instead of maintaining an independent inference stack. ## Inference Paradigm Although HSTU and large language models share several model and runtime components, their inference semantics are different. | Aspect | Large language model | Generative recommendation model | | --- | --- | --- | | Decode behavior | Autoregressively generates one token at a time | Synchronously computes scores for all candidates in a request | | Model output | Vocabulary logits for the next token | One ranking score for each candidate item | | Sampling | Requires token sampling and token ID generation | Does not generate a sampled token | | Request progress | Continues until the requested number of tokens is generated | Completes after all candidate scores are returned | | Output format | Usually `[num_tokens, vocab_size]` | Packed candidate-score output | | Scheduler signal | Uses sampled token IDs to update request state | Uses candidate scores to complete the request | The default vLLM generation path is designed around language-model execution: 1. Run the model forward pass. 2. Produce vocabulary logits. 3. Invoke the token sampler. 4. Generate token IDs. 5. Update the request state. 6. Continue decoding until the request is finished. This flow cannot be directly reused for HSTU because HSTU produces candidate ranking scores rather than vocabulary logits. Passing HSTU outputs through the normal sampler would incorrectly interpret candidate scores as vocabulary logits and could produce invalid token IDs. Therefore, this PR adds a score-only execution path: 1. Run the HSTU forward pass. 2. Extract the score corresponding to each candidate item. 3. Convert candidate IDs and scores into `LogprobsTensors`. 4. Return the scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. 5. Skip the standard token sampler. 6. Skip generated-token state updates. 7. Complete the request after all candidate scores are returned. The scheduler is also updated to support score-only recommendation requests. A request can be completed after candidate scores are produced even when no `new_token_ids` are returned. ## Implementation Overview This PR contains five main categories of changes. ### 1. Model Structure and Model Registration Files: - `vllm/model_executor/models/hstu.py` - `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` - `tests/models/registry.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU model implementation. - Add HSTU embedding layers, transformer blocks, normalization layers, and prediction heads. - Register the HSTU model with vLLM. - Support Hugging Face HSTU model loading. - Add HSTU to the model registry test data. - Add model registration and model import coverage. ### 2. Model Configuration and Configuration Registration Files: - `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/__init__.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/hstu.py` Changes: - Add HSTU-specific configuration classes. - Support HSTU model and task configuration fields. - Support `model_type = "hstu"`. - Convert HSTU configuration data from Hugging Face configuration files into the vLLM configuration representation. - Preserve compatibility with the existing vLLM configuration loading flow. ### 3. Model Operators and Operator Registration Files: - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/hstu_attn.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/selector.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU attention backend. - Integrate the external HSTU variable-length attention operator. - Register the HSTU attention backend with vLLM. - Automatically select `HSTU_ATTN` for HSTU or generative recommendation models when no explicit backend is configured. - Preserve explicit attention backend configuration as the highest-priority option. - Validate unsupported attention combinations and return clear errors. - Pass per-request context and candidate metadata to the HSTU attention implementation. Automatic backend selection is only applied when the user has not explicitly selected an attention backend. This preserves the existing backend override behavior. ### 4. Model Runner V1 Adaptation File: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` Changes: - Add generative recommendation metadata collection. - Add HSTU candidate score extraction. - Pass HSTU metadata through the forward context. - Bypass the standard token sampler for HSTU requests. - Return candidate scores through the prompt-logprobs output path. - Add recommendation-specific request completion handling. - Preserve the existing execution path for non-HSTU models. ### 5. Model Runner V2 Adaptation Files: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/gr_state.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py` - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` Changes: - Add `GRState` for request-scoped generative recommendation state. - Store user IDs, candidate count, prompt token IDs, and request stage. - Move candidate score extraction from the Model Runner into `GRState`. - Convert packed HSTU outputs into `LogprobsTensors`. - Add asynchronous score output handling. - Return candidate scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. - Skip token sampling and token-state updates for HSTU requests. - Complete score-only requests in the scheduler when candidate scores are available. - Preserve the one-token early-return behavior required by generative recommendation inputs. ## Test Plan ### 1. Environment Setup The operator is installed inside the following NVIDIA PyTorch container:`nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.06-py3` Install the required system dependency:`apt update && apt install -y libxcb1` ### 2.HSTU Operator Installation and Validation The HSTU attention operator is provided by the NVIDIA `recsys-examples` repository. Clone the recsys-examples repository:`git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/recsys-examples.git && cd recsys-examples/corelib/hstu` For H20 and other Hopper-based devices, enter the corresponding device directory before compiling: `cd hopper` Install the HSTU operator:`Install the HSTU operator:` After the compilation completes successfully, validate the operator installation with: `python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu_op.py` ### 3.vLLM Installation Clone the vLLM repository:`git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git && cd vllm` Install the current vLLM source with CUDA support:`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cuda pip install -v -e .` ### 4. HSTU Model Inference: After the HSTU changes are included in vLLM, run:`python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu.py` This test validates: * HSTU model loading. * HSTU configuration loading. * HSTU model registration. * HSTU attention backend initialization. * HSTU forward execution. * Candidate score extraction. * Candidate ID and score formatting. * Score-only execution without token sampling. * Recommendation request completion. * Model Runner integration. * CUDA Graph execution. ### 5. Model Registry and Hugging Face Loading Run the model registry tests:`pytest -q tests/models/test_registry.py -k HSTUForCausalLM` This validates that: * HSTUForCausalLM is registered. * The HSTU model class can be imported. * Hugging Face model metadata is available. * The HSTU configuration can be loaded. * The vLLM model registry can resolve the HSTU model. ## Test Result ### HSTU Operator The test returned like: ```text Input q shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Output shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Run success ``` ### HSTU Model Inference The test returned candidate IDs and their corresponding ranking scores. A truncated example of the output is: ```text Request 0: 12676:0.6602 47052:0.5078 45082:0.4336 79131:0.3984 34671:0.4844 5695:0.4570 95647:0.1777 60217:0.5273 70284:0.4258 16361:0.4238 Request 1: 8023:0.4863 24460:0.6094 ... ``` Each line follows the format:`Each line follows the format:` The output confirms that HSTU synchronously computes the scores of all candidates for a request and returns the scores through the generative recommendation output path. The test also confirms that: * HSTU outputs are not passed through the standard vocabulary sampler. * No artificial generated token IDs are produced. * Requests complete after candidate scores are returned. * Candidate scores are returned through prompt_logprobs_dict. * Both Model Runner V1 and Model Runner V2 execution paths are supported. * The HSTU attention backend is initialized and executed successfully. * CUDA Graph execution works in the validated CUDA environment. ### Model Registration and Hugging Face Loading The model registration and Hugging Face loading tests passed. HSTUForCausalLM can be resolved and imported through the vLLM model registry, and the HSTU configuration can be loaded from the Hugging Face model configuration. ### Scheduler and Score-Only Execution The scheduler validation passed for score-only recommendation requests. A recommendation request is correctly completed after candidate scores are produced, even when no new_token_ids are returned. The standard token sampling path is skipped for HSTU requests, and no regular language-model token state update is performed. ### Attention Backend Selection When no explicit attention backend is configured, the HSTU model automatically selects HSTU_ATTN. When an explicit attention backend is configured, the user-provided backend remains authoritative and is not overridden by the HSTU automatic selection logic. ### Current Scope and Limitations This initial integration focuses on bringing HSTU into the vLLM model and serving ecosystem. The current implementation assumes: * Prompt lengths are consistent across users. * Candidate lengths are consistent across users. * HSTU and non-HSTU requests are not mixed in the same batch. * Candidate scores are produced during an unchunked prefill. * Pipeline parallelism is not used. * PD-separated HSTU execution is not supported yet. * KV-cache-based or paged HSTU attention is not supported yet. * request_stage = 1 is not supported. * Each recommendation prompt contains at least one context/candidate pair. These limitations can be addressed in follow-up work after the basic HSTU execution path and serving interface are established.

signal.title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Spec Decode] Fix defects on the Kimi-K3 DSpark decode path
signal.text: ## Purpose Two defects on the Kimi-K3 DSpark decode path: 1. The draft model turns cudagraphs off for the whole target model. 2. The multi-token verify is split into one decode per token, which costs two waits on the GPU every forward. ### (1) A draft's attention decides the target's cudagraph mode Before it captures anything, vLLM asks every attention group whether it can be graphed and takes the lowest answer. Groups that belong to a spec-decode draft are asked too: ```python for group in groups: cg_support = builder.get_cudagraph_support(vllm_config, group.kv_cache_spec) if cg_support.value < min_cg_support.value: min_cg_support = cg_support # draft-owned groups included ``` That lowest answer then decides the mode for the *target*: ```python if (cudagraph_mode.decode_mode() == CUDAGraphMode.FULL and uniform_decode_query_len > 1 and min_cg_support.value < AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH.value): cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.NONE # PIECEWISE only if splitting_ops ``` Kimi-K3 meets all three conditions. The target runs AiterMLA, which reports `UNIFORM_BATCH`, and the recipe puts the draft on TritonMLA, which reports `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE`. The draft's answer is the lower one, so **5 draft layers turn cudagraphs off for all 93 target layers**. The draft never needed that help: `init_cudagraph_manager` already looks at its own support level and runs the draft eagerly when it cannot be graphed. **Fix: leave a draft that already checks itself out of the target's decision, and keep a second minimum for the check that still needs every group.** Some drafts do not check themselves. Eagle, mtp and gemma4 (`AutoRegressiveSpeculator`), and `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`, simply use whatever mode the target ended up with. For those the downgrade is doing real work: take it away and they would capture in a mode their own backend cannot run. So the test is a flag on the speculator, not its class: ```python if isinstance(speculator, DraftModelSpeculator) and speculator.sizes_own_cudagraph_mode: return speculator.draft_attn_layer_names ``` `init_attn_backend` now takes two minimums instead of one. The old `min_cg_support` still covers every group, and adaptive verification reads it, so that check is unchanged. The new `graph_min_cg_support` leaves out groups made up entirely of draft layers, and only the cudagraph decision reads it. A group that mixes target and draft layers stays in both. Today only `DFlashSpeculator` and `DSparkSpeculator` set the flag. ### (2) The verify block is split into one decode per token The draft proposes several tokens at once and the target checks them in one block — 8 of them with the `num_speculative_tokens=7` this recipe uses. Each token in the block may only look at the text before it, not after it. In bf16 there is no asm kernel for fewer than 16 heads with more than one query token, so a 12-head rank sends this block to Gluon instead. (With an fp8 cache the q-row fold — folding query rows into the head dimension — does give it an asm kernel, so only bf16 comes here.) The old code faked the "look backward only" rule by issuing one single-token decode per verify token, each with its own slice of the KV list. Building those slices meant rewriting the paged-KV table on every forward, and twice asking the GPU for a value and waiting for it: ```python new_indptr = torch.cat([old_indptr.new_zeros(1), row_len.cumsum(0)]).to(torch.int32) total = int(new_indptr[-1].item()) # host sync ... new_indices = decode.paged_kv_indices[src] # gather over the whole batch mla_gluon(..., page_table=new_indices, seq_info=new_indptr, min_kv_seq_len=int(row_len.min())) # host sync ``` **Fix: give Gluon the whole block at once, which it already accepts, and delete the splitting.** Gluon takes a `[batch, qlen, nhead, dim]` query and applies the backward-only rule itself, so reshaping the query is all that is needed. The page table goes through untouched: ```python q_nope = q_nope.view(batch_size, qlen, num_q_heads, self.kv_lora_rank) q_pe = q_pe.view(batch_size, qlen, num_q_heads, self.qk_rope_head_dim) mla_gluon(..., page_table=decode.paged_kv_indices, seq_info=decode.paged_kv_indptr, min_kv_seq_len=decode.min_kv_seq_len) ``` Net −71 lines in `rocm_aiter_mla.py`. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py # 8, CPU only pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_causal_verify_mask.py # 2, ROCm + AITER ``` The first needs no GPU: it drives `init_attn_backend` with stubs. The second builds the real AITER backend and metadata on device and replaces the Gluon kernel with a spy, so it skips off ROCm. End to end on 8x MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-aa9903490c616dc6871e5acc62cec7bb1e5e9434`, with `/model` = `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` and `/draft` its DSpark draft. Serve flags follow #51253: ```bash vllm serve /model --served-model-name k3 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 --block-size 128 --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --load-format auto --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch \ --compilation-config '{"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/draft", "num_speculative_tokens":7, "attention_backend":"TRITON_MLA"}' \ --port 8000 ``` Run it twice: as written for the fp8 numbers, then with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` dropped for the bf16 numbers. That one flag is what sends the verify to the padded asm decode or to Gluon. ```bash for C in 1 8; do vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --model k3 --tokenizer /model --trust-remote-code --port 8000 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \ --ignore-eos --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $((C == 1 ? 16 : 48)) done lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \ --model_args model=k3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 \ --apply_chat_template --gen_kwargs temperature=0 ``` `--apply_chat_template` and `tokenized_requests=False` are both needed against a chat endpoint. `--gen_kwargs temperature=0` matters because this model's `generation_config.json` sets no temperature, so the default is 1.0 and the run would otherwise be sampled. ## Test Result Unit tests: **10 passed** (8 without a GPU, plus the 2 ROCm ones). For the end-to-end runs the control is this branch's base and the patched side is its head, in the same container, against the same aiter build. Both dtypes are here because the KV cache dtype picks the decode kernel, and only one of them reaches the kernel (2) changes. **fp8 sends the verify to the aiter asm decode**, and that is the production setup — the Kimi-K3 recipe runs `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Both of Gluon's checks turn a quantized cache away, so the verify falls through to the padded asm path: `get_mla_padded_q` pads 12 heads to 16, then `mla_decode_fwd`. That run covers (1), and the asm decode is the kernel that restored capture now has to hold. **bf16 sends the verify to Gluon**, and it is the only setup that does, so it is the one that covers (2). | KV cache | decode kernel | conc. | base | patched | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | fp8 | aiter asm (padded) | 1 | 14.82 tok/s, TPOT 66.09 ms | **67.41 tok/s, TPOT 13.44 ms** | **4.5x** | | fp8 | aiter asm (padded) | 8 | 108.49 tok/s, TPOT 66.72 ms | **291.06 tok/s, TPOT 23.96 ms** | **2.7x** | | bf16 | Gluon | 1 | 15.01 tok/s, TPOT 65.00 ms | **72.22 tok/s, TPOT 12.24 ms** | **4.8x** | | bf16 | Gluon | 8 | 102.57 tok/s, TPOT 68.88 ms | **309.07 tok/s, TPOT 22.37 ms** | **3.0x** | Both control runs report `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, 8 downgrade warnings and 0 captures. Both patched runs report 0 warnings and 8 captures, with the draft eager on all 8 ranks. Accuracy, on the full GSM8K test set (1319 questions), 5-shot, greedy, fp8 KV: | | flexible-extract | strict-match | |---|---|---| | base | 0.9613 ± 0.0053 | 0.9598 ± 0.0054 | | patched | 0.9651 ± 0.0051 | 0.9644 ± 0.0051 | Operator benchmark for (2), against Gluon directly: 12 heads, kv_lora 512, rope 64, bf16 KV. The splitting work is inside the timed region, because the old code did it on every forward. Over batch 8-32, qlen 2-8 and ctx 8k-32k, sending all the tokens at once is **1.52-4.07x faster** — 383.8 us down to 148.0 us at batch 8, qlen 8, ctx 8192. Outputs agree to 1.5e-05. --- Written with AI assistance (Claude Code); the commits carry `Co-authored-by: Claude`. I reviewed every changed line, ran the unit tests and the end-to-end runs above myself, and am responsible for the result.
