signal.title: [Core][DP] Prefix-affinity tie-break in the internal DP load balancer
signal.text: ## Purpose Partial mitigation for #52463: the tie-break rotation added in #47420 degrades prefix-cache locality for multi-turn / shared-prefix traffic under the internal DP load balancer. Consecutive turns of one conversation are tied decisions at low load, so they rotate across DP ranks and every turn misses the prefix its previous turn cached. This PR remembers which engine served a prompt's first-block prefix (LRU of 16k entries, keyed on `cache_salt` + LoRA id + first `block_size` prompt token ids) and prefers that engine **only when scores tie**: - Load-aware decisions unchanged — a lower-scored engine always wins. - Unrelated tied requests still rotate — #47420's fairness fix is preserved (regression-tested). - Explicit `data_parallel_rank` and late-interaction routing bypass affinity, unchanged. - Stale entries from elastic-EP scale-in are discarded; sub-block prompts (which cannot hit the cache) are exempt. ## Test Plan - `tests/v1/engine/test_dp_lb_prefix_affinity.py` — 8 CPU-only unit tests driving `get_core_engine_for_request` directly: session stickiness across turns, tied-unrelated rotation preserved, load-beats-affinity, sub-block exemption, cache_salt separation, explicit-rank bypass, scale-in staleness, LRU bound. - Hardware A/B on 8×H100 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DP=4+EP, `--api-server-count 4`, fp8 KV, aiperf mooncake trace designed for 81.7% prefix reuse — full methodology in #52463): identical runs, only this patch differs. ## Test Result Unit: 8/8 pass (run inside `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image). Hardware A/B (prefix-cache hit rate, per-user output tok/s): | conc | hit rate before → after | tok/s/user before → after | |---:|---|---| | 1 | 37.6% → **61.5%** | 69.5 → 73.6 (+6%) | | 4 | 52.9% → 53.5% | 47.2 → 45.1 (−4%) | | 16 | 20.0% → 21.9% | 16.3 → 12.6 (−23%)* | | 32 | 16.0% → **23.2%** | 9.7 → 9.6 (−1%) | | 64 | 10.9% → 11.1% | 5.0 → 4.8 (−5%) | | 128 | 7.8% → 8.8% | 2.6 → 2.7 (+4%) | \* hit rate unchanged while throughput moved — consistent with run-to-run variance at 160 requests/level, not a cache effect; happy to re-run if reviewers want more samples. **Known limitation (why this is a mitigation, not the full fix):** with `--api-server-count N` each frontend process has its own client and affinity map, and SO_REUSEPORT spreads one session's connections across processes — client-side affinity only sees its own process's requests (this bounds the c=1 recovery at 61.5% vs 81.6% measured on v0.23.0, a pre-#47420 release — a version-level baseline, not a single-commit revert of #47420). The complete fix needs prefix-awareness at a shared layer (DP coordinator or a shared affinity table); #52463 is the home for that design discussion. FIX #52463 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [K3] Optimize K3 recover ssm kernel times
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose PR #51855 added an option to use the ReplaySSM-like recover method. But the new approach, although improving memory footprint and so occupancy, actually hurt run time. The approach should be faster, but it is simple triton vs highly optimized non-triton. Here we make some small tweaks to improve the new output-only verify kernel and the kda and convolution end-of-step commit kernels. ## Test Plan No new tests. This just changes kernel internals and reorders two kernels so are covered by existing tests. We also wrote some one-off checkers that, on fake input, found the output within expected numerical differences (due to changes in associativity) from the old kernels. @benchislett has run e2e tests. ## Test Result @benchislett to add correctness results. On perf, small speed improvements, about half a millisecond per step on batches 1,8,32,and 3ms on batch 128. --- We make a few simple changes that result in a substantial speedup. ### For commit: The biggest is that we change the KDA recover from a backward recurrence to a forward recurrence, which is the bulk of the speedup. This also lets us save register state when operating in ALIGN_MODE (for prefix caching). We reorder the computation to go plan -> kda commit -> conv commit, vs the more natural plan -> conv commit -> kda commit, and then add PDL between kda and conv. This lets us overlap kda with conv, especially as while they both depend on plan, neither depends on the other for inputs and they have separate outputs. And as kda blocks are longer-tailed the re-reordering is beneficial. However, because commit does not run with cuda graphs, the PDL could hurt more in host overhead than it helps, so we do not enable it. Lastly, for both kernels we retune num-warps and the number of output elements each handles. ALIGNED_MODE on and off want slightly different values. PDL does not impact the preferred values. To guide optimization we wrote a microbenchmark (not submitted) and optimized for B300, matching the original PRs experiment. We can only match the original PR numbers if we assume that the original PR was actually run with the kernels in unaligned mode. Our microbenchmark assumes TP=8, times the span from plan start to end of the second of conv or kda commit, simulates cold and hot L2 cache inputs, and runs with a cuda graph and CUPTI timing. Although commit does not run under a cuda graph, using one is the best way to get consistent, low-noise timings. For ease of experimentation we had all requests uniform in terms of # accepted (using 5 below, slightly higher than the 4.2 average in the e2e nsys measurements in the original PR), and also uniform in bondary behavior. We observed runtime affine in # accepted, as expected (not shown). We ran in either unaligned, aligned with no boundary crossed, or aligned with boundary crossed at the second token. The latter case would never happen at larger batches, we would expect a mix of aligned and unaligned, but it shows the costs. We get about 2x speedup across batches and align modes, more at the more production relevant aligned but no boundary. Note due to how vLLM groups KDA layers that share block tables, the commit kernels (plan, commit kda, compact conv, etc.) are launched on 5 or 4 layers at a time, not all 69 as you'd hope. I have a follow-on commit that groups them together which helps time further, especially as nsys shows the lack of cuda graphs causes substantial gaps at smaller batches. Results below, times are plan -> kda commit -> conv compact span. Small batch, with only 5 layers per invocation, is largely launch bound and so not much improvement is possible, and even larger batches there is not that much work. You can see more than 2x speedup at larger batches. Experimenting with the kernels at 69 layers at a time, we found grouping would improve total time for all layers by 3x for batch 1, 1.2x at batch 32, and 1.05x at batch 256 (not shown). Mode | B1 | B32 | B256 | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Unaligned | 13.22 → 12.22 (1.08x) | 110.63 → 64.48 (1.72x) | 827.68 → 440.01 (1.88x) | | Aligned, no boundary | 14.11 → 13.07 (1.08x) | 160.10 → 76.49 (2.09x) | 1319.62 → 551.87 (2.39x) | | Aligned, boundary at accepted token 2 | 14.31 → 13.74 (1.04x) | 168.66 → 87.14 (1.94x) | 1421.05 → 646.39 (2.20x) | ### For verify: Small changes here but surprisingly worth a lot. We had a similar microbenchmark as above but for verify. PDL surprisingly hurts us, so we report only the kernel time, not the span, although we ran and timed the conv1d -> verify span. We hoisted dt_bias out of the loop, which resulted in enough code gen change to be worth a win. Then we retuned the value-slice and num_warp params. We found value-slice should vary with batch size, which is typical as smaller value slices are less efficient but better saturate the machine if there isn't enough work. And that num-warps should be 1 everywhere. Also added some cache hints as state and V are not shared across blocks (value slicing) but everything else is. Here are timings, again B300, TP=8, with T=8 and gate_lower_bound=5.0: | Batch | Old | New | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 13.79 µs | 8.98 µs | 1.54× | | 2 | 13.95 µs | 9.38 µs | 1.49× | | 4 | 14.24 µs | 10.08 µs | 1.41× | | 8 | 15.46 µs | 13.22 µs | 1.17× | | 16 | 27.46 µs | 18.98 µs | 1.45× | | 32 | 41.55 µs | 34.40 µs | 1.21× | | 64 | 79.49 µs | 63.49 µs | 1.25× | | 128 | 147.89 µs | 111.50 µs | 1.33× | | 256 | 306.19 µs | 233.17 µs | 1.31× | | 512 | 632.17 µs | 494.05 µs | 1.28× | Surprises: Passing gate lower bound does change the results a little. As noted above, PDL does not help. A tiny bit in some places but regresses enough others that I left it off, vs making it a heuristic. I also spent a while trying to get a good result with a full chunk/prefill-style UT transform, in Triton, having had good results with that for Mamba-2 layers. Whether due to the per-channel decay (unlikely) or the triangular inverse (likely), I found many bad ways to write it, and with a lot of work I got a version that (for T=8) only tied the recurrence above. I expected big wins, but Triton limitations make it quite challenging. I'm sure in CuTe it'd be very fast. As is, it would have the cost and benefit that the runtime would be independent of T. But as it is much more complicated, and as T=8 is probably more of an upper than lower bound for draft_length + 1, better to stick with the recurrence. AI Declaration: AI assisted in the writing of this code, but I have reviewed every line. Full disclosure, I reviewed all the code in the PR, but the one-off microbenchmarks and such I did not look at too carefully. <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details> **BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

signal.title: [MoE] Generalize masked activation for padded layouts
signal.text: ## Summary - add one shared count-aware MoE activation entry point for a flat valid prefix (`[T, D]`) and per-expert valid prefixes (`[E, T, D]`) - support the gated and non-gated activation set explicitly, with a fail-closed `NotImplementedError` when a future activation lacks a masked implementation - route Humming, batched Triton, and batched Marlin through `ApplyMoEActivationConfig` instead of backend-specific SITU/clamped-SiLU branches - select Humming GEMM layout automatically: `indexed` without EP, `grouped_contiguous` with EP, and `grouped_masked` for batched experts; environment overrides remain available but are validated choices - pass DeepEP v2's cudagraph valid-prefix metadata into Humming so activation skips padded receive rows - validate padded/invalid expert IDs before indexing `expert_map` in the Humming permute path ## Why DeepEP v1 and v2 expose different padded layouts. Legacy/batched execution has one valid prefix per expert, while DeepEP v2 has one valid prefix in a flat cudagraph receive buffer. Backend-specific activation branches had diverged and made SITU especially expensive in Kimi K3. The shared op makes the layout contract explicit and specializes the flat versus batched branch at compile time. The final Kimi investigation also found a correctness issue before activation: DeepEP v2 uses `-1` for padding, but Humming's permute preprocessing read `expert_map[topk_id]` before checking the ID. Invalid IDs now become the expert sentinel before any map access. The regression covers both `-1` and a positive out-of-range ID. ## Model validation ### DeepSeek-V4 Flash Tested `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with automatic Humming selection and no `VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE` override: - DP=1, no DeepEP, Humming `indexed`, eager GSM8K 100: **0.96 accuracy**, **0 invalid** - DP=2 / EP=2, DeepEP v2, Humming `grouped_contiguous`, eager GSM8K 100: **0.95 accuracy**, **0 invalid** The close DP1/DP2 scores provide a model-level control for the new DeepEP v2 layout. A separate two-GPU correctness test covers the DSV4 topology (256 experts, top-k 6, K=4096, N=2048, MXFP4/BF16) including an idle DP rank. ### Kimi K3 Served `mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75` on four B300 GPUs with: ```bash chg run -g=4 -- vllm serve mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75 \ --tokenizer-mode kimi_k3 --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 \ --language-model-only \ --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \ --all2all-backend deepep_v2 --moe-backend humming \ --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \ --max-num-seqs 16 ``` - DP=4 / EP=4 selected `DeepEPV2All2AllManager` and Humming `grouped_contiguous` automatically - no Humming GEMM environment override was set - the default non-eager server captured **7 PIECEWISE + 5 FULL** breakable CUDA graphs; this model's V2 runner reports compilation mode `NONE`, so this is CUDA-graph rather than TorchInductor validation - a deterministic arithmetic request returned a coherent, correct answer (42) Before the invalid-ID guard, the same run emitted repeated `@` tokens; GSM8K 100 was 0% accurate with 100% invalid responses and every request exhausted 256 tokens. After the guard, chat-mode GSM8K 100 was **15% accurate / 33% invalid** with 18,611 output tokens. Inspection showed the remaining invalid responses were mostly coherent but unfinished reasoning from this 75%-pruned checkpoint; a 10-question diagnostic at 1,024 tokens improved to 30% / 20% invalid. I do not treat the latter small sample as a model-quality result, but the disappearance of repeated-token corruption plus the focused native regression isolates the kernel fix. Kimi required the 512-token batch cap on four B300s. A 2,048-token cap OOMed because DeepEP v2's worst-case receive/permute scratch must cover `max_tokens * dp_size * topk` rows. ## Coverage and intentional exclusions - flat masked activation: DeepEP v2 cudagraph padding - batched masked activation: Marlin, batched Triton, and Humming `grouped_masked` GPU correctness tests - standard unmasked activation: unchanged shared `apply_moe_activation` path - DeepEP low-latency + Humming: intentionally rejected with a clear reason because low-latency dispatch does not support Humming's deferred input quantization contract The full-model DSV4 and Kimi runs exercise DeepEP v2 `grouped_contiguous`. There is no fresh full-model run of `BatchedExperts -> grouped_masked` after the final rebase; that layout is covered at the kernel/backend-test level. Legacy DeepEP v1 was tested earlier during development, while this final validation round focused on v2 because it is the important new layout. ## Tests ```bash chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/kernels/core/test_activation.py -k masked_moe_activation -q # 53 passed, 256 deselected chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py::test_moe_permute_ignores_invalid_expert_ids_with_scratch \ -q -s # 1 passed chg run -g=2 -- env EP_DISABLE_GIN=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py::test_deep_ep_v2_humming_dsv4_expert_topology \ -q -s # 1 passed ``` Also completed: - focused DeepEP v2 Humming correctness/cudagraph suite - full native extension build: **428/428 targets built and linked** - commit hooks: Ruff check/format, clang-format, typos, mypy, SPDX/config/import checks - `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check` DeepEP v2 model tests used an isolated user-space environment with NCCL 2.30.7 and NVSHMEM 3.3.24 plus `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`; no sudo was required. The shared development `.venv` currently has NCCL 2.29.7, so its automatic DeepEP refresh cannot compile v2 GIN types. This is an environment-version limitation, not a vLLM native-extension failure. ## Duplicate-work check Open-PR searches for `masked MoE activation Humming`, `SITU Humming`, and `apply_moe_activation batched` found only this PR, so this does not duplicate another open change. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to develop and test this change. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines, understands the implementation and validation, and is responsible for defending the change end to end.

signal.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Support PCP producers
signal.text: ## Purpose Support NIXL P/D disaggregation when the producer uses prefill context parallelism (PCP) and decode context parallelism (DCP) is disabled on both sides. PCP expands the worker world without increasing the KV-cache shard count, so every PCP rank holds an equivalent KV replica. NIXL should publish and wait for one replica instead of treating all PCP workers as distinct KV shards. This change: - records each NIXL worker's PCP rank; - publishes handshake metadata only from PCP rank zero on a producer; - forwards producer send completions only from PCP rank zero; - aggregates PCP producer completions over `TP * PP`; and - rejects PCP consumers, `kv_both`, and combined PCP+DCP configurations. It does not change the NIXL handshake protocol, worker addressing, transfer topology, KV layout, or token mapping. ## Scope and related work This PR is intentionally limited to `DCP=1` on both producer and consumer. It does not enable consumer-side PCP or combined PCP+DCP layouts. PR #50611 owns NIXL DCP support and its shard-routing/configuration changes. This PR is complementary: it only selects a canonical replica along the PCP axis when no DCP sharding exists. The duplicate-work searches for `NIXL PCP`, `prefill context parallel NIXL`, and `PCP producer KV connector` found #38433, #45340, #49109, #49342, and #50611. None implements this PCP-only NIXL replica selection on current main: - #50611 handles DCP sharding and currently requires PCP to be disabled. - #45340 handles CP-scaled scheduler block accounting. - #49109 is Mooncake-specific. - #49342 is the older mixed PCP+DCP version of this work and is superseded by this smaller PR. ## Tests ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \ -k "not abort_timeout_on_prefiller and not register_kv_caches and not reqs_to_send_deadline_rebased_to_worker_clock" \ -q # 144 passed, 7 deselected ``` ```bash .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files <changed files> # passed ``` Four-GPU P/D validation on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`: - Producer: `TP=1, PCP=2, DCP=1, EP=2` - Consumer: `TP=2, PCP=1, DCP=1, EP=2` - NIXL transport: local UCX TCP/CUDA IPC - Final-commit smoke: four prompts passed, including a long multi-block transfer - GSM8K: 1,319 questions, 5-shot, accuracy `0.636846`, invalid rate `0.000758` (159,800 output tokens) ```bash chg run -g 4 --timeout 45m -- env \ MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \ GSM8K_QUESTIONS=1319 GSM8K_CONCURRENCY=64 \ bash ./pd_test.sh pcp2-nodcp-gsm8k \ '--tensor-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-batched-tokens 2048' \ '--tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel' ``` ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, testing, and drafting this PR. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line and understanding and defending the change end-to-end.

signal.title: [Kernel][ROCm] Cover OCP MX MoE emulation in the mxfp4 oracle test
signal.text: ## Purpose `test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle` covers the Triton and AITER mxfp4 MoE backends but never `Mxfp4MoeBackend.EMULATION` — which is what ROCm parts *without* native MX support actually run. This PR adds coverage for it, one row per activation scheme the backend supports: - `w_mxfp4_a_mxfp4` (`EMULATION`) - `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` (`EMULATION_A_FP8`) Both new rows run on **gfx942**. The four existing AITER rows all require gfx950, so on MI300-class hardware this test previously exercised only the two Triton rows. > [!NOTE] > **The scope of this PR changed since it was opened, and this description has been rewritten to match.** > It originally also carried a source fix in `ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py` and `triton_moe.py` for two crashes on the `w_mxfp4_a_fp8` emulation path. #46142 (merged 2026-06-23) fixed those, so the source changes are gone and **this PR is now test-only**. The previous description described that fix and no longer applied. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -q \ --deselect tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py::test_mxfp4_loading_and_execution_moe ``` ## Test Result Coming soon. ======================================= Original PR body (staled, for ones interested in the history) ======================================= ## Purpose Running an OCP MX MoE model with **fp8 activations** (e.g. `w_mxfp4_a_fp8`) through the **emulation** backend crashes on the first forward pass. There are **two** distinct crashes on this path, one per GEMM: 1. **GEMM1 (input activation):** `AssertionError: assert A_scale is None` in the bf16 Triton MoE kernel — the static fp8 activation scale leaks in from the quant config. 2. **GEMM2 (intermediate activation):** `NotImplementedError: ... quant_dtype='mxfp8' MOE quantization emulation` — the intermediate quantize call is missing the OCP MX scheme, so it routes to the unsupported `mxfp8` emulation branch instead of the fp8 QDQ branch. The emulation experts dequantize the MXFP4/MXFP6 weights to bf16 and run the plain bf16 Triton MoE, which needs no scales. This PR makes both GEMMs consistent: it nulls the activation scales in the emulation experts, and threads `ocp_mx_scheme` into the intermediate-activation quantize so the fp8 fake-QDQ path is used end to end. **Two files change:** - `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py` (GEMM1) - `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py` (GEMM2) ### Environment - ROCm, MI325 - Runtime base image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.20.0` - Model: `amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8` - MXFP4 **emulation** MoE backend `--moe-backend emulation` ### Traceback **Crash 1 — GEMM1, `assert A_scale is None`**: ``` File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 396, in determine_available_memory self.model_runner.profile_run() ... File ".../vllm/model_executor/models/gpt_oss.py", line 215, in forward x = self.experts(hidden_states=x, router_logits=g)[:, : self.hidden_size] ... File ".../fused_moe/experts/ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py", line 179, in apply super().apply(...) File ".../fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py", line 250, in apply invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel(...) File ".../fused_moe/fused_moe.py", line 746, in invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel assert A_scale is None AssertionError ``` **Crash 2 — GEMM2, `NotImplementedError` mxfp8**: ``` File ".../fused_moe/experts/ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py", line 179, in apply super().apply(...) File ".../fused_moe/experts/triton_moe.py", line 322, in apply qintermediate_cache2, a2q_scale = moe_kernel_quantize_input(...) File ".../fused_moe/utils.py", line 314, in moe_kernel_quantize_input raise NotImplementedError( NotImplementedError: moe_kernel_quantize_input does not support quant_dtype='mxfp8' MOE quantization emulation. Please open an issue. ``` ## Fix ### File 1 — `ocp_mx_emulation_moe.py`: null activation scales in `__init__` Mirror the weight-scale handling. Activations are fake-QDQ'd to bf16 in `apply`, so no activation scale should reach the bf16 kernel. ### File 2 — `triton_moe.py`: pass `ocp_mx_scheme` to the intermediate quantize Thread the scheme into the GEMM2 input quantize, matching the GEMM1/input QDQ already done in the emulation experts. For `a_fp8` this routes to the fp8 fake-QDQ branch (returns bf16, scale `None`); for `a_mxfp4` it hits the no-op branch and proceeds to the identical `mxfp4` quantize (no change); for non-OCP configs `ocp_mx_scheme` is `None` and behavior is unchanged. ## Test Plan Integration smoke test — on ROCm, emulation backend, an `a_fp8` model. ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \ python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --moe-backend emulation \ --trust-remote-code ``` ## Test Result - Before: crashes during profile run — first at `fused_moe.py:746` (`assert A_scale is None`), then after nulling the activation scales, at `utils.py:314` (`NotImplementedError: ... quant_dtype='mxfp8'`). Engine init fails before any forward completes. - After: both GEMMs run the bf16 path with the fp8 activations fake-QDQ'd; profiling and startup complete, and the model serves correctly. **gsm8k_platinum** (5-shot) on the served model: | filter | metric | value | |---|---|---| | flexible-extract | exact_match | **0.9413 ± 0.0068** | | strict-match | exact_match | 0.1919 ± 0.0113 | --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [CI] Fix MultiConnector accuracy test lifecycle
signal.text: AMD CI build [#12250](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12250#01a01b85-79bd-4cb8-9287-e5af327ff2ca) exposed a latent lifecycle race between the sequential normal and cross-layer test layouts. The first layout left its proxy on port 8192 while the API servers were still shutting down, so the next layout reused stale processes and the replacement proxy failed to bind. Readiness also used `curl -s` against a POST-only endpoint, allowing an HTTP 405 response to count as success. - Launch and track each API server and proxy in a harness-owned process group. - Require the launched process to remain alive and probe real `/health` and `/healthcheck` endpoints with HTTP failure handling. - Gracefully terminate and reap only owned process leaders and groups, with a 30-second timeout before forced cleanup. - Wait for ROCm GPU memory to settle before starting the next layout.

signal.title: [ROCm][CI] Stabilize MI355 FlyDSL MoE accuracy test
signal.text: This PR stabilizes the two MI355 FlyDSL W4A16 MoE cases that failed in [AMD CI build 12250](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12250/list). The test was introduced in #44400, and its test, kernel, and conversion code are unchanged between recent passing and failing builds; #41100 changed test collection and exposed the test's dependence on inherited RNG state. The failures contained only a few BF16 accumulation outliers among as many as 117 million output values, so a strict `torch.allclose` made the largest cases brittle. This change seeds the inputs and checks both the mismatch rate and worst normalized error, retaining sensitivity to broad or severe accuracy regressions. - Fix: Seed every parameterized case, require at least 99.999% of values to satisfy the original `atol=0.5, rtol=0.1` tolerance, and bound every permitted outlier to 3x its elementwise tolerance. - Repeated validation: 30/30 independent full-file runs passed across two gfx950 MI355 GPUs, for 900/900 collected test cases. - Input sweep: 30 distinct seeds passed both formerly failing shapes in fresh processes across two additional MI355 GPUs, for 60/60 exact-shape runs. - Control: With the original unseeded strict assertion restored, the two cases failed in 3/10 fresh processes; deterministic diagnostics observed only 0-3 mismatches out of 117,440,512 values, with a worst error of 1.086x the original elementwise tolerance.

signal.title: [ROCm][CI] Stabilize MI355 FusedMoE test group
signal.text: This PR addresses the three MI355 FusedMoE failures reported by [AMD CI build 12250](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12250/list). The MI355 group was introduced by #41100 and exposed a B200-only DeepEP cleanup that #35077 had broadened to every platform, causing rocSHMEM destroy/reinitialize failures on MI355. The EPLB case separately failed after repeatedly registering NIXL memory while iterating the broad layer matrix. This change restores the CUDA SM100-only DeepEP cleanup and selects Gloo only for gfx950 EPLB in this test, while preserving the layer coverage and dedicated NIXL coverage. - DeepEP fix: Destroy the cached DeepEP all-to-all manager only on CUDA devices with compute capability 10, restoring the original B200 scope and preventing unsupported rocSHMEM reinitialization on MI355. - EPLB fix: Use `torch_gloo` only when this test has EPLB enabled on gfx950; no MI355 layer configurations are skipped, and dedicated EPLB execution tests retain NIXL coverage. - Repeated validation: The formerly failing allgather/EPLB node passed 10/10 independent runs on MI355, exercising all 96 internal configurations per run for 960/960 total passes.

signal.title: [Bugfix] ExampleConnector: cap external match at the saved token count
signal.text: A store request is only recorded on its first scheduling step (`build_connector_meta` only inspects `scheduled_new_reqs`), so under chunked prefill the connector persists just the blocks allocated by that step. `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, however, claims `align_to_block_size(len(prompt) - 1)` for any prompt whose folder exists, based on folder existence alone. A consumer instance sharing the storage path then marks tokens as computed whose KV was never saved, and `start_load_kv` fails on the shape mismatch between the saved tensor and the request's slot mapping. Cap the claimed match at the token count actually present in the saved files (read from one layer file's safetensors header, which loads no tensor data), and truncate the worker-side injection to the same bound so the scheduler computes the uncovered tail locally. Fixes #16928 ## Purpose This PR resolves a critical shape mismatch and crash in the disaggregated KV-transfer `ExampleConnector` under chunked prefilling configurations. ### Why this happens: 1. **Producer Side (Partial Save):** Under chunked prefilling, a store request is only registered on its very first scheduling step since `build_connector_meta` only inspects `scheduled_new_reqs`. Consequently, only the blocks computed in that first chunk are written to disk. 2. **Consumer Side (False Full Claim):** On the consumer (receiver) side, `get_num_new_matched_tokens` checked folder existence and claimed a match for the entire aligned prompt. 3. **The Crash:** The consumer worker attempted to load the partial safetensors file and inject it into the full-size slot mapping, resulting in a PyTorch runtime shape mismatch / index error. ### The Fix: * **Cap Claims:** We cap the consumer's matched token count at the count actually present in the saved safetensors files (read efficiently from one layer file's JSON header via `safetensors.safe_open` with zero tensor-loading overhead). * **Tail Computation:** This ensures the consumer scheduler knows only a prefix exists, allowing it to schedule the remaining uncovered tail of the prompt for local computation. * **Truncate Injection:** Slicing is introduced in worker-side injection to match the slot mapping to the exact block-aligned count. ### Duplicate-PR Check: * There are no other open PRs addressing this specific chunked prefill mismatch in the v1 `ExampleConnector`. This is a unique and targeted fix. ## Test Plan To verify this fix and ensure no regressions are introduced, run both the newly added unit tests (specifically simulating the chunked-prefill/partial-save scenario) and the existing `ExampleConnector` tests. ### Test Commands: ```bash # Activate your environment source .venv/bin/activate # 1. Run the new unit tests for partial saves .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector_partial_save.py -v # 2. Run the existing example connector tests to prevent regression .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector.py -v ``` ## Test Result All tests pass successfully with the fix applied: ```text ============================= test session starts ============================== platform linux -- Python 3.12.3, pytest-8.3.2, pluggy-1.5.0 -- /home/user/vllm/.venv/bin/python cachedir: .pytest_cache rootdir: /home/user/vllm collected 5 items tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector_partial_save.py::test_no_match_without_saved_files PASSED [ 20%] tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector_partial_save.py::test_full_save_claims_aligned_prefix PASSED [ 40%] tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector_partial_save.py::test_partial_save_caps_claim PASSED [ 60%] tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector_partial_save.py::test_unaligned_partial_save_rounds_down PASSED [ 80%] tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_example_connector_partial_save.py::test_folder_without_layer_files_claims_nothing PASSED [100%] ============================== 5 passed in 0.42s =============================== ``` ### Model Evaluation: * **Not Applicable:** This change is strictly restricted to the `ExampleConnector` infrastructure and disaggregated prefill utilities. It does not affect model architectures, neural weights, or output generation accuracy. --- *AI assistance was used to analyze the codebase and assist in drafting this PR description and testing strategy.* Co-authored-by: Gemini CLI <gemini-cli@google.com> Signed-off-by: Shimi Bandiel <shimib@google.com>

signal.title: fix: populate draft model quant mapping and guard DFlash fused KV
signal.text: Resolves #53116 ## Purpose This PR addresses two related issues when loading quantized draft models for speculative decoding: 1. **Missing Mapping Config:** The `get_draft_quant_config` function was returning the quantization config without routing it through `configure_quant_config`. As a result, the `packed_modules_mapping` remained empty, preventing fused projections (like `gate_up_proj`) from matching correctly and leaving them unquantized. This PR routes the config through `configure_quant_config` if a draft model architecture is identified. 2. **DFlash Fused KV Crash:** Even with the mapping fixed, `DFlashQwen3Model._build_context_kv_buffers` natively reads `qkv_proj.weight` directly. For quantized models, the data type differs and the weight may be transposed, causing a crash during the slice operation. This PR adds an explicit guard that raises a clear `NotImplementedError` if the parameter dtype differs from the norm dtype, rather than allowing a cryptic PyTorch shape/dtype crash mid-forward. ## Test Plan - Added `tests/spec_decode/test_draft_quant_config.py` with two unit tests: - `test_get_draft_quant_config_populates_packed_modules`: Verifies the quant config is properly configured with the draft model class. - `test_dflash_build_context_kv_buffers_raises_on_quantized_dtype`: Verifies the `NotImplementedError` is cleanly raised when weight and norm dtypes mismatch. - Command to run: `pytest tests/spec_decode/test_draft_quant_config.py -v` ## Test Result - Unit tests pass successfully. - Quantized draft models now correctly receive their module mappings, and `DFlashQwen3Model` cleanly rejects incompatible quantized weights at buffer-build time. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bug][Spec Decode]: DFlash fused-KV projection calls F.linear on a sliced qkv_proj weight — breaks (and can silently corrupt) any weight-quantized drafter
signal.text: ### Your current environment - vLLM **0.26.0** (`vllm/vllm-openai:latest-aarch64`), also verified against current `main` by reading the source (see below) - NVIDIA **GB10 / DGX Spark**, sm_121a, CUDA 13.2, aarch64, 128 GB unified memory - Target: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (compressed-tensors NVFP4) - Drafter: `z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash`, quantized offline to FP8 (E4M3, per-tensor `weight_scale`, `activation_scheme: dynamic`) ### 🐛 Describe the bug DFlash speculative decoding cannot be used with a **weight-quantized drafter**. Serving a DFlash drafter that carries any weight-quantization config fails at engine init: ``` File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py", line 514, in <...> all_kv_flat = F.linear( ^^^^^^^^^ RuntimeError: expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype, but got: c10::BFloat16 != c10::Float8_e4m3fn ``` **Root cause.** `Qwen3DFlash` builds a fused KV GEMM by *slicing the merged `qkv_proj` weight tensor* and applying it with a raw `torch.nn.functional.linear`, which bypasses the module's quantization method entirely. On current `main`: ```python # vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py:448-449 kv_weights = [a.qkv_proj.weight[a.q_size :] for a in layers_attn] self._fused_kv_weight = torch.cat(kv_weights, dim=0) # vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py:521-522 all_kv_flat = F.linear( normed_context_states, self._fused_kv_weight, self._fused_kv_bias ) ``` When `qkv_proj` is a quantized `Linear`, `.weight` is the packed/quantized tensor, so `F.linear` is being handed something it cannot consume. **This is broader than the FP8 case that surfaced it, and it is a correctness hazard, not only a crash.** `.weight` is the packed tensor for *any* weight-only scheme (fp8, compressed-tensors, AWQ, GPTQ, …). Where the dtypes happen to line up rather than raise, this path silently omits `weight_scale` and produces **numerically wrong drafts** — which speculative decoding will not surface as an error, only as degraded acceptance. Note this is **not** a duplicate of #42588: that one was ROCm-specific, in `combine_hidden_states` (the `fc` layer), and was caused by *activations* being promoted to fp32; it was fixed by #42646. This one is on CUDA, in the fused-KV path, and is caused by the *weight* being quantized. ### Suggested fix Either de-quantize when building the buffer — apply the module's `weight_scale` and cast to the activation dtype in `_build_fused_kv_buffers` — or, preferably, route the fused KV projection through the module's quantization method instead of calling `F.linear` on a raw weight. ### Secondary observation (possibly a separate bug) Trying to exempt the module via the drafter checkpoint's `quantization_config.ignored_layers` did **not** take effect. I listed both `layers.{N}.self_attn.qkv_proj` and `model.layers.{N}.self_attn.qkv_proj` and the engine still quantized it and still crashed at the same line. Also worth noting for anyone hitting this: with `quant_method: fp8` and no `ignored_layers`, vLLM quantizes *every* `Linear` **online at load**, so simply leaving q/k/v as BF16 tensors in the checkpoint does not avoid the crash. ### Reproduce 1. Quantize `z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash` to FP8 (E4M3 weights + per-tensor `weight_scale`) and write a `quantization_config` of `{"quant_method": "fp8", "activation_scheme": "dynamic"}` into its `config.json`. 2. Serve any Qwen3.6-35B-A3B target with that drafter: ``` --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"<fp8-drafter-path>","num_speculative_tokens":6}' ``` 3. Engine init fails with the traceback above. ### Why it matters On a bandwidth-bound machine the drafter is read every speculative cycle. For this pairing the BF16 drafter is 0.772 GB of a ~4.35 GB cycle, so quantizing it is a straightforward win that is currently unavailable.

signal.title: Revert compile-cache device index regression on CPU
signal.text: ## Why This reverts #38962 because its unconditional `torch.accelerator.current_device_index()` calls break CPU-only execution before engine startup: ``` RuntimeError: Cannot access accelerator device when none is available. ``` The merged commit `6dcc5d7c` is the first affected main commit. Main Buildkite #85059 fails this way across multiple CPU suites and independent hosts. CPU Distributed PP+TP reproduced the identical startup failure on both retry hosts. Later main builds #85065 and #85078 independently reproduced the same CPU Language Generation signature. The exact PR-head Buildkite #77551 selected CPU Language Generation and failed the same accelerator-device lookup signature. The other affected CPU jobs were blocked, so the exact CI was red rather than passing or merely unselected. ## Duplicate-work check Searched open PRs for `38962`, `compile cache device index CPU accelerator`, and the exact `Cannot access accelerator device when none is available` signature. No existing revert or equivalent fix was found. Open #41688 concerns CPU-only shutdown cleanup and does not address these compile-cache paths. ## Validation - `git diff --cached --check` before commit - Verified the staged revert patch applies cleanly in reverse - This commit is the exact inverse of merge commit `6dcc5d7caeffa7f69239153b171249e867ca6050` - GitHub `pre-commit` passed at the exact signed head - Exact CPU Language Generation passed in Buildkite #85071 on `cpu-aicf-jf-cicd-08` (40m, exit 0), directly converting the repeated main/culprit-head signature to green - Exact CPU Distributed PP+TP passed in Buildkite #85086 on `cpu-aicf-jf-cicd-02` (8m38s, exit 0; 20/20 benchmark requests succeeded and `failed=0`) `pre-commit` is not installed in this emergency worktree, so repository hooks were not run locally. Exact Buildkite jobs are the merge gate. No model evaluation is applicable because this is an emergency rollback restoring CPU startup behavior present immediately before the breaking merge. ## Merge gate Exact pre-merge CPU validation is complete. Keep this draft until human line-by-line review; after merge, require exact post-merge main CPU confirmation before closing the incident. The incident remains open after pre-merge validation and closes only after merge plus exact post-merge main CPU confirmation. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to investigate the CI failure, prepare the revert, and draft this PR. The human submitter must review every changed line and can explain and defend the change end-to-end.

signal.text: ## Purpose Target model e.g. http://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash Fix FP8 block-linear kernel selection for E8M0 weight scales. The FP8 and Quark W8A8 FP8 paths now advertise E8M0 scale storage through `kFp8Static128BlockE8M0Sym`, so selection can reject backends that cannot consume it. This specifically fixes incorrect E8M0 handling in: - `HummingFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`: currently wrong `self.config.weight_quant_key.scale.dtype`: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/humming.py#L50-L60 - `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`: CUTLASS consumes block scales as float32 and must reject E8M0 storage: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_blockwise_sm90_fp8_dispatch.cuh#L56. The SM90 callsite is https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_blockwise_sm90_fp8.cu#L13-L14, which is selected by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/scaled_mm_c3x_sm90.cu#L17-L20. The top-level CUTLASS dispatcher calls the latter at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/scaled_mm_entry.cu#L236-L241. SM100 and SM120 use the same float32 block-scale type: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_blockwise_sm100_fp8_dispatch.cuh#L57 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_blockwise_sm120_fp8_dispatch.cuh#L58, respectively. - `CPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`: forwards the block scale directly to the CPU op, which requires float32 scales: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cpu.py#L300-L316 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/gemm_fp8.cpp#L1150 - `XPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`: forwards its 128x128 block scale to `fp8_gemm` without E8M0 decoding: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py#L246-L253 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2740c817ffbe6c1980507c7cbd27b4bc94d2c856/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py#L112-L118 - `BlockWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`: `_scaled_mm` Supported | [Upcasts E8M0 scales before its GEMM path](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/b12x.py#L101-L119). | | `HummingFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` | Supported | [Maps E8M0 to `torch.float8_e8m0fnu`](https://github.com/inclusionAI/humming/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/humming/dtypes.py#L200-L206). | | `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` | Supported | [Dispatches FP8 weights with E8M0 scales to the E8M0 scale type](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/marlin/marlin.cu#L601-L615). | | `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` | Unsupported | [CUTLASS block kernels consume scale storage as float32](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_blockwise_sm90_fp8_dispatch.cuh#L56), so E8M0 scales are rejected during selection. | | `CPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` | Unsupported | [The CPU FP8 op requires float32 scales](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/gemm_fp8.cpp#L1150). | | `XPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` | Unsupported | [Forwards the 128x128 block scale to `fp8_gemm` without E8M0 decoding](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py#L286-L290). | | `BlockWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` | Unsupported | [Documents float32 block scales and forwards them directly to `torch._scaled_mm`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/pytorch.py#L261-L270). | | CUDA `TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` | Unsupported | [States that Triton cannot bind E8M0 scales directly, but only decodes them on ROCm/XPU](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ee84d3c5207bd59faa53e19e60fa82e34961444/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py#L920-L927). | This change applies to `Fp8LinearMethod`, `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` only as: - `Fp8PerBlockOnlineLinearMethod`, - `FBGEMMFp8LinearMethod`, - `ModelOptFp8PbWoLinearMethod`, - `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` do NOT support e8m0 scale dtype. CUDA 13.0 + H100 rejects e8m0 scales: ```python import torch def run(scale_b: torch.Tensor) -> None: m, k, n = 4, 128, 128 a = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) b = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).to( torch.float8_e4m3fn).t() scale_a = torch.ones((m, k // 128), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) output = torch._scaled_mm(a, b, scale_a=scale_a, scale_b=scale_b, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16) if isinstance(output, tuple): output = output[0] print(f"scale_b={scale_b.dtype}: succeeded, output={output.dtype} {tuple(output.shape)}") if not torch.cuda.is_available(): raise RuntimeError("CUDA is required") print(f"torch={torch.__version__}") print(f"cuda={torch.version.cuda}") print(f"device={torch.cuda.get_device_name()}") run(torch.ones((1, 1), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)) run(torch.ones((1, 1), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float8_e8m0fnu)) ``` gives `For BlockWise 128x128 scaling, a and b should be float8, scales should be float, scale_a should be (1, 1) and scale_b should be (1, 1), and both should be near-inner-dim-major (with 16-byte aligned strides).` ## Test Plan - `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_kernel_selection.py` ## Test Results `14 passed, 14 warnings in 4.92s`

signal.title: [Spec Decode] Fix EAGLE3 MRoPE decode-step position computation to use per-request delta
signal.text: ## Purpose In the EAGLE3 proposer, `_update_positions_dependent_metadata` computes MRoPE decode-step positions by replicating dimension 0 into dims 1 and 2: ```python self.mrope_positions[1:, :batch_size] = self.mrope_positions[0, :batch_size] ``` The target model uses a per-request `mrope_position_delta` in `MRotaryEmbedding.get_next_input_positions_tensor` to compute decode positions as `delta + context_len`, writing the same value to all 3 dims. For standard text decode tokens this is numerically equivalent to dim-replication, so acceptance rate is unaffected in the common case. However, when multimodal pruning is enabled, `recompute_mrope_positions` can update `req_state.mrope_position_delta` mid-request. `_gather_mm_embeddings` is called from within the speculative decode path, so a pruning event during spec decode causes the proposer's positions to advance from a stale base rather than the updated delta — a mismatch with the target model. This fix maintains a persistent pinned CPU buffer of per-request deltas in `GPUModelRunner`, kept current by `_update_states` (on batch changes) and `_gather_mm_embeddings` (on pruning events). A dirty flag gates a CPU→GPU copy at the start of each `propose()` call, so steady-state decode steps pay no allocation or copy cost. The `[batch_size]` delta slice is passed into `_update_positions_dependent_metadata`, computing all 3 dims as: ``` decode_pos = delta + seq_lens_after_kernel - 1 = delta + context_len ``` This matches the target model's formula and remains correct after any delta update. Non-MRoPE models take a separate code path and are unaffected. Affects all `SupportsMRoPE` models (Qwen2/2.5/3-VL, GLM4V, and others) when used with EAGLE3 speculative decoding in vLLM V1. No open PR addresses this fix (searched `vllm-project/vllm` for `mrope eagle speculative` and `mrope_position_delta proposer`). Developed with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic). Every changed line has been reviewed by the human submitter. ## Test Plan Three new unit tests in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py`. No model weights are loaded; the Triton kernel is mocked in the integration test. ```bash pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py::test_mrope_decode_position_arithmetic -v pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py::test_mrope_position_delta_propagation -v pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py::test_mrope_pruning_slot_write -v ``` `test_mrope_decode_position_arithmetic`: arithmetic verification that the proposer formula is algebraically identical to the target model formula, across 4 request types including the clamp boundary. `test_mrope_position_delta_propagation`: real `EagleProposer` with `uses_mrope` patched and Triton kernel mocked; verifies all 3 dims are set correctly by the delta path and that the fallback replicates dim 0. `test_mrope_pruning_slot_write`: verifies that the `_gather_mm_embeddings` pruning slot write updates the correct buffer slot (using a sparse slot layout with 3 requests at non-contiguous indices), stores `None` deltas as `0`, and sets the dirty flag after each pruning event. ## Test Result ``` tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py::test_mrope_decode_position_arithmetic PASSED tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py::test_mrope_position_delta_propagation PASSED tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle.py::test_mrope_pruning_slot_write PASSED ```

signal.title: [Bugfix] Skip Dynamic NTK scaling when served length is below trained length
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52665. Dynamic NTK scaling in `dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py` unconditionally applies its context-extension formula even when the served `max_position_embeddings` is *below* the checkpoint's `max_trained_positions`. Reducing the served length below the trained length is ordinary truncation, not context extension, but the formula ``` inner = scaling_factor * served / trained - (scaling_factor - 1) base = original_base * inner ** (rotary_dim / (rotary_dim - 2)) ``` goes negative in that regime. Raising a negative `base` to a fractional power produces a complex result, which is then silently cast to a real dtype (discarding the imaginary part) and leaves a cache with values on the order of `1e38`. This eventually surfaces as NaN outputs. Concretely, for `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1` served with `--max-model-len 512` and `scaling_factor=2`: ``` inner = 2 * 512 / 2048 - 1 = -0.5 base = 1000 * (-0.5) ** (64 / 62) # complex ``` ## Fix Guard the NTK formula behind `max_position_embeddings > max_trained_positions`. At or below the trained length, the original base is used unchanged, matching plain RoPE and the reference Nomic implementation. Extension behavior above the trained length is untouched — the existing formula already evaluates to the original base at equality, so the branch boundary is continuous. ## Test Plan Added regression tests in `tests/model_executor/layers/test_dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py` covering served length below/at/above the trained length, each asserting the cache matches the exact expected formula (unscaled base below/at, legacy NTK formula above). ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py -v # 3 passed ruff check vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py tests/model_executor/layers/test_dynamic_ntk_scaling_rope.py # All checks passed / already formatted ``` ## Model evaluation An end-to-end serving eval of `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1` wasn't completed: vLLM's engine bootstrap fails on this local CPU/macOS sandbox before the model loads, for reasons unrelated to this change. Verification instead relies on the regression tests above (which reproduce the exact reported symptom pre-fix and pass post-fix) and the issue's own module-level CPU repro. ## Not a duplicate Confirmed open PR #41301 (whose actual diff is a whitespace-only change) does not fix this issue. ## AI assistance disclosure This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude Code). The changes were reviewed and tested as described above before submission.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Model] deepseek-vl2: restore original DeepseekV2Config defaults for omitted language_config fields
signal.text: ## Purpose Loading `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-small` (and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2`) currently crashes during model initialization: ``` TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int' ``` at `DeepseekV2Attention.__init__` (`self.kv_lora_rank + self.qk_rope_head_dim`). Working around that surfaces a second failure while loading `embed_tokens`: ``` AssertionError # loaded_weight.shape[output_dim] == self.org_vocab_size ``` Both failures share one root cause. DeepSeek-VL2 checkpoints ship an incomplete `language_config` that relies on the defaults of the *original* DeepSeek-VL2 `DeepseekV2Config` (`vocab_size=102400`, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_nope_head_dim=128`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`, `v_head_dim=128`). For example, `deepseek-vl2-small`'s `language_config` contains neither `vocab_size` nor `kv_lora_rank`. vLLM does not use the model's remote config; `DeepseekVLV2Config` parses `language_config` with the built-in Transformers `DeepseekV2Config` (`DeepseekVLV2TextConfig`), whose generic defaults differ: - `DeepseekV2Config().vocab_size == 32000` (not 102400) - `DeepseekVLV2TextConfig.kv_lora_rank` is forced to `None` So omitted fields silently resolve to wrong values: 1. `kv_lora_rank=None` makes `ModelConfig.is_deepseek_mla` return `False` (`use_mla=False`); combined with the non-zero `qk_*_head_dim` defaults the decoder falls through to `DeepseekV2Attention`, which computes `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` → `None + int` → `TypeError`. 2. `vocab_size=32000` mismatches the checkpoint's 102400-row `embed_tokens`, tripping the assertion in `VocabParallelEmbedding.weight_loader`. This fix restores the original DeepSeek-VL2 defaults **only for fields the checkpoint does not set**, before building the text config: ``` deepseek_vl2_reference_defaults = { "vocab_size": 102400, "kv_lora_rank": 512, "qk_nope_head_dim": 128, "qk_rope_head_dim": 64, "v_head_dim": 128, } for key, value in deepseek_vl2_reference_defaults.items(): language_config.setdefault(key, value) ``` ## Test Plan Serve deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-small and confirm it no longer crashes ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix int32 overflow in concat_mla_q flat warp index
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix #45373: `ConcatMLAQKernel` computes `blockIdx.x * blockDim.x` in 32-bit arithmetic. Once the launch exceeds 2^32 threads (> 2^27 token-heads — e.g. the reporter's 128 heads × 140×7491 tokens = 134.2M token-heads → 4.296e9 threads), the product wraps and later warps alias earlier token/head slots: they redundantly rewrite early `q_out` rows while their own rows are never written → incorrect `q_out`. Changes (both sites): - Kernel (`concat_mla_q.cuh`): compute `flat_warp_id` in 64-bit; compare against the 64-bit token-head count. `token_id`/`head_id` stay `int` (each individually bounded by `num_tokens`/`num_heads`). - Launcher (`cache_kernels.cu`): `total_warps = num_tokens * num_heads` was `int × int` — a second, latent overflow past 2^31 token-heads. Widened to `int64_t` with a `STD_TORCH_CHECK` on the final grid size. ## Test Plan The trigger requires a ~154 GB `q_out` (134M token-heads × 576 × fp16), which exceeds any single GPU, so validation is a standalone nvcc harness (sm_120, CUDA 13.0) compiling the **fixed header from this tree** plus an index-math probe replicating the old arithmetic: - **Leg A — wrap demonstration at the reporter's exact scale** (no giant allocation needed): probe blocks of the real launch geometry (grid=16,779,840 × 256 threads): ``` block 0: old_flat= 7 new_flat= 7 expected= 7 block 16777215: old_flat= 134217727 new_flat= 134217727 expected= 134217727 block 16777216: old_flat= 7 new_flat= 134217735 expected= 134217735 <-- OLD WRAPS block 16779839: old_flat= 20991 new_flat= 134238719 expected= 134238719 <-- OLD WRAPS ``` The old math wraps exactly at block 2^32/256 = 16,777,216, aliasing onto flat id 7 — the mechanism in the issue. The fixed math is correct at all probed blocks. - **Leg B — no-regression at feasible scale**: the fixed `ConcatMLAQKernel<__half, 512>` run on 8192×128 = 1,048,576 token-heads (~1.2 GB, below the wrap threshold), compared element-wise against a CPU reference: **0/603,979,776 mismatches (byte-identical)**. On sm_120 + CUDA 13 this exercises the 256-bit PTX path (`VLLM_256B_PTX_ENABLED=1`). - clang-format pre-commit hook passes on both files. ## Test Result Leg A: old arithmetic wraps at trigger scale, fixed arithmetic correct. Leg B: byte-identical output at non-overflow scale. (Honest framing: the >150 GB end-to-end trigger cannot be run on a single GPU; correctness at trigger scale is established by the device-level index-math probe + the unchanged data path.) ## Duplicate check No open PR addresses this: searched `45373`, `concat_mla_q in:title`, and the file history (`git log origin/main -- csrc/libtorch_stable/concat_mla_q.cuh` — last touched by the libtorch_stable migration, no overflow fix). #36743 optimizes the same kernel for ROCm (perf, not a fix) — flagging for conflict awareness. ## (Optional) Documentation Update None. --- AI assistance disclosure: prepared with AI assistance (Claude); the change was reviewed, compiled, and validated locally by the submitter.

signal.title: Bolins/shm tensor arena
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose `MessageQueue.enqueue` (`shm_broadcast.py`) already routes CPU tensors out-of-band via `_reduce_tensor` (protocol-5 `PickleBuffer`, #48442), which removed the dominant cost of the old in-band path — copying tensor bytes into the pickle stream. Two costs remain for a large multimodal `pixel_values` tensor on a TP=N worker: 1. the out-of-band buffer is published **once per node-local reader** (N transport copies for TP=N), and 2. each reader's H2D copies from a **pageable** ZMQ frame (pageable staging + first-touch faults). This PR adds an opt-in **slotted shared-memory tensor arena** that layers *on top of* `_reduce_tensor`: the writer does **one** memcpy into a free slot, every reader takes a **zero-copy view** of the *same* slot (no per-reader transport copy), and the mapping is `cudaHostRegister`-pinned so the H2D is a true DMA. Large contiguous CPU tensors are diverted by `_ArenaPickler.reducer_override`; anything it declines (too small, non-contiguous, or arena exhausted) **falls through to `_reduce_tensor` unchanged**. Net for a ~200 MB image at TP=8: **1 memcpy + 8 pinned DMAs** instead of **8 transport copies + 8 pageable stagings**. The gain scales with TP degree and tensor size, and is zero at TP=1 (no multiproc broadcast) — both now confirmed empirically below. Design doc: `docs/design/shm_tensor_arena.md`. **Safety / scope:** controlled by the `--enable-shm-tensor-arena` / `--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` CLI flag (`ParallelConfig.enable_shm_tensor_arena`, default on — happy to flip to default-off if preferred); activates only when all queue readers are node-local; the writer **never blocks** (no free/oversized slot → fall back to `_reduce_tensor`, deadlock structurally impossible); slot reuse is gated on an **H2D-completion CUDA event**, so the writer can't overwrite a slot whose async DMA is still in flight — correct under `--async-scheduling`. ## Test Plan A/B against **current `main`**: the baseline arm is the unmodified `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image (`nightly-65b7662d3f…`, includes #48442); the arena arm is the same image plus this PR's four files. A third arm runs this PR's code with `--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` as a disable-control (must be behaviorally identical to base; also bounds run-to-run noise). Two setups, so the TP axis and the model-realism axis are both covered: 1. **TP-scaling sweep** — Qwen2.5-VL-3B, TP ∈ {1, 2, 4} (ViT MLP dim caps this family at TP≤4), image sizes 512²–3072², 150 prompts @ 2 req/s. 2. **Production-scale VLM** — Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B (ModelOpt NVFP4) on 8×B300, TP ∈ {4, 8}, image sizes 1024²/2048²/3072², 120 prompts @ 1 req/s. Common method: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random-mm` (openai-chat backend), one image per request at a fixed size per cell, poisson arrivals at a **non-saturated** rate, 20 warmups (excludes the one-time arena pinning), seed 42, **2 repeats per cell**. Built-in negative controls: TP=1 (arena structurally inactive) and 512² images (~3 MB `pixel_values`, below the 8 MB divert threshold). <details> <summary>Repro commands</summary> Server (one per arm × TP; arena arms = same image + this PR's files): vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size $TP --max-model-len 32768 \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 [--enable-shm-tensor-arena | --no-enable-shm-tensor-arena] Load (per image size HW, per repeat): vllm bench serve --model $MODEL --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --dataset-name random-mm --random-mm-bucket-config "{($HW, $HW, 1): 1.0}" \ --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \ --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 64 --ignore-eos \ --num-warmups 20 --num-prompts 150 --request-rate 2 --seed 42 \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 --save-result </details> Still outstanding: port the standalone correctness harness (21 checks: byte-exact round-trip incl. bf16, zero-copy sharing, slot lifecycle with per-reader release, event-gated reuse, exhaustion/oversize/non-contiguous fallbacks) into `tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py` alongside the #48442 tests. ## Test Result **Qwen3-VL-235B (NVFP4) on 8×B300 — E2E p99, base → arena (mean of 2 repeats):** | image (`pixel_values` size) | TP=4 | TP=8 | |---|---:|---:| | 1024² (~23 MB) | 1021 → 995 ms (−2.6%) | 1025 → 999 ms (−2.5%) | | 2048² (~96 MB) | 1584 → 1298 ms (**−18.1%**) | 1807 → 1363 ms (**−24.6%**) | | 3072² (~213 MB) | 3340 → 2771 ms (**−17.0%**) | 4132 → 3083 ms (**−25.4%**) | TTFT p99 moves the same direction (TP=8: −21.5% at 2048², −11.9% at 3072²), and at these payload sizes TTFT p50 improves too (TP=8/3072²: 1185 → 948 ms). Request throughput is identical in every cell (rate-limited by design). **TP-scaling sweep (Qwen2.5-VL-3B — separate setup from the table above):** TP=1 and 512² images are neutral (negative controls behave as designed — the arena never activates); gains appear only at TP≥2 with ≥8 MB tensors and grow with TP and size. On this small model the relative effect is larger than the 235B numbers above — up to −34% E2E p99 at 3072²/TP=4 (3020 → 1992 ms) — because the same transport cost is a much bigger fraction of a 3B's per-request time, and at 2 req/s its large-image cells carry queueing that the stall removal also drains. The 235B table above is the more conservative, production-representative measurement. The disable-control arm on this setup bounds noise at roughly ±5% per cell. **Statistical honesty:** with n=2 repeats, individual p99 cells are noisy (the 235B control shows single-cell swings up to ~±17%). The claim rests on the pattern, not any one cell: the arena is ahead in **all 12** TTFT/E2E comparisons across both models, monotonically in TP degree and tensor size — the shape the mechanism predicts (per-reader transport + pageable staging replaced by one memcpy + pinned DMA), and the E2E-tail bias matches head-of-line blocking on co-scheduled decodes. **Summary:** neutral outside the large-image + TP≥2 regime; **~18–25% p99 reduction** inside it on a production-scale VLM. **Process note:** the disable-control caught a bug in an earlier revision of this PR — `--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` was silently ignored (the gate read `get_current_vllm_config()` outside its context and fell back to the default). Fixed by threading the flag explicitly through the executor; the control was re-validated inert (0 arena activations) before the numbers above. <details> <summary>Historical: original measurement vs the pre-#48442 in-band baseline</summary> Same-seed interactive multimodal workload (uncapped images, TP=4 ×2 workers on one 8-GPU node, ~1.2k aligned requests): TTFT p50 93→89, p90 401→241, p99 1321→862, max 2139→1375 ms; requests >1.5 s: 9→0. These numbers predate #48442 and therefore overstate the delta vs current main; kept only as provenance for the original problem analysis. </details> --- <details> <summary>Essential Elements Checklist</summary> - [x] Purpose of the PR - [x] Test plan — executed (repro commands above); unit-test port to `tests/distributed/` still outstanding - [x] Test results — A/B vs current `main` on two models × TP 1–8, with disable-control - [x] Documentation — `docs/design/shm_tensor_arena.md` </details>

signal.title: [Bug][KVOffload] PD Multi Tier discards parked KV after a fixed 60s, so a queued consumer recomputes
signal.text: ### Your current environment vLLM `main` (nightly `5a4c8d99`), plus #52912 applied. Two instances, prefill and decode, each running `OffloadingConnector` with `TieringOffloadingSpec` (CPU primary + `p2p` secondary tier). ### Describe the bug A PD Multi Tier producer discards stored KV 60 s after `submit_store` when no `FetchMsg` has bound the `kv_request_id` yet, so a consumer whose fetch is issued later finds nothing, burns its own 30 s load deadline, and recomputes the prompt. `_UNBOUND_STORE_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py`) is a fixed timer counted from store time. Nothing ties it to whether the consumer's request still exists or is merely queued behind other work, so the reap can fire while the request it belongs to is perfectly alive. When the late fetch arrives, the consumer waits out `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0` (`.../p2p/session/client.py`) before falling back to recompute. This is separate from #52808 and is not addressed by #52912; that fix makes a warm producer cascade its blocks, this is about how long those blocks survive while the peer has not asked for them yet. Reproduced with two vLLM instances and three curls - no router, no proxy, no scheduler involved. The only difference between the two cases is how long the consumer waits before fetching: | case | consumer fetch delay | consumer leg | bytes pulled | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | control | 5 s (inside the park) | 0.30 s | 580,962,816 | | late | 65 s (past the park) | 38.31 s | 0 | Producer log for the late case: ``` P2P <producer-ip>:7777: unbound store kv_request_id=park-late-39 timed out after 60s without a fetch - failing 1 job(s) ``` ### Why this fires in practice The 60 s clock does not start when prefill completes - it starts at the producer's FIRST stored chunk. `_build_store_jobs` iterates `scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens` (in-flight requests), `complete_store` cascades each finished store job to the secondary tiers every step, and `_reap_unbound_stores` keys off `batches[0].submitted_at`, the oldest batch, then pops the whole `kv_request_id`. Measured on an idle H200 with a 98 K-token producer leg: HTTP returned in 6.7 s, the first batch parked at +1 s, and with no fetch sent the reap fired at first-park + 60 s rather than completion + 60 s (the two predictions differ by 6 s in that setup; the log lands on the former). So the failing condition is not decoder queueing. The real budget is first-chunk-to-fetch < 60 s, where the fetch only happens after the remaining prefill, the producer's HTTP return, proxy dispatch, decode admission, and the decode scheduler's lookup/flush. The producer's own prefill spends the budget first: 6.7 s of it idle at 98 K tokens, 13.3 s under mild concurrent load on the same GPU. At real concurrency on long prompts the sum passes 60 s with the decoder never queueing at all. Each occurrence costs a 30 s stall plus a full prompt recompute, which feeds back into the load that caused the delay. Both leg-dispatch orders lose, so this cannot be fixed by the caller: - dispatch the legs concurrently and the fetch can arrive **before** the store, so demand parks and the consumer burns its 30 s deadline. This is what llm-d/llm-d-router#2451 fixes on the routing-proxy side, by running the prefill leg to completion before dispatching decode - dispatch them sequentially, as that PR does and as the NIXL path already did, and the fetch can arrive **after** the 60 s reap - this issue A post-reap fetch is also not rejected: the reap adds the id to `_failed_req_ids`, but the fetch-bind path never consults that set (it feeds only the consumer-side `lookup()` and dead-session teardown, despite the reap docstring saying otherwise). The late fetch binds, finds nothing, and parks silently until the consumer's 30 s deadline. ### Steps to reproduce Two instances, `PF` = producer, `DE` = consumer, both with the tiering spec and a `p2p` secondary tier. ```sh M=<model>; ID=park-$$ PROMPT=$(awk 'BEGIN{p="unique-'$ID' ";for(i=0;i<900;i++) p=p "alpha bravo charlie delta echo ";print p}') # producer leg: stores KV under ID, parks it (no peer has fetched yet) curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'producer http=%{http_code} t=%{time_total}\n' \ -X POST "http://$PF:8000/v1/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"prompt\":\"$PROMPT\",\"max_tokens\":1,\"temperature\":0,\"kv_transfer_params\":{\"remote_decoder\":{\"kv_request_id\":\"$ID\"}}}" sleep 65 # 5 reproduces the working control curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'consumer http=%{http_code} t=%{time_total}\n' \ -X POST "http://$DE:8200/v1/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"prompt\":\"$PROMPT\",\"max_tokens\":4,\"temperature\":0,\"kv_transfer_params\":{\"remote_prefiller\":{\"kv_request_id\":\"$ID\",\"remote_host\":\"$PF\",\"remote_port\":7777}}}" # watch vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes_total on the consumer across the pair ``` With `sleep 5` the consumer pulls the blocks in ~0.3 s. With `sleep 65` it transfers nothing and returns after ~38 s. ### The NIXL path already solves this `NixlConnector` faces the same question - how long does P hold blocks that D has not read yet - and answers it with a renewable lease rather than a fixed timer: - `_kv_lease_duration` (`nixl/base_scheduler.py`), default **30 s**, configurable via `kv_lease_duration` - `_heartbeat_interval = _kv_lease_duration // 6`, and D sends periodic lease-renewal heartbeats to P for every request it still intends to read - `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl`, default 480 s, for the client-driven turn-2 case So NIXL's nominal pin is *shorter* than the tier's 60 s, yet a queued consumer never loses its blocks: the lease is tied to consumer liveness, and only a consumer that has actually gone away lets it lapse. The p2p tier has no equivalent - no renewal, no way for the consumer to signal intent, and no config knob - so it cannot distinguish "the peer is still queued" from "the peer will never come". ### Suggested direction Tie the parked store's lifetime to the consumer's liveness instead of a fixed interval from store time. A few shapes that would work: - adopt the NIXL contract: let the consumer renew the parked store the way D renews P's lease, so a queued request keeps its KV and a dead one releases it promptly - failing that, let the consumer register intent for a `kv_request_id` before it is admitted, so the producer knows a peer is coming - at minimum make the interval configurable like `kv_lease_duration` is, since the right value depends on the deployment's admission latency Worth surfacing the reap as its own counter either way - today it is only a warning line, so operators see the consumer's recompute without the producer side that explains it. cc @liranschour

signal.title: Migrate to new tekken crate
signal.text: ## Purpose Migrate the Rust workspace's Mistral Tekken tokenizer dependency from `tekken-rs` 0.1.1 to `tekken` 0.2.0. I am the author of [tekken-rs](https://crates.io/crates/tekken-rs) and recently renamed it to simply [tekken](https://crates.io/crates/tekken) to make it easier to import, find, and align with its library name. Since crates.io has no rename mechanism, this meant publishing a new crate; tekken-rs 0.1.2 is the final release under the old name and will not receive further updates. Version 0.2.0 of tekken also adds: - Support for v15 of the tokenizer - Image tokenization support - Audio and image dependencies gated behind feature flags Notes on this PR: - No code changes are needed: tekken-rs's library name was already `tekken`, so all existing `use tekken::...` imports keep working. Since the crate is now actually named `tekken`, the `package = "tekken-rs"` alias in the workspace dependency goes away too. - The existing `default-features = false` was a no-op on 0.1.1 (it had no feature flags, the audio dependencies were unconditional), but on 0.2.0 it takes effect: since the Rust workspace only uses tekken for text tokenization, `hound`, `rubato`, `rustfft`, and `ndarray` drop out of the dependency tree, and the new image feature is never pulled in. ## Test Plan ```bash cd rust cargo test -p vllm-tokenizer cargo test --workspace Test Result - cargo test -p vllm-tokenizer: 62 passed, 0 failed - cargo test --workspace: 1555 passed, 0 failed
