signal.title: [Core][Distributed] Size custom all-reduce buffers at init so batch-invariant mode can use them
signal.text: ### Purpose Fixes #50136. `CustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar()` decides per call whether to use the custom all-reduce or fall through to NCCL, based on `inp_size < self.max_size`. The all-reduce tensor is `[num_tokens, hidden_size]`, so that decision tracks the token count of the forward pass — i.e. batch composition — and the same request can take different reduction orders in different batches. Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` that is a correctness bug, which is why `ParallelConfig` currently forces `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` and every batch-invariant TP run pays the pinned-NCCL path. This removes the size dependency instead of the whole code path. **Which review this is, settled.** The open question was whether the intended guarantee is *per request* (a request is bitwise reproducible under any batching) or *per engine* (a given engine configuration is internally consistent) — a bug under the first reading, a documented limitation under the second. @tolleybot answered it on this thread: per-request is what the production case needs, since regression tests and trusted production output require a prompt to give bitwise-identical logprobs however it is batched, across runs and restarts. This PR is therefore a fix, not a feature. ### What changed **1. Decide once, at init** (`custom_all_reduce.py`). Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, derive the largest all-reduce the engine can ever issue from `max_num_batched_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size` and size `max_size` — and therefore the IPC buffers — to cover it. The gate can then never flip mid-run. If the requirement exceeds the cap, or the config cannot be read, custom all-reduce declines at init and logs why, rather than disabling itself silently. **2. Fail loud, never fall back silently** (`should_custom_ar`). If an all-reduce still exceeds the buffer, raise instead of falling through to NCCL. This is the load-bearing design decision. A silent fallback is precisely the mechanism in #50136; a fix whose failure mode reproduces the bug it fixes would be worse than no fix. If the bound is ever wrong — an unmodelled path, a padded width I did not account for — the run stops with a message naming the tensor size and the buffer, instead of quietly producing non-reproducible logprobs. **3. Pin the kernel** (`csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh`). Force `cross_device_reduce_1stage` for all sizes under batch invariance, and hard error on an explicit `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage`. The 1-stage kernel sums over absolute rank indices with no address reordering (its own comment notes the result is bitwise identical across ranks); the 2-stage kernel partitions by size and rotates accumulation order per rank, so it cannot be invariance-safe. **4. Drop unaudited backends** (`cuda_communicator.py`). Under batch invariance, exclude AITER's custom all-reduce from the dispatch chain. FlashInfer is already excluded upstream by #52998, which landed the same guard while flipping the FlashInfer default on; this change builds on that guard rather than repeating it. QuickReduce is not excluded — it is constructed only on ROCm (`current_platform.is_rocm()`), so it is unreachable on the CUDA configurations validated here, but on ROCm it would be tried first. Under batch invariance on CUDA the chain is `['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']`. The env pin in `override_envs_for_invariance()` is retained as belt-and-braces: since #52998, the communicator itself excludes FlashInfer under batch invariance, so the pin is redundant for dispatch but guards against future refactors of that logic. **5. Stop forcing the disable** (`config/parallel.py`), now that (1) makes the decision fixed for the process lifetime. The platform-support disable (`if not current_platform.use_custom_allreduce()`) is untouched. **6. Test + docs.** A TP≥4 batch-invariance test in `tests/v1/determinism/` (the suite currently runs everything at TP=1, so the all-reduce path was untested — that gap is why #50136 was possible to write), and `docs/features/batch_invariance.md` updated to describe the new behaviour. ### Validation Bitwise comparison of output token IDs **and** per-step logprobs as raw float32 bit patterns (not `allclose`) across batch compositions: bs=1 reference, full mixed batch, shuffled batch, and tile-boundary batches of 17 and 65. | Arm | Config | Invariance | Custom AR engaged | Largest tensor | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | dense, TP=4, patched | clean | 4/4 ranks, 9918 calls each | 25,165,824 B | | 2 | dense, TP=4, `disable_custom_all_reduce` (control) | clean | none, as expected | — | | 3 | dense, long context (2048/4096) | clean | 4/4 ranks | 25,165,824 B | | 4 | MoE (Qwen3-30B-A3B), TP=4 | clean | 4/4 ranks | 33,554,432 B | | 5 | fault injection (buffer forced to 4 KiB) | raises | — | — | | 6 | throughput, patched vs control | clean both | 4/4 vs none | 25,165,824 B | Three things make those greens checkable rather than merely green. **The bound predicts the observed maximum exactly.** Dense: largest tensor through the custom kernel = 25,165,824 B = `8192 × 1536 × 2`. MoE: 33,554,432 B = `8192 × 2048 × 2`. Both are exactly `max_num_batched_tokens × hidden_size × dtype_size`, which is the formula the buffer is sized from. Resulting buffers were 30 MiB and 40 MiB per rank. Engagement counts are read from each worker with `collective_rpc`, so they are exact per-rank values (`calls=9918`, identical on ranks 0–3), not log-derived estimates. **Every patched arm crossed the old threshold.** 25,165,824 B is 3.0× the 8 MiB constructor default that applied before this change, and the MoE arm's 33,554,432 B is 4.0×. (The `CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES` clamp is unreachable under batch invariance, since `override_envs_for_invariance()` sets `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0`.) So these runs exercised tensors that previously fell through to NCCL — they sat in the regime where the gate used to flip, not one where it never would have. **Both guards fire with their intended messages.** Injecting a 4 KiB buffer so a real all-reduce exceeds it: ``` RuntimeError: custom all-reduce received a 25165824 byte tensor, above the 4096 byte batch-invariant buffer. Falling back to NCCL would break batch invariance. Re-run with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT unset, or file a bug with the model and max_num_batched_tokens so the bound can be corrected. ``` And `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage` under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: ``` VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=2stage is incompatible with VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1: cross_device_reduce_2stage partitions the message by size and accumulates in a rank-rotated order, so an element's summation order changes with message size (i.e. with batch composition) and differs across owning ranks. ``` Throughput, batch-invariant mode, same workload, identical output (14,784 tokens in both arms): ``` patched (custom AR) 8006.4 tok/s TTFT p50 53.40 ms TPOT p50 8.48 ms control (NCCL only) 3906.0 tok/s TTFT p50 67.61 ms TPOT p50 17.34 ms → 2.05x ``` See the note on this number in "Tested / not tested" below — an earlier run on a different workload measured +84%, so the direction reproduces but the magnitude does not. #### Re-validation on current main (post-#52998) Rebased onto `main` @ `6259572b2` (which includes #52998's FlashInfer default flip and its batch-invariance guard) and re-validated on the same hardware class: 4× A100-SXM4-40GB, NVSwitch NV12 all-to-all (P2P 262.0 GB/s, 24 µs/hop — matching the original run). - Dispatch under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, TP=4, with FlashInfer **installed**: resolves to `['CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']`; FlashInfer, AITER, QuickReduce, and both symm-mem paths not constructed. - Dense arm: CLEAN across all 5 batch compositions, 4/4 ranks engaged (exact per-rank counts via `collective_rpc`), largest tensor 25,165,824 B = 8192 × 1536 × 2 — byte-identical to the original bound prediction — within the 30 MiB buffer, `largest <= max_size` on every rank, zero tracebacks. - Routing tests 5/5 green; `pre-commit --all-files` clean for this PR's files (mypy ran and passed; the one repo-wide failure, `test-nonroot-entrypoint`, also fails on unpatched main). Two recorded deviations from the original run: host driver 595.71.05 (vs 580.65.06; same nvcc 13.0.88 toolchain), and `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="8.0;9.0a"` — required because current main does not compile for SM 8.0 alone (a GDN/KDA `#ifdef` guard mismatch in `csrc/libtorch_stable`, upstream and unrelated to this PR; will be reported separately). The A100 still executes SM 8.0 code. GPU evidence above was gathered at `d3cb5924b6`; the pushed commit `edfb2f5b2d` differs from it by a one-line ruff-format wrap in a test file (no runtime code). The full determinism harness used for the matrix above now lives on a follow-up branch -- https://github.com/mosafariuk/vllm/tree/test/batch-invariant-validation-harness -- so this PR carries the fix plus its regression test: 131 LOC functional (`vllm/` + `csrc/`) and 158 LOC of test. ### Tested / not tested **Tested.** 4× A100-SXM4-40GB with NVSwitch (`NV12` all-to-all), driver 580.65.06, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, built from source. TP=4, bf16, chunked prefill and CUDA graphs enabled, for a dense model (Qwen2.5-1.5B, `hidden_size=1536`) and an MoE model (Qwen3-30B-A3B, `hidden_size=2048`). **Not tested, and guarded rather than assumed:** - **The MXFP4-padded MoE path.** `fused_moe` pads the routed hidden dimension before the all-reduce and truncates after, so the reduced tensor is wider than `hidden_size`. That padding is gated to the TRT-LLM MXFP4 path (`hidden_dim_unpadded > 0`), which needs Blackwell-class hardware I do not have. The MoE arm exercised MoE collectives and expert-parallel shapes but not the padded width. - **Multi-node symmetric memory / MNNVL multicast.** It disables itself when the group is not single-node, so TP=4 on one node cannot reach it. - **TP sizes other than 4**, non-NVSwitch topologies, and speculative decoding. - **QuickReduce on ROCm.** It is constructed only on ROCm and would be tried first in the dispatch chain there; the CUDA validation cannot reach it. Not excluded and not validated. Every unreached path above except QuickReduce on ROCm either declines custom all-reduce at init with a logged reason or hits the fail-loud `RuntimeError` in `should_custom_ar()`; QuickReduce is unguarded and would be selected ahead of the custom path there. **The throughput result is directional, not a specification.** Two runs on this configuration measured **+84%** and **+105%** on different workloads — same direction, materially different magnitude. The control is not ordinary NCCL: `override_envs_for_invariance()` pins `NCCL_MIN/MAX_NCHANNELS=1` and `NCCL_NTHREADS=1`, so the baseline is deliberately serialised NCCL, which is the cost this change removes. Treat the direction as reproducible and the magnitude as workload-specific. ### The memory trade-off — the call I made The buffer now scales with model width. Measured and projected, per rank: | `hidden_size` | raw bound | with 1.25× margin | outcome | |---|---|---|---| | 1536 (Qwen2.5-1.5B, measured) | 24 MiB | 30 MiB | fits | | 2048 (Qwen3-30B-A3B, measured) | 32 MiB | 40 MiB | fits | | 8192 (70B class) | 128 MiB | 160 MiB | fits | | 16384 | 256 MiB | 320 MiB | exceeds cap → declines at init, uses NCCL | Only the 1536 and 2048 rows are measured; the 8192 and 16384 rows are the formula evaluated, not runs. I capped it at 256 MiB/rank — a number chosen against that arithmetic rather than against a wide-model run — so everything up to roughly `hidden_size ≈ 13k` gets the custom path and wider models fall back cleanly at startup with a logged reason. That is where I chose to stop paying, given the alternative is the serialised-NCCL path. Both the cap and the 1.25× margin (which exists because I could not bound the MoE padding exactly) are policy numbers and one-line changes if you would put them elsewhere. If you would rather not spend the memory at all, the alternative is to keep the blanket disable and document why it is load-bearing — I am happy to send that instead; it is a small docs-and-comment change. ### How the validation was checked Five defects were found during this work by cross-checks rather than by the tests passing. Each is listed with the check that now catches its class, because the checks are the part that generalises. 1. **`git apply --3way` reported per-file success, then rolled the whole patch back** when a later file failed — leaving the kernel gate, the config change and the backend filtering absent with no error printed. Caught by a semantic grep for the changed symbols, not by the tool's output. That grep now runs before every build. 2. **The hand-port to current `main` dropped `self._custom_ar_calls = 0` and `self._custom_ar_max_bytes = 0`** while keeping all six uses. `__init__` has ten early returns, so grepping the attribute name still passed; the defect surfaced as an `AttributeError` at engine init. Now covered by an AST check asserting that any attribute other methods read is assigned at the **top level** of `__init__`, so completing the constructor guarantees it exists. The check was verified to fail on the pre-fix file. 3. **The semantic grep itself produced two false alarms** — it matched lowercase `batch_invariant` where the code says `envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, and matched `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` against upstream's unrelated platform-support guard. It now asserts the batch-invariance disable is absent **and** the platform guard is present, as separate conditions. 4. **The test's engagement assertion read `capfd` before engine shutdown.** Under `capfd`, fd 1 is a regular file rather than a tty, so worker processes block-buffer their output and flush only on exit. The assertion read zero markers while 21 were present in the log — a false red that, if "fixed" by weakening the assertion, would have removed the guard. The test now reads the counters directly from each worker via `collective_rpc`, which is immune to buffering, yields exact per-rank counts, and additionally asserts `largest <= max_size`. 5. **An earlier harness summed per-rank milestone floors** and reported a call count the data did not support. It now reports rank count and per-rank floor separately, and the test reports exact counts. The test ships with a counterpart, `test_engagement_assertion_can_fail`, that runs the same engine with the custom path disabled: output stays invariant, so a test checking only reproducibility would pass, and the engagement assertion must fail. It runs by default rather than being skipped. ### The contract question — resolved Is the intended guarantee **per request** (this request is bitwise reproducible under any batching) or **per engine** (a given engine configuration is internally consistent)? The size gate is a bug under the first reading and a documented limitation under the second. I had assumed the first because it is what makes batch invariance useful for RL rollouts where trainer and sampler must agree, but flagged it as an assumption about intent. @tolleybot resolved it in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50505#issuecomment-5246281546: per-request is what the production case needs — regression tests plus trusted production output mean a prompt has to give bitwise-identical logprobs no matter what it is batched with, across runs and restarts, and per-engine consistency does not help there. He also noted that the `ParallelConfig` guard in #51292 was a placeholder rather than a vote for per-engine. This PR is scoped as a fix on that basis. --- *Disclosure: this work was done with AI assistance (Claude). I ran the experiments, reviewed the changes, and take responsibility for the content.*

signal.title: [ROCm][Model][Bugfix] Enable GLM-5.2-MXFP4 on the deepseek_v32 path and fix sparse attention correctness
signal.text: ## Purpose Enables GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) end-to-end on `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/` for gfx942/gfx950. Routing is opt-in via `--model-class-overrides`; the registry entry is unchanged, so the default path for GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 is untouched. The following issues were also fixed as a result of this overall enablement since it surfaced dormant bugs from a prior deepseek_v32 porting work: - **`launch_pdl` forwarded to a Triton runtime that doesn't accept it** — the shared `common/kernels.py` passed this CUDA-only kwarg unconditionally; ROCm's Triton rejects it by name even when `False`, so the engine died at startup with `KeyError`. Now passed only when the platform actually supports PDL. - **fp4 bmm invoked with mismatched positional args** — the output tensor landed in the kernel's `dtype` slot (`Expected 'Optional[int]' for 'dtype' but found Tensor`). Routed through the existing `rocm_aiter_ops.batched_gemm_a16wfp4` wrapper rather than calling aiter directly, so the argument contract lives in one place. - **fp4 MLA bmm silently wrong for non-power-of-two K** — `batched_gemm_a16wfp4` only supports power-of-two K, and returns wrong values without erroring otherwise. GLM-5.2's `qk_nope_head_dim=192` lands in the unsupported set; DeepSeek-V3.2's 128 does not. Guarded on both `qk_nope_head_dim` and `kv_lora_rank` to fall back to the fp8 bmm, with a warning. `W_K`/`W_K_scale` are also made contiguous after the transpose, which otherwise produced NaN. - **Indexer-K cache written in the plain layout while its reader expects the shuffled one** — affects DeepSeek-V3.2 identically, not just GLM-5.2. The AMD path writes this cache from the shared `fused_norm_rope`, which only implemented `[n_blocks, blk, head_dim]`, while the reader selects `SHUFFLE` above block size 1: the write kept storing row-major, but the reader expected shuffled, so the indexer scored garbage K and output degenerated once a sequence exceeded `index_topk=2048`, with no error raised. Refactored so the shared kernel stays platform-agnostic — it writes whichever layout the cache reports via a new `uses_shuffled_layout` property — and the AMD-specific shuffled write (`[n_blocks, blk/16, head_dim/16, 16, 16]`, used above block size 1) lives in the AMD backend. The base class returns `False`, so CUDA is unchanged. - **Sparse-MLA block sizes narrowed instead of extended** — the ported backends replaced the inherited `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` with `[16, 32]`, which made `select_common_block_size` silently downgrade a requested 64 to 32 via its largest-divisor fallback. Now concatenated with the base list. - **Kernel tests gated on `is_cuda()` and running against dims that matched neither model** — the tests were skipped entirely on CDNA. The gate is now `supports_fp8()`, so the suite runs on gfx950. The hardcoded attention dims were written as if one set served both GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2, which it did not; they are now taken from each model's published config and parametrized over both. ## Test Plan Server: VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \ HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \ vllm serve /path-to-your/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \ --model-class-overrides '{"GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM": "vllm.models.deepseek_v32:DeepseekV32ForCausalLM"}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype auto \ --max-model-len 65536 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --trust-remote-code \ --port 8000 Variants: --kv-cache-dtype fp8 for the fp8 KV row; --block-size {16,64} for the block-size matrix. Drop --model-class-overrides to run the legacy deepseek_v2 path for comparison. Accuracy: lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args "model=/models/GLM-5.2-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False,max_retries=3,timeout=3600" \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048 --limit 200 Throughput: vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model /shareddata/models/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 1024 \ --num-prompts 200 --max-concurrency 32 --ignore-eos --port 8000 \ --save-result --result-filename glm52_v32amd_bench.json Kernel unit tests: pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py -v ## Test Result **gsm8k** — GLM-5.2 200 samples, 5-shot, `exact_match`, `deepseek_v32` AMD path | KV cache | Before (flexible / strict) | After (flexible / strict) | |-------------|----------------------------|------------------------------| | auto (bf16) | 0.0000 / 0.0000 | **0.9400 / 0.9400** ± 0.0168 | | fp8 | 0.0000 / 0.0000 \* | **0.9350 / 0.9350** ± 0.0175 | \* Not separately measured. fp8 KV goes through the same absorbed-weight bmm where the bug was, so it fails identically; only the bf16 run was evaluated pre-fix.

signal.title: vLLM v0.26.0: intermittent startup wedge — `shm_broadcast` block starvation kills rank 0 during `_initialize_kv_caches`, API stays up but generation is dead
signal.text: ## Summary On an 8-rank tensor-parallel deployment of GLM-5.2-FP8, vLLM v0.26.0 intermittently fails during engine start. ~60 s of shared-memory broadcast block starvation is followed by `RayWorkerProc rank=[0] died unexpectedly`, `RuntimeError: cancelled` from `shm_broadcast.acquire_read`, and `EngineDeadError`. **Observed in 5 of 7 startup attempts.** When a start does survive, the server is stable — one surviving instance served 40 consecutive authenticated generation requests over 2 hours with zero failures. So this is a startup-time race, not runtime decay. **Most damaging detail:** in 2 of 3 controlled trials the HTTP server still came up and answered `GET /v1/models` with 200 while generation was already dead. Any readiness check based on the models endpoint reports a healthy start for a wedged engine. Only an authenticated completion request detects it. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | vLLM | 0.26.0 | | Hardware | 8 × NVIDIA GB10, compute capability 12.1 (SM121), 128 GB unified LPDDR5X per node | | Driver / CUDA | 580.173.02 / 13.0 | | OS / kernel | Ubuntu 24.04.4, 6.17.0-1029-nvidia, aarch64 | | Model | `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` | | Executor | Ray, `distributed_executor_backend=ray` | | Topology | TP8, PP1, DP1, expert-parallel off, speculative decoding off | | Attention backend | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` | | KV cache dtype | `fp8_ds_mla` | | CUDA graph | `NONE` | | Interconnect | RoCEv2, dual 200 Gb/s ConnectX-7 rails, NCCL over IB | Serve arguments (constant across all trials): --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.83 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 \ --enable-chunked-prefill --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}' ## Observed sequence Timestamps from two independent trials. The starvation warning precedes the worker death by ~60 s in both, which suggests the block starvation is the primary event and the rank-0 death is downstream of it. Trial A: 13:11:01 INFO [shm_broadcast.py:705] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work... 13:12:05 ERROR [ray_executor_v2.py:514] RayWorkerProc rank=[0] died unexpectedly, shutting down executor. 13:12:05 ERROR [core.py:1332] File ".../shm_broadcast.py", line 779, in dequeue 13:12:05 ERROR [core.py:1332] File ".../shm_broadcast.py", line 701, in acquire_read 13:12:05 ERROR [core.py:1332] RuntimeError: cancelled 13:12:05 ERROR [async_llm.py:704] vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. Trial B (same signature, 59 s gap): 13:35:55 INFO [shm_broadcast.py:705] No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds 13:36:54 ERROR [ray_executor_v2.py:514] RayWorkerProc rank=[0] died unexpectedly 13:36:54 ERROR [core.py:1332] RuntimeError: cancelled 13:36:54 ERROR [async_llm.py:704] EngineDeadError Full call path captured on an earlier occurrence: core.py:136 __init__ -> core.py:324 _initialize_kv_caches -> abstract.py:124 initialize_from_config -> multiproc_executor.py:405 collective_rpc -> multiproc_executor.py:91 result -> multiproc_executor.py:95 _wait_for_response -> multiproc_executor.py:390 get_response -> mq.dequeue -> shm_broadcast.py:779 dequeue -> shm_broadcast.py:701 acquire_read -> RuntimeError("cancelled") The failure occurs inside `_initialize_kv_caches`, i.e. during the compilation / KV-config collective, before the model serves any request. ## Reproduction 1. Deploy `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` across 8 GB10 nodes with the arguments above. 2. Start the server; wait for the API to bind. 3. Issue an **authenticated completion** request (not `/v1/models`). 4. Repeat the full stop/start cycle. Roughly 5 of 7 cycles fail. Weight load is ~15 min per cycle, so failures are expensive to reproduce. ## Expected vs actual **Expected:** engine start either succeeds or fails loudly; a bound HTTP server implies a functional engine. **Actual:** the engine core dies during KV-cache initialisation, yet the API server can remain bound and answer `/v1/models` with 200. `POST /v1/completions` returns no tokens. A readiness probe on the models endpoint therefore reports success. ## What was ruled out - **Speculative decoding / MTP** — reproduced with MTP fully disabled. - **Context length** — reproduced at 16384 after 16384 had previously succeeded; also seen at 32768. - **Memory pressure** — no kernel OOM on any rank; engine reports 88.73 GiB weights, 1.4 GiB peak activation, 2.3 GiB non-torch against a 101.0 GiB budget, and separately advertises ~18 GiB of unused headroom. - **Interconnect** — NCCL reports `ncclCommInitRank ... Init COMPLETE` on all 8 ranks across both IB devices with ECE negotiated in ~2.3 s. Fabric counters show zero discards, zero retransmits and zero link events across the affected windows. - **KV dtype support** — `FlashInferMLASparseSM120Backend` declares `fp8_ds_mla` among its `supported_kv_cache_dtypes`. ## Patched-build isolation This runs on an image with local patches layered on v0.26.0, so the obvious question is whether those patches are implicated. They are not: **every file in the failure path is byte-identical between the patched build and an unpatched v0.26.0 build of the same base.** | file | unpatched | patched | |---|---|---| | `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py` | `7ff67c2ef6b8a33a` | `7ff67c2ef6b8a33a` | | `vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py` | `fb279ff0e0a08681` | `fb279ff0e0a08681` | | `vllm/v1/engine/core.py` | `3ae1381a6af841e2` | `3ae1381a6af841e2` | | `vllm/v1/executor/abstract.py` | `419002195d13cf05` | `419002195d13cf05` | | `vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py` | `5920e5924bd74b85` | `5920e5924bd74b85` | | `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashinfer_mla_sparse.py` | `550079022e858952` | `550079022e858952` | | **aggregate of all `vllm/**/*.py`** | `af932612311083bf` | `8d3fa2ce4a73bcc0` | (sha256, first 16 hex chars.) The aggregate row differs, confirming the two images are genuinely distinct — the patches exist, they simply do not touch any module the traceback passes through. The local patch set targets speculative-decoding/MTP paths (`dsa_mtp_index_sharing`, `mtp_compact_shared_topk`, `glm52_mtp_indexer_correctness`), and this issue reproduces with **speculative decoding disabled**. ## Workaround Retry the start. Surviving instances are stable. At the observed rate this needs 3–4 attempts (~25 min each), which is not viable for production bring-up, so we have reverted to vLLM v0.23.0 with `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` and `bfloat16` KV. That combination has started reliably every time. Note the cost of the workaround: v0.23.0's `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` does not support any fp8 KV dtype, so reverting forfeits the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache. Measured on identical context and utilisation, `fp8_ds_mla` on v0.26.0 gave **152,000 KV tokens / 9.28x max concurrency** versus **61,184 / 3.73x** on v0.23.0 — a 2.5x capacity difference. ## Suggested follow-up 1. `_initialize_kv_caches` appears to exceed the `shm_broadcast` block-acquisition window on slow multi-node startups. A longer or configurable timeout for the initialisation-phase collective may be sufficient. 2. Rank 0's own termination reason is not surfaced — the executor reports only "died unexpectedly". Propagating the worker's exit cause would make this diagnosable in one cycle rather than seven. 3. Consider having the API server refuse to bind, or report unready, when `EngineCore` has died, so that `/v1/models` cannot answer 200 for a dead engine. ## Evidence available Per-rank engine captures from 3 controlled trials (all 8 ranks each), full Ansible run logs, and fabric counter deltas across each window.

signal.title: [Quantization] Clarify MXFP4 MoE W13 layout requirement from backends
signal.text: ## Background GPT-OSS checkpoints store fused gate/up weights in interleaved row order [g0, u0, g1, u1, ...], while standard MoE checkpoints (DeepSeek, Kimi-K3, and most of the ckpts from different quantizers etc.) store them contiguously [gate; up]. In the beginning when mxfp4 oracle was initially created, this interleaved weight format is overlooked. Some backends accepts interleaved format while others accepts contiguous format. They are all mixed together in the same `convert_weight_*` and `select_mxfp4_moe_backend` call. Later when DSV4 was added, two parallel functions (convert_gpt_oss_weight_* and convert_weight_*) were created. The original `convert_weight_*` was renamed `convert_gpt_oss_weight_*`, despite it handles more models than just gpt-oss. Now several backends shared identical code between them, meaning they silently accepted either layout without converting, which is incorrect for backends that assume a specific layout. ## Audit DeepDive This PR starts a complete, deepdive audit to the existing state of all the backends. **NOTE:** The audit is produced by Claude Code, and verified carefully by the author. There could be mistakes. ### Terminology - **Contiguous [w1;w3]** = `[gate_0..gate_N; up_0..up_N]` (standard vLLM checkpoint layout) - **Contiguous [w3;w1]** = `[up_0..up_N; gate_0..gate_N]` (FlashInfer CUTLASS convention, halves swapped) - **Interleaved [g,u]** = `[gate_0, up_0, gate_1, up_1, ...]` (GPT-OSS checkpoint layout) - **Interleaved [u,g]** = `[up_0, gate_0, up_1, gate_1, ...]` (TRTLLM convention, w1/w3 swapped within pairs) ### w13 Layout Expected by Backend x Activation | Backend | Activation | w13 Layout | Proof | |---|---|---|---| | **DEEPGEMM_MXFP4** | SILU | **Contiguous [w1;w3]** | [`fp8_utils.py:143`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py#L143): `hidden_size: tl.constexpr = N // 2`; [`fp8_utils.py:165-178`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py#L165): loads gate from `input_ptr + offset`, up from `input_ptr + hidden_size + offset` | | | SWIGLUSTEP | **Contiguous [w1;w3]** | [`layers/activation.py:37-38`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/vllm/model_executor/layers/activation.py#L37): `gate = tl.load(x_row_ptr + offsets)`, `up = tl.load(x_row_ptr + offsets + d)` with `d = n // 2` at [line 55](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/vllm/model_executor/layers/activation.py#L55) | | | SITU | **Contiguous [w1;w3]** | [`activation_kernels.cu:483-484`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/csrc/libtorch_stable/activation_kernels.cu#L483): `gate_ptr = input + row * 2 * d`, `up_ptr = gate_ptr + d` | | **TRTLLM** | SWIGLUOAI, SILU, SITU | **Interleaved [u,g]** | [`mxfp4.py:1310-1317`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py#L1310): comment "TRTLLM kernel expects interleaved [w3_0, w1_0, ...]"; `torch.stack([w3_weight, w1_weight], dim=2).reshape()` produces `[up_0, gate_0, up_1, gate_1, ...]` | | | | | [`trtllm_mxfp4_moe.py:139-146`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_mxfp4_moe.py#L139): SITU support gated behind `has_flashinfer_situ_activation()` | | **FLASHINFER_CUTLASS** | SILU, GELU_TANH, SWIGLUOAI, SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE, RELU2_NO_MUL | **Contiguous [w3;w1]** (swapped halves) | [`flashinfer_utils.py:53-56`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/flashinfer_utils.py#L53): `swap_w13_to_w31` reshapes to `(-1, 2, half, cols)` and `.flip(dims=[1])`, swapping gate and up halves | | | | | CUTLASS consumes [w3; w1]" | | | | | [`activation_kernels.cu:410`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/csrc/libtorch_stable/activation_kernels.cu#L410): comment `// Interleaved gate/up: input has [gate0, up0, gate1, up1, ...]`; vectorized path at [line 448](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/csrc/libtorch_stable/activation_kernels.cu#L448): `ACT_FN(vp[2*j], vp[2*j+1], ...)` | | | SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE | **Contiguous [w1;w3]** | [`fused_moe/activation.py:262-268`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/activation.py#L262): dispatches to `silu_and_mul_with_clamp` → [`activation_kernels.cu:102-108`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/csrc/libtorch_stable/activation_kernels.cu#L102): `x_ptr = input + token_idx * 2 * d`, `y_ptr = x_ptr + d` | | | SILU, GELU, SWIGLUSTEP | **Contiguous [w1;w3]** | [`fused_moe/activation.py:230-236`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4be4e9a580/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/activation.py#L230): dispatches to `silu_and_mul` etc. → signal.title: [Perf][ROCm] Dual-stream decode with hipgraphs
signal.text:
## What's new since reverted in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52024 TLDR: changes since this PR was reverted: [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52033/changes/b25620205d5529e8e36ca143050770ce31969428..1b7ff2c22beb1fddbebaed5c08ef62367e986528). **Context:** Re-opened https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48223 after it failed CI due to poor gsm8k acc for Qwen3.5 with DP2EP. **Root cause of failure:** Qwen3.5 uses the same tensor for hidden state and shared expert inputs, and never creates any copies of either tensor throughout the MoE. This causes a race condition during multi-stream. Specifically, it uses the same tensors because it's **not quantizing the routed experts' input**. When quantizing the input (as in DSv3) a copy is "implicitlly created" and hence the two buffers are different. **Fix:** **Disable dual-stream if not quantizing the routed experts' input**. To retain Nvidia behavior, we only do this check on ROCm. This (1) ensures Qwen3.5 does not have a race condition, and hence accuracy is preserved (but multi-stream is off), and (2) DSv3 uses multi-stream. **Validation:** Get traces for both DSv3 and Qwen3.5 when running DP, and re-run gsm8k with this config: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \ --max-model-len 4096 \ --data-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --trust-remote-code \ --disable-uvicorn-access-log ``` ### **Qwen3.5**: mulistream overlap **disabled** automatically. No overlap: This is because its MoE layer is using **unquantized GEMMs**: Accuracy OK! |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8453|± |0.0100| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.8332|± |0.0103| ### **DSv3**: proper multi-stream overlap for DPA+TP8 (with no extra copies) This works because it's using quantized (fp8) fmoe: --- _From original PR:_ ## Purpose Fixes #48111. Enables (1) dual-stream decode for CUDA-like platforms with proper overlap (2) make them hip/cudagraph compatible. Only enabled on ROCm when using DP, as we observed [performance regression under TP](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48223#issuecomment-4993855510). Mutually exclusive with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS`. Disable with `VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM=1` as usual. **Gain:** About -3-4% TPOT on 1k/1k and 8k/1k when using DPA vs default. **Note:** When Fused Shared experts (FSE) can be used, it provides even better TPOT than dual-stream. However, FSE cannot be used everywhere (like with MoRI a2a kernels). ### Technical details - Simply allowing `MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAPPED` for CUDA-like platforms is not sufficient for performant dual-stream decode (on ROCm, at least), because the shared expert was launched on the aux stream only _after_ the routed experts had completed. That leads to a sequential launch with no overlap: - Instead, we need to launch the shared expert in the aux stream _before_ the dispatch. #### After this PR we get the following traces - Pure decodes: properly overlapped - Mixed batches: no aux stream - Pure prefills: no aux stream ## Test Plan Tested on 8xMI300. 1. Run DSv3 with DPA+TP: ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm bench deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \ --max-model-len 16K ``` 2. Bench serve sweep, 1k/1k and 8k/1k ISL/OSL - 10x as many prompts as the concurrency level; 2x number of warmups. - Comparing to nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-a16dbd5b8572d4128be9f10b9dcff4999b594b25` with fused shared experts ```bash vllm bench serve \ --backend vllm \ --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 1024 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --host localhost \ --port 8000 \ --ignore-eos \ --ready-check-timeout-sec 6000 \ --seed 5678 \ --max-concurrency 128 \ --num-prompts 1280 \ --num-warmups 256 ``` 6. GSM8k accuracy non-regression ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True,num_concurrent=256 \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5" ``` ## Test Result - Couple % improved TPOT ### 1k/1k (P50's only) | Concurrency | Variant | QPS | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | % TPOT improved | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | this branch | 0.04 | 232.57 | 23.67 | **+4.24%** | | 1 | nightly | 0.04 | 273.16 | 24.72 | - | | 2 | this branch | 0.08 | 258.38 | 24.16 | **+4.58%** | | 2 | nightly | 0.08 | 298.14 | 25.32 | - | | 4 | this branch | 0.15 | 397.90 | 25.52 | **+7.03%** | | 4 | nightly | 0.14 | 366.23 | 27.45 | - | | 8 | this branch | 0.25 | 602.93 | 30.84 | **+3.41%** | | 8 | nightly | 0.24 | 664.92 | 31.93 | - | | 16 | this branch | 0.44 | 1268.65 | 35.02 | -6.77% | | 16 | nightly | 0.46 | 851.06 | 32.80 | - | | 32 | this branch | 0.71 | 1830.04 | 42.03 | **+2.75%** | | 32 | nightly | 0.70 | 1698.74 | 43.22 | - | | 64 | this branch | 1.34 | 3228 | 43.51 | **+4.71%** | | 64 | nightly | 1.29 | 2528 | 45.66 | - | | 128 | this branch | 2.15 | 4487.07 | 53.85 | **+1.86%** | | 128 | nightly | 2.10 | 4543.42 | 54.87 | - | | 256 | this branch | 3.46 | 6554.86 | 65.74 | **+3.12%** | | 256 | nightly | 3.37 | 6386.54 | 67.86 | - | Note: TTFT numbers seems highty variable. Ran 64 concurrency yet another time, and then I got 1902 ms TTFT @ 1.37 QPS, substantially better than the first time. This PR should not affect prefills anyhow so not focusing too much on TTFT here anyways. ### 8k/1k | Concurrency | Variant | QPS | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | % TPOT improved | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | this branch | 0.04 | 1868.16 | 25.22 | **+3.59%** | | 1 | nightly | 0.04 | 1860 | 26.16 | - | | 2 | this branch | 0.07 | 2034.06 | 25.42 | **+5.47%** | | 2 | nightly | 0.07 | 2014.35 | 26.89 | - | | 4 | this branch | 0.11 | 3800.62 | 31.35 | **+2.82%** | | 4 | nightly | 0.11 | 3687 | 32.26 | - | | 8 | this branch | 0.19 | 4105.90 | 37.01 | **+5.54%** | | 8 | nightly | 0.18 | 4122.95 | 39.18 | - | | 16 | this branch | 0.31 | 6355 | 45.37 | -3.07% | | 16 | nightly | 0.31 | 6321 | 44.02 | - | | 32 | this branch | 0.45 | 9616.31 | 60.48 | **+11.44%** | | 32 | nightly | 0.41 | 9173.59 | 68.29 | - | | 128 | this branch | 0.85 | 15579.93 | 131.24 | -3.71% | | 128 | nightly | 0.89 | 13966.30 | 126.55 | - | ### GSM8k This branch: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9416|± |0.0065| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9409|± |0.006| Nightly: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9484|± |0.0061| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9492|± |0.0060| ---

signal.title: [Bugfix] Reload speculative draft weights after Level 2 sleep wake
signal.text: Addresses #52479 ## Problem After the documented Level 2 sleep/wake sequence, MTP speculative decoding silently stops helping: every drafted token is rejected (`Mean acceptance length: 1.00`, `Accepted throughput: 0.00`) and decode throughput falls to approximately the no-speculation rate. Target-model outputs remain correct, so the failure appears only as a large performance regression. Level 2 sleep discards draft parameters together with the target parameters. `wake_up()` restores the saved draft buffers, but the documented subsequent `reload_weights()` call reloaded only the target model. The drafter is a separate module and therefore continued with discarded parameter storage. ## Fix Put the disk-backed draft reload in `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`), on the existing `weights_iterator is None` path, before the target load: - Resolve the draft through the existing `get_draft_model()` accessor. - Read the configured draft checkpoint with its model loader. MTP configurations without a separate `draft_load_config` use the target load configuration. - Load in place through `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload`, preserving the parameter addresses captured by the compiled runtime. - Invoke the helper unbound (`GPUModelRunner._reload_draft_weights_from_disk(self)`) because Model Runner V2 already delegates this method with a V2 `self` and does not inherit the helper. - During that draft load, temporarily unbind any draft submodule that is the same object as a target module. A discard dummy swallows checkpoint tensors for those aliases so layerwise reload and `load_weights` cannot shape-mismatch or rewrite live target storage (Gemma4 MTP after `_maybe_share_embeddings`). - If a detached `embed_tokens` weight shape differs from the draft `lm_head` (Gemma4 MTP: tied draft-dim head, then embed replaced with the backbone-dim target module), load those embed tensors into the still-live `lm_head`. Same-width shared embeds are discarded; a distinct head loads from its own entry. - Reload the target last so same-width shared storage (typical Qwen MTP / EAGLE) is restored from the target checkpoint. - Leave iterator-based reloads unchanged; those weights are supplied by their caller and are not assumed to contain a second draft checkpoint. Model Runner V2 keeps its existing one-line delegate into that method. There is no V2 wrapper and no production-file diff under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`. This mirrors Level 1 sleep semantics: both paths restore the existing target and draft modules in place. Level 1 restores their tagged allocations from host RAM, while Level 2 restores saved buffers during `wake_up()` and reloads model parameters from their disk checkpoints during `reload_weights()`. ### Why not `start_draft_weight_update()`? The draft weight-update API added by #46725 selects the draft as the destination of an already-configured `WeightTransferEngine`. Its built-in NCCL and IPC backends receive weights supplied by an external trainer; they do not accept a checkpoint path or read weights from disk. The API also requires the server to start with `weight_transfer_config`. It remains the correct path for runtime trainer/RL weight transfer; this PR does not replace it. The failing workflow is the separate, documented disk-restore path and does not require a trainer or weight-transfer engine: ```python llm.sleep(level=2) llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"]) llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights") llm.wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"]) ``` This change reuses #46725's `get_draft_model()` accessor and the same layerwise reload lifecycle used by checkpoint-format transfer engines, while keeping the checkpoint source appropriate to this workflow. This is not a duplicate of #46725: that change added externally supplied runtime draft updates, while this PR completes the separate documented disk-backed `reload_weights()` recovery path. ## Live evidence ### Qwen3.8 MTP (same-checkpoint, same-width share) Measured on an earlier MRV2-wrapper revision of this PR (same disk draft loader, layerwise lifecycle, and draft-first / target-last order) on 2x RTX 5090, TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=2`, with sleep mode enabled. Each throughput entry is the median of three 256-token HTTP generations. | State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Cold baseline | 109.4 tok/s | not recorded | — | | L2 wake cycle 1 | 108.9 tok/s (100% of baseline) | 2.17 | 4.18 s | | L2 wake cycle 2 | 104.9 tok/s (96% of baseline) | 2.43 | 4.11 s | Unpatched reproduction on that stack: 51.8 tok/s, acceptance length 1.00, zero accepted draft tokens. ### Gemma4 E2B MTP (dim-mismatched shared embeddings) Measured on this follow-up (identity detach + tied-embed sink) on the same 2x RTX 5090, TP=2, `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` + `google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant`, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=1`, sleep mode enabled. Each throughput entry is the median of three 64-token HTTP generations. Assistant `hidden_size=256`, `backbone_hidden_size=1536`. | State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Cold baseline | 297.5 tok/s | 1.50 | — | | L2 wake cycle 1 | 293.0 tok/s (98% of baseline) | 1.50 | 1.15 s | | L2 wake cycle 2 | 304.6 tok/s (102% of baseline) | 1.50 | 1.08 s | Both models used the documented staged sequence plus a prefix-cache reset. Outputs were coherent. No shape-mismatch traceback. A discard-only detach avoided the crash but left acceptance at 1.00 (tied `lm_head` never refilled); the sink is what restored 1.50. ## Tests Seven focused unit tests cover: 1. A disk-backed reload restores the draft through its configured loader and the layerwise lifecycle before reloading the target. 2. The same disk path through Model Runner V2's existing `GPUModelRunnerV1.reload_weights(self, ...)` delegate. 3. A disk-backed reload without a draft still reloads the target normally. 4. A caller-supplied weight iterator does not trigger an implicit draft reload. 5. A dim-mismatched aliased `embed_tokens` is not written; the tied draft-dim `lm_head` still receives the embed checkpoint tensor. 6. A same-width shared embed is discarded; a distinct `lm_head` is not filled from `embed_tokens`. 7. The same target `lm_head` aliased at `draft.lm_head` and every `shared_head.head` is detached (`named_modules(remove_duplicate=False)`). ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::TestReloadDraftWeights -q # 7 passed ``` ## Scope and limitations - The serving path of interest is Model Runner V2. The implementation lives in the shared `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` that V2 already calls, so a legacy V1 engine using that method also gets the disk draft reload. - Live validation covers Qwen3.8 same-checkpoint MTP and Gemma4 E2B MTP with a separate assistant checkpoint, both TP=2. EAGLE3 and DSpark were not run live. Independent drafts are unbound only when a module is the same object as the target; embed tensors are redirected to `lm_head` only when that head's weight shape differs from the shared embed. - The configured draft checkpoint remains the source of draft weights. This change does not redefine draft selection during `weights_path` model swaps. - Draft formats whose loaders do not implement `get_all_weights` raise `NotImplementedError`, matching the existing target-model disk reload. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, review-response analysis, and test orchestration. The submitter reviewed the changes and the live validation described above.

signal.title: [RFC]: First-class agentic inference support in vLLM
signal.text: # RFC: First-class agentic inference support in vLLM ## Motivation The [vLLM Agentic API project](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api) has completed an MVP supporting Codex and Claude Code with vLLM as the inference engine. It is a high-performance Rust runtime for the capabilities these clients need beyond token generation: stateful continuation, tool loops, web search, MCP, streaming, and Responses/Messages compatibility. Agentic workloads are increasingly important to llm-d and the broader serving community. The question is how vLLM and Agentic API should evolve together as these workloads become more stateful and operationally complex. Emerging capabilities such as [Computer History](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/customization/computer-history) show how agentic systems are beginning to use persistent activity, search, and external context to resume work and understand what happened across tools. vLLM already supports Responses and Messages APIs, an optional in-process Responses store, and MCP/tool-server integrations. Agentic API builds on that foundation with a broader runtime for stateful continuation, tool loops, web search, vendor-neutral integrations, and the operational needs of agentic inference workloads. These capabilities are complementary, but vLLM does not currently plan to pursue the full Agentic API scope in its existing serving surface. How should vLLM and Agentic API evolve together to support this next generation of agentic inference workloads? ## Proposed change We propose that vLLM make agentic inference a first-class supported capability by integrating more tightly with Agentic API. The project’s MVP provides a working starting point for stateful Responses and Messages APIs, tool orchestration, and vendor-neutral integrations. The options below describe different ways to bring those capabilities into the vLLM ecosystem; this RFC seeks agreement on the desired integration model and the boundaries that should remain stable. ### Goal Agentic API aims to provide a vendor-neutral integration layer connecting agentic clients to databases, third-party APIs, and external tools while preserving and optimizing vLLM’s inference capabilities. It should also provide llm-d with practical Responses API and Messages API solutions that externalize conversation state and orchestration without forcing hard affinity to the engine that served an earlier turn. ### Scope and boundary The boundary is intentional: vLLM Core focuses on model execution, scheduling, batching, tokenization, rendering, parsing, and structured decoding; Agentic API focuses on state, external integrations, tool orchestration, and client compatibility. The goal is to make these capabilities more tightly integrated and accessible through the vLLM ecosystem. ### Desired outcome The goal is for the vLLM ecosystem to expose a first-class agentic inference experience by building on vLLM’s existing Responses, Messages, response-store, and MCP/tool-server support and integrating the broader capabilities provided by Agentic API. This RFC seeks alignment on how Agentic API and vLLM should become more tightly integrated to reach that goal. ## Options These options are not mutually exclusive. A first-class boundary could be the near-term step before deciding whether to merge or formally package Agentic API with vLLM. | Option | Description | Proposed change | Main tradeoff | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **1. Merge** | Move Agentic API into vLLM Core. | Merge the code, consolidate APIs and tests, and document the agentic serving experience in vLLM. | One project and release process, but vLLM takes on persistence, integrations, and workflow orchestration. | | **2. Remain separate** | Continue with today’s architecture and independent evolution. | Improve documentation, publish a dedicated Agentic API website or landing page, and clearly document how it integrates with vLLM. | Clear boundaries, but leaves the broader agentic workload experience outside vLLM’s existing serving surface and risks capability gaps and compatibility drift. | | **3. Official dependency** | Keep a separate repository, but officially distribute or depend on Agentic API for Responses and agentic inference. | Add supported packaging and version compatibility, vLLM documentation and examples, and a maintained integration path. | Better integration, but tighter versioning and packaging coupling. | | **4. First-class runtime boundary** | Keep the repositories separate while defining supported interfaces, compatibility guarantees, and shared tests. | Establish shared contracts, conformance tests, release coordination, and cross-linked documentation or landing pages. | Preserves flexibility, but requires sustained coordination. | ## Key questions 1. How should vLLM extend its existing Responses, Messages, response-store, and MCP/tool-server support to provide a broader agentic inference experience? 2. What should agentic applications, including coding harnesses, be able to rely on from the vLLM ecosystem? 3. Which responsibilities should remain separate even if the projects are distributed together? 4. What interfaces and tests should vLLM, Agentic API, and llm-d share? ## Additional context - [vLLM Responses API and Tool Calling lookahead (#34857)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34857) - [vLLM session-centric KV-cache orchestration (#48501)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48501) - [vLLM Agentic API Codex CLI integration (#54)](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/issues/54) - [vLLM Agentic API response-store semantics (#14)](https://github.com/vllm-project/agentic-api/issues/14) - [vLLM multi-turn Responses API support (#33089)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33089) - [vLLM Rust frontend / Anthropic Messages RFC (#47753)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47753) - [llm-d-router session-centric KV lifecycle orchestration (#1979)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1979) - [llm-d-router external Responses state store (#1104)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1104) - [llm-d-router Session Control Protocol (#2003)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/2003) - [llm-d-router agentic routing profiles (#1867)](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1867) ## Recommended direction The long-term goal should be for vLLM to provide a first-class agentic serving experience that builds on its existing Responses, Messages, response-store, and MCP/tool-server support and adds the orchestration and integrations needed by real agentic workloads. The immediate goal is tighter integration between Agentic API and vLLM Core so that vLLM’s support for agentic workloads is visible and accessible throughout the ecosystem. The options above provide several paths to that outcome, from merging the projects to establishing an officially supported dependency or first-class integration contract. ## CC list @qandrew @vMaroon @blasrodri @BugenZhao @njhill @chaunceyjiang @mgoin @bbrowning @robertgshaw2-redhat @noobHappylife @maralbahari @tjtanaa @ashwing

signal.title: [Bugfix] Guard missing end_token substring in streaming reasoning parsers
signal.text: ## Motivation In `BaseThinkingReasoningParser` and `DeepSeekR1ReasoningParser`, when `end_token_id` is present in `delta_token_ids`, `delta_text.find(self.end_token)` is called to split reasoning and content text. If `self.end_token` literal string is not present in `delta_text` (e.g. during multi-token deltas where the special token is detokenized as empty or formatted separately), `find()` returns `-1`. Previously, slicing `delta_text[:end_index]` evaluated to `delta_text[:-1]`, silently clipping the last character off the reasoning buffer and slicing into `content`. ## Proposed Changes - Added presence check `if end_index != -1:` before slicing `delta_text` in `BaseThinkingReasoningParser` and `DeepSeekR1ReasoningParser`. - If `end_index == -1`, safely keeps `reasoning = delta_text` without character truncation. - Added unit test `test_end_token_id_without_literal_substring` in `tests/reasoning/test_base_thinking_reasoning_parser.py` covering multi-token delta handling.
signal.author: arnavahire19

signal.title: [Bug]: Prefill misdispatched into spec-decode FULL cudagraph when prompt length == 1 + num_speculative_tokens → silent GDN state loss, garbage output (hybrid/Qwen3-Next models)
signal.text: ## Summary When speculative decoding is enabled, a **prefill** whose scheduled token count happens to equal `uniform_decode_query_len * num_reqs` is misclassified as a uniform-decode batch and dispatched into the **FULL cudagraph captured for spec-decode**. For hybrid models with GDN/linear-attention layers (e.g. Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5-MoE), this silently skips **all recurrent-state writes** for that request: every subsequent decode step then computes from a zero initial state, producing deterministic garbage output and a collapsed draft acceptance rate. The trigger is absurdly easy to hit: with `num_speculative_tokens=2`, **any 3-token prompt** (e.g. the Chinese prompt `中国的首都是` under the Qwen tokenizer) poisons the request from its very first step. I have root-caused this with per-block checksums of the GDN state pools and verified a one-line-of-logic fix. Code on current `main` is identical to what I debugged on 0.27.1. ## Root cause `GPUModelRunner._is_uniform_decode` (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py) is a **pure shape check**: ```python return ( ((max_num_scheduled_tokens == uniform_decode_query_len) and (num_tokens == max_num_scheduled_tokens * num_reqs)) if force_uniform_decode is None else force_uniform_decode ) ``` With MTP `k=2`, `uniform_decode_query_len = 1 + 2 = 3`. A virgin single request whose prompt is exactly 3 tokens gives `max_num_scheduled_tokens == 3` and `num_tokens == 3 * 1`, so the **prefill** is classified as uniform decode and `cudagraph_dispatcher.dispatch(..., uniform_decode=True)` routes it into the FULL graph captured for spec-decode. The failure mechanism for GDN layers: 1. The GDN metadata builder correctly classifies the step as a prefill (`num_prefills=1, num_spec_decodes=0`), **but** the persistent-buffer refresh in `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` only happens in the spec/decode branches (gated on `num_prefills == 0`). A prefill build never touches the persistent buffers. 2. The FULL graph replays with **stale capture-time metadata**: `spec_state_indices_tensor` still holds `0 == NULL_BLOCK_ID` from `build_for_cudagraph_capture`. 3. The FLA kernels (`fused_recurrent`, `fused_sigmoid_gating`) and `causal_conv1d_update` all have null-block guards that **silently skip stores** when the state index is `NULL_BLOCK_ID` — correct padding hygiene, but here it swallows the entire prefill state write. 4. The request's conv/SSM states stay zero forever. The first sampled token already diverges; everything after is computed from a wrong recurrent state → deterministic garbage, and the drafter (whose own state is equally poisoned) gets ~0% acceptance. ## Measured evidence Same weights, same 3-token greedy prompt, per-block checksums of the GDN state pools after the prefill step (instrumented `execute_model` with `torch.cuda.synchronize`): | Config | state blocks written by the prefill | output | |---|---|---| | `PIECEWISE` (healthy) | `{1, 4, 7}` (target model, matching the request's block-table rows) + `{10}` (draft) | correct, deterministic | | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (bug) | **only `{10}`** (draft runs piecewise); target blocks stay all-zero | deterministic garbage from token 1 | Weight checksum identical in both boots; capture leaves the pools clean (all-zero before the first real step in both). Acceptance rate on mixed probes: 12% (bug) vs 79% (fixed/piecewise/eager). This also explains the confusing symptom pattern that made the bug look like a "speculative rejection/rollback corruption" (#40880-style reports): prompts that don't tokenize to exactly `1+k` tokens are dispatched normally and stay healthy, genuine uniform-decode FULL replays are correct (the spec branch does refresh persistent buffers), and the garbage is byte-identical across reboots because everything is deterministic. ## Reproduction vLLM 0.27.1 (logic identical on current main), Qwen3.5-MoE hybrid (30 GDN + 10 full-attn layers), 1 GPU: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-MoE-FP8 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "...", "prompt": "中国的首都是", "max_tokens": 24, "temperature": 0}' # prompt must tokenize to exactly (1 + num_speculative_tokens) tokens; garbage output. # Same request with cudagraph_mode PIECEWISE or --enforce-eager → correct output. ``` Note the aliasing is generic: any batch of fresh `num_reqs` prompts scheduled as exactly `(1+k)` tokens each hits the same path, and `q_len==1` aliasing with 1-token prompts at `k=0` is possible in principle too. ## Suggested fix (verified locally) Uniform-decode classification should require every request in the batch to actually be **past its prompt**, not just match the shape: ```python def _is_uniform_decode(self, *, max_num_scheduled_tokens, uniform_decode_query_len, num_tokens, num_reqs, force_uniform_decode=None): if force_uniform_decode is not None: # keep capture-path bypass return force_uniform_decode if not (max_num_scheduled_tokens == uniform_decode_query_len and num_tokens == max_num_scheduled_tokens * num_reqs): return False ib = self.input_batch return bool((ib.num_computed_tokens_cpu[:num_reqs] >= ib.num_prompt_tokens[:num_reqs]).all()) ``` Aliased prefill batches then fall back to the PIECEWISE path (which is where prefills belong anyway); genuine uniform decodes keep the FULL graph. Verified on my deployment: garbage gone (byte-exact vs piecewise golden on the trap prompt), acceptance restored 12%→79%, no measurable perf regression (FULL graph retained for real decode batches; a 100k-context needle gate and short-decode throughput both match or beat the eager baseline). ## Related issues - #28015 — the inverse aliasing (uniform-decode batches mis-shaped by padding for MLA backends); same root class: shape-only dispatch classification. - #40880 / #40914 — Qwen3-Next hybrid × MTP × cudagraph degraded output; the fix merged there was TurboQuant-specific and this mechanism explains the remaining reports. - #34571, #39273, vllm-ascend#7148 — adjacent mamba/GDN spec-decode state-corruption reports. ## Environment vLLM 0.27.1 (bug verified byte-identical in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` on current main), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration, 30 GDN + 10 full-attn), MTP k=2, fp8 KV, single ROCm gfx1151 GPU — the bug is in platform-independent dispatch logic (also reproduced with two different attention backends).

signal.title: [Bugfix][Parser] qwen3: start in CONTENT when the prompt closed the think block
signal.text:
## Purpose Fixes #53284. With `--reasoning-parser qwen3`, a request whose rendered prompt already ends with a **closed** think block gets its whole answer returned as `message.reasoning` with `content: null`, and loses the answer entirely under `include_reasoning=false`. `Qwen3Parser.__init__` decides the engine's initial state from `chat_template_kwargs["enable_thinking"]` alone, and nothing looks at the prompt: ```python self.thinking_enabled = chat_kwargs.get("enable_thinking", True) ... initial_state=ParserState.REASONING if thinking else ParserState.CONTENT ``` A chat template is free to close the think block for other reasons. The widely used community templates for Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 do it for `chat_template_kwargs: {"reasoning_effort": "none"}`, for an inline `<|think_off|>` tag in the user message, and for `auto_disable_thinking_with_tools=true`. In every one of those cases the prompt ends with ``` <|im_start|>assistant <think> </think> ``` so the model has nothing left to close and emits its answer as plain text. The engine, still in `REASONING`, turns every token into a `REASONING_CHUNK`, and `finish()` only appends `REASONING_END`. This is the same hook Gemma4 already overrides for the opposite polarity: a prompt ending *inside* an open reasoning block pre-initialises to `REASONING` (#45834). Qwen3 had no override for "prompt ends with a *closed* block", which is why the base no-op in `ParserEngine.adjust_initial_state_from_prompt` applied. ## Changes `Qwen3Parser.adjust_initial_state_from_prompt` resets the engine to `CONTENT` when the prompt already ended reasoning, and latches `_streaming_initialized` so a later default `initialize_streaming()` cannot restore the configured state. That is the same three-line shape as `Gemma4Parser`'s override. The predicate needs no new logic. `is_reasoning_end` already scans back to the last think marker, so: | prompt tail | `is_reasoning_end` | initial state | |---|---|---| | `<think>
` (thinking on) | `False` | `REASONING`, unchanged | | `<think>

</think>

` (template closed it) | `True` | `CONTENT` | | earlier turn's `</think>`, then this turn's `<think>` | `False` | `REASONING`, unchanged | | paired `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` before the generation `<think>` | `False` | `REASONING`, unchanged | ## Scope, and what this does not cover This fixes the **engine** path, which is `--reasoning-parser qwen3` together with `--tool-call-parser qwen3_xml` or `qwen3_coder`, the recommended Qwen3.x configuration: `ParserManager.get_parser` returns the `Qwen3Parser` engine itself, and `ParserEngine.parse_delta` calls the prompt hook. It does not fix the non-streaming half of #53284, and I want to be explicit about that rather than let it read as a complete fix. `Parser.parse` and `ParserEngine.parse` take no `prompt_token_ids`, so nothing can seed them from the prompt today. #50015 is already adding exactly that plumbing for the Gemma4 case, so I have deliberately not duplicated it here. Worth flagging for whoever reviews both: #50015 calls the hook only when `not is_reasoning_end(prompt_token_ids)`, which is the Gemma4 polarity, so this Qwen3 case would still be skipped on the non-streaming path even after it lands. That guard likely wants to widen once both are in, but that is a call for #50015, not something to pre-empt from here. This change is complementary either way and touches no file #50015 touches. `--reasoning-parser qwen3` **alone** already streams correctly, because `Parser.parse_delta` checks `is_reasoning_end(prompt_token_ids)` before the first delta and marks reasoning ended. That path does not reach this hook, so it is unaffected. ## Test Plan Four tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3_reasoning.py` under `TestPromptClosedThinkBlock`, driving `Qwen3Parser.parse_delta` with `prompt_token_ids` against the file's existing mock tokenizer: 1. prompt ending in a closed think block streams the answer as `content`, with `reasoning` None (fails without this change) 2. control: an open `<think>` tail still streams as `reasoning` 3. control: a previous turn's `</think>` in the history does not disable the new turn 4. control: no `prompt_token_ids` keeps the configured initial state ## Test Result **I could not run the suite locally and do not want to imply otherwise.** This is a macOS box with no vLLM build; `import vllm.parser.qwen3` segfaults here (exit 139) before any test collects, so `tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3_reasoning.py` never ran on my machine. CI is the test runner for this change, and that file is the one to watch. What I did verify locally, by reading the code rather than executing it: - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both touched files. - Both files parse (`ast.parse`). - The `is_reasoning_end` table above is read off `ParserEngine.is_reasoning_end` (backwards scan, first of `</think>` / `<think>` wins) and `Qwen3Parser.is_reasoning_end` (unpaired `<tool_call>`, returning False as soon as it sees the reasoning start token). The existing tests in `TestIsReasoningEnd` already pin every row of it. The runtime symptom in #53284 was reproduced by a third party on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8`; neither the reporter nor I ran a GPU server for it. AI assistance was used in preparing this change.

signal.title: [CPU][GDN] Support NIXL DS convolution-state layout
signal.text: # [CPU][GDN] Support NIXL DS convolution-state layout ## Summary Make CPU GDN convolution and recurrent-state handling compatible with both the NIXL-required DS physical layout and the existing SD layout. The branch: - selects DS convolution-state storage automatically when a CPU KV-transfer configuration uses NIXL; - validates and materializes CPU GDN recurrent inputs and state views with dense inner strides before entering the native CPU kernels; - extends native CPU convolution dispatch to accept both SD and DS state layouts across prefill, decode, speculative, and multi-token update paths; ## Why NIXL's Mamba descriptors interpret the convolution state as DS `[conv_dim_local, conv_rows]`, while the CPU GDN path historically assumed an SD-compatible view in several native-convolution branches. That mismatch made the automatically selected NIXL cache layout incompatible with native CPU convolution and required layout-specific assertions or fallback behavior. ## Duplicate-work Check Open PR [#49650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49650), `[CPU][Spec Decode] Centralize CPU causal-conv dispatch`, is related but not a duplicate. It centralizes Python-side causal-convolution dispatch for speculative decoding. This PR instead adds CPU platform layout selection, NIXL layout validation, recurrent-state staging, and native `conv.cpp` support for both SD and DS stride layouts. ## Test Plan CPU GDN correctness suite: ```bash OMP_NUM_THREADS=32 numactl --physcpubind=160-191 -N 5 -m 5 \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py -q ``` ## Test Result `158 passed, 16 warnings in 21.75s` in `tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py`. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for implementation, source review, build/test verification, upstream overlap research, and drafting. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines and is responsible for understanding and defending the complete branch. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Model] Enable batch-invariant mixed decode and prefill for Qwen GDN
signal.text: Fixes #48613. Related to #42960 and #45819. ## What Enable `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` for Qwen GDN models on CUDA SM90+. This PR makes three Qwen GDN execution choices independent of unrelated requests: - cached decode rows use packed recurrent decode in both decode-only and mixed decode-plus-prefill steps; - FlashInfer prefill uses one implementation under BIC instead of selecting context parallelism from batch shape; - non-final chunked-prefill calls end on the 64-token arithmetic grid used by the GDN chunk kernel. The shared Kimi and Olmo GDN backend remains unsupported. ## Why Qwen3.5 interleaves regular attention with Gated DeltaNet layers. vLLM currently refuses to initialize these models in batch-invariant mode because `GDN_ATTN` does not declare BIC support. Allowing the backend through that check was not sufficient. I found three ways that traffic shape could change the arithmetic used for a target request. First, a cached decode row changed recurrent kernels when a fresh prefill arrived in the same step: ```text decode-only: cached row -> packed recurrent decode mixed: cached row -> fused recurrent update ``` Second, FlashInfer GDN prefill used `use_cp="auto"`. On H100, repeating the same 64-token sequence at batch sizes 1 and 8 changed 4,284 of 131,072 output values and produced a maximum state difference of 0.002197265625. Third, scheduler chunk boundaries changed the recurrence graph. One 192-token prefill and three state-carry calls of 64 tokens were bitwise equal. Splitting the same tensors at `[73, 128, 192]` changed 54,452 output elements and 131,061 final-state elements in the Triton probe. FlashInfer showed the same boundary dependence. ## How The Qwen-specific backend declares BIC support on CUDA SM90+. The shared GDN backend stays fail-closed because its other model implementations have not been validated. Cached rows at the front of a mixed batch call the same packed recurrent decode helper used by decode-only steps. Fresh rows continue through the existing prefill path. When BIC is enabled, FlashInfer prefill uses `use_cp=False`. Normal serving keeps automatic selection. The Qwen backend also advertises `FLA_CHUNK_SIZE=64` as its canonical BIC prefill partition. The scheduler rounds non-final recurrent prefill calls down to that absolute grid. The final tail stays in the last call, so a 193-token prompt can run as `64 + 64 + 65`. An effective scheduler budget or long-prefill threshold below 64 fails at startup. Mamba cache alignment also fails closed for this path: its current 544-token cache grid is incompatible with the 64-token arithmetic grid and needs separate state-materialization work. ## Tests The retained regressions cover the three boundaries: - decode output and recurrent state are exactly equal when cached rows run alone or at the front of a mixed batch; - FlashInfer prefill output and state are exactly equal at batch sizes 1 and 8; - one-shot and 64-token state-carry prefills are exactly equal for each supported platform backend; - an online test starts a 193-token target while another request is decoding, forcing chunked prefill to share a 128-token scheduler budget. The online test is non-vacuous. Removing only the scheduler alignment keeps the generated token IDs equal but changes the first selected-token logprob from `-0.3462445139` to `-0.3380798995`. The patched branch matches all target tokens and selected-token logprobs exactly. Latest H100 targeted results: ```text scheduler canonical-chunk regression: 1 passed GDN mixed-decode, batch-shape, and partition regressions: 4 passed online chunked-prefill regression: 1 passed ruff and diff checks: passed ``` Before the chunked-prefill extension, the full H100 BIC Buildkite command sequence passed 500 tests in 29m19s. The updated H100 and B200 jobs are CI gates for the current branch; I do not have direct access to a B200 runner. ## Online serving validation For the mixed decode change, I ran `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` on one H100 with TP 1, chunked prefill enabled, prefix caching disabled, and concurrency up to 8. Poisson background traffic used 116, 321, and 1,059-token prompts while target requests generated 16, 64, or 128 tokens. The run completed 823 background requests and 69 target requests. Scheduler traces showed 36 target requests crossing 71 mixed decode-and-prefill steps. ```text request failures: 0 generated-token mismatches: 0 selected-token-logprob mismatches: 0 top-logprob-map mismatches: 0 maximum selected-token-logprob diff: 0.0 ``` ## Performance The mixed-decode route improved BIC performance in the original fixed serving benchmark: | Mode | Output tok/s | p50 TTFT | p50 ITL | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | upstream, normal | 252.87 | 107.94 ms | 29.56 ms | | patched, normal | 252.37 | 106.34 ms | 29.65 ms | | support-only BIC | 193.35 | 134.42 ms | 39.01 ms | | patched BIC | 206.39 | 127.29 ms | 36.54 ms | Normal-serving output throughput changed by -0.20%. The mixed-route patch improved BIC output throughput by 6.74% over support-only. For canonical chunked prefill, I ran 24 concurrent ragged requests containing 27,540 prompt tokens and 192 output tokens with an 8,192-token scheduler budget: | Mode | Request throughput, run 1 | Request throughput, run 2 | | --- | ---: | ---: | | mixed-route BIC without alignment | 21.68 req/s | 21.73 req/s | | canonical chunk BIC | 20.79 req/s | 21.01 req/s | Canonical chunking retained 96.3% of mean throughput. At the deliberately small 128-token test budget it retained about 61%, since a step can leave up to 63 token slots unused. ## Scope Validated here: - Qwen GDN on CUDA SM90+ - unquantized execution - TP 1 - mixed decode and prefill - chunked prefill with prefix caching disabled - no speculative decoding Out of scope: - tensor-parallel and expert-parallel execution - prefix caching - speculative decoding - quantized Qwen GDN execution - SM80, ROCm, Kimi, Olmo, and other GDN implementations - global BIC matmul performance TP, EP, and prefix-caching work will be submitted separately once each path has an isolated regression and public-model validation. This contribution was developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex. I reviewed the final diff and remain responsible for the implementation and results.
