signal.title: [Docs] Document 7 undocumented kv_cache_dtype values
signal.text: ## Summary `docs/features/quantization/quantized_kvcache.md`'s `kv_cache_dtype` options list covers 3 of the 17 values `CacheDType` (`vllm/config/cache.py`) actually supports. This documents 7 of the remaining 11: `fp8_inc`, `fp8_ds_mla`, `int4_per_token_head`, `int8_per_token_head`, `fp8_per_token_head`, `nvfp4`, `nvfp4_4over6`. Scoped to these 7 specifically because the other 4 undocumented values are the `turboquant_*` family, already the subject of the open (stalled, needs-rebase) #45422 — adding them here would collide with that PR. ## Why this doesn't duplicate an existing PR Checked #49050 (open — despite how it's been described elsewhere, its actual diff only adds a performance section and swaps an example model, it doesn't touch this options list) and #45422 (open, TurboQuant-only, explicitly excluded from this PR's scope for that reason). Searched for any other open PR touching `quantized_kvcache.md`, `nvfp4 docs`, or `per_token_head docs` — no other open PR documents these 7 values in this file. (#48782 is an NVFP4 doc PR but touches a different file, `modelopt.md`, about ModelOpt's weight quantization, unrelated to KV-cache dtypes.) ## How each was verified All 7 documented from source (no hardware available to verify beyond that) — grepped every implementation site for each dtype and cross-checked backend-support lists and existing docstrings against `vllm/config/cache.py`, `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py`, `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/backends/{triton_attn,flashinfer}.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/{flashmla_sparse,flashinfer_mla_sparse}.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/ops/int4_per_token_head.py`, and `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/inc.py`. Notable corrections from an early draft, caught during review before submission: - `fp8_inc` is not "calibrated via Intel Neural Compressor" — INC's actual code path is model-weight quantization, not KV-cache calibration. Worded to state only what's confirmed. - `fp8_ds_mla`'s byte layout is model-specific, not universal: DeepSeek-V3.2 uses 656 bytes (512 NoPE + 16 scale + 128 RoPE), DeepSeek-V4 uses a different 584-byte layout (448 NoPE + 128 RoPE + 8 scale, different scale format). Both are now called out explicitly. - `nvfp4`/`nvfp4_4over6` require FlashInfer's TensorRT-LLM-gen kernel path on SM100 (Blackwell datacenter GPUs) specifically, not just "the FlashInfer backend" generally. - Added the CUDA SM89+ requirement for `fp8_per_token_head` and the power-of-two head-dimension constraint for `int4_per_token_head`'s Hadamard transform, both enforced in source but missing from the first draft. - "per-(token, head)" corrected to "per-(token, KV head)" throughout — this is per-KV-head granularity, not per-query-head. ## Test Plan Docs-only change, no code touched. Ran `npx markdownlint-cli2@0.21.0` (the exact version pinned in this repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) against the file with `--fix`: 0 errors, 0 changes beyond the content edit. ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance (Claude) was used to research the source locations for each dtype and draft this documentation, and a second AI review pass (Codex, run independently against the live source) was used specifically to adversarially check the draft's technical claims — it caught the five corrections listed above before this was submitted. I independently re-verified each of those corrections against the cited source lines myself, and reviewed every line of the diff.

It does not match a clean run with no connector, even though the rejected load moved no data. Recovery reports success (`Recovered from KV load failure: 1 request(s) rescheduled`), but the decoded result is garbage under synchronous scheduling and an offset continuation under asynchronous scheduling. This also breaks the invariant that the `examples/disaggregated/kv_load_failure_recovery_offline` example checks, which is a `cmp -s` of the recovered output against the baseline. That example runs Llama-3.2-1B, which uses the V2 runner, but it is an example script that is not run in CI, so the regression went unnoticed. ### Setup - vLLM `0.25.1`. The affected code is byte-identical on `main`. - The V2 GPU model runner, which is the default for any non-MoE generative model (Qwen3, Llama-3.2, and similar). The startup log shows `Using V2 Model Runner`. - Single GPU, TP=1, FlashAttention-2, `--enforce-eager`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. - A custom `KVConnectorBase_V1` (`kv_role="kv_both"`) doing a synchronous load (`get_num_new_matched_tokens` returns `load_async=False`), with `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`. The two scheduling modes fail differently. They share a root cause, and async scheduling adds a second problem on top of it: | Run | Scheduling | Output (greedy, prompt "...The capital of Italy is") | |-----|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------| | baseline (no connector) | either | `[' Rome', ',', ' and', ' the', ' capital', ' of', ' Spain', ' is']` | | reject, then recompute | sync (`--no-async-scheduling`) | `' tntn tntn tnt'` (garbage) | | reject, then recompute | async (default) | `' country in Europe. It is known for'` (wrong) | The exact corruption depends on the residual KV. If the promised-but-never-filled prefix block happens to hold usable stale KV, the output can read like a coherent one-token shift; otherwise it is garbage. ## Minimal reproduction A connector that promises a block-aligned prefix synchronously, then rejects the load: ```python # rogue_connector.py (runs on 0.25.1 and main; kv_role=kv_both) from dataclasses import dataclass, field from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base import ( KVConnectorBase_V1, KVConnectorMetadata, KVConnectorRole, ) if TYPE_CHECKING: from vllm.config import VllmConfig from vllm.forward_context import ForwardContext from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheBlocks from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import SchedulerOutput from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVCacheConfig from vllm.v1.request import Request @dataclass class RogueMetadata(KVConnectorMetadata): reqs: list[tuple[str, list[int]]] = field(default_factory=list) class RogueSyncRejectConnector(KVConnectorBase_V1): def __init__(self, vllm_config, role, kv_cache_config): super().__init__(vllm_config=vllm_config, role=role, kv_cache_config=kv_cache_config) self._block_size = vllm_config.cache_config.block_size self._need_load: dict[str, bool] = {} self._load_errors: set[int] = set() def get_num_new_matched_tokens(self, request, num_computed_tokens): n = len(request.prompt_token_ids or []) matched = ((n - 1) // self._block_size) * self._block_size new = matched - num_computed_tokens return (new, False) if new > 0 else (0, False) # SYNC load def update_state_after_alloc(self, request, blocks, num_external_tokens): if num_external_tokens > 0: self._need_load[request.request_id] = True def build_connector_meta(self, scheduler_output): meta = RogueMetadata() for r in scheduler_output.scheduled_new_reqs: if r.req_id in self._need_load: meta.reqs.append((r.req_id, list(r.block_ids[0]))) self._need_load.clear() return meta def start_load_kv(self, forward_context, **kwargs): # REJECT: load nothing meta = self._get_connector_metadata() for _rid, block_ids in meta.reqs: self._load_errors.update(block_ids) def get_block_ids_with_load_errors(self): errs, self._load_errors = self._load_errors, set() return errs def wait_for_layer_load(self, layer_name): return def save_kv_layer(self, layer_name, kv_layer, attn_metadata, **kwargs): return def wait_for_save(self): return ``` ```bash PYTHONPATH=. vllm serve facebook/opt-125m --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"RogueSyncRejectConnector","kv_connector_module_path":"rogue_connector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute"}' # send a fresh prompt, temperature 0; diff the greedy output against a server started # WITHOUT the connector. Add --no-async-scheduling for the sync case. ``` Expected: the recompute output equals the no-connector baseline, since the rejected load contributed no KV. Actual: garbage under sync scheduling, and an offset continuation under async scheduling. ## Root cause (traced with per-step instrumentation) ### Part 1 worker side, affects both scheduling modes. In the V2 runner, `RequestState.num_computed_tokens` is a GPU-backed `StagedWriteTensor` alongside an optimistic CPU mirror (`num_computed_tokens_np`), and the GPU copy is advanced forward-only by `post_update_num_computed_tokens`. A recompute truncates `num_computed_tokens` backward, but `GPUModelRunner.update_requests` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) writes that only to the CPU mirror, so the GPU tensor stays stale. `prepare_prefill_inputs` and `prepare_pos_seq_lens` then read the stale GPU value and gather the recompute's input tokens and positions from the wrong offset. On the instrumented recompute step under sync scheduling, `num_computed=0` but `gpu_num_computed=19`, and `input_ids` is `[<3 tail tokens>, <16 uninitialized garbage>]` instead of the real prompt. ### Part 2 Scheduler side, async scheduling only. Under async scheduling the failed request has in-flight output frames reserved via `num_output_placeholders`, and `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`) never rolls them back, so the recompute is scheduled with extra placeholder tokens (`num_scheduled = num_tokens + num_output_placeholders`) and appends garbage tokens past the prompt. ## Suggested fix Two small changes. Both functions are byte-identical between 0.25.1 and `main`: 1. In `GPUModelRunner.update_requests`, when `num_computed_tokens` is a backward jump, push it to the GPU tensor with `num_computed_tokens.stage_write_elem` followed by `apply_write`. 2. In `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks`, for each affected request, roll back `num_output_placeholders` and add `num_output_placeholders - 1` to `async_tokens_to_discard`. This mirrors the preemption handling in `reset_prefix_cache`. Verified live (Qwen3-8B-AWQ, RTX 5090, V2 runner) and independently re-verified on a clean install. With both fixes, the reject-then-recompute output is byte-identical to the no-connector baseline under both `--async-scheduling` and `--no-async-scheduling`, with the recovery path confirmed to fire. A PR follows. ### Scope and caveats - **Part 1** is precisely scoped: the backward-jump guard can only fire on the recompute path. Resumed and preempted requests take the V2 new-request path (they are not in `scheduled_cached_reqs`), and decode, chunked prefill, and spec decode advance `num_computed_tokens` strictly forward, so the `<` comparison never trips there. The staged GPU write does not collide with `post_update_num_computed_tokens` (a Triton kernel), and `apply_write` is idempotent and guarded. - **Part 2**'s `num_output_placeholders - 1` is correct only when each in-flight frame carries one token. `num_output_placeholders` is incremented in tokens (`num_sampled_tokens_per_step + cur_num_spec_tokens`), but `async_tokens_to_discard` is consumed one per frame. So `- 1` is exact for the vanilla case and for pipeline parallelism, since the increment has no PP term. With speculative decoding or diffusion a frame carries `1 + k` tokens, so `- 1` over-discards by `k` and shifts the output. The proposed fix scopes correctness to the non-spec-decode and non-diffusion case; a general fix needs the true in-flight frame count. Note that simply zeroing the counter and discarding nothing would under-discard at pipeline-parallel depth greater than 1. - Related and pre-existing: the same token-versus-frame conflation already exists in `reset_prefix_cache` (`async_tokens_to_discard = num_output_placeholders`, with the comment "1 + spec/PP frames"), which would likewise over-discard under speculative decoding. ## Workaround Promise the load as asynchronous, so `get_num_new_matched_tokens` returns `(N, True)`. The request then parks in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` with `num_new_tokens=0`, so the tail is never forwarded before the load resolves, and a reject recomputes cleanly. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Do not report a tool call when none could be parsed
signal.text: ## Purpose The DeepSeek V3.1 and ERNIE 4.5 tool parsers report `tools_called=True` even when they parsed zero tool calls. The visible effect is that the assistant message gets truncated at the start token. Both take the same shape. `extract_tool_calls` checks that the start token is in the output, runs a regex over it, and then returns `tools_called=True` with whatever the regex produced. When the regex matches nothing, that flag is wrong. This breaks the invariant the test helper already asserts in `tests/tool_parsers/utils.py`: ```python assert extracted.tools_called == bool(extracted.tool_calls) ``` ### What the wrong flag actually causes `chat_completion/serving.py` recomputes `auto_tools_called` from `len(tool_calls)`, so the response does not gain a bogus tool call and `finish_reason` stays correct. The damage happens earlier, in the auto tool choice branch of `DelegatingParser._extract_tool_calls` (`vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`), which branches on the parser flag: ```python if tool_call_info is not None and tool_call_info.tools_called: tool_calls.extend(...) # nothing to add content = tool_call_info.content # truncated content wins else: # No tool calls. Original content is kept. ``` Because the flag is `True`, the truncated content replaces the real content. Content served through that path, with `--enable-auto-tool-choice`: | Parser | Model output | Content on main | With this PR | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `ernie45` | `I could call <tool_call> here but let me answer directly instead.` | `I could call ` | full text | | `ernie45` | `Checking now.\n<tool_call>{"name": "get_weather", "argum` | `Checking now.` | full text | | `deepseek_v31` | `Let me look that up.<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>get_weather` | `Let me look that up.` | full text | ERNIE is the easiest one to hit, because its start token is the bare string `<tool_call>`. A model that writes that token in ordinary prose has its answer cut off mid sentence. A generation that stops part way through a tool call block, for example on `max_tokens`, hits the same path in both parsers. Both parsers now return `tools_called=False` with the full output as content when nothing parses, which is what these same functions already do in their exception handler. Valid tool calls are unaffected. This matches `tools_called=len(tool_calls) > 0` as already used in `cohere_command`, `hunyuan_a13b`, `step3p5` and `xlam`. ### Not a duplicate `#48367` fixes the same class of bug in `deepseekv3_tool_parser.py`. This PR does not touch that file, and neither parser here is covered by it. I found no open PR or issue for the V3.1 or ERNIE 4.5 parsers. Searched open PRs for `deepseekv31`, `deepseek_v31 tool parser`, `ernie45 tool parser`, `ernie tool` and `tools_called`, and open issues for the same terms. I found these two by checking every registered tool parser against the invariant above, rather than from an existing report. ## Test Plan ``` pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_ernie45_moe_tool_parser.py pytest tests/tool_parsers/ ruff check <changed files> ruff format --check <changed files> ``` Added `test_extract_tool_calls_unparsable_block` to both test files, covering a start token in prose and a truncated block. ## Test Result Targeted files, with the fix: ``` 13 passed ``` Same tests with the source change reverted and the new tests kept: ``` 4 failed, 9 passed ``` Full tool parser suite, with the fix: ``` 615 passed, 3 skipped, 34 xfailed, 25 errors ``` No failures. The 25 errors are all local environment problems, not test failures: gated Hugging Face repos returning 401 for `meta-llama`, and the optional `cohere_melody` and Rust parser extensions not being installed. They are unrelated to these files and reproduce on an unmodified checkout. The content table above was produced by running both parsers through the same branch logic quoted from `_extract_tool_calls`, once on this branch and once with the two parser files reverted to main. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on all four files. No accuracy or performance testing was run. This only changes what the parser reports for output it already failed to parse, so it does not affect model outputs, kernels or scheduling. ## Note AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, and can explain the change.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fall back to native sampling when FlashInfer cannot target the GPU
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #42393. On SM 12.x GPUs with a CUDA toolkit older than 12.9 (e.g. RTX 5090 + nvcc 12.8), FlashInfer swallows the real arch-detection error while building its compilation context: `_normalize_cuda_arch` raises `"SM 12.x requires CUDA >= 12.9"`, but the `except Exception` in `CompilationContext.__init__` downgrades it to a warning and leaves `TARGET_CUDA_ARCHS` empty. Every subsequent JIT spec then fails `check_cuda_arch()` with a misleading: ``` RuntimeError: FlashInfer requires GPUs with sm75 or higher ``` Since the FlashInfer top-p/top-k sampler is enabled by default on CUDA, this kills the engine during startup profiling — the server never comes up, regardless of the attention backend selected (the reporter was using `--attention-backend flash_attn`). Changes: - Add `_flashinfer_jit_unsupported_reason()` to the sampler gate in `vllm/v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_sampler.py`: probe FlashInfer's `check_cuda_arch()`, and when it fails, re-derive the underlying reason by calling `CompilationContext._normalize_cuda_arch` with the current device capability — so the true message (e.g. `"SM 12.x requires CUDA >= 12.9"`) is produced by FlashInfer itself rather than duplicating its version rules in vLLM. - The existing gate machinery then does the rest: fall back to native sampling with a clear warning by default, or raise an actionable error if the user explicitly set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=1`. - The probe is defensive against FlashInfer refactors: if the internals move, it keeps the original error message or skips the check entirely (`ImportError` → no gating change). The root cause (swallowed exception) lives in FlashInfer — flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3675 and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3945 track the same symptom upstream. This PR makes vLLM degrade gracefully on affected systems either way. The rejection sampler is pure torch, so speculative-decoding configs (as in the issue report) are fully covered by fixing this gate. ## Test Plan - Unit (mocks the FlashInfer failure mode, so it runs anywhere): ```bash pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py -k fallback_when_jit ``` - End-to-end on the affected configuration (RTX 5090 / SM120, system nvcc 12.8), no mocks: offline `LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", enforce_eager=True)` + `generate` with `temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9, top_k=20`, without setting `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER`, on main vs. this branch; plus a run with `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=1` to exercise the explicit opt-in path. - `pre-commit run --files` on both changed files (ruff check/format, mypy, typos, SPDX, etc.). ## Test Result - Unit: fails on main (`assert True is False` — the gate reports the sampler usable), passes with the fix. The rest of the suite is unaffected (same pass/fail set as main on the same machine). - E2E **main**: engine dies during startup profiling with the misleading `sm75` error — exact reproduction of the issue. - E2E **this branch**: `WARNING ... FlashInfer top-p/top-k sampling unavailable: SM 12.x requires CUDA >= 12.9; falling back. Set VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 to silence.` — engine starts and generates coherent output with top-k/top-p sampling. - E2E **`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=1`**: `RuntimeError: FlashInfer top-p/top-k sampling unavailable: SM 12.x requires CUDA >= 12.9. Unset VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=1.` — the real reason instead of the misleading one. - `pre-commit`: all hooks pass on both changed files. --- ### AI-Assisted Work Disclosure (per AGENTS.md) - **Duplicate check:** no open PR addresses #42393 or FlashInfer sampler gating for untargetable GPUs (`gh pr list` searches by issue number and area keywords, re-run immediately before opening this PR). - **AI assistance:** this contribution was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above; the end-to-end before/after verification was performed on my hardware, which reproduces the reported configuration exactly. - **Serving impact:** gating/fallback fix only. On systems where FlashInfer can target the GPU, sampler selection is unchanged. On affected systems, serving goes from crashing at startup to running with the native sampler.

signal.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Restore state after KV load rejection
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #49250. When a synchronous external KV load is rejected under `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, scheduler state is rewound but Model Runner V2 can retain the old device-side computed-token offset. With overlapping batches, output already in flight can also mutate reset scheduler state or be delivered after the request has been rescheduled. The result does not match full recomputation. This change: - marks the exact in-flight token positions stale and clears speculative and placeholder state when a failed load is recomputed; - propagates an explicit `rewound_req_ids` marker with cached-request data; - applies the scheduler's absolute computed-token offset to Model Runner V2's device-side request state only for those explicit rollbacks; and - adds focused scheduler and worker regression tests, including a multi-token speculative async frame. There is no connector-specific special case. This is materially different from #49252. That PR's scheduler fix derives a frame count from `num_output_placeholders - 1` and explicitly scopes out speculative decoding and diffusion. This change uses the existing exact `num_in_flight_tokens` accounting and an explicit CPU-to-GPU rewind signal; it was validated with EAGLE3. The difference was documented on #49250 before this draft was opened. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest -q \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py ruff check \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \ vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py \ vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py ruff format --check \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \ vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py \ vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py git diff --check origin/main...HEAD ``` GPU negative-control protocol: 1. Run greedy decoding without a KV connector and record token IDs. 2. Use a connector that promises a block-aligned synchronous load and rejects it before copying KV. 3. Compare clean-base and patched output against the no-connector baseline for sync, async, and async EAGLE3 scheduling. 4. Repeat with real `LMCacheConnectorV1`, injecting a one-shot failure in a 16-token retrieval before KV is copied. ## Test Result - Focused tests: **16 passed**. - Ruff check and format: **passed** for all five changed files. - `git diff --check`: **passed**. - Rebased cleanly onto `main` at `fe76112ff2`; focused tests and static checks were rerun after the final rebase. Single-GPU negative control (NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti, Model Runner V2 asserted, greedy token-ID comparison): | Configuration | Clean base | Patched | |---|---:|---:| | Controlled rejection, sync | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 | | Controlled rejection, async | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 | | EAGLE3 async, 2 draft tokens | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 | | Real LMCache rejection, sync | differs from scratch | exact | | Real LMCache rejection, async | differs from scratch | exact | The sync, async, EAGLE3, and real-LMCache async smoke cases were rerun after the preceding main rebase and remained exact. The final intervening upstream commit only changes ROCm/DeepSeek files; the five files in this PR were unchanged. Not covered: multi-GPU pipeline parallelism, hybrid KV cache manager, layerwise LMCache loading, or multi-request shared-block recovery. A separate ordinary LMCache-hit fused-layout corruption observed on this stack is outside this change's scope; the forced-failure test rejects before any cached KV copy. AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation, implementation, and test orchestration. The human submitter reviewed all five changed files, understands the change, and accepts maintenance responsibility. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][Scheduler] Clamp num_new_tokens to non-negative at max_model_len
signal.text: ## Purpose Prevent a scheduler crash (np.repeat with a negative count) when a running request reaches max_model_len during speculative decoding. One-line defensive clamp; no behavior change on the normal path. ## Issue With speculative decoding (MTP) — most reliably under disaggregated serving where the optimistic spec-advance runs ahead — a decode request can reach `num_computed_tokens >= max_model_len` before its stop-check finishes it. The `max_model_len` cap then produces a `negative` `num_new_tokens` (with `num_sampled_tokens_per_step == 1` the existing `num_new_tokens == 0` guard does not catch it), which flows into `num_scheduled_tokens` and crashes at `np.repeat(np.arange(...), num_scheduled_tokens)` with a negative repeat count. ### Reproduction Serve a spec-decode (MTP) model with a finite `--max-model-len` and drive a request whose generation crosses that length within a step (long-context decode to the boundary). Without the fix: `ValueError`/crash at `np.repeat` (negative count) in `scheduler.py`. With the fix: the request ends cleanly with `finish_reason=length`. ## Test Plan E2E: disagg + MTP long-context decode to the max_model_len boundary → expect finish_reason=length, no np.repeat crash. ## Test Result Boundary E2E: 5/5 requests driven to the 262144 `max_model_len` boundary finished with `finish_reason=length` and zero `np.repeat crashes` (prior repro without the clamp: crash at the negative-count `np.repeat`) --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [ROCm][Perf] Optimize DeepSeek V4 C4A top-k with AITER
signal.text: ## Summary This replaces the DeepSeek V4 C4A selector's ROCm top-k bottleneck with a correctness-adapted AITER path for short/medium contexts and a graph-safe tuned native fallback for long contexts on gfx950. - Route C4A prefill/decode top-k through the public AITER v0.1.19 operations. - Convert AITER prefill's packed/global indices back to sequence-local indices, preserving the `-1` sentinel. - Treat every vLLM MTP query row independently (`seq_lens.reshape(-1)`, `next_n=1`) so the existing exact 2-D per-token bounds are preserved for `num_speculative_tokens=2,3,4`. - Make the measured gfx950 hybrid selector the default C4A top-k path, with transparent native fallback when AITER is unavailable or slower. - Tune the existing two-launch native split/merge path for gfx950, FP32, `k=1024`, and up to 64 rows. Add a capture-stable specialization for 65-256 rows: three split blocks below 64K active columns and two blocks above it. Shapes above 256 rows select AITER. - Add focused correctness coverage; report the complete 84-shape kernel matrix below. Tracking issue: #41820. ## Relationship to related work This draft is intentionally a more complete superseding alternative to #46172, #50470, and the decode top-k portion of #52878, not an independent repetition of their unconditional decode call-site swaps. This change materially differs in four ways: 1. vLLM supplies exact 2-D `(batch, next_n)` MTP bounds. AITER v0.1.19 consumes 1-D request lengths and reconstructs per-row bounds, so passing the vLLM tensor with the original `next_n` is not equivalent. This patch flattens the exact bounds and calls AITER with `next_n=1`. 2. It covers prefill. AITER returns packed/global prefill indices while vLLM's consumers require sequence-local indices; this patch performs the required localization and preserves padding sentinels. 3. It covers AITER absence, automatic hybrid dispatch, MTP 2/3/4, short rows, packed nonzero row starts, and unordered threshold ties. 4. It includes the 500K/1M fallback design and avoids AITER's persistent multi-block decode path. The native fallback uses separate split and merge launches, so it has no cross-block spin barrier. #46012 also touches the native sampler, but addresses Wave32 LDS build safety; the gfx950 Wave64 performance specialization here is separately gated. The now-closed #52878's batched GEMM and `exp2` changes are orthogonal. Its top-k change routes every decode shape to AITER, whose v0.1.19 decode API is one-block only. Against that unconditional selector, this hybrid has identical kernel latency at 10K and 100K, while improving the long-context geometric mean: | Context | Hybrid / unconditional AITER | Cells faster / total | Range | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 10K | 1.00x | same 21/21 | 1.00-1.00x | | 100K | 1.00x | same 21/21 | 1.00-1.00x | | 500K | 1.21x | 19/21 (1 equal) | 0.98-1.46x | | 1M | 1.76x | 20/21 (1 equal) | 1.00-2.29x | This is why the long, low/mid-row fallback is part of the same standalone change rather than following an unconditional AITER decode switch. ## Kernel A/B Hardware/software: one gfx950 MI355 OAM, Torch `2.12.0+git6bbd260`, HIP `7.2.53211`, amd-aiter `0.1.19`. Production C4A shape is FP32 logits with fixed allocated width `1,048,576 / 4 = 262,144`, `k=1024`, and active compressed length `context / 4`. Each cell uses 20 warmups and 100 HIP-event samples; the reported metric is median speedup over the original vLLM `_C` implementation. `N` below is `num_speculative_tokens`; each request contributes `N + 1` target query rows. signal.title: [CPU][Bugfix] Fallback to eager sampling when Inductor C++ compile fails
signal.text: ## Purpose On the macOS CPU backend with a non-Apple clang++ first in PATH (e.g. homebrew llvm), Inductor's C++ codegen fails: the bare clang++ has no default SDK sysroot. Model compilation can be sidestepped with enforce_eager, but compiled_random_sample is @torch.compile'd regardless, so startup dies in warmup with CppCompileError. This warns once on the first failure and falls back to the eager sampling path for good. Couldnt find an existing report for this. Claude assisted with the investigation and the fix. cc @bigPYJ1151 ## Test Plan M3MAX, macos, torch 2.11.0: ``` VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv pip install -e . ``` ``` from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams if __name__ == "__main__": llm = LLM(model="facebook/opt-125m", enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=256, gpu_memory_utilization=0.2) outs = llm.generate( ["Once upon a time,"] * 2, [ SamplingParams(max_tokens=8, temperature=0.0), SamplingParams(max_tokens=8, temperature=0.8), ], ) for o in outs: print(o.outputs[0].text) ``` Three runs: 1. main, homebrew llvm first in PATH 2. this patch, same PATH 3. this patch, `PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH` (Apple's clang) ## Test Result Run 1 dies at startup with CppCompileError(`pthread.h` file not found). Run 2 warns once, then both prompts generate: ``` WARNING ... [topk_topp_sampler.py:280] compiled_random_sample failed (CppCompileError: C++ compile error); falling back to the eager sampling path. ``` Run 3 emits no warning, the compiled path compiles and runs as on main. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [ROCm][Perf][DeepSeek V4] Fuse native FP8 shared expert with MXFP4 routed experts
signal.text: ## DO NOT MERGE: requires ROCm/aiter#4891 and a matching AITER pin ## Summary Enable AITER heterogeneous fused MoE (FHMoE) for the DeepSeek V4 ROCm path. The guarded path combines native-FP8 shared-expert weights with MXFP4 routed experts for model-visible MoE input rows covered continuously by AITER's active FHMoE CSV on gfx950/TP8. The currently shipped table covers `1 <= M <= 2048`; unsupported M retains the existing separate routed/shared path. The implementation keeps the native per-rank intermediate width at 384: - shared W1: `[1, 768, 7168]` - shared W2: `[1, 7168, 384]` - fused intermediate: `[M, 7, 384]` It does **not** restore the old 384-to-512 weight or activation padding. Only the W2 E8M0 scale descriptor is neutral-aligned from 12 to 16 columns. The feature remains opt-in through `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. It fails closed unless the exact gfx950, TP8/DP1/PCP1, BF16, no-EP/EPLB/offload, `noaux_tc`, DSV4 quantization, routed-tensor, and AITER capability contracts pass. ## Dependency / merge blocker **Do not merge until [ROCm/aiter#4891](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4891) lands and vLLM consumes a revision or release containing it.** Stock AITER v0.1.20 exposes the heterogeneous tensor API but is insufficient for this widened policy. AITER #4891 adds the dedicated physical-I384 FHMoE configuration and the public `supports_dsv4_i384_fhmoe(max_tokens)` capability query. That query derives continuous padded-bucket coverage from the active resolved FHMoE CSV. vLLM requires the result to be literal `True` for the actual M and separately validates the shared-tensor API. Missing, older, malformed, incomplete, or unreadable AITER configurations therefore preserve the separate fallback. PR #52826 is only a baseline v0.1.20 bump, not the complete dependency. ## Related work / duplicate check This PR supersedes closed #48728, submitted by the same author. That draft was based on the older I384-to-I512 padded implementation and had become stale and conflicted. This replacement is rebuilt from current `main`, retains native I384, adds bounded/fail-closed dispatch, and includes matched performance, accuracy, trace, and KV-capacity evidence. This is distinct from #51918 (expert-parallel MegaMoEV2), #53097 (homogeneous block-FP8 compatibility), and merged #53040 (NVIDIA MegaMoE). Open-PR searches for the predecessor and DeepSeek-V4 FHMoE found no other PR implementing this native-FP8-shared/MXFP4-routed TP8 path. ## Token-range policy The selector uses model-visible MoE rows `M = x.shape[0]`, not client concurrency. AITER metadata is power-of-two bucketed: for example, actual `M=1536` selects the `token=2048` CSV row while the kernel still receives a 1536-row tensor. This is config selection, not tensor padding. With the current table, coverage includes no-speculation through 512 sequences, MTP2 through 512 sequences (`M=1536`), and MTP3 through 512 sequences (`M=2048`). MTP4 at the full 512-sequence limit reaches M=2560 and currently uses the separate fallback. At B<=64, even MTP4 reaches only M=320. The range is not duplicated in vLLM code. Adding one valid `token=4096` row to AITER's already-complete 1..2048 table automatically enables every actual `M<=4096`; `M=4097` then requires an 8192 row. Capability results are cached, and changing the active CSV requires a server restart. ## Performance ### Isolated FHMoE A/B at concurrency 8 Configuration: 8x gfx950, TP8, 80 identical random 8K/1K requests, no MTP, `max_model_len=9472`, `max_num_seqs=512`, and `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`. Only the fusion flag changed. | Metric | Separate | FHMoE | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 366.46 tok/s | 396.28 tok/s | **+8.14%** | | Mean TPOT | 20.822 ms | 19.205 ms | **-7.77%** | | Mean E2EL | 19853.10 ms | 18358.23 ms | **-7.53%** | | Mean TTFT | 573.87 ms | 574.19 ms | +0.06% | The decode trace showed steady step wall time `21.201 -> 18.926 ms` (-10.73%), classified MoE time -27.34%, and kernel launches -15.57%. ### Expanded token range Matched feature-on runs comparing the former M=2..8 guard with M=1..2048: | Concurrency | Metric | M=2..8 | M=1..2048 | Delta | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | Output throughput | 58.565 tok/s | 65.696 tok/s | **+12.18%** | | 1 | Mean TPOT | 16.686 ms | 14.830 ms | **-11.12%** | | 16 | Output throughput | 607.933 tok/s | 659.472 tok/s | **+8.48%** | | 16 | Mean TPOT | 24.701 ms | 22.701 ms | **-8.10%** | Exact production-composed operator comparisons at the upper boundary: | M | Separate shared+routed | FHMoE | FHMoE latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.31595 ms | 0.20640 ms | 34.67% | | 1536 | 0.471638 ms | 0.451771 ms | 4.21% | | 2048 | 0.497949 ms | 0.483047 ms | 2.99% | | 2049 diagnostic | 0.534067 ms | 0.736905 ms | -37.98% | The M2049 result is why the current CSV intentionally stops at 2048. A future 4096 row should only be added after a better kernel is tuned and validated. ### Final combined-stack validation The final AITER dedicated-table path was rerun in a clean TP8/no-MTP server with this change, fused mHC, and the local C4A top-k enabled. All request length arrays matched the earlier prototype exactly. | Concurrency | Output tok/s | Delta vs prototype | Mean TPOT (ms) | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 65.523 | -0.561% | 14.864 | | 2 | 123.454 | -0.272% | 15.714 | | 4 | 219.332 | -0.449% | 17.307 | | 8 | 395.523 | -0.654% | 19.250 | | 16 | 655.551 | -0.476% | 22.820 | | 32 | 1019.757 | -0.580% | 29.442 | | 64 | 1366.400 | -0.415% | 44.259 | All 1270 accepted C1-C64 requests completed. The final implementation was within 0.7% of the prototype at every point. Against the prior matched feature-off/new-top-k C8 reference, output throughput improved `354.133 -> 395.523 tok/s` (+11.69%) and TPOT improved `21.576 -> 19.250 ms` (-10.78%). This combined-stack sweep is integration evidence; the isolated flag A/B above remains the attribution measurement for FHMoE itself. ## Accuracy Full 5-shot GSM8K, greedy, thinking disabled, max output 2048, concurrency 64: - strict exact match: **1265/1319 = 0.95906**; - flexible extract: **1264/1319 = 0.95830**; - 1319 unique documents, no empty/error responses, and all HTTP requests 200. This exceeds the 0.94 acceptance floor and replaces the earlier 64-sample smoke result. ## Memory / KV capacity | Metric | Separate | FHMoE | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Model memory | 104.13 GiB | 104.97 GiB | +0.84 GiB (+0.81%) | | Peak activation | 11.95 GiB | 12.25 GiB | +0.30 GiB | | Available KV memory | 107.13 GiB | 106.49 GiB | -0.64 GiB (-0.60%) | | KV token capacity | 195054 | 193894 | -1160 (-0.595%) | | Max concurrency at 9472 | 20.59x | 20.47x | -0.12x | The final dedicated-table run exactly matched the prototype's 12.25-GiB peak activation, 7.05-GiB graph pool, 106.49-GiB KV memory, and 193894-token KV capacity. The additional persistent storage is the shuffled native shared copy plus one dummy routed row, not I512 padding. ## Validation ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py -q # 64 passed, 14 warnings .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/_aiter_ops.py \ vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py \ tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py # all hooks passed ``` - `git diff --check`: passed. - Native-I384 FP32-oracle, high-expert-ID, graph replay, and exact-storage checks passed at representative low/high M including 1536 and 2048. - FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graph capture completed with no MTP. - No JIT warning or server/client error occurred inside the accepted timed C1-C64 intervals. This remains a draft until AITER #4891 lands, vLLM pins a containing release or revision, and the human submitter completes final review. ## AI assistance OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, testing, profiling analysis, and drafting. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and is responsible for understanding and defending the change end-to-end.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix AOT caching for decorated forward methods
signal.text: ## Purpose The Transformers backend can fail to save its AOT artifact when a model's `forward` is wrapped by decorators. The artifact may reference a function from the `__wrapped__` chain which is no longer importable by identity, so standard pickle fails with errors such as: ```text Can't pickle <function Qwen3Model.forward ...>: it's not the same object as transformers.models.qwen3.modeling_qwen3.Qwen3Model.forward ``` This makes every warm start compile again even when the rest of the compile cache is warm. This PR uses PyTorch's `external_data` support to save and restore the non-canonical functions in a decorated `forward` chain. The external keys include a deterministic fingerprint of the whole chain, including defaults, keyword defaults, and supported immutable closure state, so an artifact is not reused when decorator configuration changes. The mapping is all-or-nothing and unsupported state falls back to the existing save/load behavior. The existing PyTorch 2.10 call path is unchanged; `external_data` is only passed on PyTorch 2.11+. This addresses the AOT warm-start cache failure identified in #50128. It does not claim to eliminate or fully explain the remaining Transformers-backend startup gap tracked by that issue. ## Test Plan - Added unit coverage for decorated-forward resolution, deterministic chain fingerprints, unsupported state, canonical inner functions, inherited forwards, invalid/cyclic chains, and PyTorch 2.10 API compatibility. - Added real AOT compile/save tests for the unsupported-state non-fatal path. - Added cross-process tests for cold save + forced warm load and for fingerprint mismatch in normal and forced-load modes. - Ran the complete AOT compile test file with the configuration that executes the functorch test instead of conditionally skipping it: ```bash VLLM_USE_MEGA_AOT_ARTIFACT=0 pytest -q tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py ruff check vllm/compilation/decorators.py tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py ruff format --check vllm/compilation/decorators.py tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py git diff --check ``` - Ran fresh-process cold + three warm-start checks on an NVIDIA L20 with PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129 and Transformers 5.15.0. Warm runs used `VLLM_FORCE_AOT_LOAD=1` so a failed load could not silently recompile. ## Test Result ```text 71 passed, 16 warnings in 178.91s ruff check: passed ruff format --check: passed git diff --check: passed ``` The warnings are existing dependency deprecations from PyTorch JIT (14) and CUDA Python (2). Fresh-process results: | Model | Cold init | Warm init median | Warm compile median | Improvement | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Qwen3-0.6B | 38.391 → 38.704 s | 25.737 → 17.632 s | 8.28 → 0.13 s | 31.5% | | TinyLlama-1.1B | 29.360 → 29.056 s | 19.739 → 13.837 s | 5.80 → 0.12 s | 29.9% | | Qwen3-14B | 50.103 → 50.033 s | 36.520 → 24.792 s | 11.36 → 0.13 s | 32.1% | Values are `before → after`. All after-fix forced warm runs loaded the AOT artifact with `compiles=0, loaded=1`. <details> <summary>Raw runs and AOT counters</summary> | Model | Revision | Warm init runs | Warm compile runs | Cold counters | Warm counters | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Qwen3-0.6B | Before | 25.755 / 25.737 / 25.571 s | 8.28 / 8.40 / 8.26 s | `1/0/0` | `1/0/0` | | Qwen3-0.6B | After | 17.403 / 17.632 / 17.757 s | 0.13 / 0.12 / 0.13 s | `1/1/0` | `0/0/1` | | TinyLlama-1.1B | Before | 19.807 / 19.739 / 19.723 s | 5.80 / 5.82 / 5.77 s | `1/0/0` | `1/0/0` | | TinyLlama-1.1B | After | 13.962 / 13.800 / 13.837 s | 0.12 / 0.12 / 0.12 s | `1/1/0` | `0/0/1` | | Qwen3-14B | Before | 36.307 / 36.520 / 36.533 s | 11.36 / 11.41 / 11.33 s | `1/0/0` | `1/0/0` | | Qwen3-14B | After | 25.005 / 24.754 / 24.792 s | 0.13 / 0.14 / 0.13 s | `1/1/0` | `0/0/1` | Counters are `compiled/saved/loaded`. Before the fix, every warm process compiled again because artifact saving failed. After the fix, every forced warm process loaded the artifact without compiling. </details> For every model, cold and warm runs produced identical token IDs. ## AI Assistance Developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex. I reviewed all changes and verified the reported tests and benchmarks.

signal.title: Require a PyAV build with the fixed IAMF parser
signal.text: # Require a PyAV build with the fixed IAMF parser ## What this fixes vLLM's speech path opens uploaded audio with PyAV, which includes FFmpeg parsers. Older PyAV/FFmpeg builds contain an IAMF parser bug that can corrupt the process's native memory while opening a malformed audio file. For example, an attacker can upload a specially formed IAMF file to `/v1/audio/transcriptions`. Before this change, `av.open()` ran before vLLM checked whether the installed parser contained the upstream fix. The malformed file could crash the API process and, because memory was overwritten inside native code, had the potential for more serious process compromise. After this change, vLLM refuses to call `av.open()` on a vulnerable stack and gives an actionable upgrade error instead. ## Why it matters A client able to submit speech-to-text audio could crash the serving process on deployments using an affected PyAV/FFmpeg combination. The request does not require a valid audio stream; the parser is reached while opening the file. The demonstrated outcome was process memory corruption and a crash. Code execution was not demonstrated. ## The change The audio dependency floor is now PyAV 17.1.0. A shared `require_safe_pyav_stack()` guard checks the runtime PyAV and FFmpeg versions before container parsing, and speech callers preserve its specific upgrade message. Requirements and test locks are updated to the same safe floor. ## How it was tested The unpatched focused suite could not be collected in the reconstructed environment; with the patch, all 23 collected tests passed. A separate dependency-floor check showed 6 failures and 4 passes against the old requirements, then passed with the new floor. Tests also verify that `av.open()` is never reached for a vulnerable stack. The positive "known-good IAMF file decodes" check remained environment-limited and failed once because the reconstructed fixture/runtime combination could not perform that decode. The security-relevant version-floor guard and the fail-before-`av.open()` behavior are verified. ## Reference Advisory: GHSA-m52c-39rh-f3gp Track B: this is a public PR against `vllm-project/vllm@main`. ## Credit - @KernelClint (Clinton Thomas) and @dhalf (Lucas Bourtoule) - Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration); discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber All commits include DCO `Signed-off-by` trailers. ## Upstream FFmpeg references The overflow is in FFmpeg's `scalable_channel_layout_config()` (`libavformat/iamf_parse.c`) and was fixed upstream in Dec 2025: - Issue: https://code.ffmpeg.org/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/issues/21013 - Patches: https://code.ffmpeg.org/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/pulls/21017 · https://code.ffmpeg.org/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/pulls/21107 · https://code.ffmpeg.org/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/pulls/21115 - Fix commit `2d5abf27e5b0bf48a779368499d754f130bae4f4`: https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/commit/2d5abf27e5b0bf48a779368499d754f130bae4f4 It is distinct from the IAMF allocation-DoS CVE-2026-66037 (`mix_presentation_obu()`, same file, different function). This PR is a vLLM-side guard for deployments that link a still-vulnerable FFmpeg via PyAV.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Remove heuristic speculative method inference
signal.text: ## Summary This PR removes speculative-method guessing from model and path names. The method must now come from the user or a checkpoint schema that explicitly declares it; ambiguous configurations fail with an actionable error instead of silently falling back to `draft_model`. This matters for neutral training paths. In the original Qwen3-8B + DFlash reproduction, the misdetected `draft_model` path had acceptance length **1.02**, while explicit `method="dflash"` reached **3.88**. ## Configuration contract - `method` is the sole algorithm selector. It may come from `"method"` in `--speculative-config`, `--spec-method`, or a known schema declaration such as speculators format. - Paths, names, architectures, and structural `model_type` values never select the method. - `model` identifies an external draft source only; it does not select or validate the method. - An ordinary target with no speculative configuration remains non-speculative, even if it contains auxiliary weights. - `mtp` and `dspark` may omit `model` to reuse weights embedded in the target checkpoint. The explicit method selects the corresponding loader. - Model-free methods such as `ngram` and `suffix` reject `model`. - After method selection, checkpoint metadata fills only missing implementation settings. User values win field by field. - Proposal depth can default from speculators `speculative_tokens`, `n_predict`, or DFlash/DSpark block metadata. When block metadata is known, an explicit DFlash/DSpark value may reduce but not exceed the trained proposal depth. - A speculators-format checkpoint used as the top-level model continues to work without explicit flags because its schema declares the algorithm and proposal depth. For checkpoints such as DeepSeek-V4 that can support multiple implementations, metadata configures the method selected by the user; it does not choose among `draft_model`, `mtp`, and `dspark`. ## Behavior change and compatibility This PR does **not** introduce a new configuration interface. - **Existing interfaces, unchanged:** `--speculative-config` and the existing `--spec-method`, `--spec-model`, and `--spec-tokens` aliases all remain supported. - **Behavior before this PR:** when `method` was omitted, vLLM could guess it from model/path substrings and otherwise fall back to `draft_model`. - **Behavior after this PR:** path/name guessing is removed. `method` must be supplied through an existing interface or declared by a known checkpoint schema. Therefore, an existing JSON configuration that relied on guessing only needs an explicit `method`: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \ --speculative-config '{ "method": "dflash", "model": "/path/to/checkpoints/6" }' ``` When the checkpoint exposes its proposal depth, `num_speculative_tokens` can be omitted; otherwise it remains required. A generic autoregressive draft should use `method="draft_model"`. The old `"model": "ngram"` and `"model": "[ngram]"` sentinels are rejected; use `method="ngram"`. ## Validation - Model evaluation from the motivating reproduction: acceptance length **1.02** with the misdetected `draft_model` versus **3.88** with explicit `dflash`. GPU evaluation was not rerun for the configuration-only follow-up. - `tests/test_config.py`: **238 passed, 2 deselected**. - Focused method/schema/default matrix: **24 passed, 216 deselected**. - DSpark configuration tests: **11 passed**. - All configured pre-commit hooks passed on the follow-up files, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown lint, SPDX, and configuration validation. <details> <summary>Commands run</summary> ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \ -k "not test_rope_customization and not test_eagle_draft_model_config" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py \ -k "spec_model_declaration or block_drafters or explicit_method_selects_deepseek_v4_loader or dspark_reuses_embedded_target_and_defaults_tokens or speculators_format_declares or speculators_format_preserves" .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/transformers_utils/test_dspark_mla_config.py .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ docs/features/speculative_decoding/README.md \ docs/features/speculative_decoding/adaptive_verification.md \ tests/test_config.py \ tests/transformers_utils/test_dspark_mla_config.py \ vllm/config/speculative.py \ vllm/transformers_utils/configs/k3_dspark.py ``` </details> ## Contribution notes - This is not a duplicate of #47490, which preserves auto-detection and validates explicit mismatches; this PR removes auto-detection. - This is not a duplicate of #44566, which only propagates speculators token depth. - This is not a duplicate of #52165, which detects DeepSeek-V4 DSpark metadata for routing; here the explicit method remains authoritative. - AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

signal.title: [Feature]: Cache-aware waiting QoS with optional cooperative prefill preemption
signal.text: #### Summary Add an opt-in V1 scheduling policy that improves time-to-first-token (TTFT) for cache-warm continuations under long-context contention: 1. **Cache-aware waiting admission/order**: within a bounded window, prefer a waiting request when its *estimated remaining service cost* is materially lower because a local or external KV prefix is already available. 2. **Optional cooperative prefill preemption (later phase)**: at an ordinary chunked-prefill scheduling boundary, checkpoint and pause a cold running prefill only when doing so is predicted to let a warm request reach its first streamed token significantly sooner, without losing the victim's completed work. This issue is intended to track one concrete policy/use case. It is compatible with the scheduler extension framework proposed in #51608 rather than a duplicate of that framework. #### Motivating workload A single engine may serve many concurrent, long-lived agent sessions with distinct 100k–500k-token histories. Under load, one or more uncached chunked prefills can occupy the running set while a continuation with hundreds of thousands of tokens already present in local APC or an external KV cache remains waiting. FCFS is fair by arrival time, but it can produce poor interactive latency in this case: the warm continuation may need only a cache transfer, a short uncached suffix, and one decode step, while a cold request ahead of it still has a very large prefill remaining. This is a QoS/tail-latency proposal, not a claim that cache affinity universally improves throughput. The corrected experiment reported in #42185 found no meaningful benefit for workloads sharing one already-resident prefix; multi-session workloads with distinct competing prefixes are the target case. #### Residency should be time-aware A large external-cache hit is not free: the cached prefix must still be loaded into GPU KV and resident while the request runs. However, that occupancy is temporal. For a warm request, the approximate active residence is: ``` cache load + uncached tail prefill + actual output tokens / effective per-request decode throughput ``` `max_tokens / effective_decode_tokens_per_second` is a useful upper bound for the decode portion (not multiplication); under mixed prefill/decode load, effective per-request decode throughput may be lower. Output KV pages are allocated progressively, while the loaded prompt prefix remains resident until completion or preemption. The admission objective should therefore consider **KV block-seconds**, not only instantaneous block count or cache-hit percentage. A huge warm prefix with a small output budget can still be an excellent latency trade: large compute avoidance, short expected residence. #### Phase 1: cache-aware waiting policy Implement an opt-in policy through #51608's future Score/QueueSort hooks, or initially as a narrowly scoped built-in scheduler policy: - Preserve explicit request priority as the outer ordering key. - Inspect only a bounded FCFS/priority-ordered candidate window. - Use side-effect-free, cycle-cached features. - Never perform connector RPC or blocking I/O in the scheduler hot path. - Consider an external hit only after the connector's asynchronous lookup has completed. - Keep deterministic tie-breaking. A candidate score should estimate TTFT improvement rather than rank raw hit tokens: ``` warm_ttft_cost = ready_cache_transfer_time(tier, bytes) + uncached_tokens / observed_prefill_rate + first_decode_step_cost residency_cost = required_prompt_blocks * predicted_active_seconds benefit = estimated_head_wait_avoided - warm_ttft_cost - admission/displacement cost - weighted_residency_cost ``` Useful read-only features: - local cached tokens; - external cached tokens, lookup readiness, and cache tier; - estimated transfer bytes/time; - uncached prompt remainder; - blocks required for admission; - prompt-prefill versus active-decode state; - waiting age, explicit priority, and optional tenant/SLA weight; - output-token budget as a conservative residence estimate. The KV connector API may need a side-effect-free snapshot such as: ```python CacheAdmissionInfo( ready: bool, matched_tokens: int, tier: CacheTier, estimated_load_bytes: int, estimated_load_seconds: float | None, ) ``` This API must not allocate/touch blocks, emit cache events, increment hit metrics, or start a transfer. Fairness and anti-thrash controls: - bounded candidate window; - maximum FCFS-head wait / aging deadline; - minimum predicted benefit and hysteresis; - per-session/tenant bypass budget; - do not bypass preempted recovery work indefinitely; - expose decision reasons without high-cardinality metric labels. #### Phase 2: cooperative cached preemption Queue reordering alone cannot admit a warm request when running prefixes occupy the required GPU KV. A later opt-in phase could reclaim a running **prefill** at an existing scheduler-step boundary. Required connector/scheduler contract: 1. Select only a prefill victim; protect active decodes, remote-KV loads, and near-finished prefills. 2. Identify the latest complete cache chunk common to every TP/PP rank. 3. Ensure that prefix is durable and reloadable before freeing its GPU blocks: - wait for store completion, or - pin the blocks until all-rank completion; - do not treat store submission as durability. 4. Requeue the victim with an explicit checkpoint token count. 5. Admit the warm request only if predicted benefit exceeds checkpoint/reload cost. 6. Reload the victim later; recompute only an incomplete tail. 7. On any connector timeout/failure, retain or safely recompute the victim rather than trusting partial external state. Suggested safeguards: - cooldown and maximum preemptions per request; - one cooperative preemption per scheduling cycle; - no preemption while connector store backlog/failure rate is elevated; - all-rank acknowledgement and failure injection tests; - no zero-progress preemption loops; - request cancellation and repeated-preemption coverage. #### Observability and evaluation Split waiting/deferred reasons sufficiently to distinguish cache lookup, KV load, capacity, grammar, and other constraints. Record: - candidate local/external hit and tier; - estimated versus actual load/prefill time; - scheduler decision reason; - prompt blocks and predicted/actual block-seconds; - checkpointed tokens and store-fence latency; - reload tokens/time and recomputed tail; - TTFT/time-to-first-stream won or lost; - preemption count, cooldown rejection, and fairness age. Acceptance criteria: - default FCFS and priority behavior is unchanged when disabled; - scheduler hot path performs no external I/O; - deterministic unit tests for bounded reorder, aging, explicit priority, and starvation; - connector tests for delayed/failed all-rank checkpoint and immediate block-ID reuse; - A/B traces with multiple distinct long-context sessions; - report scheduler CPU overhead, p50/p95/p99 TTFT, time-to-first-stream, throughput, cache transfer bandwidth, GPU-KV churn, and fairness. ### Alternatives - **Existing integer priority**: useful for explicit interactive/batch QoS, but it does not estimate cache reuse or residency cost and currently has limited ability to displace running work (#40004, #40087). - **Smaller prefill chunks / lower `max_num_batched_tokens`**: creates more frequent scheduling boundaries but does not reclaim GPU KV and can reduce aggregate prefill throughput. - **Session affinity only**: #51384 is a safer and useful local-APC specialization, but external-cache readiness/tier and residency cost remain unmodeled. - **Residual SJF only**: #51375 captures remaining local work and aging, but does not incorporate external connector transfer cost. - **External proxy/router**: lacks exact per-engine KV allocation, cache readiness, and preemption state. - **Whole scheduler subclass**: possible through `scheduler_cls`, but unnecessarily couples a policy experiment to the full scheduler compatibility surface. - **Separate engines for interactive and batch traffic**: provides isolation but can strand GPU capacity and duplicates large model residency. ### Additional context Prior art and adjacent work: - #51608 — extensible scheduler Score/Filter/QueueSort/Preemption hooks. - #51384 — bounded session-affinity scheduler with local cache confirmation and aging. - #51375 — residual-aware SJF with aging. - #42185 — cache-affinity scheduling experiment and workload-dependent result. - #7883 / #10128 — prefix-cache-aware capacity and token-budget accounting. - #40004 / #40087 — waiting priority and running-request preemption. - #31731 / #36390 — KV-heavy head-of-line blocking. - #30256 — SLA-tiered scheduling. - LMCache/LMCache#4612 — reload already-cached KV for MP preempted requests. - vLLM #52360 / #52372 — precedent showing that async stores must not read freed/reused paged-KV blocks. A staged implementation is important: **waiting-order affinity should land and be measured independently; forced cooperative preemption should remain disabled until durable checkpoint/reload semantics are proven.** ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing and past issues/PRs and reviewed the related proposals above.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Set breakable graph env before Ray actor import
signal.text: ## Purpose DSv4 automatically enables breakable CUDA graphs in `VllmConfig`. Native multiprocessing workers inherit that setting before importing the model, but Ray creates its worker actors first and copies the driver environment only later in `initialize_worker`. That ordering matters because `@eager_break_during_capture` makes its decision when the model module imports. Without the setting, the decorator permanently returns the original attention and indexer functions. Ray later enables breakable capture, but the breakpoints needed to keep those functions outside the graph are missing, producing an oversized graph and garbled output. Copy only `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` into the actor `runtime_env` before import, for both Ray executors. All existing general environment propagation, worker exclusions, and node-local values remain unchanged. This follows the existing pre-actor environment pattern used for Ray device visibility in #33308. No open PR duplicates this Ray import-order fix; #41834 concerns unrelated SM12x model support. AI assistance was used to investigate and prepare this patch; I reviewed every changed line and the reported test results. ## Test Plan Run the focused Ray environment tests: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_ray_env_utils.py -q ``` Validate DeepSeek-V4-Pro with Ray V2 using two replicas, each TP8 across two physical GB300 hosts. Retain production CUDA graphs, expert parallelism, MNNVL, and custom collectives, and do not explicitly set `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` so the test exercises automatic enablement. Send 10 deterministic color and 10 deterministic math requests to each backend and through the normal router. Repeat after 128 requests at concurrency 16. ## Test Result ```text 9 passed in 0.83s ``` | Variant | Captured graph | Color | Math | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Unpatched Ray, automatic enablement | 0.69 GiB | 0/10 | 0/10 | | Ray, explicit setting at actor startup | 0.37 GiB | 10/10 | 10/10 | | Native MP, automatic enablement | 0.37 GiB | 10/10 | 10/10 | | Patched Ray, automatic enablement | 0.37 GiB | 10/10 | 10/10 | Both patched TP8 replicas passed the color and math checks before and after load. The router also passed both checks, and the concurrency-16 run completed 128/128 requests successfully. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results. - [x] Documentation impact was considered; no user-facing option or API changes require documentation. </details>
signal.author: alexeldeib

signal.title: [XPU][MoE] Tune Triton fused MoE for Intel XPU
signal.text: ## Purpose The Triton fused MoE kernel runs on Intel XPU but has no tuned configs there, so it always falls back to `get_default_config()` and logs "Using default MoE config. Performance might be sub-optimal!". This PR makes `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py` usable on XPU and ships tuned configs for Intel Arc Pro B70. ## Changes - Route CUDA graph capture, default device and cache clearing through `torch.accelerator` / `current_platform` instead of hardcoded `torch.cuda`. - Add `--no-ray`. Ray keys its parallelism on the `"GPU"` resource, which XPU does not register, so `ray.remote` is now applied dynamically rather than at class definition and the same worker class serves both paths. - Add an XPU search space (`num_warps` up to 32, `num_stages` from 3, smaller `BLOCK_SIZE_K`, `grf_mode`) and `prune_xpu_search_space()`, which drops tiles wider than the routed row count since those are pure padding and the slowest to compile. Adapted from `intel-xpu-backend-for-triton`. - Keep `grf_mode` in `sort_config()`. No plumbing is needed for it, as `**config` already forwards extra keys into the launch, the same way ROCm passes `waves_per_eu`. - Ship tuned configs for `E=64, N=1024`, `E=64, N=512` and `E=128, N=384`. ## Results Kernel time from `benchmark_moe.py`, Intel Arc Pro B70, bf16, `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924`. Baseline is the built-in heuristic config, tuned is the shipped JSON. `E=64, N=1024` (tp=1): | batch | baseline (us) | tuned (us) | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 331.56 | 234.54 | 1.41x | | 2 | 650.32 | 386.58 | 1.68x | | 4 | 1150.53 | 674.60 | 1.71x | | 8 | 1740.73 | 992.18 | 1.75x | | 16 | 2333.32 | 1302.85 | 1.79x | | 24 | 2540.36 | 1411.62 | 1.80x | | 32 | 2628.54 | 1449.64 | 1.81x | | 48 | 1734.96 | 1499.30 | 1.16x | | 64 | 1750.65 | 1506.59 | 1.16x | | 96 | 1842.48 | 1550.00 | 1.19x | | 128 | 4789.70 | 1585.79 | 3.02x | | 256 | 2229.38 | 1737.90 | 1.28x | | 512 | 3140.05 | 2183.39 | 1.44x | | 1024 | 11349.81 | 3594.97 | 3.16x | | 1536 | 14507.93 | 4985.24 | 2.91x | | 2048 | 18100.66 | 6417.00 | 2.82x | | 3072 | 25021.64 | 9352.32 | 2.68x | | 4096 | 32101.63 | 12095.05 | 2.65x | `E=64, N=512` (tp=2): | batch | baseline (us) | tuned (us) | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 157.82 | 130.36 | 1.21x | | 16 | 1160.66 | 688.16 | 1.69x | | 128 | 2353.28 | 845.63 | 2.78x | | 512 | 1635.36 | 1180.34 | 1.39x | | 2048 | 8910.22 | 3443.63 | 2.59x | | 4096 | 15361.95 | 6500.82 | 2.36x | Geometric mean 1.86x and 1.91x respectively. Two things drive the larger wins. The heuristic escalates `BLOCK_SIZE_M` with batch size, which is wrong for a 64-expert layer at `topk=8` where the rows an expert receives stay small; that makes its cost curve non-monotonic (batch 128 costs more than batch 256, for half the tokens) while the tuned curve is monotonic. And half the winners sit outside the default space: `num_warps=16` wins at 9 of 18 batch sizes, where the default space only explores 4 and 8. Every shipped config was checked against an fp32 reference; relative L2 error is 4.1e-3, which is the bf16 output quantization step rather than kernel error. End to end, `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924` on one B70 with `--moe-backend triton`, the shipped configs supplied through `VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER` and the baseline being the same run without them: | workload | baseline | tuned | speedup | |---|---|---|---| | `generate`, 32 prompts x 64 tokens | 2.107 s | 1.280 s | 1.65x | | `lm_eval arc_challenge`, 4687 requests | 67 s | 57 s | 1.18x | Accuracy is unchanged: `arc_challenge` scores acc 0.4727 and acc_norm 0.4829 on both. Greedy continuations are not bit-identical, since a different reduction order moves logits by less than a bf16 step and flips near-ties, but the identical loglikelihood scores show behaviour is unaffected. The third config, `E=128, N=384`, is the shape `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` and `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct` present at tp=2, and the most expert-dense topology tuned here. All 18 winners pass the fp32 check, but it has no end-to-end number: the bf16 checkpoint is 57 GiB against a 32 GiB card, so that shape needs two cards and one was available. It is also where pruning matters most, since at 128 experts and topk=8 an expert receives `M/16` rows, and `BLOCK_SIZE_M=16` duly wins every batch size up to 128. The space leaves out `BLOCK_SIZE_N=32` and `num_warps=32`. Neither won at any of the 31 tuned batch sizes across `E=64, N=1024`, `E=64, N=512` and `E=40, N=512` (Granite 3.1 3b-a800m), and on a Mixtral-shaped kernel (`E=8, N=14336, K=4096, topk=2`) they stay far off the best even though that is the corner where wide tiles get the most rows per expert: | value | M=128 | M=1024 | M=4096 | |---|---|---|---| | `BLOCK_SIZE_N=32` | +46% | +85% | +90% | | `num_warps=32` | +44% | +54% | +17% | | `BLOCK_SIZE_M=256` (kept) | +112% | +17% | +7% | `BLOCK_SIZE_M=256` is kept because its margin keeps shrinking with batch size on that shape, and `prune_xpu_search_space()` already drops it whenever the routed row count is small. The space is 360 candidates rather than 720, which roughly halves tuning time. `E=128, N=384` was tuned after the narrowing, so it is not evidence that the removed values lose, only that nothing needed them: `BLOCK_SIZE_N=128` wins 14 of 18 batch sizes and `num_warps` is 8 or 16 at 17 of 18, well inside the boundary. ## Test plan - `benchmark_moe.py --model allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 --tp-size 1 --no-ray --tune` completes on XPU and writes a config JSON - serving that model on B70 with `--moe-backend triton` picks the shipped config up (the "default MoE config" warning is gone) and generates 1.65x faster at identical `arc_challenge` accuracy - the same command with `--model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --tp-size 2` writes the `E=128, N=384` config, whose 18 winners all pass the fp32 check; it has no serving run, since that shape needs two cards - CUDA and ROCm paths are unchanged: the Ray path still wraps the worker with `ray.remote(num_gpus=1)`, and pruning is only reached under `current_platform.is_xpu()`

signal.title: [Kernel][Perf] Support DSpark K=8 in fused GDN MTP decode
signal.text: ## Purpose #52539 enabled the production Qwen GDN head ratios, but the fused MTP post-convolution kernel accepted at most eight verification tokens. Qwen3.6 DSpark K=8 verifies `K + 1 = 9` tokens, so all 30 GDN layers otherwise fall back to the Triton sequence. This PR adds a width-9 specialization while preserving the existing `MaxTokens=8` specialization for older widths. The public operator ABI and build configuration are unchanged. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py python -m pytest -q tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py python -m pytest -q \ 'tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py::test_dspark_correctness_and_acceptance_rate[qwen3.6-speculators]' pre-commit run --files \ csrc/libtorch_stable/gdn/fused_gdn_decode_kernel.cu \ vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py \ tests/kernels/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py \ tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py ``` ## Test Results - Low-level post-convolution tests: **77 passed**. - GDN MTP model-path tests: **16 passed**. - Pre-commit on all four changed files: **passed**. - Official 200-question NVFP4 DSpark test: **passed**; GSM8K accuracy `0.875`, acceptance rate `0.454`, acceptance length `4.630`. ### Full-model generation The official `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` target and `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark` draft were tested at TP1 in eager mode with greedy 64-token generation, three warmup rounds, and 15 measured ABBA rounds within one model load: | Batch | Full-model generation speedup | TPOT speedup | Generation / TPOT wins | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | **1.121x** | **1.135x** | 15/15 / 15/15 | | 4 | **1.119x** | **1.130x** | 15/15 / 15/15 | `Full-model generation` is synchronized elapsed time for one complete offline `LLM.generate` call over the full batch, including prefill and decode; model loading, warmup, arm switching, probes, metrics, and HTTP/network serving are excluded. At B4 it is full-batch completion time. The table reports the median of 15 paired fallback/fused ratios. Non-timed probes confirmed that all 30 GDN layers saw width nine: the fused arm used CUDA on every eligible call and the fallback arm used it on none. All 300 measured requests had identical prompt IDs, output IDs, and speculative work across arms, with zero cached tokens. B2/B8/B16 timings were excluded because speculative work differed, although output IDs matched. ### Kernel boundary Fixed-input Qwen3.6 TP1 width-9 benchmarks used 60 paired ABBA samples per batch and mode; ranges below cover B1/B4/B16/B64: | GPU | Eager paired-median range | CUDA Graph paired-median range | Outcomes | |---|---:|---:|---:| | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) | **1.017x-1.644x** | **1.009x-1.359x** | 479 wins, 1 tie, 0 losses | | NVIDIA H20 (SM90a) | **1.442x-1.918x** | **1.423x-1.789x** | 479 wins, 1 tie, 0 losses | Maximum width-9 output/full-state relative L2 was `4.174e-5 / 5.521e-8` on the RTX PRO 6000 and `3.37e-5 / 5.48e-8` on H20 at the production FP32-state geometry. For tested widths up to eight, outputs and full state were bitwise equal to base, and audited `MaxTokens=8` device code was byte-identical. These are custom out-of-tree kernel-boundary measurements. The H20 audit did not use a Qwen3.6 DSpark checkpoint and makes no model-level or serving end-to-end claim.

signal.title: [Bug]: LoRA + Muse-Glimmer-30B: AssertionError in lora_shrink (token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M) at startup profiling, on stock nightly and regardless of adapter targets
signal.text: Enabling LoRA on Muse-Glimmer-30B kills the engine at startup, during the profiling dummy run, before any request is served. We hit this on our production fork first, then reproduced it on stock nightly in a fresh environment, so we ran a small discrimination matrix before reporting. All four cells fail on the same assert. **Failure:** ``` File ".../vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_shrink_op.py", in _lora_shrink assert token_lora_mapping.size(0) == M AssertionError EngineCore failed to start. ``` **Minimal repro:** ``` vllm serve bullerwins/Muse-Glimmer-30B-NVFP4 \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 4 \ --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 8 \ --lora-modules probe=<rank-8 adapter> ``` The adapter content does not matter. Ours is a no-op probe (lora_B all zeros, rank 8, q/k/v/o + gate/up/down over the 52 text layers). Boot without `--enable-lora` is clean on the same checkpoint. **The matrix we ran (all four fail identically):** | stack | adapter targets | result | |---|---|---| | nightly `0.26.1rc1.dev1054+g6feafb8b7`, py3.12, torch 2.13.0+cu130, RTX 5090, fresh RunPod env | bare module names (`q_proj`, ...) | AssertionError | | same stock nightly, second fresh env | regex anchored to `model.language_model.layers...` (the pattern community adapters use) | AssertionError | | our fork (older base + local patches unrelated to LoRA), RTX 5090 | bare names | AssertionError | | our fork, `--enforce-eager` | anchored regex | AssertionError | The eager run rules out a compile or cudagraph interaction. Anchoring the target_modules to the language model, which is how every published Muse-Glimmer adapter on the Hub scopes its targets, changes nothing at boot time, so the failure is not about the adapter accidentally matching vision modules by name. **What looks relevant:** Muse-Glimmer is a multimodal ConditionalGeneration model, and this smells like a cousin of #26976 (visual encoder wrongly marked LoRA-enabled during profile_run, closed but per the last comments still biting qwen3-vl users on 0.11.0). The profile dummy run on this model includes vision tokens, and the LoRA token mapping length ends up desynchronized from M as lora_shrink sees it. For contrast, a hybrid but text-profiled model (Qwen3.5-9B, standard docker image) accepts the same style of no-op adapter without trouble on our side, which points at the multimodal profiling path rather than LoRA in general. Worth noting for whoever picks this up: as far as we can tell nobody currently serves Muse-Glimmer LoRA adapters through vLLM. The published adapters (lemuralabs, PursuitOfDataScience, sequelbox and others) all document transformers + peft on the bf16 base only. So this path may simply never have worked for this model. And if the startup assert gets fixed, #48862 (NVFP4 + LoRA illegal memory access on first request) is probably waiting right behind it for the quantized case. Happy to test patches, we have the repro down to a few minutes on a rented 5090. Full tracebacks from both stacks available on request.
