signal.title: [RFC]: PyTorch vLLM correctness audit
signal.text: ### Motivation #### Fix coincidentally correct tests flagged by numeric stability audit Our goal is to smoothen the handoff between PyTorch and vLLM during release. Some tests in vllm may either expect a guarantee in correctness from PyTorch that is not valid causing misleading test failures that aren't true failures or they do not verify the property they intend to. This can lead to hard to debug failing tests against new releases costing significant development time and CI costs. The audit identifies tests that are **coincidentally correct** (CC) — tests that pass today but rely on unstated numeric assumptions that a PyTorch update could silently break. These patterns are identified as a contract of correctness between PyTorch and vLLM, which is documented at [correctness-contract](https://github.com/morrison-turnansky/vllm-test-audit/blob/main/skills/audit-contract/SKILL.md). While we believe that these tests can be identified automatically via agents, we first want to introduce the idea to the community. All issues and PRs involved with this audit will be reviewed and verified during this initial phase. If the community finds value in this, we can consider adding this agentic linting to the CI or run at regular intervals (nightly, monthly, etc.). We will present evaluation metrics of our agents performance before anything is exposed to upstream CI. ### Proposed Change. This issue tracks incremental PRs that fix individual CC-flagged tests. Each PR will reference this issue, cite the specific audit clause, and make the test compliant. If a test is made compliant and is now failing that is useful signal, but we should separate source code fixes from test code fixes during out initial pass. ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. @zou3519 @dougbtv ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Currently, using `vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv4-cu129`, the model fails during initialization with: ```text RuntimeError: Assertion error (.../deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/hyperconnection.hpp:56): Unsupported architecture ``` This still happens with --enforce-eager, so it seems related to the DeepGEMM / HyperConnection kernels rather than torch.compile. signal.title: [KV offload] Order CPU->GPU loads against the compute stream
signal.text: On models that zero freshly allocated KV blocks (any model with mamba layers, i.e. `needs_kv_cache_zeroing`), a CPU->GPU load in the offloading connector can be silently wiped. `SingleDirectionOffloadingHandler.transfer_async` waited on the compute stream only for GPU->CPU. Loads ran on their own stream with no ordering against the compute stream, which zeroes freshly allocated blocks. When the copy lands first, a pending zeroing of its destination blocks wipes it and the request attends over zeros for its whole cache-hit prefix. No crash, no error, just degraded output. Why the scheduler-side guard doesn't cover this: `_skip_zero_block_ids` only edits the zero list of the step being scheduled — it cannot retract a zeroing already shipped in an earlier step's `SchedulerOutput` for a since-reallocated block. Sync scheduling makes that safe implicitly: the engine blocks on each step's output, so shipped zeroing has provably executed before any later load submits. Async scheduling removes that wait, leaving the pair unordered across the two streams — safe by timing only, which nothing enforces. The skip set remains the only possible guard for writers that bypass CUDA streams (NIXL/RDMA); the stream wait is the only ordering against zeroing already dispatched. Verified on H100 that it is a real guard — same test, same image, with and without the one-line change: | | result | |---|---| | without the fix | fails, 4/5 trials, all 32 loaded blocks zeroed | | with the fix | passes, 5/5 trials |

signal.title: [Bugfix] Include device index in compile cache paths
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix compile cache collisions when multiple vLLM engines share a process but target different CUDA devices (e.g. multi-engine threaded inference). The inductor and AOT compile cache paths (`backends.py`, `decorators.py`) include rank and data-parallel index but not the CUDA device index. When two engines on different devices (cuda:0 vs cuda:1) resolve to the same rank/dp_rank, they share a cache directory. Inductor-generated code embeds device-specific stream references (via `get_raw_stream`), so loading artifacts compiled for one device on another causes `CUDA driver error: invalid argument`. This PR appends the current accelerator device index to the cache directory name (`rank_{rank}_{dp_rank}` → `rank_{rank}_{dp_rank}_dev{dev}`), giving each device its own cache. For the common single-device case the path simply gains a `_dev0` suffix with no behavioral change. ## Test Plan This was tested using the [experimental free-threaded Python build](https://github.com/nascheme/vllm-ft-build) of vllm. - Multi-device: run two vLLM engines on different CUDA devices within the same process with `torch.compile` enabled; verify each engine writes to its own cache directory and no cross-device cache loading occurs. - Single-device: confirm the cache path gains the `_dev0` suffix and compilation/loading works as before. ## Test Result Confirmed that with the fix, multi-engine inference on separate devices no longer produces `CUDA driver error: invalid argument` from cross-device cache hits. Assisted-by: Claude

signal.title: [Frontend] Use VLLMValidationError for batch request URL validation
signal.text: ## Purpose Small follow-up to the ongoing effort to adopt the typed `VLLMValidationError` in the OpenAI-compatible frontend (merged #49214, #49217). This converts the remaining raw `ValueError` raises in `download_bytes_from_url` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/run_batch.py`) to `VLLMValidationError`. These branches all validate the **user-provided URL** of a batch request (data-URL encoding/format, allowed media domain, and URL scheme), so they now carry `parameter="url"` and, where the value is small and useful, the offending `value` (the rejected hostname or URL scheme). No behavioral change: `VLLMValidationError` subclasses `ValueError`, so existing `except ValueError` handling keeps working while callers additionally get structured validation metadata (`parameter`/`value`), consistent with the rest of the frontend. **Not a duplicate:** the broader error-handling standardization in #49665 (`VLLMError` hierarchy) and status mappings like #43380 do not touch `run_batch.py`; no open PR modifies this file. This is a narrow, file-scoped follow-up to the already-merged #49214/#49217, orthogonal to those efforts. ## Test Plan - `pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/openai/run_batch.py tests/entrypoints/openai/test_run_batch.py` - `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/test_run_batch.py -k download_bytes -q` - `rg "raise ValueError" vllm/entrypoints/openai/run_batch.py` returns no matches. ## Test Result - Added unit tests asserting the structured metadata (`parameter="url"`, rejected hostname/scheme as `value`) on the domain- and scheme-rejection paths. Existing `download_bytes_*` tests are unaffected — `VLLMValidationError` subclasses `ValueError`, so `pytest.raises(ValueError, match=...)` still matches. - `download_bytes_from_url` unit tests run in the entrypoints CI job (cannot build vLLM locally on macOS/arm64 — no precompiled wheel). - `rg "raise ValueError" vllm/entrypoints/openai/run_batch.py` returns no matches. --- AI assistance (Cursor + Claude Code) was used to draft this change; I reviewed every changed line and am responsible for its correctness.
signal.author: tanchao

signal.title: [Core] Add dynamo_timed tracing for print_readable
signal.text: ## Purpose When analyzing compile-time traces via TORCH_TRACE / tlparse, there is an unexplained gap at the tail of `VllmBackend.__call__`, after `vllm_piecewise_interpret` and before `vllm.generate_execution_code`. This change adds `dynamo_timed` instrumentation for `vllm_print_readable`, which serializes the split graph to a readable Python string for the computation_graph.py cache file. Note: `generate_execution_code` and `compile_execution_fn` already have `@dynamo_timed` decorators in `codegen.py`, so no additional wrappers are needed for those. This runs only once during startup and is cheap. ## Test Plan Run vLLM with `TORCH_TRACE` enabled on Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct and verify the new timing entry appears in the trace output. ## Test Result Verified end-to-end on Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct. The new timing entry appears in traces and accounts for the previously unexplained gap. No performance regression. --- This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude).

signal.title: (security) fix: enforce decoder prompt-length validation for skip-che…
signal.text: Multimodal processors that set skip_prompt_length_check=True (Nemotron Parse, Whisper, FireRedLID) were bypassing decoder prompt-length validation, allowing overlong token_ids to reach the worker's fixed-width input batch via the /inference/v1/generate features path. Restrict the skip to encoder prompts only, which is the original intent (encoder prompts are padded).

(EngineCore pid=436) ERROR 07-20 06:56:35 [v1/engine/core.py:1569] File ".../vllm/multimodal/cache.py", line 607, in get_and_update_features (EngineCore pid=436) ERROR 07-20 06:56:35 [v1/engine/core.py:1569] feature.data = self.get_and_update_item(feature.data, cache_key) (EngineCore pid=436) ERROR 07-20 06:56:35 [v1/engine/core.py:1569] File ".../vllm/multimodal/cache.py", line 660, in get_and_update_item (EngineCore pid=436) ERROR 07-20 06:56:35 [v1/engine/core.py:1569] assert mm_item is not None, f"Expected a cached item for {mm_hash=}" (EngineCore pid=436) ERROR 07-20 06:56:35 [v1/engine/core.py:1569] AssertionError: Expected a cached item for mm_hash='deadbeef...deadbeef' (APIServer pid=1) INFO: 127.0.0.1:41576 - "POST /inference/v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` For contrast, the same body with valid features.kwargs_data, or the same hash once warmed, returns finish_reason":"length" at HTTP 200. signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #49181. The non-streaming `/inference/v1/generate` path serialized an engine `finish_reason="error"` as a successful HTTP 200 response. signal.title: [Bug]: runai_streamer + MTP drafter fails to load weights from model_streamer local cache
signal.text: ### Your current environment docker image vllm-openai:v0.20.1 ### 🐛 Describe the bug - Model: s3://models/Qwen_Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8/ - Loader: runai_streamer - All model files present in S3 (see listing below). **Behavior:** - If I start vllm (vllm-openai:v0.20.1) without MTP (speculative decoding) enabled, the model loads and serves correctly from S3 via runai_streamer. - If I add `speculative_config={"method": "mtp", ...}` (e.g., for Qwen-3 MTP), the engine fails with: ``` RuntimeError: Cannot find any safetensors model weights with `/root/.cache/vllm/assets/model_streamer/<hash>` ``` (See full log excerpt below.) - Review of the S3 path shows all expected safetensors (layers-*.safetensors, mtp.safetensors, outside.safetensors, model.safetensors.index.json, etc.) are present. - The error only happens when MTP is enabled, and only during the drafter model load phase. **Theory / Tracing:** - vLLM loads the main model weights from S3 directly via runai_streamer. - For speculative MTP/drafter, vLLM attempts to reload (from a local cache path like `/root/.cache/vllm/assets/model_streamer/<hash>`) and uses the runai_streamer loader's list_safetensors() function. - This function (by design) is non-recursive and only searches for top-level `*.safetensors` files. - The model_streamer cache structure does NOT expose the weights at the root, and so loader returns none found, even though the S3 source is correct. **Log excerpt (abridged):** ``` (Worker_TP1 pid=170) ERROR ... RuntimeError: Cannot find any safetensors model weights with `/root/.cache/vllm/assets/model_streamer/d7905c16` (Worker_TP0 pid=165) ERROR ... RuntimeError: Cannot find any safetensors model weights with `/root/.cache/vllm/assets/model_streamer/d7905c16` (EngineCore pid=150) ERROR ... Exception: WorkerProc initialization failed due to an exception in a background process ... (APIServer pid=1) RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. ``` **Sample S3 path listing (abridged):** ```text layers-0.safetensors layers-1.safetensors ... layers-39.safetensors mtp.safetensors outside.safetensors model.safetensors.index.json config.json README.md ... ``` **Summary:** - Model works with runai_streamer loader unless MTP is enabled. - With MTP, drafter load fails due to not finding weights in the local streamer cache (used by vLLM for the draft model). - The root cause seems to be vLLM pointing the loader at a local cache dir whose layout doesn't expose safetensors at the root, which list_safetensors() does not recurse into. - Possibly a vLLM cache layout or loader usage bug, or a need for recursive search in the loader for this scenario. Would appreciate insight if this is a known bug or wrong configuration, or if a workaround exists. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix MTP draft model using local cache path instead of S3 URL with runai_streamer
signal.text:
## Purpose Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42060. ## Root Cause - `ModelConfig.__init__` calls `maybe_pull_model_tokenizer_for_runai()`, which on detecting an S3 URI: - Sets `self.model_weights` = original S3 URL (for weight loading) - Sets `self.model `= local cache path (for HF config parsing) - SpeculativeConfig creates a new `ModelConfig` for the MTP draft model using `self.target_model_config.model`, which is already the local cache path - The new `ModelConfig.__init__` runs `maybe_pull_model_tokenizer_for_runai()`, but the local cache path is not an S3 URI → skipped → model_weights is never set - `RunaiModelStreamerLoader.load_model()` checks `model_config.model_weights`, finds it empty, falls back to `model_config.model` (the local cache path) - The local cache directory structure has no top-level `safetensors` files → `list_safetensors()` finds nothing → `RuntimeError` ## Test Plan Unable to reproduce E2E without a runai_streamer + S3 environment; added a unit test with mocks to verify the config-layer fix. `python -m pytest tests/test_config.py::test_mtp_draft_uses_model_weights_not_local_cache -v` ## Test Result ---

signal.title: fix(security): widen int32 pointer arithmetic to int64 in CUDA kernels
signal.text: ## Summary - Widen 32-bit integer pointer offset arithmetic to 64-bit in CUDA kernels to prevent cross-user data disclosure when `num_tokens * stride` overflows `2^32` - Applies the established fix pattern from `451227cb3f` (activation_kernels.cu): cast `blockIdx.x` to `int64_t` before multiplying by stride/dimension - Covers LayerNorm, LayerNorm-quant (FP8), MoE routing, and AllSpark W8A16 GEMM kernels ## Affected kernels | Kernel | File | Risk | |---|---|---| | `rms_norm_kernel` | `layernorm_kernels.cu` | High -- confirmed exploitable with PoC | | `rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High -- FP8 quantized path | | `fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` (both specializations) | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High | | `moeSoftmax` / `moeSigmoid` / `moeTopK` | `topk_softmax_kernels.cu` | Moderate | | AllSpark W8A16 GmemTile / ComputeTile | `allspark_qgemm_w8a16.cu` | Low (defense in depth) | ## Root cause CUDA built-in `blockIdx.x` is `unsigned int` (32-bit). When multiplied by a 32-bit `hidden_size` or stride, the product wraps at 2^32, causing a kernel block to read/write another user's hidden state within the same batch. With `hidden_size = 8192`, the overflow triggers at ~524,288 tokens. ## Fix pattern ```cpp // Before (32-bit overflow) scalar_t* out_row = out + blockIdx.x * hidden_size; // After (64-bit safe) const int64_t token_idx = blockIdx.x; scalar_t* out_row = out + token_idx * hidden_size; ``` For host-side code, `int input_stride` is widened to `int64_t input_stride` to match the kernel parameter change. ## Test plan - [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (clang-format, typos, etc.) - [ ] Existing LayerNorm kernel tests pass - [ ] Existing MoE kernel tests pass - [ ] CI build succeeds on CUDA targets Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signal.title: [DCP] Default query replication for GLM sparse attention
signal.text: ## Summary - add `--dcp-q-replicate` and `--no-dcp-q-replicate` as explicit CLI options; - preserve `VLLM_DCP_Q_REPLICATE` as the highest-precedence override; - enable query replication automatically for `glm_moe_dsa` models when decode DCP is enabled and PCP is not enabled; - keep query replication opt-in for other MLA model families. The automatic default removes GLM's decode query all-gather at the cost of replicating the query projection weights across DCP ranks. Explicit CLI or environment selections still override the model default. ## Performance and memory GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP=4, DCP=4, 32K input tokens, 128 output tokens, batch 8, two warmups, five measured iterations: - QREP off: 20.1777 s - QREP on: 19.7426 s - delta: -0.4351 s (-2.16%) With QREP enabled, a fresh DCP backend comparison measured: | DCP backend | Average latency | | --- | ---: | | `ag_rs` | 19.7636 s | | `a2a` | 18.0213 s | For the matched 32K benchmark configuration, model-loading memory increased from 110.37 GiB/rank to 114.94 GiB/rank with QREP, approximately +4.57 GiB/rank. ## Model evaluation GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP=4, DCP=4, GSM8K 5-shot, 300 questions: - automatic GLM QREP default: 94.0% accuracy, 0% invalid outputs; - explicit QREP off: 95.0% accuracy, 0% invalid outputs. The QREP-off evaluation used `max_num_seqs=32` because FlashInfer's sparse-MLA workspace overflowed when all prompts were scheduled concurrently. Both runs evaluated the same 300 questions with the same decoding settings. The one-point difference is not significant at this sample size. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, benchmarking, profiling analysis, and drafting this description. The human submitter has reviewed.

signal.title: [ROCm] Cpu offload for ROCm 7.13+ to align the hipMemcpyBatchAsync params and perf in 7.14x
signal.text: ## Purpose This is related to the issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44341 In a previous enablement PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40549, we enabled cpu offloading on ROCm, and we noticed the shortcoming of the hipMemcpyBatchAsync API lacked support on numAttrs paramter. This PR is to fix that situation. This PR is intended to be future compatible and backward compatible. Below is the details: For the hipMemcpyBatchAsync API, (1) ROCm 7.13 will accept numAttrs > 0 while ROCm 7.2.1 - ROCm 7.2.3 do not. Prepare the code to accommodate this change so that it works now and after the vllm is upgraded to ROCm 7.13+ base. While testing, found that the hipMemcpyBatchAsync performance was not really doing any batching. Issue was discussed internally, and was addressed later and the fix would be packaged to rocm 7.14x. (2) On rocm 7.14 or rocm 7.15, the hipMemcpyBatchAsync performance is optimized comparing with the non-batching hipMemcpyAsync API. (3) When testing with a staging rocm 7.15 docker image, found an problem with `count` in the `hipMemcpyBatchAsync` API. hipMemcpyBatchAsync faults (GPU memory access fault -> abort/segfault) when count > 8192, regardless of copy size, direction, or numAttrs. This is being addressed by runtime team. For now, I added an enviornment variable VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS to chunk the batch copies to work around this problem. It has similar problem on a rocm 7.14 docker. ## Test Plan (1) vllm unit test, regression test with vllm nightly image (1.1) Tested hipMemcpyBatchAsync API in a rocm7.13 container and verified it accepts numAttrs=1. (1.2) Tested the micro-benchmarking to compare hipMemcpyBatchAsync and hipMemcpyAsync performance, and found the performance issue of hipMemcpyBatchAsync and filed an internal ticket. (2) Tested with a rocm 7.14 or 7.15 to check the micro-benchmarking to compare hipMemcpyBatchAsync and hipMemcpyAsync performance, after the hipMemcpyBatchAsync is optimized and packaged. (3) regression test with vllm nightly, rocm 7.2.3 ## Test Result (1) micro-benchmarking test: Using a hip program to benchmark the hipMemcpyBatchAsync(numAttrs=1) performance vs hipMemcpyAsync. In ROCm 7.2.3, the performance of hipMemcpyBatchAsync is almost the same (i.e., 1x) as hipMemcpyAsync, as there is no batching implemented. The optimization is happening rocm 7.14+. So on a wheel-packaged ROCm 7.15 nightly (8× MI350X, gfx950), `hipMemcpyBatchAsync(numAttrs=1)` is now 6–19× faster than a per-op `hipMemcpyAsync` loop, reproducible across two runs: dir | block | batch | per-op | ratio -- | -- | -- | -- | -- store (D→H) | 4 KiB | 25.4 GB/s | 1.6 GB/s | ×15.4 store (D→H) | 64 KiB | 48.9 GB/s | 6.3 GB/s | ×7.7 load (H→D) | 4 KiB | 31.5 GB/s | 1.7 GB/s | ×19.1 load (H→D) | 64 KiB | 49.0 GB/s | 5.8 GB/s | ×8.4 (2) agentic workflow test: On the same rocm 7.15 docker, performed an agentx vllm workflow test, and found an issue with hipMemcpyBatchAsync api when count > 8192, GPU would seg fault. Discussed internally, and the fix is on the way, but will not be in rocm7.14x. So, for now, added an env to chunk the batches to avoid the seg fault VLLM_KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_BATCH_DESCRIPTORS . (3) regression test (similar test in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40549): Phase | Result -- | -- Build from source | ✅ 0.27.2rc1.dev181+gbd573eced.rocm723 on nightly (ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.12); PR symbols verified in the imported vllm (1) Unit tests | ✅ 53/53 passed — descriptor chunking at the 8192 cap, HIP-version numAttrs gate, HIP loader fallbacks, scheduler (12), worker (2) Integration | ✅ 2/2 runnable passed — gpt-oss-20b eager + lazy: CPU KV hits beat cold prefill on the patched path. 6 cases deselected (gated models, no HF token) (3) Serve smoke | ✅ amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-Preview TP8 + VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1 --kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 600 — startup complete, /v1/models healthy (4) gsm8k (200q) | ✅ offload 0.950 / baseline 0.955 (both filters) — 1 question apart, inside ±0.0154 stderr; matches #40549's 0.955/0.940

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix HYV3 shared_mlp prefix for compressed-tensors ignore matching
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes a `KeyError: 'layers.N.mlp.shared_mlp.down_proj.weight'` raised at load time when serving a W4A16 compressed-tensors hy_v3 checkpoint whose shared expert (`shared_mlp`) is intentionally kept in BF16. ## Root cause `HYV3MoEFused` builds its shared expert as an `HYV3FeedForward` with `prefix=f"{prefix}"`, omitting the `.shared_mlp` segment. The `Linear` layers inside it (`gate_up_proj`, `down_proj`) register their parameters under `...mlp.shared_mlp.<proj>.*` — the `shared_mlp` attribute name is appended by `nn.Module` regardless of the `prefix` argument. `CompressedTensorsConfig` decides whether a `Linear` is quantized by matching the **prefix** against its `ignore` list. With the missing segment, the ignore check saw `...mlp.down_proj` instead of `...mlp.shared_mlp.down_proj`, so a `re:.*shared_mlp.*` ignore entry failed to match. Consequence: the shared expert was built as a quantized `Linear` expecting `weight_packed`/`scale`/`shape`, while real W4A16 hy_v3 checkpoints (produced by llm-compressor) correctly keep `shared_mlp` in BF16 as `.weight`. This raised the `KeyError` at load. ## Fix Pass `prefix=f"{prefix}.shared_mlp"` so the ignore check matches the real parameter registration path and the shared expert is built unquantized (`UnquantizedLinearMethod`), aligning with the BF16 checkpoint. Parameter registration names are unchanged. ## Duplicate-work check Searched `vllm-project/vllm`: - Open PRs matching `shared_mlp` / `hy_v3 compressed` / `shared_mlp prefix`: only #47813 (`[NPU][0-DAY] Hy3 0-day adaptation on Ascend NPU`) — a hardware-backend adaptation, unrelated to compressed-tensors prefix matching. - Issues matching `hy_v3 shared_mlp` / `hy_v3 compressed tensors`: none. No existing PR addresses this fix. ## Test commands and results This is a one-line fix to the prefix passed at module construction. Validation: - End-to-end: on a CUDA server, before the fix the W4A16 hy_v3 checkpoint failed to load with the `KeyError` above; after applying this one-line fix the checkpoint loads and the vLLM service starts successfully. The fix changes which Linear method the shared expert is built with; it does not alter the forward computation (the unquantized shared expert computes exactly the BF16 path the checkpoint was quantized against). No model-eval accuracy regression is expected; reviewer may request evals if deemed necessary. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used in producing this change: root-cause diagnosis was developed with AI assistance. The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and validated the fix end-to-end on a CUDA server.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix six quantization exception messages split across positional args
signal.text: ## Purpose Six `raise` statements pass their message fragments as separate positional arguments to a builtin exception. Python stores those as `args`, so the rendered message is the tuple repr rather than the sentence: ``` RuntimeError: ('Quantization scheme is not supported for ', 'the current GPU. Required capability: ', '90. Current capability: 80.') ``` ``` ValueError: ('For NVFP4 weights, input quantization must also be NVFP4 format, ', 'None for NVFP4A16') ``` The sites, all found by walking the AST for `raise <builtin>(str, str, ...)`: | file | line | exception | |---|---|---| | `compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py` | 386 | `RuntimeError` | | `compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py` | 394 | `RuntimeError` | | `compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py` | 739 | `ValueError` | | `compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe.py` | 90 | `ValueError` | | `compressed_tensors_moe/compressed_tensors_moe.py` | 188 | `ValueError` | | `quark/quark.py` | 273 | `RuntimeError` | These are the messages a user sees when a checkpoint's quantization scheme doesn't match the GPU, so they land in exactly the situation where the text needs to be readable. ## Test Plan Joined the fragments into a single string at each site, then compared the concatenated message text before and after by parsing both revisions with `ast` and folding each `raise`'s string arguments together: ``` compressed_tensors.py: 10 messages / 0 changed compressed_tensors_moe.py: 5 messages / 1 changed quark.py: 11 messages / 0 changed ``` The one intentional text change drops a doubled space that the split form had: ``` before: 'For Fused MoE layers, only format: {} and bits: {} is supported but got format: {} and bits: {}' after: 'For Fused MoE layers, only format: {} and bits: {} is supported but got format: {} and bits: {}' ``` ## Test Result `ruff format --check` reports all three files already formatted. `ruff check` flags `I001` on `compressed_tensors.py` and `quark.py`, but both report the same `I001` on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout, so it is pre-existing and untouched here. No behaviour changes beyond the message text — the raise conditions, exception types and control flow are unchanged.

signal.title: [Frontend] Prevent Kimi K3 reserved markers in response text
signal.text: ## Summary - exclude the one-token Kimi K3 reserved marker heads (`<|open|>`, `<|close|>`, and `<|end_of_msg|>`) from response text - apply the same constraint to the Python and Rust frontend structural-tag builders - add grammar behavior coverage for reserved-marker prefixes ## Why Kimi K3 channel markers are multi-token sequences. For example, the tools-open marker is emitted as: ``` <|open|> tools <|sep|> ``` The response body previously excluded only the complete `<|open|>tools<|sep|>` string. `any_text_excluding` masks the token that completes an excluded string, so the matcher could first accept `<|open|>` and `tools` as ordinary response text and reject the transition only when `<|sep|>` was sampled. A real failure followed exactly this path: 1. The model tried to transition into the tools channel by generating `<|open|>tools<|sep|>`. 2. The grammar consumed `<|open|>tools` inside response text. 3. It masked `<|sep|>` after that prefix had already been committed. 4. The model had to choose a different continuation. Observed outputs appended filler such as `工具`, `请稍等`, or a zero-width character, exposing a partial `<|open|>tools...` marker as response content while the tool channel never opened. The same failure mode applies when the model reaches for `<|close|>message<|sep|>`: excluding the complete marker can strand generation after `<|close|>message`. Excluding the one-token reserved heads moves the decision to the first token. `<|open|>` and `<|end_of_msg|>` are blocked inside response text. `<|close|>` remains available through the response tag's valid `<|close|>response<|sep|>` end branch, so accepting it commits the grammar to that boundary before a sibling marker suffix can enter text. ## Related work #51355 covers a broader set of Kimi K3 structured-output fixes and currently uses complete-marker exclusions. This PR isolates the prefix-safe constraint and keeps the Python and Rust frontend builders aligned. ## Testing - `python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -k kimi_k3 -q` — 30 passed - `cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser kimi_k3` — 32 passed - Ruff 0.14.0 format and lint checks - `cargo fmt --check` - `git diff --check` ## AI assistance This PR includes code developed with OpenAI Codex assistance. I reviewed the complete diff and validation results.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode]Preserve user --speculative-config overrides for speculators-format models
signal.text: ## Purpose When the target model is in speculators format, [`maybe_override_with_speculators`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/transformers_utils/config.py) rebuilds `speculative_config` from the speculators `config_dict` and returns it without merging `vllm_speculative_config`. Any field passed via `--speculative-config` is silently dropped on that path — including `attention_backend` introduced in #39930, `moe_backend`, and `num_speculative_tokens`. This PR applies the user-provided overrides on top of the speculators-extracted config and locks `model` to the speculators model path so the drafter still loads from the right weights. ## Test Plan - Unit: `pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py -v` — 5 new tests covering baseline extraction, `attention_backend` override preservation, `model` lock, runtime knob overrides (`num_speculative_tokens`, `moe_backend`), and non-speculators pass-through. - E2E repro on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` + `nm-testing/dflash-qwen3-8b-speculators` (DFlash, fp8), iterating `attention_backend ∈ {None, FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, FLEX_ATTENTION}`. ## Test Result Unit: ``` $ pytest tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py -v ======================== 5 passed in 2.35s ======================== ``` E2E (Qwen3-8B + DFlash speculator, single RTX PRO 4500): | `attention_backend` | Before fix | After fix | |---|---|---| | `None` (auto) | `cfg.attention_backend == None` | `cfg.attention_backend == None` (baseline) | | `FLASH_ATTN` | `cfg.attention_backend == None` (dropped) | `AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN` — same greedy tokens as auto | | `TRITON_ATTN` | `cfg.attention_backend == None` (dropped; ran with auto-selected backend) | `ValueError` at init: `Selected backend AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN is not valid for this configuration. Reason: ['non-causal attention not supported']` — user now told upfront | | `FLEX_ATTENTION` | `cfg.attention_backend == None` (dropped) | `AttentionBackendEnum.FLEX_ATTENTION` — same greedy tokens as auto | ## Follow-up A separate PR will add an end-to-end matrix test covering `(speculator × attention_backend)` combinations exercising this code path — kept separate to keep this fix focused. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Align OpenAI request and response edge cases
signal.text: ## Purpose Align the Rust frontend Chat Completions and Completions wire behavior with Python vLLM for several independent request and response edge cases: - Treat absent, null, and empty `model` values as selecting the default served model across inference and render routes, while continuing to validate non-empty model IDs. - Return `prompt_logprobs` in the vLLM token-ID-keyed shape, including `logprob`, `rank`, and `decoded_token` metadata, for both Chat Completions and Completions responses. - Accept `logprobs=-1` on Completions as the full-vocabulary request and retain configured maximum-logprobs validation for bounded values. - Accept the vLLM `top_k` sentinels `-1` and `0` on both APIs. A null value inherits model generation defaults; an explicit sentinel disables top-k sampling. The signed-value normalization is public beside `SamplingParams`, with serde adapters kept local to generation config and OpenAI request types. - Accept `min_tokens=0` on Chat Completions and preserve it through text sampling lowering. - Default an omitted tool `type` to `function` and omitted function `parameters` to null. - Reject empty `cache_salt` values on both APIs. Each compatibility change is isolated in its own commit and covered by focused request, conversion, response-shape, or lowering tests. ## Test Plan - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` - `cargo nextest run -p vllm-text -p vllm-server` - `cargo clippy -p vllm-text -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` ## Test Result - Formatting check passed. - 438 tests passed; 1 test was skipped by the configured nextest profile. - Clippy passed with warnings denied.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Elastic EP] Restrict target-group warmup to eager mode
signal.text: - Only pre-warm Elastic EP target DP/EP groups when `enforce_eager` guarantees that graph replay is disabled; otherwise defer communicator initialization to the synchronized commit phase. - The leaf failure is lazy `ProcessGroupNCCL`/RCCL communicator connection overlapping HIP graph replay, which can hang or segfault even when the graph is compute-only and NIXL, model execution, and old-group collectives are absent. The motivating failure was [AMD CI build 12228](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12228/list?sid=01a0193f-ea9d-443a-9e06-e4f117c3b1ad&tab=output), where only `cuda_graphs_heavy` hung after target-group creation and before `Prepared reconfiguration`, eventually reaching the 300-second store timeout. #51885 introduced the asynchronous warm collective to reduce eager-mode downtime, but under graph execution it can connect the lazy target communicator while the serving thread is still replaying HIP graphs. A later run of the unchanged code passed, matching the timing-sensitive local reproducer rather than indicating a source-level fix. This change preserves the eager optimization while removing the unsafe graph-mode overlap.
signal.author: AndreasKaratzas

signal.title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Revert adaptive C128A metadata packing
signal.text: ## Summary Revert the adaptive C128A top-k width and packed persistent-buffer views introduced by #50004. The C128A metadata builder runs before FULL CUDA graph replay, but the sparse decode consumer is captured and reuses its capture-time row layout. With #50004, runtime metadata writes packed rows using a batch-dependent `active_topk_width`, while the captured consumer retained the capture-time row stride. Row 0 still started at offset 0, but later rows could be read from stale offsets. This change restores: - `c128a_max_compressed` as the metadata width - capacity-strided slices of the persistent decode and prefill buffers - each persistent buffer's `stride(0)` for Triton metadata writes - removal of the test that asserted the packed layout being reverted Fixes #52448. ## Validation ```text git diff --check .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sparse_mla.py ``` All applicable hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, typos, mypy, SPDX, lazy-import, and forbidden-import checks. The full revert was also evaluated with the exact #52448 request on 2x NVIDIA GB300 using `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` revision `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062`, TP=2 plus expert parallelism, DSpark-7, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, `max_model_len=70000`, concurrency 32, and `max_tokens=16384`: - 256 priming requests plus 256 measured requests - 0/256 issue-signature hits - 0 request errors and 0 `length` finishes - 253 `tool_calls` finishes and 3 `stop` finishes - 8.445 s median measured latency ## Contribution notes - Not a duplicate: `52448 in:body` found no other open PR. The open C128A/sparse-MLA keyword matches (#48805, #41836, and #41834) address warmup, prefill, or model enablement rather than reverting #50004. This updates the existing #51318 instead of opening another PR. - AI assistance was used for investigation, patch preparation, validation, and this PR update. The submitting human must review every changed line and be able to defend the change before merge.

signal.title: [Build] Propagate vLLM version to Rust binaries
signal.text: ## Summary - derive a device-independent vLLM source version with setuptools-scm for Python-driven and standalone Rust builds - embed the same version in `vllm-rs`, `vllm-bench`, and the Rust frontend version endpoint - expose Git metadata to selective Docker Rust build stages while suppressing the artificial dirty state caused by omitted tracked files ## Affected outputs | Surface | Effect | | --- | --- | | `vllm-rs --version` | Reports the embedded vLLM source version. | | `vllm-bench --version` | Reports the embedded vLLM source version instead of the workspace crate version (`0.1.0`). | | Rust frontend `GET /version` | `rust_frontend_version` reports the embedded vLLM source version. The engine-reported `version` field keeps its existing behavior. | ## Affected build paths | Build path | Embedded Rust version | | --- | --- | | Nightly/release wheel builds from a Git checkout | The setuptools-scm source version. `VLLM_VERSION_OVERRIDE` is honored through `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`. | | Docker builds using `docker/Dockerfile`, `.cpu`, `.rocm`, `.rocm_gfx1250`, or `.xpu` | The source version resolved from the mounted Git metadata. Selective-copy stages set `dirty=false` because omitted tracked files would otherwise make the partial worktree appear dirty. | | Local `bash build_rust.sh` | The setuptools-scm source version when Git metadata is available. | | Direct `cargo build` | `VLLM_RS_BUILD_VERSION` when explicitly supplied; otherwise the workspace crate version (`0.1.0`). | The embedded Rust version stays device-independent. Python distribution version handling remains unchanged, including platform suffixes such as CPU, CUDA, ROCm, TPU, and XPU variants. Repackaging an existing prebuilt Rust binary preserves the version embedded when that binary was built. ## Motivation Rust artifacts currently identify themselves using workspace crate metadata, which stays at `0.1.0` and does not identify the corresponding nightly or release vLLM source revision. This change resolves the source version before compiling Rust and passes it through `VLLM_RS_BUILD_VERSION`. `get_vllm_version()` runs first during Python packaging so `VLLM_VERSION_OVERRIDE`, propagated through `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`, also applies to the Rust artifacts. ## Validation - `cargo nextest run -p vllm-build-info -p vllm-bench -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-server --no-fail-fast` (552 passed, 10 skipped) - injected version output: `vllm-bench 9.8.7` and `vllm-rs 9.8.7` - Cargo fallback output: `vllm-bench 0.1.0` - existing Docker build metadata tests (7 passed) - Ruff, Dockerfile parsing, shell syntax, and `git diff --check`
signal.author: BugenZhao

signal.title: [SM100] Hdim 256 optimized
signal.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> ## Purpose Re-enables FA4 for `head_size=256` on Blackwell, which was temporarily disabled in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52050 because the SM100 2-CTA hd256 kernel rejected `seqused_q/seqused_k` — something vLLM's decoder attention always supplies. That gap is now closed upstream in https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/180, which adds forward `seqused` support along with hd256 optimizations. This PR reverts #52050 and integrates the kernel properly, with a fallback to FA2 for everything it cannot serve: - The kernel reads paged KV through TMA only, with one page per 128-token tile, so the backend now advertises an exact KV cache block size of 128 for hd256. That 128 is chosen automatically when the user does not pin one; a user-pinned `--block-size` that is not a multiple of 128 makes FLASH_ATTN ineligible for hd256 (an error if the backend was requested explicitly). - `forward()` page-aligns `max_seqlen_k` and slices the block table to match; the over-hang is masked out by `seqused_k`. - The kernel has no SplitKV support, so `num_splits=1` is pinned for this path, and cascade attention is disabled. - Selection falls back to FA2 for attention sinks, logits soft capping, mm_prefix, R-SWA and DCP. In practice Gemma-2 (soft capping) and multimodal Gemma-3 (mm_prefix) keep using FA2, while Gemma-1, text-only Gemma-3 and PaliGemma/ColPali get FA4. - The hd256 kernel is opt-in (`supports_fa4_hd256`), so callers that do not build the required call shape — ViT/`mm_encoder_attention`, turboquant, MLA prefill — keep resolving to FA2. - Only `(head_size=256, head_size_v=256)` uses this kernel; `(head_size=256, head_size_v=128)` still takes generic FA4, exactly as it did before #52050. Sliding window on the decoder path is enabled again, since the kernel handles it; encoder inputs (dense `cu_seqlens_k`, no `seqused_k`) still fall back to FA2. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn.py -k fa4_hd256 pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn.py # reproducer from #52050 pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_colpali.py::test_colpali_multimodal_text_query_image_docs ``` ## Test Result On B200 (SM100): ``` tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py 52 passed, 10 skipped tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn.py -k fa4_hd256 8 passed ``` --- AI assistance was used for the vLLM-side changes. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests reported above.
signal.author: simon-veitner-redhat

signal.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash: non-deterministic output at temperature=0, rate scales with concurrency
signal.text:
### Your current environment ``` vLLM : 0.27.1 (installed from PyPI wheel, verified unmodified — all 4735 .py files hash-match the wheel) Model : nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark (NVFP4, DSpark draft head) GPU : NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, 1x, TP=1 (compute capability 10.3) Driver : 580.126.09 torch : 2.13.0+cu132 (CUDA 13.2) OS : Ubuntu 24.04 ``` Serve command: ```bash vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \ --max-model-len 1048576 --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \ --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --enable-prefix-caching \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \ --attention-config '{"use_fp4_indexer_cache":true}' \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 128 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary:** with `temperature=0`, the same prompt returns **different completions** depending only on how many requests are in flight. Greedy decoding should be reproducible, so any variation is a bug. The rate rises with concurrency. #### Reproducer `repro.py` — sends the identical greedy request N times and counts distinct completions: ```python import concurrent.futures as cf, json, sys, time, urllib.request from collections import Counter URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions" MODEL = "nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-nvfp4-DSpark" IDS = [ "c_mhw9v76obuh72x98f4pb8xr3", "o_ftcj97ua0p5heapj5fpng02e", "c_3exww35axs739igmh42hvph1g", "c_8oold74tm25kw4uag86kyj16z", "c_6adnmt0f3gs4xfl4ne2x5zkjo", "c_z72re6iq4gltfujr1zrwll11y", "o_9klm2xr7ta4bnvq8wsdf31hgc", "c_pw4nz8tqm6ykxj02hcv5rb7ed", ] PROMPT = ("Echo each of these identifiers back to me, one per line, prefixed " "with 'ECHO: '. Do not modify any character. Do not add commentary.

" + "
".join(IDS)) BODY = {"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}], "temperature": 0.0, "max_tokens": 2000} def call(_): req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=json.dumps(BODY).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600).read() )["choices"][0]["message"]["content"] n, conc = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]) if conc == 1: outs = [call(i) for i in range(n)] else: with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=conc) as ex: outs = [f.result() for f in cf.as_completed( [ex.submit(call, i) for i in range(n)])] v = Counter(outs) minority = sum(c for _, c in v.most_common()[1:]) print(f"n={len(outs)} conc={conc} DISTINCT={len(v)} " f"minority={minority} ({100*minority/len(outs):.2f}%)") print("EXPECTED at temperature=0: DISTINCT=1") ``` ```bash python repro.py 500 32 ``` #### Results — stock 0.27.1, 10/10 runs non-deterministic Each row is an independent run against the same server. | concurrency | n | runs | minority-output rate | |---|---|---|---| | 8 | 400 | 2 | 0.25%, 0.50% | | 16 | 400 | 3 | 2.25%, 1.75%, 1.75% | | 32 | 500 | 5 | 2.40%, 1.00%, 0.40%, 1.20%, 0.80% | `DISTINCT` was >1 in **every** run (up to 8 distinct completions in 500 requests). "minority" = responses differing from the modal completion. A typical divergence — one identifier comes back altered, the rest of the completion is byte-identical: ``` majority: ...ECHO: c_6adnmt0f3gs4xfl4ne2x5zkjo... variant : ...ECHO: o_9klm5t0f3gs4xfl4ne2x5zkjo... ``` #### This is not float non-determinism from reduction order Requesting `top_logprobs=20` at the divergent position: ``` conc=1 (correct): conc=32 (corrupt): '2' 0.000000 '5' -1.377942 'x' -18.375000 '7' -2.252942 '3' -20.250000 '6' -2.377942 '27' -21.125000 '8' -2.502942 '22' -21.125000 '4' -2.627942 ``` The correct arm is maximally confident: an **18-logprob** gap between top-1 and top-2 (~1e8 probability ratio). The corrupt arm collapses to a near-uniform distribution over digits, margin **0.1–2.0**. Batched-reduction float noise perturbs logits on the order of 1e-3 and could only flip a near-tie. Turning an 18-logprob margin into a coin flip means the **attention output feeding that position differs**, not that a tie broke the other way. The divergence also lands at a consistent token index across runs. #### Notes - Reproduced on **unmodified** 0.27.1 from PyPI (hash-verified against the wheel). - Also reproduces with `--enforce-eager` (4/5 runs non-deterministic), so it is not CUDA-graph capture/replay. - Not `seed`-related: at `temperature=0`, `SamplingParams.sampling_type` returns `GREEDY` before `seed` is consulted (`sampling_params.py`), and passing a seed changes nothing. - Requests were verified to complete successfully; runs with any transport error were discarded rather than counted. The flags above are the standard serving configuration for this model (sparse-MLA block size, fp8 KV cache, FP4 indexer cache, DSpark draft head). I have not isolated the mechanism and don't want to speculate. Happy to run further diagnostics on this hardware — e.g. with speculative decoding or prefix caching disabled, or with different `num_speculative_tokens` — if that helps.
signal.author: apejcic

signal.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Anthropic API: honor the `thinking` request parameter
signal.text: ## AI Claude Code, Opus 5 was part of this change including writing this PR, overseen and validated with human. ## Purpose `AnthropicMessagesRequest` never declared a `thinking` field, so the documented Anthropic request parameter was silently discarded — the model sets no Pydantic `extra` policy, so the default `extra="ignore"` drops it without an error. Clients asking for disabled thinking, a token budget, or omitted reasoning display were answered as though they had asked for nothing, at whatever `output_config.effort` implied. This is user-visible: Claude Code sends `{"type": "adaptive", "display": "omitted"}` on every request. Both instructions were dropped, so every request reasoned at the effort ceiling *and* streamed the reasoning back. On a DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 deployment an ordinary coding question produced 2237 reasoning events over 151 seconds without a single visible output token — the client gave up before the model finished thinking. This adds `AnthropicThinkingConfig` and maps it onto reasoning controls `ChatCompletionRequest` already exposes: | `thinking` | maps to | |---|---| | `{"type": "disabled"}` | `reasoning_effort = "none"` | | `{"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N}` | `thinking_token_budget = N` | | `{"display": "omitted"}` | `include_reasoning = False` | | `{"type": "adaptive"}` | nothing pinned — the model chooses depth | Two design points worth reviewer attention: - **`adaptive` deliberately pins nothing.** Per Anthropic's API, `output_config.effort` is the ceiling and `adaptive` lets the model choose depth beneath it. No frontend-side action makes a model adaptive, so the correct behaviour is to avoid forcing a static value. - **`display` maps to `include_reasoning`, not to any depth control.** It governs visibility only — reasoning still runs and is still billed — so it must not be conflated with effort. `_handle_thinking` runs *after* `_handle_output_config` so an explicit `thinking` overrides the effort-derived default rather than being overwritten by it. ## Test Plan Frontend-only change, so the Python-only dev install is enough — no CUDA rebuild, no GPU: ```bash uv venv .venv --python 3.12 VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . uv pip install pytest pytest-asyncio httpx tblib # tblib is required by tests/conftest.py # New unit tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k TestThinkingConfig # Affected files in full, as a regression check .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \ tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_protocol_exports.py ``` `TestThinkingConfig` covers nine conversion cases: | Case | Asserts | |---|---| | `thinking` absent | `reasoning_effort is None`, `thinking_token_budget is None`, `include_reasoning is True` (regression guard) | | `{"type": "disabled"}` | `reasoning_effort == "none"` | | `disabled` + `output_config.effort="high"` | `reasoning_effort == "none"` — ordering: `thinking` beats the ceiling | | `{"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 2048}` | `thinking_token_budget == 2048` | | `{"type": "enabled"}` without a budget | nothing pinned | | `{"type": "adaptive"}` + `effort="low"` | `reasoning_effort == "low"`, budget unset | | `{"display": "omitted"}` | `include_reasoning is False`, depth untouched | | `{"display": "summarized"}` | `include_reasoning is True` | | `effort="high"` + `adaptive` + `omitted` | the exact payload Claude Code sends | End-to-end against a served model with a reasoning parser (`--reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice`): ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "'"$MODEL"'", "max_tokens": 800, "thinking": {"type": "disabled"}, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain why sourcing an untrusted config file is risky."}] }' | jq '[.content[] | select(.type=="thinking") | .thinking | length]' # expected after this change: [] (or [0]); before: a non-empty reasoning block ``` ## Test Result Unit tests: ``` $ pytest -q tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k TestThinkingConfig ......... [100%] 9 passed, 55 deselected in 2.97s $ pytest -q tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py \ tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_protocol_exports.py .................................................................. [100%] 66 passed in 13.66s ``` The remaining tests under `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/` (`test_messages.py`, 7 tests) error at fixture setup on this machine with `DeviceConfig` unable to detect a device — they boot a real model server and need a GPU. Unrelated to this change; they fail before any of it executes. Lint: `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `check-spdx-header` and `typos` all pass via `pre-commit run`. End-to-end on `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, TP=2, `deepseek_v4` reasoning parser, reasoning-block length in the response: | Request | Before | After | |---|---|---| | no `thinking` field | 149 chars | 149 — unchanged | | `{"type": "disabled"}` | **3058** (silently ignored) | **0**, content returned | | `{"type": "adaptive", "display": "omitted"}` | reasoning streamed | **0** returned, `stop_reason: end_turn` | | `{"type": "adaptive"}` | pinned to the ceiling | 641 chars, nothing pinned | `thinking_token_budget` is rejected by the V2 model runner on current builds ("not yet supported by the V2 model runner"), so the `budget_tokens` branch is covered at the conversion layer rather than end-to-end. ## Impact No behaviour change for requests that omit `thinking`: the field defaults to `None` and the handler returns immediately, so `output_config.effort` remains the only input to reasoning configuration for existing callers. The `thinking`-absent unit test guards this.

signal.title: [Bug]: V1 engine + MTP + GLM-5.1 (DSA + MoE + MLA) — workers hang under sustained traffic, sample_tokens RPC timeout, EngineDeadError
signal.text: ### 🐛 Describe the bug Under V1 engine + MTP speculative decoding + TP=8 + GLM-5.1-FP8 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), workers hang under sustained production traffic. The scheduler is unable to advance — `step_counter=0` in the dump, requests stuck in flight — and after 30s the `sample_tokens` RPC times out, killing EngineCore. The container's outer process survives so vLLM internally restarts the engine (~12-17 min downtime), but this is a recurring failure pattern. This is the same bug `jsboige` diagnosed for `new-TonyWang` in [#35104](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35104#issuecomment-4308377748) — a different bug than what PR #40303 fixes (no `SystemError`, no `memory_fence` on the stack). new-TonyWang's report is buried in #35104 comments and has no standalone issue, so filing here. ### Stack trace ``` File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 1205, in _process_engine_step outputs, model_executed = self.step_fn() File ".../vllm/v1/engine/core.py", line 523, in step_with_batch_queue model_output = future.result() ... File ".../vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 388, in get_response raise TimeoutError(f"RPC call to {method} timed out.") from e TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out. ``` The underlying cause: ``` File ".../vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py", line 756, in dequeue with self.acquire_read(timeout, indefinite) as buf: File ".../shm_broadcast.py", line 675, in acquire_read self._spin_condition.wait(timeout_ms=read_timeout.timeout_ms()) File ".../shm_broadcast.py", line 632, in timeout_ms raise TimeoutError ``` Workers are stuck upstream of the message queue — no output coming back. Scheduler dump confirms it: ``` SchedulerStats(num_running_reqs=2, num_waiting_reqs=0, step_counter=0, kv_cache_usage=0.405, prefix_cache_stats=PrefixCacheStats(reset=False, requests=0, ...), spec_decoding_stats=None, ...) ``` ### Reproduction (deterministic given enough wall clock) | Setup | |---| | Image: built from v0.20.0 tag, `--target vllm-openai`, CUDA 13.0, Py 3.12, torch 2.11 | | Hardware: 8× NVIDIA H200 (140 GB each) | | Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` — DeepSeek Sparse Attention + MoE + MLA) | | TP=8, EP=true | | KV: fp8, prefix-caching on, max-model-len 202752 | | Speculative: `{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}` | | Allocator: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` + `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (required to avoid torch 2.11 fragmentation OOM at boot) | | LMCache enabled via `kv_connector=LMCacheConnectorV1` | | Workload: real chat-completion traffic, ~0.2 RPS sustained, prompt sizes 1k–70k tokens | ### MTTF measured | Config | Mean Time To Failure | |---|---| | Baseline (above) | **~38 minutes** | | + `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` | **~5h 12min** | | MTP off (`speculative_config=None`) | stable indefinitely | `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` mitigates but does not fix. Disabling MTP entirely is the only path to stable serving. ### What we ruled out - Not OOM: GPU memory peaked at ~133 GB (94% util) sustained without exhausting. `expandable_segments:True` resolves the torch 2.11 fragmentation regression we initially hit. - Not the descriptor-corruption bug fixed by [#40303](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40303): no `SystemError`, `memory_fence` not on stack. - Not specific to autotune compiling kernels mid-request: disabling autotune extends MTTF 8× but doesn't eliminate the hang. - Not capacity-bound: only 2 in-flight requests when crash occurs, kv_cache_usage 0.40. - Not LMCache-specific: same crash signature on Plan B v3/v4 attempts (cu130-nightly + MTP) before LMCache wheel work. ### Likely candidates for the actual root cause (per `jsboige`'s diagnosis) 1. **MTP speculative decoding deadlock** in V1 + `step_with_batch_queue` + the multi-token draft path. `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={req: [-1, -1, ...]}` (all rejected on the failing iteration) suggests the spec decode draft itself may be the hang site. 2. **DSA (Deepseek Sparse Attention) interaction** with the MTP draft head. GLM-5.1's `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` uses DSA, and the MTP head appears to feed forward through this path. 3. Some interaction with the V1 `step_with_batch_queue` async pipeline that's specific to MoE+MLA+MTP. ### Suggested debug Per `jsboige`'s recommended isolation in #35104: - `py-spy dump --pid <Worker_TP0 PID>` at the moment of hang to identify which subsystem the worker is actually stuck in. - Reduce to TP=4 to see if the hang persists (TP-related?). - Try MTP n=1 instead of n=2 — we observed n=1 still hangs in earlier testing. We can collect `py-spy dump` next time it occurs in our deployment if helpful. Auto-rollback fires within 2s of the log signature, so we have a narrow window. ### Cross-references - [#35104](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35104) — `jsboige` diagnosed `new-TonyWang`'s report as this same bug (different from #35104's primary fix scope). - [#34449](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34449) — closed; was the original GLM-5 + MTP malformed tool-calls bug, **fixed** in v0.20.0 (we confirmed: tool tests 16/16 with MTP). This issue is the *next* MTP blocker after that one.

signal.title: [Frontend] Add Holo2 reasoning parser
signal.text: ## Purpose Add Holo2 reasoning-parser support to the Rust frontend parity roadmap. Python registers `holo2` through `DeepSeekV3ReasoningWithThinkingParser`, which defaults to DeepSeek R1 behavior. The Rust `DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser` alias has a different no-boundary default, so this adds a semantic `Holo2ReasoningParser` alias directly to the prompt-first `DeepSeekR1ReasoningParser`. The change: - exposes `holo2` as an explicit reasoning-parser name; - automatically routes `HCompany/Holo2-*` models to it; - reuses the shared `<think>...</think>` parser without adding another state machine; - adds factory registration and model-routing coverage; - adds a real `HCompany/Holo2-4B` tokenizer/template roundtrip covering enabled, disabled, and default thinking behavior. No tool-parser or inference-engine behavior is changed. Refs #44280 ### Duplicate-work check I reviewed the roadmap comments and searched open PRs by the roadmap issue number and Holo2/Rust reasoning-parser keywords. No existing claim or open PR overlaps this implementation. ## Test Plan - Verify explicit parser registration and factory listing. - Verify automatic routing of `HCompany/Holo2-4B` to `holo2`. - Exercise the real Holo2 tokenizer and chat template through the existing reasoning-and-content roundtrip. - Cover `thinking=true`, `thinking=false`, and omitted/default thinking. - Run the complete `vllm-parser` and `vllm-chat` test suites. - Run repository pre-commit hooks on the changed files. ## Test Result Passed: ```text cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all --check ``` Passed all 698 tests: ```text nix develop path:. cargo nextest run \ --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml \ --locked \ -p vllm-parser \ -p vllm-chat ``` Passed: ```text nix develop path:. -c pre-commit run ``` The real HCompany/Holo2-4B tokenizer/template roundtrip passed for enabled, disabled, and default thinking. Model-generation or accuracy evaluation is not applicable because this change does not modify inference, logits, or model output generation. The real-tokenizer/template roundtrip provides parser integration evaluation. Documentation was not changed because the existing reasoning-output documentation already lists holo2; this PR adds Rust frontend parity. ## AI assistance disclosure AI assistance was used for repository exploration, implementation planning, code review, and identifying a model-ID casing correction. I reviewed every changed line and ran all tests listed above.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Do not report finish_reason="tool_calls" when no tool call was made
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #53255. With `tool_choice="required"`, the non-streaming chat handler translates the engine's `"stop"` into `finish_reason="tool_calls"`. That translation assumes a tool call was produced, but it never checks. When the parse yields no calls — for example when no tool parser is configured, so `parser` is None and `tool_calls` is `[]` — the response goes out with `finish_reason="tool_calls"` next to an empty `tool_calls`. `finish_reason` is the documented way to detect a tool call, so a client takes the tool-execution branch and finds nothing to execute. The streaming path in the same file already gets this right — it requires `tools_streamed[i]`, set only when a tool-call delta was actually emitted, before reporting `"tool_calls"`. So today the same request answers differently depending only on `stream`. This makes the non-streaming path agree: ```python is_finish_reason_tool_calls = auto_tools_called or ( request.tool_choice and request.tool_choice == "required" and output.finish_reason == "stop" + and bool(tool_calls) ) ``` Scope is deliberately narrow: - `auto` is unaffected — `auto_tools_called` already implies non-empty tool calls. - `required` **with** a real tool call still reports `"tool_calls"`. - Named `tool_choice` is untouched; it continues to report `"stop"`, which is the existing intended behaviour documented in the comment above this expression. ## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR Checked before opening, and re-checked since: ``` gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "is_finish_reason_tool_calls" gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "finish_reason tool_calls" gh issue list --repo vllm-project/vllm --search "tool_choice required finish_reason" ``` - #46303 and #47963 both change the **streaming** path for a different defect (a tool call truncated by `max_tokens` losing its `"length"` reason). Neither touches `is_finish_reason_tool_calls`, and neither fixes the non-streaming case here. I opened #53270 for that streaming defect before finding those two, and closed it as a duplicate; my reproduction data is now on #47963. - #53258 is a bot-generated PR opened ~15 minutes after this one against the same issue. This PR came first and carries the end-to-end measurement below; only one of the two needs reviewing. ## Test Plan Unit test added: `test_required_tool_choice_does_not_claim_a_tool_call_it_did_not_make` in `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py`, extending the existing suite and reusing its `_build_minimal_metrics_serving_chat` helper (which already configures no tool parser — the exact condition that triggers this). ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \ -k required_tool_choice_does_not_claim -v ``` I could not run the suite locally — no CUDA/GPU on the machine used to prepare this — so the unit test is offered for CI. The behavioural claims below come from running a real server. End-to-end: the server was exercised over HTTP with the request from the issue, on the same host and image with the patch as the only variable, in two arms — tool parser off (the broken case) and tool parser on (the case this change could regress). ## Test Result End-to-end, `tool_choice="required"`: | Arm | `tool_calls` | `finish_reason` | | |---|---|---|---| | unpatched, no tool parser | 0 | `"tool_calls"` | contradicts the empty array | | **patched**, no tool parser | 0 | `"stop"` | fixed | | **patched**, tool parser enabled | 1 | `"tool_calls"` | unchanged — no regression | The third row is the one that matters most: the working path is untouched, and the returned call is still well formed (`get_weather({"city": "San Francisco"})`). Named `tool_choice` was checked in the same runs and is unchanged by this patch, still returning its call with `finish_reason="stop"` as before. No model evaluation is included: this changes only the `finish_reason` field selected by the serving layer. Token generation, sampling and model output are untouched. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to prepare this change (investigation, patch, test and this description), with `Assisted-by:` recorded in the commit trailer. The submitter has reviewed every changed line, ran the end-to-end verification above, and stands behind the change.

signal.title: [New Model]: TR-HASH deterministic token-routed MoE
signal.text: ## The model to consider - Model: https://huggingface.co/AETHORIA-AI/TR-HASH-MoE-200M-160B-SFT - Reference implementation: https://github.com/Complexity-ML/complexity-framework - Current serving engine: https://github.com/Complexity-ML/TR-Hash-i64 - License: Apache-2.0 for the SFT checkpoint TR-HASH is a 201.2M-parameter decoder-only causal language model with 16 layers, GQA, tied embeddings, four stored experts, top-2 activation, and an always-on shared SwiGLU path. Unlike conventional sparse MoE models, expert selection is not produced by a learned router. It is a deterministic function of token IDs, the layer index, and persisted multi-hash routing tables. ## The closest model vLLM already supports Mixtral is the closest execution shape because it combines a decoder-only transformer with top-k sparse experts: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/mixtral.py Llama is also relevant for the surrounding decoder/GQA structure. However, neither model has TR-HASH's deterministic token-ID routing or its stacked expert-weight representation. ## What's the difficulty of supporting this model? The principal differences are: 1. The MLP needs token IDs in addition to hidden states so that each layer can look up deterministic expert routes. 2. Routing tables are persisted integer buffers and must remain paired with the expert weights. 3. Routed projections are stored as stacked tensors rather than separate Linear modules: - `expert_gate`: `[num_experts, hidden_size, expert_width]` - `expert_up`: `[num_experts, hidden_size, expert_width]` - `expert_down`: `[num_experts, expert_width, hidden_size]` 4. A shared SwiGLU path is always active alongside the top-2 routed experts. 5. The public checkpoint currently uses custom framework configuration and weights. A full Hugging Face `AutoModelForCausalLM` adapter is planned but is not yet complete. The core implementation is here: - Engine: https://github.com/Complexity-ML/complexity-framework/blob/main/complexity/tr_hash/engine.py - MLP adapter: https://github.com/Complexity-ML/complexity-framework/blob/main/complexity/core/mlp/tr_hash_engine.py vLLM's Transformers backend documentation notes that custom MoE blocks should expose an `experts` attribute. We would appreciate guidance on whether TR-HASH should first target that backend through a Transformers-compatible adapter or whether the deterministic routing contract warrants a native vLLM model implementation. ## Motivation We want a standard high-throughput serving path for this open model and a deployment target for low-bit checkpoints produced through Intel AutoRound. The immediate integration chain is: `TR-HASH Hugging Face checkpoint -> AutoRound W4A16 -> vLLM serving -> Intel Low-Bit Open LLM Leaderboard` Intel leaderboard: https://huggingface.co/spaces/Intel/low_bit_open_llm_leaderboard AutoRound model support is being requested separately because its current Linear-oriented quantization path does not directly cover TR-HASH's stacked 3D expert tensors. ## Definition of done Support would be complete when: 1. vLLM can load the public TR-HASH checkpoint. 2. Deterministic routing tables remain unchanged and expert selection matches the reference implementation. 3. Fixed-prompt logits match the reference PyTorch implementation within an agreed tolerance. 4. Greedy generation produces the same token sequence for a small regression panel. 5. The model can be served through vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API. 6. The integration has a documented path for a future AutoRound W4A16 checkpoint. We are the model authors and can provide reference logits, routing traces, small test fixtures, and help with an implementation or PR.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Normalize FlashInfer prefill LSE before merging
signal.text: ## Purpose Prefix-cache hits could produce different logits from a cold prefill and eventually lead to repetitive output. This was initially observed with GLM-5.2 in a disaggregated prefill/decode deployment. KV cache digests matched before and after transfer, and the issue also reproduced with BF16 KV cache. A local prefix-cache cold/warm comparison then reproduced the logits divergence without KV transfer, narrowing the issue to the cached-context attention path. A cold prefill computes attention in one operation. On a prefix-cache hit, vLLM computes attention over the cached context and new suffix separately, then combines the two partial states with `merge_attn_states`. FlashInfer prefill kernels, including the TRT-LLM ragged kernel, return base-2 log-sum-exp values. vLLM's CUDA and Triton `merge_attn_states` implementations use natural `exp` and `log`. Passing base-2 LSE values directly therefore produces incorrect context/suffix weights. This PR: - adds a shared `log2_lse_to_ln` conversion helper; - converts LSE returned by the FlashInfer MLA prefill backend; - converts LSE returned by the TRT-LLM ragged MLA prefill backend; - converts generic FlashInfer DCP prefill LSE after the base-2 cross-rank reduction and before the natural-log attention-state merge. The conversion is performed at the external kernel boundary so the rest of vLLM continues to use the natural-log LSE contract. ### Duplicate-work check No open PR currently fixes the MLA prefill paths changed here. PR #36503 previously experimented with scaling generic FlashInfer prefill LSE in an older commit (`f10579e`), but that change is not present in its current diff. Its current scope is persistent buffer management for FlashInfer DCP decode. This PR fixes the missing conversions on current main and additionally covers both FlashInfer MLA prefill and TRT-LLM ragged MLA prefill. PR #47779 concerns SM120 sparse MLA decode DCP and does not modify these prefill merge paths. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -rs \ tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py \ -k 'test_chunked_context_backend_correctness and \ (FLASHINFER or TRTLLM_RAGGED)' .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flashinfer.py \ vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/trtllm_ragged.py git diff --check ``` Before/after error measurements used the same B300 GPU, test selection, and random sequence. The old behavior was simulated by replacing the conversion helper with an identity function at runtime. ## Test Result Affected auto/FP8 matrix: - 6 passed - 2 skipped because FlashInfer does not support the tested GLM dimensions Maximum absolute output error against the SDPA reference: | Prefill path | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | FlashInfer / DeepSeek | 0.236328 | 0.0078125 | | TRT-LLM ragged / DeepSeek | 0.228516 | 0.0078125 | | TRT-LLM ragged / GLM | 0.265625 | 0.0078125 | The results were identical across CUTLASS_MLA, FLASHINFER_MLA, and TRITON_MLA, which is consistent with the error originating in the shared context/suffix merge. Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed. The complete `test_chunked_context_backend_correctness` matrix produced 10 passed, 8 skipped, and 2 failures. Both failures are in the unchanged FlashAttention FA4 path because the local extension does not accept the `fp8_kv_dequant` keyword. They occur before LSE merging. ### AI assistance AI assistance was used. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR is described. - [x] The test plan and commands are included. - [x] Local test results and the environment-specific failures are included. - [ ] Model evaluation results must be added before submission. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix] Make Rust HF dataset endpoint configurable
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #50271. The Rust `hf` dataset loader built its Dataset Viewer API URLs from a fixed `datasets-server.huggingface.co` origin. This prevented users from routing dataset metadata and parquet discovery through an accessible Dataset Viewer service. The client also had a 120-second request timeout but no shorter connection timeout, so an unreachable host could appear to hang before prompt generation. This change: - reads the Dataset Viewer base URL from `HF_DATASETS_SERVER_ENDPOINT`, while preserving the current Hugging Face endpoint as the default; - constructs both `/info` and `/parquet` URLs with `url::Url`; - applies a 10-second connection timeout while retaining the existing request timeout and retry policy; and - documents the endpoint override. No other open pull request references #50271 or addresses this endpoint configuration. AI assistance was used in developing this change. This only changes Dataset Viewer endpoint routing and connection-failure latency; it does not affect model output or accuracy, so no model evaluation is applicable. ## Test Plan ```text cargo fmt --all --check cargo test -p vllm-bench test_dataset_server_url --no-fail-fast cargo test -p vllm-bench datasets::hf_dataset::tests --no-fail-fast cargo test -p vllm-bench --no-fail-fast git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check ``` ## Test Result - Endpoint regression tests: 2 passed. - HF dataset module: 49 passed, 2 network tests ignored. - Full `vllm-bench` suite: 169 passed, 12 ignored, 0 failed. - Rust formatting and diff checks passed.
