signal.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Pass AITER MoE the rank row count, not per-expert counts
signal.text: ## Summary `AiterExperts.apply` forwards `ExpertTokensMetadata.expert_num_tokens` — one count per *local expert* — into AITER's `num_local_tokens`. AITER defines that argument as a single value, the number of `hidden_states` rows the rank holds, and dereferences element `[0]`: ```c // aiter csrc/include/moe_sorting_opus.h const void* p_local_tokens; // [1] if not nullptr, tokens read from here ... return reinterpret_cast<const opus::index_t*>(kargs.p_local_tokens)[0]; ``` It also passes the same value as `num_rows` to activation quantisation, so AITER treats local expert 0's share as the whole rank's token count. With DeepSeek-R1's 256 experts over 8 expert-parallel ranks that entry is usually `0`: the rank quantises nothing, the fp8 activation and scale buffers keep their uninitialised `torch.empty` contents, and the GEMM turns them into NaNs. Symptom: completions come back empty, and any request with `logprobs` fails with `Out of range float values are not JSON compliant`. ## Fix Reduce the vector to the value AITER asks for. The sum is exactly the number of routed rows the rank received, and doing it on device keeps the cudagraph path free of host synchronisation. ## Test DeepSeek-R1 FP8, 8x MI350X (gfx950), `TP=1 / DP=8 / EP=8` over DeepEP, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`. Same prompt, only this change: | `num_local_tokens` | Completion | `logprobs` | |---|---|---| | after (`shape=(1,)`, `[4096]`) | `" Paris. 法国的首都是巴黎。"` | finite | | before (`shape=(32,)`, `[0, 0, 0, 0, ...]`) | `""` | HTTP 400 `Out of range float values are not JSON compliant` | In the failing case the expert output tensor comes back with the same numeric range as its input, i.e. the experts never ran. ## Scope Every `FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize` that reports `ExpertTokensMetadata` builds this argument the same way, so the DeepEP high-throughput path is affected too.

signal.title: [Rust Frontend] Fix adjacent DeepSeek V4 user content rendering
signal.text: ## Purpose The DeepSeek V4 reference encoding merges adjacent tool responses and user messages into a single user turn, joining their content with two newlines. The Rust renderer previously merged only consecutive tool responses. A tool response followed by a user message therefore produced two consecutive user role tokens: ```text <｜User｜><tool_result>result</tool_result><｜User｜>follow-up ``` Consecutive user messages had the same problem. The expected encoding uses one user role token: ``` <｜User｜><tool_result>result</tool_result> follow-up ``` The change treats contiguous user and tool-response messages as one user-content block. It emits the user role token once, joins adjacent content with two newlines, and preserves tool-result sorting without moving intervening user text. The resulting prompts match the DeepSeek V4 reference encoding and avoid non-canonical consecutive user role tokens. ## Test Plan ```bash cargo fmt --all -- --check cargo clippy -p vllm-chat --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat deepseek_v4 --locked cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat ``` ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Core][RL] Support sparse checkpoint updates through native weight loaders
signal.text:
## Purpose ### Motivation Online RL trainers commonly produce updates in checkpoint/Hugging Face coordinates: a checkpoint name, the full checkpoint shape, and either a dense tensor or flat changed indices and values. These coordinates are not the same as vLLM's runtime parameter coordinates. For example, a checkpoint tensor may be split across tensor-parallel ranks, packed with another checkpoint tensor, or mapped into expert-parallel runtime weights. The existing `sparse_nccl` backend expects an already-resolved runtime parameter name and rank-local indices, so it cannot serve as a general bridge for checkpoint-coordinate updates. This PR adds a small model-loader API that keeps the model's native `model.load_weights()` path as that bridge. The native loader continues to own checkpoint-name mapping, TP/EP placement, and packed/model-specific layouts. ### Design ```mermaid flowchart LR A["One patch-loading call
checkpoint name, full shape/dtype,
values and optional flat indices"] A --> B{"All patches in this call"} B -- "Dense" --> C["Build full checkpoint tensors"] B -- "Sparse" --> D["Build full checkpoint-shaped NaN tensors
index_copy_ fills changed checkpoint positions"] C --> L["One or more model.load_weights(...) calls
native checkpoint-to-runtime mapping
for TP/EP and packed/model-specific layouts"] D --> P["Temporarily replace process-wide
torch.Tensor.copy_
during each serialized sparse loader call"] P --> L L -- "Dense: native loader semantics" --> U["Runtime tensors updated"] L -- "Sparse: each Python Tensor.copy_" --> E{"Floating source and destination
with the same shape?"} E -- "Yes" --> M["Cast source, merge with
where(isnan(source), destination, source),
then call the original copy_"] E -- "No" --> N["Call the original copy_ unchanged
unsupported for sparse patches"] L -. "Sparse custom or non-copy_ write" .-> X["Not intercepted
unsupported for sparse patches"] M --> U N --> Y["Outside the supported sparse behavior"] X --> Y P -. "finally, after model.load_weights
returns or raises" .-> R["Restore the original Tensor.copy_"] ``` `CheckpointWeightPatch` represents either: - a dense checkpoint replacement (`indices=None`), or - a sparse checkpoint patch (`indices` and `values` over the full checkpoint shape). Sparse patches are expanded into checkpoint-shaped NaN staging tensors. The model's native loader maps those tensors into runtime-local destinations. For the supported single-copy loader path, the final same-shaped floating-point `Tensor.copy_` keeps the existing destination at NaN positions and copies the changed values elsewhere. Patches are validated before the first load. Loader calls are bounded by a checkpoint-byte batching target, and a repeated checkpoint name begins a new loader call so repeated patches preserve input order. ### Scope and failure semantics The current implementation is intentionally narrow: - sparse patches require a floating checkpoint dtype and cannot carry NaN as a real update value; - the loader must preserve NaNs through checkpoint-to-runtime mapping and end in a same-shaped floating-point `Tensor.copy_`; - the validated integration uses exclusive, serialized weight updates and a single-copy loader; - composed/multi-stage loaders and custom write paths are not supported; - sparse application is not O(nnz): it allocates a full checkpoint-shaped NaN tensor and runs a dense `torch.where`/copy at the runtime destination; - updates are not transactional. A loader error can leave a partial update, so the caller must restore a known baseline or restart and reseed before serving. ### Companion VERL integration [VERL #7227](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7227) uses this API to add a vLLM consumer for VERL's `delta_sharded` checkpoint-engine wire format. The first update is a dense seed; steady updates contain checkpoint-coordinate indices and changed values. ### Duplication check I searched open vLLM PRs for checkpoint-coordinate weight patch loading and found no matching implementation. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/model_executor/model_loader \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py -q .venv/bin/ruff check --no-cache \ vllm/model_executor/model_loader/checkpoint_weight_patch.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check --no-cache \ vllm/model_executor/model_loader/checkpoint_weight_patch.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py ``` The focused CPU test covers the dense seed, checkpoint-global sparse indices, TP-local slicing, packed Q/K destinations, repeated patch ordering, and restoration of `Tensor.copy_` after the supported path. The companion VERL integration tests additionally cover: - Qwen3-30B-A3B TP8+EP8 sparse-vs-dense and restore comparisons; - real CUDA IPC/ZMQ transfer through the companion VERL adapter; - a two-node full-NCCL versus `delta_sharded` weight-sync comparison. ## Test Result ### Focused repository test - Pytest: **1 passed**. - Ruff check: **passed**. - Ruff format check: **passed**. ### TP8+EP8 integration correctness Qwen3-30B-A3B, BF16, vLLM TP8+EP8: - 8/8 workers passed. - 32/32 selected runtime tensors matched the dense-load target with `torch.equal` after sparse apply. - 32/32 tensors returned to the checkpoint baseline after restore. - The probe covered packed QKV, norm, routed-expert `w13`, and routed-expert `w2` mappings. This is a representative runtime-tensor mapping probe, not a full-model digest or a phase-for-phase training-trajectory comparison. ### Companion VERL integration performance These are end-to-end results from the companion VERL integration, not a microbenchmark of this helper alone. | mode | steady samples | mean | median | range | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Full NCCL | 11 | 51.814 s | 51.812 s | 51.457-52.051 s | | `delta_sharded` + vLLM | 11 | 7.200 s | 7.740 s | 5.943-8.686 s | The ratio of means is **7.196x**; the conservative observed steady ratio is **5.924x**. The mean changed ratio was **0.646%**, and the mean sparse payload was **1129.4 MiB**. The one-time dense seed took **51.9 s** and is excluded from steady-state statistics. Environment: two nodes with 8 H20 GPUs per node; Qwen3-30B-A3B; FSDP1 trainer on one node; vLLM TP8+EP8 Triton-MoE rollout on the other; BF16; VERL V1 `separate_async`; NCCL `NET/Socket` over `eth0`; 12 delta and 12 full steps, with steps 2-12 used for the primary statistics. The two async jobs did not produce phase-aligned reward trajectories. The performance claim is limited to sustained weight-sync time; correctness comes from the independent bit-exact probe. ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex was used for code exploration, implementation assistance, testing, and review.
signal.author: ShuoleiWang

signal.title: [Bugfix][MLA] TritonMLA: fix illegal memory access on causal multi-token decode
signal.text: ## Purpose `TritonMLA` declared single-token decode support, so a speculative-decode verify block reached `forward_mqa` unflattened: `query_len * num_reqs` query rows against `num_reqs` rows of `block_table` / `seq_lens`. `decode_attention_fwd` launches one program per query row and indexes `tl.load(B_Seqlen + cur_batch)`, so every row past `num_decodes` is an out-of-bounds read. Reaching it takes a group whose reorder threshold is raised past 1. Ordinary MLA spec decode does not qualify: `TritonMLAMetadataBuilder` inherits `query_len_support = SINGLE_ONLY`, so multi-token queries route to prefill. The threshold is raised by the non-causal route (DSpark draft) which sets its flags after the base `__init__` has asserted `SINGLE_ONLY ⇒ threshold == 1`. `build()` then splits a *causal* batch with the raised threshold, and `forward_mqa` expands tables only under `if not causal`. Where that happens there is no fallback on either affected platform: - **NVIDIA sm_86** — `triton_mla` is the only MLA backend whose `supports_compute_capability` admits `major == 8` (CUTLASS/FlashInfer require 10, FlashAttn 9, FlashMLA 9 or 10). Reported as `Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access` (#51848). - **ROCm without AITER MLA** — `rocm.py` falls back to `[TRITON_MLA]` alone. Fixes #51848. On Kimi-K3 + DSpark, TP8, MI325: (18.01 → 45.00 tok/s), no quality regression (verified on gsm8k: **95%**) ## The fix `decode_attention_fwd` has no causal flag, but it reads each row's KV extent from `seq_lens`. A uniform verify block is a contiguous suffix, so intra-block causality is expressible as per-row extents: flatten to one decode row per query token and give row `t` extent `seq_len - (query_len - 1 - t)`. 1. `forward_mqa`: derive `query_len` from `q.shape[0] // seq_lens.shape[0]` and expand `block_table` / `seq_lens` to match, causal or non-causal. 2. `_cudagraph_support` → `UNIFORM_BATCH`, `query_len_support` → `UNIFORM`, so the reorder threshold admits `query_len > 1`. `attn_logits` workspace grows to match (workspace locks after capture). 3. `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()` asserts layers agree on `non_causal_multi_token_decode` instead of `any()`, so a non-causal draft group cannot be merged with a causal target group. ## Testing Validated on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (`ba07e4a48f`), gfx942. Rebased onto `origin/main` `9fd750f00d` ### Unit tests `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_mla_causal_verify_flatten.py` (new, 15) plus `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` (87): **102 passed**. The new file replaces the kernel with a spy and asserts on the `block_table` and `seq_lens` the backend actually submits, so it needs no GPU or Triton runtime. ### The decode path actually taken `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py` already covers this: `spec_decode_small` (4x4) and `spec_decode_medium` (6x8) install an ngram `SpeculativeConfig`, with `torch` SDPA as reference. `decode_attention_fwd` was instrumented to confirm which path runs. ```bash HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0 \ pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -q -k "1.0-1.0-auto-1-" ``` | | result | TritonMLA decode launches | |---|---|---| | before, spec_decode only | 4 passed, 16 skipped | 0 (routed to prefill) | | after, spec_decode only | 4 passed, 16 skipped | 4, causal staircase | | before, all batch specs | 24 passed, 96 skipped | 12 (single-token) | | after, all batch specs | 24 passed, 96 skipped | 16 (12 + 4 causal) | The "after, all batch specs" row re-verified on 2026-08-21 against the final tree, with 16 launches and the same shapes: ``` x2 q_rows=1 bt_rows=1 seq_lens[:8]=[1024] x4 q_rows=2 bt_rows=2 seq_lens[:8]=[32, 40] x2 q_rows=3 bt_rows=3 seq_lens[:8]=[512, 1024, 2048] x2 q_rows=8 bt_rows=8 seq_lens[:8]=[128, 256, 512, 1024] x2 q_rows=16 bt_rows=16 seq_lens[:8]=[125, 126, 127, 128, 253, 254, 255, 256] x2 q_rows=32 bt_rows=32 seq_lens[:8]=[2048] x2 q_rows=48 bt_rows=48 seq_lens[:8]=[505, 506, 507, 508, 509, 510, 511, 512] ``` Extents match `seq_len - (query_len-1-t)`. The 12 single-token launches are unchanged in count and shape, so the ordinary decode path does not regress. `bt_rows == q_rows` throughout, confirming the `block_table` expansion tracks the flatten. Skips are prefill-backend unavailability on this platform, not decode skips. ## Model evaluation GSM8K, all 1,319 questions, greedy (`temperature=0`, `seed=42`), `max_tokens=1024`, 8 concurrent clients, raw completions: | | | |---|---| | accuracy | **0.9507** (1254 / 1319) | | mean acceptance length | **3.279** of max 4.0, 40,823 drafts | | throughput | 0.449 q/s, 46.0 tok/s, 135,175 output tokens | | wall | 2,936 s | | worker faults / NaNs | none | Configuration: gfx942, 8x MI325X, TP8 + EP, target `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, drafter `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` on `TRITON_MLA` via `--attention-backend`, `dspark` method with 3 speculative tokens, 32,384 ctx. ```bash vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --enable-prompt-tokens-details --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --max-model-len 32384 --max-num-seqs 8 --speculative-config '{ "model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark", "num_speculative_tokens":3, "method": "dspark", "attention_backend": "TRITON_MLA", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}' ``` Spec-Bench: ```bash ---------------Speculative Decoding--------------- Acceptance rate (%): 63.11 Acceptance length: 2.89 Drafts: 16798 Draft tokens: 50394 Accepted tokens: 31804 Per-position acceptance (%): Position 0: 81.74 Position 1: 61.65 Position 2: 45.94 ================================================== ``` **The drafter is on TRITON_MLA precisely because this is the path the PR fixes.** **There is no same-flags unpatched baseline.** Without this patch the above configuration is the crash the PR fixes, so "unpatched, same flags" does not produce a number. This run is evidence that the causal flatten is correct under sustained load, not a before/after comparison. Independently corroborated by @maeehart on gfx942, 8x MI325X, TP8+EP, 7 spec tokens, same target/draft backend pairing, 262144 ctx: **GSM8K 95.6% strict and flexible over all 1,319 questions**, needle retrieval passed at 65K/131K/250K, 98.26% prefix-cache hit, no faults or NaNs. Their run bundles #50578 and AITER fixes, so it is integration evidence rather than an isolated measurement. @reger-men's gfx950 throughput numbers were obtained with a different implementation and are explicitly **not** a measurement of this PR. | | before | after | |---|---|---| | cudagraph mode | PIECEWISE (downgraded) | **FULL + PIECEWISE** | | throughput | 13.01 tok/s | **61.3 tok/s (4.0×)** | | per-step latency | 233.9 ms | **50.4 ms** | Removing per-launch overhead also removed cross-rank arrival skew that had been making TP collectives spin-wait: `vllm::all_reduce` 2.157 s (60.8% of Self CUDA) → 0.061 s (2.85%), arrival spread 313.8 µs → 7.1 µs. ## Correctness Same config (61.3 tok/s, including two unrelated tuning changes not in this PR): | benchmark | result | |---|---| | GSM8K, full test set (1319) | **97.2%** (1282/1319), 95% CI [96.3, 98.1] | | GPQA Diamond, 0-shot CoT (198) | **90.9%** flexible / **90.4%** strict | Hardware: - [x] Boots with FULL cudagraph capture, no downgrade message - [x] GSM8K 97.2%, GPQA Diamond 90.9% - [x] Concurrency sweep 1→128, zero errors across 100 800 generated tokens - [x] Causal-tail A/B showing acceptance is unaffected - [x] NVIDIA sm_86 — [nickus](https://github.com/nickus) on 4x RTX 3090: illegal memory access without the patch, serves with it ## AI assistance AI assistance was used. The submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. ## Related work - [#47310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47310) predates this PR and proposes the `query_len_support` half of this change and diagnoses the same flag coupling — credit there for that analysis. It has gone stale: Unmodified since 2026-07-09. - [#51171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51171) (open, 2026-08-05) also corrects cudagraph support reporting for non-causal draft groups, but keys a conditional `get_cudagraph_support` override on `non_causal_multi_token_decode`. That leaves the *causal* path still declaring single-token support — which is this bug. Causal is the base case, so the flag pair is set unconditionally here. The two changes are compatible; #51171 additionally moves an AITER host sync out of `forward_mqa`, which this PR does not touch. - [#51685](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51685) (open, 2026-08-10) reworks the same decode path for a native fp8 KV cache (`triton_mla.py` +97/-33). Different purpose, no overlap in intent. - [#51705](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51705) (open, 2026-08-10) is a Kimi-K3 DSpark decode-context-parallelism feature (+760/-107) that happens to carry this PR's `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()` fix verbatim — the same `any()` → set-and-pop rewrite under a byte-identical assertion message, differing only in a local variable name. This PR is six days earlier and is scoped to the bug; #51705 needs the same correction as a prerequisite for its own grouping work. - [#51848](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51848) is an issue, not a PR, and was closed on 2026-08-11. It is the independent sm_86 report of this bug. Its reporter confirmed there that this PR supersedes it and declined to open a competing one. - [#50911](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50911) is complementary: the non-causal draft path on TokenSpeed/NVIDIA. No file overlap. - [#52218](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52218) (draft, opened 2026-08-13) — *"[Attention] Support speculative decode in Triton MLA"*. Same fix, same mechanism: uniform multi-token query support, the verify block flattened to decode rows, causal prefix lengths per row, padding rows clamped, split-KV workspace grown. This PR predates it by nine days and is a superset: #52218 is a draft touching only `triton_mla.py`, and does not correct `MLAAttentionSpec.merge()`, so a non-causal draft group can still be merged into a causal target group.

signal.title: [6/N] Share HiSparse host cache across TP ranks
signal.text: ## Summary This PR optimizes #51324 with the following improvements: - Resolve shared/private Host pool mode in the KV cache planner. - Fall back to private pools when the Indexer block layout cannot be represented by the shared mmap layout. - Propagate the resolved mode and physical Host block stride through `KVCacheConfig`. - Roll back the shared Host region when GPU KV allocation or HiSparse worker initialization fails. - Check physical Host RAM only in the shared mmap creator process. - Fail joiners promptly when the creator fails and unlinks an incomplete mmap. - Add real multiprocess same-slot visibility coverage. - Clarify logical versus physical `host_pool_gib` capacity and startup logging. This is intentionally based on `feat/hisparse-metrics` so it remains the [3/N] change in the HiSparse stack. cc @MatthewBonanni

signal.title: [Core] Disable fuse_allreduce_rms under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT (non-deterministic under TP)
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51290. `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` is bit-stable on a single GPU but **non-deterministic under tensor parallelism**: repeating a byte-identical workload against the same engine returns different logprobs (and, on near-ties, different tokens) once `tensor_parallel_size > 1`. The cause is the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm pass (`fuse_allreduce_rms`, a FlashInfer kernel), which reduces in a run-to-run-varying order under TP. It is enabled by `enable_allreduce_rms_fusion()` exactly when `TP > 1` on Hopper/Blackwell with flashinfer, i.e. the regime where batch invariance is expected to hold. This disables the fusion when batch invariance is requested, mirroring the existing `disable_custom_all_reduce = True` guard in `ParallelConfig` (which handles the analogous non-batch-invariant custom all-reduce path). It is an 8-line early return; TP=1 and non-batch-invariant runs are unaffected. ### Relationship to #50505 This is the Hopper/Blackwell-side complement to #50505. On cc≥90 the `fuse_allreduce_rms` pass replaces the TP all-reduce with a FlashInfer fused kernel, bypassing the custom all-reduce that #50505 pins to its deterministic 1-stage path. Disabling the fusion here lets the all-reduce fall through to that path. The two compose: with #50505 the fallback is the fast 1-stage custom all-reduce (~97% throughput); without it, NCCL (see Performance). On A100 the fusion pass is inactive (cc<90), so #50505 alone covers that hardware; this PR is what extends the fix to Hopper/Blackwell. ## Test Plan Run the same workload 8 times against one engine and count distinct bit-exact outputs (from #51290). Requires the `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard because TP>1 uses spawn. ```python import os, itertools os.environ["VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT"] = "1" from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams def main(): llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", tensor_parallel_size=4, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, enable_prefix_caching=True) sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=1, logprobs=20) prompts = [f"{'the quick brown fox ' * 50} item {i}:" for i in range(2000)] runs = [] for _ in range(8): out = llm.generate(prompts, sp, use_tqdm=False) runs.append([(o.outputs[0].token_ids[0], o.outputs[0].logprobs[0][o.outputs[0].token_ids[0]].logprob) for o in out]) groups = [] for i, r in enumerate(runs): if not any(runs[g[0]] == r and g.append(i) is None for g in groups): groups.append([i]) print(f"{len(groups)} distinct bit-exact outputs over {len(runs)} identical runs") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ## Test Result Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, H100, vLLM 0.25.1 (the fix function is byte-identical on `main`): | config | distinct bit-exact outputs / 8 | verdict | |---|---|---| | `tensor_parallel_size=1` | 1 | deterministic (unaffected) | | `tensor_parallel_size=4`, before | 8 | non-deterministic | | `tensor_parallel_size=4`, after this PR | 1 | deterministic | With the fix, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` at TP=4 auto-disables the fusion (the `Enabled custom fusions: allreduce_rms` / `Auto-selected flashinfer allreduce` log lines disappear) and the 8 identical runs collapse to a single bit-exact output. Also confirmed on Llama-3.1-70B (dense, TP=4), and the bug reproduces on both 0.20.2 and 0.25.1. ## Performance Disabling the fusion has a throughput cost, confined to `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` + TP>1 (non-batch-invariant runs and TP=1 are unaffected). Decode-heavy generation, TP=4, H100: | model | fusion on (baseline) | fusion off (this PR) | cost | |---|---|---|---| | Qwen2.5-7B (128 x 256 tok) | 18,355 tok/s | 7,450 tok/s | ~2.5x slower | | Llama-3.1-70B (64 x 128 tok) | 1,618 tok/s | 935 tok/s | ~1.7x slower | This cost reflects the NCCL fallback used before #50505. With #50505's deterministic 1-stage custom all-reduce enabled, the all-reduce falls through to that path instead, which runs at ~97% of fused throughput at default dispatch. So the number above is a pre-#50505 artifact, not an inherent cost of this PR. The cost is largest for decode-heavy workloads, where the all-reduce runs every layer per token; prefill-heavy workloads (long prompt, few output tokens) see considerably less. I checked whether a cheaper, performance-preserving fix inside the fused kernel exists, and none does. The fused kernel is nondeterministic by construction, and no config knob restores determinism: - **Backend:** both `mnnvl` and `trtllm` are nondeterministic on 0.25.1 (H100). `mnnvl` (multicast/Lamport) diverges with token flips. `trtllm` (fixed-order fp32 reduction, but Lamport/two-shot) is smaller-magnitude yet still not bit-exact: 8 distinct logprob groups over 8 identical runs (0 token flips that run, but the sub-bit-exact residual still tips near-ties at scale). - **`fp32_acc`:** already `True` by default, insufficient. - **Autotune:** `enable_flashinfer_autotune=False` does not help. The divergence is intra-process (repeated `generate()` against one engine diverge with the kernel selection already fixed), so it is the kernel's runtime reduction order, not autotune selection. - **One-shot:** forcing `use_oneshot=True` overflows the one-shot workspace on large tensors, and the one-shot path is itself nondeterministic on small tensors. So disabling the fusion under BI is the correct trade, consistent with the existing `disable_custom_all_reduce` guard. Performance is recovered by #50505 (the deterministic 1-stage custom all-reduce this PR falls through to). A fully-fused deterministic kernel would only claw back the last few percent over that and is not needed here.

signal.title: perf: Optimize sliding window cache hit search time complexity to O(N/K) from O(N)
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR implements an outstanding TODO in find_longest_cache_hit for the sliding window manager, reducing the worst-case time complexity of cache miss searches from $O(N)$ to $O(N/K)$ (where $N$ is max_num_blocks and $K$ is sliding_window_contiguous_blocks). Previously, searching for a contiguous cache sequence scanned backward block-by-block. In low cache-hit rate scenarios, this resulted in an **O(N)** linear scan overhead. By replacing the sequential for loop with a while loop, this PR introduces a Boyer-Moore-style lookahead: we now probe the beginning of the required contiguous window (i - K + 1) before evaluating the rest of the sequence. If the boundary block is a cache miss, we can conclusively skip the entire window, aggressively pruning the search space. ## Test Plan 1. Correctness: Ran the v1 core test suite to ensure the jump logic does not break block alignment or drop_eagle_block behavior. pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py -vv pytest tests/v1/core/ -vv 2. Performance: Created a localized micro-benchmark script using mock vLLM objects to simulate cache hit/miss scenarios without full engine initialization overhead. Tested on a local RTX 3070 Ti. ## Test Result The optimization eliminates severe CPU blocking delays during large context misses, speeding up worst-case scenarios by ~15x to ~45x. As expected, the jump logic introduces a negligible constant-factor overhead (1-37µs) in highly fragmented cache scenarios due to occasional double-lookups, which is a highly favorable trade-off for flattening the O(N) scaling. Main Branch Original (O(N)) Scenario | Avg Time | Iterations ----------------------------------------------------------------- 100% Cache Miss (N=1024, K=64) | 49.56 us/iter | 50000 iters 100% Cache Hit (N=1024, K=64) | 23.08 us/iter | 50000 iters Scattered Misses (N=1024, K=64) | 411.15 us/iter | 50000 iters Hit at end of sequence | 23.73 us/iter | 50000 iters Large Context Miss (N=8192, K=256) | 414.51 us/iter | 50000 iters The PR (Optimized O(N/K)) Scenario | Avg Time | Iterations ----------------------------------------------------------------- 100% Cache Miss (N=1024, K=64) | 3.31 us/iter | 50000 iters ~15x speedup 100% Cache Hit (N=1024, K=64) | 24.29 us/iter | 50000 iters ~1x Scattered Misses (N=1024, K=64) | 448.64 us/iter | 50000 iters ~0.9x expected because of double lookup of block Hit at end of sequence | 24.28 us/iter | 50000 iters ~1x Large Context Miss (N=8192, K=256) | 9.06 us/iter | 50000 iters ~ 50x speedup Please view attached benchmark script for how the benchmark was produced. [bench_cache.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31309313/bench_cache.py) --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Kernel] Support head_dim=512 in fused QK-norm+RoPE (enables Gemma4)
signal.text: ### Purpose vLLM ships a fused Q/K-RMSNorm + RoPE path — the `fused_qk_norm_rope` CUDA/HIP kernel and the `enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion` inductor pass that rewrites `rms_norm(q) → rms_norm(k) → rotary_embedding` into one op. Both were capped at `head_dim ∈ {64, 128, 256}`: - The pass (`vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/qk_norm_rope_fusion.py`) loops over the model's `Attention` layers and, if **any** `head_size` is outside `SUPPORTED_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_HEAD_DIMS`, logs a warning and returns **without registering the pattern** — so the fusion is a no-op for that model. - The C++ dispatch (`csrc/libtorch_stable/fused_qknorm_rope_kernel.cu`) has `switch(head_dim) { case 64/128/256; default: STD_TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unsupported head dimension") }`. **Gemma4 uses `head_dim=512`**, so the fusion never applied — its `q_norm`, `k_norm`, and RoPE ran as separate per-layer kernels. This PR adds head_dim=512 so the fused path can be used for Gemma4 (and any future head_dim=512 model). ### Changes 1. **`csrc/libtorch_stable/fused_qknorm_rope_kernel.cu`** — two parts: - Add `case 512:` to both `switch(head_dim)` dispatchers: the single-head `launchFusedQKNormRope` (`<<<…, 0, stream>>>`) and the `LAUNCH_N_TOKEN_HEADS` macro in `launchFusedQKNormRopeNTokenHeads` (`<<<…, smem_bytes, stream>>>`). - Add a **`packed_as<uint, 8>`** specialization. The kernel's vectorized load/store uses `packed_as<uint, head_dim/64>`, previously specialized only for 1/2/4 (`uint`/`uint2`/`uint4`, ≤16 B). head_dim=512 → `head_dim/64 = 8`, i.e. a 32-byte per-thread vector; without the specialization the template is undefined and the build fails (`implicit instantiation of undefined template 'packed_as<unsigned int, 8>'`). No native vector type exceeds 16 B, so the new type packs two `uint4` (`struct alignas(16) uint8_pack { uint4 x, y; }`). Safe because `vec_T` is only ever reinterpreted as a raw byte buffer (never `.x/.y/.z/.w`), so a 32-byte aligned load/store lowers to two 128-bit accesses. The `static_assert(head_dim % 64 == 0)` already holds for 512. 2. **`vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/qk_norm_rope_fusion.py`** — add `512` to `SUPPORTED_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_HEAD_DIMS` (the comment already says "keep in sync with the switch statements"). Launch/occupancy notes: the single-head kernel maps one warp (32 threads) to a token-head, so head_dim=512 → 16 elements/thread (vs 8 for 256) — well within registers, no dynamic smem. `token_heads_per_warp` auto-selects to 1 except on SM 9.0, so the single-head kernel is the path taken on ROCm; the NTokenHeads case is added for CUDA/completeness (its auto-heuristic caps `N ≤ 4` for `head_dim ≥ 256`, whose dynamic smem fits H100 LDS). ### Scope / what is intentionally not changed - **Additive only.** The 64/128/256 paths, all other models, and non-fused paths are untouched. Nothing changes unless `enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion` is on and the model has head_dim=512. - Fuses **Q/K-norm + RoPE only** (what the existing pattern covers). Gemma4's weightless **`v_norm`** is not part of the pattern and stays a separate kernel; **KV-shared layers** (which RoPE only Q) don't match the two-sided pattern and stay as-is. Both are correct, just not fused. ### Relation to existing PRs (not a duplicate) Searched open `vllm-project/vllm` PRs (`fused_qk_norm_rope head`, `qk_norm_rope 512`, `FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE`). No open PR adds a head_dim=512 dispatch. Related but distinct: - **#50466** *[Helion] Optimize fused QK norm RoPE on B200/H100* — perf tuning of the existing dims on NVIDIA; no new head_dim. - **#43166**, **#50903** — bugfixes (32-bit offset overflow; divergent warp collectives), not new head_dims. - **#49744**, **#52676**, **#50670** — enable the fusion for *other* models (Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.6, LFM2.5); none add 512. - **#40922** — a register-based cos/sin variant for the NTokenHeads kernel; orthogonal. This PR is the only one extending the supported head_dim set to 512. ### Test Plan > **Not yet verified end-to-end** — requires rebuilding the C++ extension (`_C_stable_libtorch`) for the `.cu` change. 1. **Op unit check.** Call `torch.ops._C.fused_qk_norm_rope` with head_dim=512 tensors and compare to an eager `q_norm/k_norm + rotary_emb` reference (`torch.allclose`, bf16 tol). Include a **partial-rotary** case (`rotary_dim < 512`) since Gemma4 sets per-layer rope. 2. **Pass actually fires (key risk).** Serve Gemma4 with `-O.pass_config.enable_qk_norm_rope_fusion=true`; confirm the pass match-summary logs > 0 matches and a trace shows the per-layer q/k-norm + RoPE replaced by `fused_qk_norm_rope`. **Caveat:** the pattern keys on the `_C.rms_norm` custom op; if the model's q/k norms lower to a different rmsnorm op (e.g. CK-tile/aiter on ROCm), the pattern may not match even with head_dim=512 supported — this must be confirmed on the target backend. 3. **Accuracy (output-affecting → required).** gsm8k via `lm_eval`, with fusion on vs off — must match within noise. 4. **Serving benchmark.** `vllm bench serve` sweep, fusion on vs off (**being run by submitter**). ### Test Result _To be filled._ | eval | fusion off | fusion on | |--|--|--| | gsm8k (flexible-extract) | _x.xxx_ | _x.xxx_ | | gsm8k (strict-match) | _x.xxx_ | _x.xxx_ | Benchmark (`vllm bench serve`, input 4096 / output 140, mean of 3 seeds), fusion off → on: | concurrency | output tok/s | median TTFT ms | median TPOT ms | req/s | |--|--|--|--|--| | 1 | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ | | 4 | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ | | 16 | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ | | 64 | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ | | 128 | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ | _ → _ |

signal.title: [Bug] DeepseekV4 cannot start on sm_121 (GB10): DeepGEMM assumed available, with no working fallback path
signal.text: ### Your current environment - vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev608+g99a10304d` (container image, aarch64) - 2× NVIDIA GB10 (**sm_121**, 121 GiB unified memory each), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.173.02 - Two-node TP=2 via the built-in multi-node `mp` executor (`--nnodes 2 --node-rank {0,1} --master-addr … --distributed-executor-backend mp`, rank 1 `--headless`) - Model: `MJPansa/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4` (mixed precision: routed experts NVFP4, attention / shared experts / head not quantized) - `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` and `VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` are set Other models start and serve fine on the same two-node setup with the same image (Qwen3-235B-A22B-NVFP4, Mistral-Small-4-119B, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8), so the cluster wiring itself is good. ### 🐛 Describe the bug DeepseekV4 cannot start on sm_121. There are two separate architecture gates that report "supported" and then fail inside compiled kernels. **1. `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` calls DeepGEMM unconditionally** `vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py` has three call sites for `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`. Two of them are guarded: ```python use_deep_gemm = is_deep_gemm_supported() ... if use_deep_gemm: tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm(...) else: _tilelang_hc_prenorm_gemm(...) ``` The third one, inside `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` (the first-layer 2-D input path taken from `models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py`), is not: ```python from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm( residual_flat, fn_broadcast, gemm_out_mul, gemm_out_sqrsum, n_splits, ) ``` On sm_121 this aborts during `determine_available_memory`: ``` RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Assertion error (/workspace/.deps/deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/hyperconnection.hpp:56): Unsupported architecture' ``` The shipped DeepGEMM extension only contains kernels for two architectures: ``` $ strings vllm/third_party/deep_gemm/_C.cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu.so | grep -oE 'sm[0-9]{2,3}' | sort -u sm100 sm90 ``` Note this happens **even with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`**. That env var does work — `is_deep_gemm_supported()` returns `False` with it set and `True` without it — but this call site never consults it. A fix that works: guard the call and fall back to `_torch_hc_prenorm_gemm`, which already exists in the same file and implements exactly this contract (`out[0] = x.float() @ fn.t()`, `sqrsum[0] = x.float().square().sum(-1)`); the broadcast shapes line up as-is. It requires a single split, so `n_splits` has to be forced to 1 on the fallback path before the output tensors are allocated. With that patch the model loads all 48 shards and gets past this point. **2. `CutlassScaledMM.is_supported()` ignores compute capability** Past the first issue, DeepseekV4's attention input projections fail: ``` File "vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py", line 493, in _run_parallel_input_projections File "vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 461, in apply File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/BlockScaledMMLinearKernel.py", line 132, in apply_weights File "vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py", line 320, in apply_block_scaled_mm RuntimeError: dispatch_scaled_mm, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_helper.hpp:17 ``` The selection gate in `kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py` is: ```python @classmethod def is_supported(cls, compute_capability: int | None = None) -> tuple[bool, str | None]: if not current_platform.is_cuda(): return False, "requires CUDA." return True, None ``` `compute_capability` is accepted and never used, so the CUTLASS c3x kernel is selected on any CUDA device and then rejects sm_121 in the C++ dispatcher. A Triton implementation exists in the same directory, but `use_triton` on `BlockScaledMMLinearKernel` only affects the input-quantisation step, not the matmul, and there is no env var to override the backend choice. ### Suggested fix Both gates should consult compute capability rather than assuming Hopper/datacenter-Blackwell: - `CutlassScaledMM.is_supported()` should return `False` on architectures without the compiled c3x kernels so selection can fall through to the Triton kernel. - `is_deep_gemm_supported()` should reflect the architectures actually compiled into the extension (currently sm90/sm100), not just the env var — otherwise every DeepGEMM call site needs to be individually correct. - `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` should be guarded like its two siblings regardless. Happy to open a PR for the `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang` guard if that shape of fix is acceptable.

signal.title: [MooncakeStore] Report KV load tier in cache events
signal.text: ## Purpose Report the actual MooncakeStore replica tier in KV cache events. Mooncake already exposes whether a loaded replica is memory-backed or disk-backed, but this information was not propagated to `BlockStored` events. This change maps: * memory-backed replica → `CPU` * disk-backed replica → `STORAGE` * unknown tier → `None` Successful events are emitted only for blocks that actually load successfully. Scheduler lookup and connector protocol behavior are unchanged. ## Test Plan Run the focused MooncakeStore worker tests: ```bash python -m pytest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \ -v \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit \ -k "test_recv_thread_emits_tiered_events_after_rotation_and_split or test_recv_thread_emits_unknown_tier_with_no_medium or test_recv_thread_does_not_emit_event_for_failed_load or test_recv_thread_skips_tier_lookup_when_events_and_logging_disabled" ``` Also run an end-to-end MooncakeStore smoke test on the DGX/A100 setup to exercise the real replica-tier lookup path. ## Test Results ### Focused unit tests ```text 4 passed, 112 deselected in 7.02s ``` Validated: * memory-backed replicas map to `CPU` * disk-backed replicas map to `STORAGE` * unknown tier leaves `medium` unset * failed loads do not emit successful `BlockStored` events * replica-tier lookup is skipped when both KV events and tier logging are disabled * block hashes remain correctly aligned through rotation and disk-budget splitting ### Integration smoke test Ran vLLM with MooncakeStore on an A100 using a 256 MB embedded Mooncake segment. A real Mooncake-backed reload reported: ```text batch_keys=35 memory_keys=35 disk_keys=0 unknown_keys=0 success_keys=35 failed_keys=0 bytes_by_tier={'memory': 82575360, 'disk': 0, 'unknown': 0} ``` This confirms that the runtime replica metadata path correctly identifies real memory-backed loads. Disk persistence was also exercised successfully, but a disk-only reload could not be observed with the embedded-store setup because the in-memory replica remains available. A true disk-backed reload would require a standalone-store configuration. The focused unit tests directly validate the disk-replica → `STORAGE` event mapping.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Allocate packed outputs in fused_q_kv_rmsnorm so q_b_proj keeps its low-latency GEMM path at decode
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix a silent performance bug: `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` allocates its outputs with `torch.empty_like(qr)`, but `qr`/`kv` are column slices of the fused `qkv_a` projection output. PyTorch preserves the strides of size-1 dims, so at `num_tokens == 1` (single-sequence decode) `empty_like` returns a tensor carrying the **parent buffer's row stride** — e.g. `(2112, 1)` for a `[1, 1536]` `q_c` slice: ```python >>> qkv = torch.empty(1, 2112) >>> q = qkv[:, :1536] >>> torch.empty_like(q).stride() (2112, 1) # is_contiguous() is True, but not packed row-major ``` The Kimi-K3 low-latency GEMM dispatch (`low_latency_gemm._is_packed_row_major`, which requires `stride == (shape[1], 1)`) then rejects `q_c`, and `q_b_proj` silently falls back to `F.linear` → cuBLAS on **every decode step**, even though `(2304, 1536)` is listed in `KIMI_K3_PROJECTIONS`. `num_tokens >= 2` happens to produce packed strides, so only decode is affected — which is why this never showed up in prefill or batched benchmarks. The fallback is not just a missed fusion. On one SM103 machine (148 SMs) the cuBLAS heuristic picks `nvjet_sm103_tst_16x64_64x16_2x1_v_bz_TNN` at ~10.9 µs/call for this `[1,1536]×[1536,2304]` GEMM, vs 4.5 µs (in-graph) for the intended `dsv3_fused_a` kernel — ~150 µs per decode step across Kimi-K3's 24 MLA layers at TP8. On another SM103 machine (152 SMs) the heuristic happens to land on a faster kernel (~3.1 µs), so the cost of this bug is machine-dependent and easy to miss. Fix: allocate packed row-major outputs explicitly. Packed outputs are strictly better for every downstream consumer of these tensors. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py ``` Adds `test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_outputs_are_packed`, which feeds column slices of a fused buffer (the real call pattern from `mla.py`) at `num_tokens ∈ {1, 16}` and asserts packed output strides plus numerical correctness. The `num_tokens == 1` case fails before this change (`stride (768, 1) != (192, 1)`) and passes after. End-to-end A/B on Kimi-K3, TP8, single 8×GPU SM103 node (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, isl 128 / osl 32, torch-profiled serving, identical config except this one file): ## Test Result Unit tests: 13 passed (8 correctness, 3 grid-cap, 2 new packed-stride). Serving A/B (decode-step stats over 31 steps, per-rank torch traces): | metric (concurrency 1) | before | after | |---|---|---| | decode step wall p50 | 9.251 ms | **9.075 ms (−1.9%)** | | TPOT | 9.54 ms | 9.36 ms | | q_b_proj kernel | `nvjet_…_16x64_64x16_2x1` 10.87 µs ×24/step | `fused_a_gemm_kernel<1,2304,1536>` 4.48 µs ×24/step | | gemm-group exclusive time | — | −148.5 µs/step | Concurrency 16 (control, bug does not trigger at `num_tokens >= 2`): step wall p50 16.054 → 16.035 ms — unchanged within noise, as expected. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [CI][Bugfix] Use a prompt that survives offload-resume rounding in mamba offload test
signal.text: ## Summary `test_mamba_cpu_offload_boundary` asserts that text generated with CPU KV-offload is identical to the same prompt generated cold. Those two paths are not bit-exact, so the assertion holds only by luck of the prompt, and the current prompt stopped being lucky on the torch 2.14 / triton 3.8 pin (tracked in pytorch/pytorch#193431). Per layer, the two paths call different kernels: | path | calls | |---|---| | cold | `causal_conv1d_fn` `(4096, 33)` then `selective_scan_fn` `(4096, 33)`, `has_initial_state=False` | | resume | `causal_conv1d_update` `(1, 4096)` then `selective_state_update`, with `conv_state_indices` set | The cold path scans the whole prompt; the resume path reloads the offloaded state and runs the decode-style update for the single recomputed token. They round differently, and the SSM recurrence amplifies it to **~0.8% mean relative error** at the last prompt token by layer 47, on **torch 2.13 as well as 2.14** (47 of 48 layers differ on both). Whether that flips a greedy argmax inside the 128-token window is prompt-dependent. Screening 12 prompts through the failing case (`all`, `block-mid-prompt`) on both channels: | prompt | torch 2.13 | torch 2.14 | |---|---|---| | `Hi. Give me a set of trivia questions and their answers ` (current) | pass | **FAIL** | | `The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog repeatedly ` | **FAIL** | **FAIL** | | `To be or not to be, that is the question posed by Hamlet ` | **FAIL** | pass | | other 9 | pass | pass | Two prompts fail on torch 2.13 and a different pair fails on 2.14, so neither channel is the "correct" baseline. Roughly 1 prompt in 4 trips this. This PR switches `_PROMPT_TEXT` to one that holds on both channels and documents the constraint so it is not changed casually. It deliberately keeps the `cold == cpu` assertion rather than pinning golden outputs, which would be GPU- and pin-specific. Note this is a test fix, not a correctness fix. Making the paths bit-identical would require the resume path to recompute through the same kernel and shape as the cold path, which defeats resuming from stored state. `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` would address it but currently raises `VLLM batch_invariant mode is not supported for MAMBA1_ATTN`. ## Not a duplicate Checked open PRs for `test_offloading_connector`, "mamba cpu offload boundary", and `193431 in:body`. The only open PR touching this file is #50087 (per-request store strategy hook), whose diff contains no reference to `test_mamba_cpu_offload_boundary` or `_PROMPT_TEXT`. No open PR addresses this failure. ## Test plan Ran the full test on both torch channels using the CI images for commit `6accb779`, same vLLM code, only the torch/triton channel differing, on an NVIDIA H100: ``` cd /vllm-workspace/tests && python3 -m pytest -q \ v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py::test_mamba_cpu_offload_boundary ``` | image | torch / triton | before | after | |---|---|---|---| | `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:6accb779…` | 2.13.0+cu130 / 3.7.1 | 2 passed | **2 passed** | | `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:6accb779…-torch-nightly` | 2.14.0.dev20260810+cu130 / 3.8.0 | 1 failed, 1 passed | **2 passed** | Lint: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.14.0, the pinned version) both clean on the changed file. ## Model evaluation Not applicable: this changes only a test prompt, no library code, so no model output or serving behaviour changes. ## AI assistance AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation and to prepare this change.

signal.title: [RFC]: Opt-out control for individual startup kernel warmups
signal.text: ### Motivation. `kernel_warmup()` (vllm/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py:98-215) runs a fixed warmup sequence from `Worker.compile_or_warm_up_model` (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:728), just before CUDA graph capture. Per the module docstring (kernel_warmup.py:3-7) the sequence exists for JIT'ed kernels. Some entries are already individually controllable — `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip` (:162-166), `kernel_config.enable_cutedsl_warmup` (:149), `kernel_config.enable_flashinfer_autotune` (:176-183) — and `kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup` (:110) is an all-or-nothing gate for the registry. But the set is ad hoc, and some entries have no switch at all: `qwen_triton_warmup` (:126) sits outside every gate. We maintain an out-of-tree hardware platform plugin for a non-CUDA accelerator, which redirects the GDN ops to an AOT-compiled kernel library. With no JIT to hide, the warmup is pure startup cost for us — and the dummy inputs upstream builds for the reference Triton kernels do not satisfy our AOT kernels' host-side argument validation. Concretely, `_warm_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel` (vllm/model_executor/warmup/qwen_triton_warmup.py:203-241) builds `initial_state` as a rank-2 tensor (:216-220) and passes it at :235. The reference Triton path never notices, since it only reads `initial_state.stride(0)` (vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/fused_sigmoid_gating.py:231) and forwards the tensor as a raw pointer (:253). Our kernel requires rank 4 and rejects it, so engine startup fails. ### Current workaround. Our plugin monkeypatches the private `qwen_triton_warmup._warm_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel` into a no-op. It depends on a private symbol and breaks on any upstream refactor, which is what prompted this RFC. ### Proposed Change. One generic opt-out axis, rather than a new env var per warmup. Two sketches: **A — named warmups + skip list.** Give each entry in `kernel_warmup()` a stable name and add e.g. `VLLM_SKIP_KERNEL_WARMUPS=qwen_triton,deep_gemm`. This mirrors `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS` (vllm/envs.py:1716-1724, consumed at kernel_warmup.py:218-234), which is already a comma-separated name skip list. **B — platform hook.** `current_platform.get_skip_kernel_warmups() -> set[str]`, consumed where `KernelConfig.set_platform_defaults` (vllm/config/kernel.py:285-311) already calls `current_platform.get_default_ir_op_priority` (vllm/platforms/interface.py:1299). A platform knows whether its kernels are JIT or AOT, so a plugin can declare this itself instead of asking operators to set env vars. The two compose: B supplies the default, A lets a user override it. Default behaviour is unchanged — an empty skip list or an unimplemented hook runs every warmup exactly as today. Purely additive and backward compatible. ### Feedback Period. _No response_ ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. _No response_ ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
